I grew up on 62nd and richmond on the southside of chicago. i was hoping that a pizza place like home would come to tn. I lovedeepdish pizza and 312 you were on point. The best pizza i have had in the state of tn. Thankyou for coming to tn.

Brunch was awesome.  Service excellent! 
The breakfast burrito with brisket was incredible. 

We loved the atmosphere and felt the great vibe. You have to order up at the counter and bring your number to your table.  

I have to compare this place with Peg Leg Porker and I'd have to say i prefer Edley's hands down.  Peg Leg felt like more of a production with  a few too many tight tables and had the cafeteria feel. Edley's felt more comfortable and had a friendly family like vibe. 

Tammy, one of the food runners was awesome.  My friend wanted a second breakfast burrito and stood in the long line to order another one and was disappointed to learn they had stopped serving from the brunch menu and was only serving from the lunch menu. A few minutes later Tammy walked up to our table and asked what we had wanted. We told her what happened and within a few minutes she returned  with a banana pudding as a consultation. WOW. The pudding was awesome, but the sentiment was even better. 

The bloody Mary's were excellent too (one of the best we've had). Spencer, the bartender hooked us up. Oh and the Nashville Nasty (fried chicken covered with sausage gravy) is a must try. The breakfast biscuit was our least favorite.

So if you are one of the people trying to figure out if you should go to Peg Leg or Edleys,  my vote is Edley's. Our group came back 4 times in 3 days.

Tuna Bar is a new sushi digs in Old City, a relatively upscale neighborhood in a city flooded with mediocre sushi restaurants. I frequent laban's favorites, bubblefish being one of them and the last visit left something to be desired. The fork in the road left me with two options, Royal Izakaya or Tuna Bar, and boy am I glad I chose the latter.

The ambiance is on point, and the service is friendly and welcoming. The menu is curated beautifully, from my understanding they narrowed it down quite a bit from the other location. This means everything on the menu is guaranteed to be fantastic and FRESH.

We started with the steamed chicken dumplings which were light and steamed to perfection. The ginger salad followed with slices of avocado and wonderfully balanced ginger dressing that wasn't too sweet. And they even do spring mix, which was great considering romaine isn't the best these days. 

For our sushi selections we went with the classic dragon roll, the east roll, the j & j roll, and 4 pieces of the tasmanian salmon, which is a fattier cut of wild caught alaskan salmon. The fish absolutely melted in your mouth and highlighted the night beautifully. The dragon roll was crafted wonderfully and the rice on every selection seemed to highlight the delicate subtleties of genuinely fresh fish. The wasabi was even a notch above. I don't know what else I can say besides try it for yourself. The preparation of everything was so wonderfully thought out and you can tell they care about what they do here. Ken was also present and very humble about my compliments.

6/5

We came here last night and it was tasty.  Of course we had spend a long day of Black Friday sales so we were famished.  We said we would stop at the next place we saw so here it is.
My kids loved the food I must say I was really jealous of their choices.  My son had ribs with potato wedges, and beans.  My daughter had a bbq beef sandwhich that couldn't even fit in her mouth.   For my fiance he had the steak sandwich which was the size of half the plate.  My kids had sarsaparilla in a boot mug.
We are from the midwest and enjoyed our meals thoroughly.
My mother in law will be here around Christmas and we will definitely be back! 
I recommend it for a nice steak dinner--it is tasty!
Now the interior decorations....hmmm just have to get past that.

Food is excellent, sides are massive. But HORRIBLE customer service i waited nearly 2 hours for my food to be delivered not to mention i was on hold for 15minutes waiting to order. I will pick up my food next time before i ever think of having it delivered. Always heard great things about this place glad i got to give it a try sadly i had to rate it a 4 because of the wait time.

The shrimp enchilada with goat cheese was spectacular. Unfortunately, the restaurant was so loud I would hesitate to go back. (We visited on a Sunday evening in February when the weather was unusually warm. Maybe everyone who is suffering from Cabin Fever went out that night. I don't know.)  Also, the free Margarita tasted like Sweet Water. However the enchilada was worth the price alone.  I would give the food five stars.

Good cofffee...
Great service, a small cramped restaurant. Crab omlette was delightful, perfect poach eggs with corned beef hash, needed to caramelize with potatoes and onions a bit more before serving. 
French toast was old school with real loaf french bread soaked and pan fried in butter. Great. 
Biscuits were hard and lacked that soft fluffy interior I enjoy. 
Fresh squeezed grapefuit juice, fresh and cold.
Shrimp and grits to die for. 

T Bert

Always delicious food, very convenient. They are quite friendly, but not in a pushy way. Affordable. I wish they have a more eco-friendly approach (even eat-in is served on disposable plates), but I can understand how that might not be affordable.

As a born and raised Peruvian living in NYC, I can safely say I've had my share of Peruvian food in and out of this country. The Pollo a La Brasa was superb. Excellent taste, moist, juicy.. delicious! Even the fries were amazing. Every restaurant offering this dish will have their own version of "green sauces" or "ajis" served on the side and these didn't not disappoint! The quality of food and taste rival much of what you will find at some of the most famous restaurants in Lima. Bonus: excellent waitstaff! I had Lorena and she was particularly awesome and friendly. I will be back again when visiting Tampa.
Always good food, great views and a relaxed environment. Definitely worth the wait when they're busy and by far the best burger in Carpinteria.

I usually like the oysters here but this time I had lunch.  Mediocre at best and really enjoyed a disgruntled server dropping the fbomb through the bar cause the bartender was busy and they had to pour a glass of wine.

A favorite spot that I will forever remember from college and surely return to. Relaxing, cozy, unpretentious. It's very popular during peak hours so you often have to be strategic in snagging a table. The staff are attentive and nice. Great coffee. Just bear in mind they stock a certain amount of food and can often run out of certain breads, meats, etc. if you come in on the later side of their serving hours (3PM-4PM). My favorite sandwich is the prosciutto with brie on a french baguette -- see picture.

My group hosted a party in Stone Creek's large private room last evening.  We had about 40 attendees.  The service provided by Lexi, Gina and Alan was excellent.  The drinks and food arrived in a timely manner considering the size of our group.  Everyone was pleased with their choices.  Thank you so much for making our outing so enjoyable!

I just recently found out that I have an allergy to a lot of foods that I've been eating. Doctors orders are to avoid those foods as much as possible to see if I feel better. Cue the sad violin while I say goodbye to almost everything in my pantry and refrigerator.

Publix has a few items that I could purchase but I was looking for a more diverse selection of items for my new diet. Decided to check out this Rollin' Oats place I kept hearing about and WOW. Really did not look as big from the outside as it is. Parking lot was jam packed. And really hard to get in/out of. But this won't deter me from coming back!

Their produce section was a dream. Fresh fruits and veggies right as soon as you enter the store and the section was awesomely huge! The rest of the store was nicely laid out and so clean. Every employee that passed by smiled and said hi or asked if I needed assistance. But in a non creepy way (sometimes I get the heebie-jeebies at other places from employees).

There is a deli in the back that I definitely want to try soon. Lots of sandwiches, wraps, soups etc you can order. Very big beer section, have never heard of these brands but they all looked tasty. Didn't get a chance to really browse the selection but will go back to do so (Is there such a thing as gluten free beer?!). 

We went up and down the aisles just looking at all the different items. I found plenty of foods that I could purchase that day and plenty more that I want to come back and try! Checkout was quick and the cashier was one of the friendliest I've ever encountered. The owner even came by and entertained my son for a minute. Great vibes in this store and is now my favorite grocery store in the area!

Redemption! Not just because it was playing in the cafe either. This was my second visit here. The first time in they forgot to put in my order. Once the server realized it she delivered my food to me quickly. The bacon wasn't crispy as I like it but the breakfast was decent. 

Today I visited for my second time. The service was prompt and the servers were polite. I ordered the crab cake eggs Benedict. Now, I really don't like hollandaise sauce. I despise mayonnaise and it's always been a little too close to that flavor to me. This sauce was delicious. It was not overpowering in any way. The poached eggs were cooked perfectly and it was served on top of a delicious crab cake and a hot croissant. I was in heaven. 

Let's get to the grits. These were amazing! They were whipped to perfection with a smooth buttery flavor. 

The food and the atmosphere will not disappoint. If you're in New Orleans make sure you stop by and enjoy yourself.

Got a good deal almost half off on Priceline which was still a little high for the room but if anyone paid the internet full price of $189/night-it would be a terrible deal! We parked out in the back lot for $16 for 24 hours and walked through all of Union Station to Marriott - no ramps, LOTS of stairs! Tried to check in at 3:45pm and no rooms were ready (checkout is 11am though so that is 5 hours to clean rooms). The rep said she would call us when the room was ready (only about 10 minutes). Our room was fine-clean & pleasant. Bathroom was a bit small, I really prefer 2 sinks at hotels. I find I spend about 50-60% of my hotel time in the bathroom getting ready for various outings so I wouldn't mind my room to be smaller & bathroom bigger. I did love all the cubbys around the sink to store everything. Shower had good pressure and again everything was spotless. (maybe that's why it takes 5 hours to clean rooms!)

The lobby was gorgeous and the bar out there had great bites and nice wine choices. Was really handy to grab drinks & an app to have while getting ready for dinner. The Metro station is RIGHT out the back door, through the parking lot and you are there. $7.50 per person buys you unlimited rides for 24 hours and that was a great deal for us. Everything we wanted to do was a couple of blocks from one or another of the stations and the subway attendants were incredibly FRIENDLY! That was the most amazing part. Chicago CTA workers literally act like they cannot see you. You can stand directly in front of them and speak into their face and you will feel like maybe you suddenly became invisible. The nicest guy ever helped us with tickets and then chatted with us about the Cards game while we waited for the train. The train was clean and I didn't smell even a trace of the urine stench so familiar to the CTA. Outstanding experience and what a deal! 

There was a toronado warning while we were getting ready and hotel employees came through the halls banging on doors and asking us to wait in the hallway. They were really serious too. They kept banging and if you didn't come out, they would come in to see if anyone was in the room. They kept checking to make sure we were staying out there too. We had friends in 2 other hotels and neither of them had to wait in the hall. Made me think Marriott actually cared if we were harmed by broken glass or sucked up like Dorothy! 

I don't choose hotels but if I got this place again on Priceline I wouldn't be mad!

I literally had the best grilled salmon of my life here! This place is amazing. The food is extremely good. My husband had chimichanga and he is also very happy  with his food. The service was great too. I can't recommend this place more!

Soup, sesame bread a side of rice and you the cook! Well kinda. You choose the ingredients. My dishes are are ways delicious, but what can I say... I have great taste. I always enjoy coming here. So does my out of town family, it's become somewhat of a tradition when they visit and I don't mind. With a great selection of fresh veggies and meats you always have a different plate. I stick to chicken and steak on the protein side. I always avoid any seafood unless I can dip my toes in the ocean at the same time so I'll leave that seafood adventure to those more daring than I.
Best pizza in Sparks. Crust is so good. The meat eater is my favorite. Call in advance and show up to pay at least 15 minutes before its supposed to be done. The line can get out of control.
Cold food does not rock my boat. I had a soft shell crab Poboy and my husband had grilled shrimp. I think it would have been wonderful if served hot.

We were looking to pass the time while waiting to do something in town and stumbled upon this place. I got a petit four and my boyfriend got a strawberry swirl cheese cake. They were small, but satisfying, as I don't need a ton of sweets to satisfy my sweet tooth. However, they do have larger cakes and cupcakes for those that like a little more. The cappuccino was delicious and I loved the little cafe environment. The music they played was relaxing, but hip. We will definitely be back. Probably before our trip is over.

I've just about had it with this place. Nothing is good anymore. I do not know if it is because new management is taking over in a few months and you have decided to slack, but get your sh*t together. The food is so mediocre now, skimping portions like no other. I pay nearly $13 for an omelette that I swear is smaller than the palm of my hand. God forbid you ask for a side of anything, you will receive the SMALLEST portion 

It isn't just the food that is ridiculous, the staff is the worst of all time. The little old lady working in the back is the rudest woman I have ever met. Constantly yelling at her staff for no reason. I kindly asked her if the order placed on the counter (which had been sitting out for 20 minutes and was cold) was mine and she snapped. "You are slowing me down, give me the bloody ticket!" Real nice manners! She also prepared my omelette wrong, forgetting to add avocado to it. I am SO sorry you have to serve students that, wait for it, go to college here! And to be honest, if you are having trouble serving eggs and avocado toast in a timely manner, than all you staff need a wake up call. This is not rocket science. No one wants to wait 25 minutes for a piece of toast with avocado when we have classes to get to. 

Condescending staff, horrible service, ridiculous prices - what else could go wrong you say? Well, there is more! Fun! 

Every single day, they will be out of something. Whether you get here bright and early when they open the kitchen or late at night, something is "out". Pastrami? Forget about it. Smoked Salmon? If you're lucky. That being said, the last time I had the smoked salmon, I felt like I was eating fish that had sat out for weeks. Gross. 

Man I wish I could give zero stars. You know what is good though? Their tea. Stick to that and nothing else. Unless you do not want to pay upwards of $4 for a small tea, than you know, stick to Snapple.

THE BEST THAI FOOD EVER!!! My husband and I recently moved to Nashville and had read some awesome reviews for this place and it was SOOOO much better than I expected! My mom was in town so we got to sample a few different things and they were all so incredibly delicious.( spring rolls, red chicken curry, peanut chicken, and tofu woonsen) If you want good fresh Thai food then you have to try THAI TASTE!!!

If you like practicing your lip reading skills (noisy) and daydreaming about who on earth trained the wait staff (who can't manage simple things like a water refill when they bring your food and your glass is dry; who can't bother to serve an a la mode dessert with less than completely melted ice cream; who don't warn you that one of the desserts is drastically different from the description on the menu), this is your place.  The mediocrity of the food won't distract you much from that core experience, though the bill might.

Not the best nor the worse Taiwanese food. They do have a large menu to choose from. The spicy braised beef noodle soup was ok -- mildly spicy with hard not tender beef. The broccoli beef reminds me of Panda Express (PE) but a notch better. The chow mien was clean and tasty and not burnt like PE. The almond milk was excellent very tasty like Quickly.  Overall 3-stars.
Great food ,great service  ,!! I love French food!!!! The wine was also very good i whent there with my friends  from here and we have a very good time

We had a vow renewal and made reservations for a party of 21, the general manager was very accommodating and super pleasant. Our servers were Fernandez and Katrina, they were BEYOND AMAZING!! Seriously the best service we ever received. I was impressed by the general managers attention to detail. The food was delicious, the view was amazing, and I will definitely return.

Nestled in the French Quarter is Mr B's bistro which is part of the Brennan family dining empire and quite popular in New Orleans.

Decided to try the Yaya Gumbo, a nice seafood mixture of crab, shrimp, oysters, rice and okra.  The soup was tasty but not large chunks of seafood. Decided to go for the smaller portion of the BBQ shrimp which is served with the infamous French bread.  The temperature could have been a little hotter but the flavor was descent.  I prefer the BBQ shrimp at Emerils New Orleans which has a richer taste and hotter temperature.

Service started off a little on the slow side but our head waiter made up for it.

Cheap, quick, delicious

Gotta take it for what it is.. This is not gourmet Indian food by any means and it's not trying to be. This place is great if you have a craving for Indian food, want something affordable and have limited time.
Went got a tiny expensive donut that I didn't love. The coffee was subpar as well. The place was really nice and clean but I won't be visiting again.

I get crispy duck red curry. This is the best. The duck is perfectly cooked with the crispy crust. I've ordered this dish multiple times dine in & carry out, lunch time and dinner. The quality has been the same every time. The inside of the restaurant also creates a very ornate environment that is good ambiance for a dinning experience.

This is the best burger I've had in Nashville so far; I put it over Burger Up and The Pharmacy. The Tennessee is deserving of its title as one of Zagat's 50 Burgers In 50 States. Their salads are good as well - well-made and generous but not overwhelming. And, getting a spiked milkshake is a must after your meal!

Frankly, The Dish was one of my very special favorite small restaurants in Tucson before they moved across the street. Now it seems the restaurant owners can't decide whether to be a restaurant or an appetizer bar. I don't think they can have it both ways, especially with rude servers, cold  food and multiple mistakes in the plate orders. OK, perhaps it was an off night. I have plenty of those myself. At least they only burnt two of the steaks, as the other two orders were fish and shellfish.But it made me long for the days of The Dish before this last  disastrous move.

I liked this place a lot more than I thought I would. It's kind of like a Long John Silvers or Captain D's set up but not a chain I don't think.

We were greeted by a ton of personality at the register. Guessing the owner by his tone.

It's kinda older and kitschy on the inside but inviting nonetheless.

They have a lot of drink (boozy and non) and a lot of sauce choices. Always a plus.

We loved everything, everyone's food was fresh and tasty. Very flaky white fish, no one's was greasy and that's always awesome for eating everything that's fried. Lol. 

Their fries could use a boost, they are kinda limp and I prefer crispy.

They are a little bit pricey but we had plenty of food so can't really complain too much. 

There were a lot of teenagers running the show and that's always a so so experience but these kids were pretty attentive and friendly.

Will return.

I certainly had higher expectations for this place. Maybe it's due to the fact that I'm not a burger kind of gal, but impress me, it did not. A group of ten recently had lunch here for my niece's birthday, and I think about 25% of our party enjoyed their meal, while the other 75% shared my way of thinking. 

We were seated right away, which is a definite plus for having such a large group. However, they sat us at this super long table in the center of the space where it was impossible to hold a conversation with anyone other than the person directly across from you or next to you. Whatever, I had a headache and didn't feel like being too social anyway. The waitress came around to take our drink order, and most people at the table ordered a shake. I'm on a current health kick, so I had ice tea instead. When the shakes arrived, I didn't feel like I was missing out on anything though. The small size was just that... super tiny... like, two dixie cups worth in a glass tiny. Definitely not worth the $3.50 price tag. 

On to the food. Everything here is served a la carte. Most of the specialty burgers come at a set price, but if you order the basic and add anything to it, we found that you could be up another $4 or more just by switching your bun and adding a slice of cheese and bacon. You want a side of fries or onion rings? That'll be a few more dollars. Oh, you expect silverware? How much is it worth to you? (Ok, they don't really charge for silverware, but you get where I'm going with this... I hate being nickeled and dimed for every little thing!) Everyone in our group ordered something different, and though I don't recall what each person got, I only heard the verdict from everyone as we were walking out (note the 25% / 75% above). I had the veggie burger and quinoa side salad. The veggie burger was decent. It was a sweet potato patty topped with pecan butter and spinach. The quinoa salad was not my favorite and I was actually proud of myself for finishing at least half of it. It's served cold and mixed with dried cherries, onions, and balsamic vinaigrette. The onions were overbearing though... that's the only flavor that came through.

At least the birthday girl enjoyed her shake, but as for me, I don't expect that Bailey's will get another nickel or dime from my wallet anytime in the near future.
Don't like pancakes?  Try the grill cooks medley. Prepare to wait in line and if you park out back, don't forget to get a ticket and put on your dash or you will be ticketed

Excellent experience! We came with a group of 10 at 9pm and they set the table for us in advance. It was our first time there and all of their food was good. Especially the salt and pepper pork, Mapo tofu, pork chop over rice, string bean. Everything was quite good!

We had a large group here and had a semi-private area. The area's dedicated staff and coordinator were great and the food was amazing. We ordered way too much and everything was eaten. I cannot recommend Luke enough for a large group. Only minor complaint was the drink service was a bit slow.

I travel from Ventura to Santa Barbara on Saturdays and have some time to kill - watching football and eating lunch.  This place has a great setup for sports nuts to watch games on tv.  Unfortunately, they have no one working there that knows how to work the tv remotes.  The food is good, the service is good and they have a great atmosphere for watching sports but... how about training someone to mange all those flat screen tvs?  Very maddening to be watching CNN and last weeks pro game on a college football filled Saturday afternoon!!!!
Good beer. Small but pleasantly funky menu. Did not dig the walk along 13th to get here.

The wings were awesome! 
But the service is a little ehhh, our waitress was good, but the manager working didn't know how to change a check once he split it up. 
My guess is, too lazy and didn't want the hassle. It would be nice to know, if you don't want to split (or can't split) a check, please tell the customers up front, there were 6 of us and 4 were splitting 50 wings. 
Also, the four us of wanted to have multiple sauces, but you can only separate sauces by two ways on orders of 50 or more, but yet they have numerous sauces to choose from. 

This location is new and is packed all the time, make sure you get there earlier or you can be waiting quite a while.

This is one of those places that I really want to love. I've lived down the block for a few weeks now, but visited Crazy Sushi even when I was living up in UC.

To start off, the food is good. The rolls are priced fairly, and the veggie gyoza compares to the best of the same that I've had in Cali (full disclosure: I think Cali has the best Japanese food in the country). The plates are beautifully decorated, and I think the decor inside the place, bar the color changing effects, are absolutely beautiful (I'm a fan of contemporary design). In particular, the sweet potato roll and the cucumber+avocado roll are my favorites, although I'm looking forward to trying the mango one soon too.

In any case, I really want to like the place, but the constant finding of hairs (not ours) in the food during our two visits and the subsequent 'not-caring' of the wait staff has been somewhat disappointing. Further, the lack of attention to detail - not bringing over new soy sauce containers when the other one is empty, not refilling water, etc. is disappointing as well, and in all, costs Crazy Sushi 2 stars.

With that being said, the food is still good, but if they just wore hair nets or whatnot and kept things more hygienic, and improved service a tad bit, that would definitely go a long way!

As usual John Besh never disappoints, the best crab bisque I have had in a long time in a restaurant. Not too rich and full of crabmeat, a great treat for supper served with hot french bread for dipping.

Without a doubt, the fried chicken was delicious. And considering that a chicken dinner at KFC can run upwards of $8, it's not really that expensive. But please--the whole place is knocked together from unfinished 2X4s, and the seats are just sawn plywood with a coat of varnish. Our cheap table wobbled like a prop in a comedy film. I understand we're going for a rustic look, but rusticity should not be an excuse for doing everything on the cheap. If I wanted to sit on raw lumber I'd order take-out and find a construction site. Spend a few bucks, for pete's sake. I'll be back when I can sit in a comfortable chair and enjoy my meal.

30 minute wait to sit, 45 minutes to get food. Pancakes and juices are good. Meat lovers omelette was not impressive.  At least one party who sat after us was served before us. Very busy Saturday morning, so I  sympathize with the staff. Food wasn't bad, but wasn't worth the wait.

Our experience at Sun Diner was pretty ridiculous. We came here because it was one of the only places in the area that was open 24/7 and we needed food. Came in around 230 in the morning and the place was pretty busy. The seating in here is interesting; bar-like, two sections shaped in a U. There were also some tables in the back if you didn't feel like sitting at the bar. We were able to find a spot soon after coming in. The menu was surprisingly small, maybe it was the late night menu only or something, not sure. For whatever reason I thought it was a good idea to order three meals for the two of us. We went with the quesadillas, breakfast tacos and a cheeseburger grilled cheese type thing. Wasn't too expensive but the food wasn't great. The breakfast tacos had braised pork belly in them and while it's known that pork belly is fatty, it was hard to eat, too chewy, too fatty. The quesadillas were just alright and the cheeseburger grilled cheese was decent. 

Here's why the experience was ridiculous. There was a fight going on between two couples next to us over a seat. Apparently one girl got permission from one of the employees to sit down but the seat was occupied by a girl who was using the restroom, long story short, the fight never should have happened in the first place but it was a HUGE blow out scene and was so uncomfortable for my boyfriend and me who were also sitting right there and nothing was being done about it! The server just carried on, didn't react, didn't call for help, I couldn't believe what was happening to be honest. Eventually security came and broke up the fight but it took way too long and we ended up getting all our food to go and getting the heck out of there. It was not an enjoyable experience and we wished we opted for a slice of pizza instead.

I am so happy we found this place!!! Korean fried chicken is amazing. Get it half and half sweet and spicy. The owner is so awesome and great she is super sweet and gets to know you and your order fast. This is by far my favorite sushi and Japanese/Korean restaurant in Nashville. Do yourself a favor and go here

My family and I just had dinner at the boiling house and it was nothing short of Amazing! 
The staff was extremely friendly! We made a reservation so we didn't have to wait. ( I would recommend doing the same). While we were exploring the menu trying to decide what to pick(which is extremely hard to do as everything looks amazing). The manager came out to introduce himself and welcome us he was really kind and chatted with us for quite some time as we waited for our food to arrive which is btw made to order and super fresh . 
For appetizer we ordered the calamari, bang bang shrimp tacos and house salad. For dinner we had the crabs, garlic noodles, and fried seafood rice! Oh, and you must try the lemonade with your meal as it was also really fresh and delicious! All in all it was a great experience and we most certainly will return!

GREAT FOOD!  I love everything they have.  Nice atmosphere and great service.  

We've been to Zea on St. Charles at least a dozen times and are never disappointed.
Went last night with a group of 10. Service was excellent, food was great, and the hibachi chef was great! Highly recommend this place to everyone!
This place was amazing. The food was spiced perfectly. The salad was a fantastic touch. Even the Ethiopian spiced tea was wonderful. This is definitely a must visit spot when I'm in Reno.

Muriel's made my 25th birthday amazing. Due to flooding, we had to push our reservation back from 8:00 PM to 9:00 PM and still ended up being late due to traffic and this was no problem at all for the restaurant staff who accommodated us and greeted us with a smile. Our two servers, whose names I forgot unfortunately were astounding. We even found out that one was on his second day of training and you absolutely could not tell. Thanks to the Coolinary menu, we were able to take advantage of the wonderful goat cheese crepes, the pork chops, duck, Bayoubaisse, and creme brûlée. Every last dish was amazing. Thank you Muriel's for turning what could've been a truly terrible day into an amazing birthday I will never forget. I will for sure be returning on my future trips to Nola.
This is a great breakfast spot! All of the employees are very kind and professional. Kathryn was our server and she did a great job! Overall a great experience and I will definitely be coming back.

Yum yum yum!

Delicious food, great service and a very nice place in the midst of bourbon street. 
We got the shrimp and grits -amazing!! The jambalaya and a hurricane. 
Everything tastes good and service was nice. Definitely worth visiting!

I want to move to Tennessee so I can come here every day. Cute decor, helpful staff, huge portions. I had the ham, Gouda macaroni, and green beans. Family had the Jerusalem chicken, meatloaf (only mediocre review), baked beans, mashed potatoes, and fruit (berries). I liked the corn bread better than the rolls. Cold salads and desserts looked amazing. I kept the menu so I can come back on our next road trip!

After hearing friends talk about this little specialty gourmet shop, I went since its across the street from me. I ordered a few hoagies and sandwiches and then some pastas/sauce. The hoagies were good and the service is great.
My family's favorite pizza in town- awesome!  Good beers on tap too.  BBQ chicken pizza is the beat I've had.  They also have a great lunch special, 8.00 for pizza and salad.

Mmm! 4.5!
Classy but not pretentious. I tried a bite of multiple dishes (BBQ shrimp, bacon wrapped shrimp, filet mignon, halibut, soft shelled crab) and everything was great! Each good enough to choose as your main dish, really depends on your personal taste. BBQ shrimp is messy and strong- pretty sure they use shrimp heads in the sauce, halibut is the opposite end, light with lots of lightly sautéed veggies and not fishy at all. Fried oysters and truffle fries are also good. 
Great busy lively French quarter location (if that's what you're looking for) and friendly enthusiastic service. Very NOLA, classy, but still very fun, restaurant.

We have been here a few times before and really want to like this place because it is so convenient to where we live.  We walked in and stood at the hostess stand for over 5 minutes while the hostess remained on the phone without even acknowledging us.  We were seated and then it took an additional 12 minutes for a server to come to our table.  We both ordered hibachi dinners and were extremely disappointed.  The soup tasted like dish water and our entrees were served at room temperature (at best).   The waiter gave most of his attention to the hibachi tables, and walked by us with an "Oh Crap!  I forgot their food" look.  Granted, it looked like he was one of only two servers working a nearly full restaurant.  He was very nice to us when we brought up how unsatisfactory the food was.  At $15 for an entree, it should be served hot.  Right?  He apologized and offered to have the kitchen make us new meals, but we had already been there over an hour and could not wait through that process again.  We ate the remainder of our meals, and were really not surprised when we got the check and no discount whatsoever was there to at least attempt to make amends for our awful experience.  No manager came by the table.  If they don't care more than that, then we do not care to go back.  We'll drive out to Smyrna and got o Tokyo Restaurant.

Stopped by for a quick late night dinner. Even tho it was right before closing they graciously seated us and made us feel welcome. Mussels with chorizo were delish, Caesar salad was fine and the Mediterranean skillet rounded out the meal. We'll definitely be back

We had the waffles the huevos rancheros the spinach parmesan cheese omelette the cheesy grits and the French toast. The food was delicious service was fantastic. Lots of outdoor dining available but for some reason my daughter chose to eat inside. Lots of beautiful art and atmosphere is casual. Also in a cute part of Gulfport. Enjoy you know when you want to leave

I want to love this place, I really do. One the surface, the atmosphere is good, the ingredients seem top notch, and the pizza selections well chosen. But every pie I had has been to cold and floppy to really win me over.
A great place to relax and enjoy good food. Frank I'd one heck of a guy. A fantastic place. Diner atmosphere,  friendly and caring waiting staff. Definitely a must.

I came here with a bachelor party group on a Saturday evening.  We sat in the back, and first ordered our drinks and some oysters.  Not a very impressive beer selection...and pretty hefty on the pricing.  The oysters came out and were excellent.  This was my first time doing raw oysters and I was impressed...but then again, it's pretty hard to screw up raw oysters....guess I'll give more credit to the Gulf of Mexico on that one.  Next, for my meal, I ordered the duck confit and white bean cassoulet with bacon and sausage.  The meal came out and I first went for the duck wing.  It was simply roasted with some seasonings.  Very tender and very good tasting.  Of course, it seems pretty hard to screw this up too.  I'll give more credit to the duck.  Next came the garlic sausage.  This was not good.  It was a giant six inch long sausage, about 1.5 inches in diameter....just a giant chunk of meat that didn't have much taste.  It was overall pretty bland.  I don't know where the garlic they were talking about is in it.  Next was the smoked bacon.  It was more of a bacon cube.  Just a fatty piece of pork belly....which was almost all fat.  Not impressive.  Last came the white bean cassoulet.  This was also very unimpressive.  I'm not sure what seasonings they added to this or if they added any at all.  It was just white beans with cheesy/mooshy tasteless stuff in between topped with breadcrumbs.  Very, very unimpressive.  Overall, I was very unimpressed with this place, especially considering the reviews and prices.  You're better off getting a few Krystal burgers on Bourbon...yes, I am serious.
I love Thai food and am glad to know that I can find it in Nashville.   Everything is fresh and light.

A wonderful dining experience, food AND drinks are phenomenal! We did Cochon, Restaurant August and Compere Lapin for our nicer dining experiences in NOLA, and this one completely beats our Restaurant August hands down. Anyways, I rarely leave reviews, but this is actually for Ziggy, our busser. He is THE BEST! Such a fun, likable and hilarious guy. He totally made our night. Ziggy - if you're ever in LA... :)
Just perfect burgers. This is our place to go on Girard, now. The toppings are great, the service is quick, and the price is good given the quantity of food.

So my wife picked this place and to be honest I wish she had not. The staff was great. The food was a different story. All of the food we had was way to salty. I don't want to be mean so I will sum up this experience as a can miss. Maybe in a few months we will give this place a second chance.
yum!!!!!!!! fanatasic soup!!!!!!!!!!! great and cheap lunch specials!!!!! just walk in and you will know how good the food tasts by the smell in here! great service....no negativity!
Got the turkey blt. Excellent! Service was a little slow but we weren't in a rush.

Came here for lunch with a coworker. The hostess/waitress was friendly. I ordered panzanella salad and toasted ravioli and my friend got the house salad and pasta con broccoli. When our salads came, my friend commented on the huge pieces of veggies that she had to cut up to eat. My panzanella did not have any bread in it. We also did not get any bread or crackers served. But the veggies in my salad were fresh and the basil in it was nice. The pasta con broccoli came. Again, my friend had to cut the broccoli which was almost raw. But she said the pasta was hot and the sauce well seasoned. They forgot my toasted ravioli, but rectified it fairly quickly and comped the dish. They also gave us a neighborhood discount, and these two things earned them an extra star. The ravioli was pretty tasteless. First of all, they were as big as my hand,  which was unexpected. Bigger is not always better. They were nicely toasted, but the meat inside was bland. As was the tomato sauce for dipping. So some good, some bad. But overall, nothing to make me want to return

Normally I love everything about 'feine, but I had a really bad experience there today that made me have a change of heart. I ordered a classic grilled cheese sandwich, which is supposed to contain - you guessed it - just cheese. However, some of the staff members seemed distracted while they were making it. I didn't think anything of it until I got in my car and started chowing down. I thought it was odd that the sandwich tasted spicy (like, reeeeeally hot spicy) but I was SO hungry, so I kept eating half of it. Then I tasted something funny. When I opened up my sandwich, I saw turkey. Now, for most people this would not be a big deal, but for me, I've been a strict vegetarian since I was a kid, and meat makes me really sick, so it was a big freakin' deal. Made me throw up. Now I'm grossed out and sad because I used to love 'feine, but am now really disappointed - they should have been more careful. Turkey wasn't even on the grilled cheese menu, so I'm really confused as to how it got into my sandwich. Ughhh.
Would rate them higher if not for the people working behind the counter. The cashier acted as if she was doing us a favor taking our order! Tacos are good, the experience..not so much!

The pho here is magical. It is definitely the best tasting base soup I've had in pho in the city. The combo pho is great, although the meatball has weird amounts of gristle. The rice with spicy tofu is also great. The tofu is incredibly tasty, has good texture, and goes great with the rest of the ingredients added on to the rice to make a great dish. 
The staff is also very friendly. The pho chef sometimes comes out to greet me and check on the quality of the pho. There is little pretension here, just good food and good people.
I highly recommend it for people looking for Vietnamese food in New Orleans.

Recently had breakfast here, which was the first time I've ever been to The Roost. I had a belgian waffle with butter and maple syrup-- pretty standard fare-- and it was good. This is a solid breakfast place, and is on par, if not better than, many of the other breakfast restaurants in the area.
Awesome food, good beer selection. My only complaint is they should really rename the Mac's macs to Mac's Famous Mac and Cheese. I think Dennis would appreciate it.

Really terrific, low-key, friendly place, with the best mofongo I've had since Puerto Rico (but note, this place is Dominican!)- also highly recommend the whole red snapper and the Tres Leches!! Jose and his staff have created a very welcoming atmosphere

From service to food everything was just damn good! The bakery is delish, their selections of beers and cocktails is good and accompanies their menu nicely. We will be back on our next trip to Nashville and recommend this place if you are in the Gulch area.

Great food, excellent service! Best pizza in Spring Hill - love the thin crust....

Server always so nice ...

Walking down the street lioking for a place to eat, saw an empty seat and had one of the better cubam sandwiches i have had in a while. Meaty, hot and almost too much to eat... the Irish Channel Stout was the icing on the cake for this  quick afternoon stop. I give a pass to the newer bartender, we all need to start somehwere. Worth the $20 bill I spent.

First visit, truly fantastic! Had the chimichanga with steak and was thoroughly impressed. Everything was fresh and tasty, prepared in view of the counter. Will post a more complete review once I've had a couple more things, but based on the first visit, that should be in short order!
Apparently the best ice cream place on honky tonk according to the shuttle driver.. Not that I could find that many ice cream place but it's always bz & the serving is oretty decent.

DO NOT ORDER FROM THIS IMOS. I have never had a worse experience with any pizza delivery service than I have in the multiple times I have tried to give this location a chance. The first time I ordered it took them over an hour to deliver and my pizza was cold and hard. Literally not even edible. I requested a refund but was denied, of course. I also ordered a salad with the cold hard pizza which they left at the store. They said it would be over an hour before they could go get it. Never got it. And never got refunded. The second and last time I gave this place a chance they took over an hour to get to me once again and delivered my pizza and salad but forgot the salad dressing. I called the manager and was assured the dressing would be brought to me in 15 minutes. Needless to say it was another hour before I got the dressing. Do not waste your time or energy on this location.

The only thing interesting on the menu was the dry aged steak, but the portion offered was too large for one person and made it a waste to get any sides.  So I did not order it.  The fish and shrimp was all farm raised since there was no indication it was wild caught.  I don't even eat that in my own home, so why would I pay for that at what is supposed to be an upscale restaurant.  So instead I ordered the lobster bisque, tuna tartare and flat bread so I would have some variety.  I assumed the lobster and tuna were wild caught and the flatbread was supposed to have truffle in it. The tuna was good but the bisque and flatbread were so over salted, they were unenjoyable. I felt like my head was going to explode as I was walking out and I don't have high blood pressure. My old fashioned was loaded with syrup and I could not even taste the whisky.  I was kind of surprised, because the chef touts himself as so good, so why can't he put appropriate levels of salt in his dishes?  There were also no chunks of lobster in the bisque. As for the atmosphere, the view is great, but we were seated away from the windows despite that we politely asked 3 times to be moved to a window table and there were open tables available.

My wife and I went to Cinco de Mayo on a busy Friday night. We waited over 40 minutes to have our orders taken. Then another 30 minutes for our food. When it did come out, it was relatively burnt/dry, and unseasoned. We also feel like we got a paltry serving portion, and very poor service. Water glasses stayed empty the whole time. Chips were very dry and stale. They also said they don't have drink specials. We have been to the Cinco de Mayo in Brentwood MANY times, received excellent service, food, and drinks, and will return there if we wish to frequent a CDM in the future.
I love this place, great food, awesome atmosphere, reminds me of the Brady Bunch.

Back on my taco binge, I had to find a new place to get my fixing. I like this little place, a lot. Came in on a Wednesday night around 8 o'clock to a dimly lit, friendly-faced, moderately occupied restaurant. We were able to grab a table right away and considering it was such a nice night, we decided to step out back to dine in the courtyard.

There's plenty of seating here, they've done well with the tight warehouse district space. Our server was friendly, but the service was standard. I remember it taking a moment to get our orders together as they input them using an iPad. Seems their U.I. could use a little upgrade for user friendliness.

Margaritas were pretty good, I usually get headaches from em' but I also didn't pound four of them. For the app we got the tres queso (didn't add any meat) which was nice. Came with a ton of chips and you're gonna want to get at that queso fast because we all know what happens when we let it sit for a few minutes. I would have liked a little more of a spicy kick in the queso tho, but I'd get them again.

My date ordered the sweet potato quesadilla witch she (and i) liked a lot, careful tho because they come out HOT! I went with the fuego burrito with a salad and that thing was massive! It's rare that I have to box up a meal but I had to, I would've died trying to put it all away that night. It could have been all the chips I decimated also.

The two of us ate for about $30 or so, not a bad deal. I can see myself returning for more, we were very pleased with the food.

One more thing, my date had been here before and they charged her for something that was wrong, so long story short, she was told that they would put her name in "the book" and they would take care of it next time. Well folks, there is no "the book" so if it happens to you, don't fall for it. Get something written from management.

****UPDATE****
My date clarified that there IS in fact a book. My Apologies to any staff affected.
11/10/2015

This is a fun place to grab sushi. The dinners are "crazy" with my friend receiving her sashimi platter with an ice sculpture and its own purple light, topped off with a tiny pink paper umbrella. The fish was fresh and the service was attentive. 
I'd come back here, but I'd also grab take out!

Came back for brunch. It's now official, every meal is just as amazing as the last. Ordered the aborada: which is fried dough stuffed with plantains, cheese, guava paste and some other ingredients. So delicious, the sweet plantains and guava and melty cheese - how have I not heard of these before? The papas rellenas are more of a small plate than an appetizer - cheese, rice, beans, seasoned with spices, a totally different dish than American stuffed potatoes. The fuzzy navel is tropical and strong, like most of their drinks I've tried, has a taste of tangerine juice. The dominicana chicken comes with the tender marinated chicken in a side dish and the rice and beans mix in the main plate. The owner is so amazing - I had a party of 7 for brunch, and we called a day or 2 before, and he opened 30 minutes early for us so my out of town friend could experience the awesomeness before she had to hit the road. Love this place!

I went back here to try the dishes again after the owner responded to my review about it being too bland the first time I was there when they just opened.  He said they made some adjustments to the recipes and they certainly did!  AND they added a stone bowl upgrade! 3 dollars was a bit much to pay for the upgrade but Bimbimbop is not the same without it, so I had to have it! It was outstanding!  The flavor was just right..I did not even have to add any red sauce it was so good, my 6 year old keeps asking to go back!  We also ordered the chicken wings which were superb this time and the potstickers were great as well.  All around we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves and will be back!  It would be great for them to expand the menu to include a few more choices...like maybe the seafood soft tofu bowl..mmm.

The food is a bit better than average, however the staff are wonderful.  You feel like more than just a customer, as if you are joining family breakfast.  Socks not knocked off by the food, but that was ok.
Decent food but gave me indigestion from another planet i swear.  Do yourself a favor and just microwave a frozen acme pizza

Love this place!  Only place to sit is the Bar where you are over the chatter of dining patrons and you get to watch the performers and artisans at the Bar.  They use fresh juices daily and create amazing concoctions.  Am trying the lambs sliders based on other reviews.

"Burger Up" Burgers...are?? Ok.
     Maybe the over extended rants and hype about the burgers at "Burger Up" escalated my expectations. The burger I had was "ok" good. It wasn't "soooooo gooood" that I could say its in the top 3 of BNA. I gotta stick by my standards. Burger up has some things I think rock but they don't really transpire over into everyday awesome food for a good price. 
   
The location alone exudes a "Wannabe Snooty" type of a burger place. I've always believed, that burgers are better made.. "un-gourmeted". You grill some exotic meats, so what, its still the meat that makes them taste great. (Say that in a Christopher Walken Tone) 
   
   I couldn't tell if the fries were really done in truffle oil.The parmesan cheese flakes worked. I really think its a gimmick for the "Richy Riches "in the area to make themselves feel better about eating a burger. The selection of locally raised beef was a plus. The homemade ketchup was refreshing. The atmosphere is respective and I will say the service was excellent. The menu offers a comfortable selection of entrees to both carnivores and herbivores. The highlight here is fancy schmancy burgers made from beef.

  My Synopsis: Its for "Sheeple" who wanna buy a burger and not feel bad about eating one cause its "Organic or something??"

They have the best sandwiches ever . They are fast and every hoagie I have gotten from there is just delicious. Counter person was very helpful . My favorite is the : Caprastami and Italian .   Recommend totally
We had the 4x4 pizza, and I must say it was excellent definitely will come back, husband enjoyed the beer selection, the wood-fire gives the pizza such a great taste.

Looks could be deceiving! We stopped  by complete accident for a late lunch. It reminded  us of an old diner. But boy were we shocked  how amazing  the food was and the service was perfect!  We both had burgers.  They were seasoned and cooked perfectly.  We couldn't  stop talking how amazing  they were. They came w thick cut homemade  fries  that needed nothing on them because they were seasoned perfectly.  Definitely put this place on your  list.

I found this place through an Instagram photo, then I saw the place on yelp; I had to check it out since it had such great reviews. I went there around 2:30 yesterday, there wasn't a long line, thank God! I order so many things from their menu, for example, the Thai short rib tacos, satay chicken tacos, cap n crunch tilapia burrito, and the chicken katsu platter with egg and a Thai tea; everything was absolutely delicious!!! My most favorite one was the cap n crunch burrito, it's so tasty and crunchy; it had a lot of flavor. You can tell they use high quality ingredients, and the guy working behind the truck was super friendly! Great customer service, I would definitely come back and get more!

Lost my business over customer service. Use to go here regularly and order the same thing every time. Ordered #8 sandwich but upon going home realized they gave me the wrong sandwich. Normally not a big deal but thought I'd take it back to exchange for the correct sandwich. Upon going back the lady at the counter refused to correct the mistake.  In her mind I ordered the #10 because on the ticket that is what she wrote down. Her attitude was horrible and completely smug the whole time to actually make this a big deal. To not fix a sandwich order over a 2 dollar upcharge is absolutely ridiculous especially when I made the effort to drive all the way back. Then to add her lack of empathy is what really pissed me off enough to write my first review. Excellent business plan, lose customer over a 2 dollar mistake.

Love this place! Been here twice, once during the week & again on Saturday around 11:30am. Saturday was busy but we got seated right away. You MUST get the house made potato chips; they are amazing!  They serve breakfast & lunch all day on the weekend, so we had 2 scrumptious menus to choose from...but wait there's more. They were also celebrating pancake day & had a 3rd special menu of just pancakes. I was in a lunch mood & got the French onion dip with short rib & balsamic drizzle pizza. Yum! Different & tasty. The hubs got the "chicken in a pancake" which were 3 gigantic pancakes with a generous amount of bacon crumbles throughout & a runny egg baked into the center of each pancake. Wow! Definitely eat here if you are anywhere around Mullica Hill!

I will say this: it's a bit of a turnoff when a waitress starts out service with a warning of food that they currently don't have on the menu -- and then goes on to rattle off more dishes than I can keep track of.  Came here recently at around 7pm on a Sunday night, and I suppose they were running out of supplies at the end of the week. 

THAT ASIDE, this meal was delish. My favorite from the evening was the Sweet Potato Hash with bacon, sausage and  the de rigueur fried egg. Also had some sort of brussel sprouts dish with crispy shallots and pecorino romano (also really tasty). 

I've had brunch here before, but this was my first time in for dinner. Looking forward to coming back and having more of the menu!

Our second time here was as great as the first! Drinks are cheap AND good even on the weekends. Our food always comes out super quick and is the best Mexican food I've had in St. Louis, and I have lived here all my life. The service is fantastic and it's great quality food for the price.
Amazing. Burgers and Mac and cheese were everything. Ambiance was laid back and relaxing as well.
These guys are the best!  Love this restaurant, and I think it's the best chinese food in Reno.  Do not discount it for it's location!  A MUST!
Ron's always tastes good and uses many natural ingredients! There's good reason for its frequently being packed.

They Have authentic Chinese and sea food, and karaoke rooms upstairs.
This meal consisted of Two lobsters for $19.95. 
Walnut shrimp, and salt baked scallops and squid.

Wish we had a Blaze in Miami, Florida! After searching on Yelp for gluten free restaurants in the area, I stumbled upon Blaze. The concept of this pizza joint is similar to Chipotle. You start off by selecting your dough and YES they have gluten free dough. There is a huge variety of toppings to chose from all very fresh and delicious. The oven they make you pizza is is quick and gives it amazing taste. I am from New York and though I had tried the best pizza in the world, well now I have. Staff was friendly and the pizza was done in no time. I love it so much I would even consider buying a franchise and take it to Miami!! You will not regret going to Blaze

I love the Brewpub. It's a great place for hanging out with friends in the evenings you don't want to deal with the craziness of the Broad Ripple strip. It just has a really nice, cozy, laid-back feel. The beers are excellent - I highly recommend getting a sampler. The food is also really just really good pub food and lots of options on the menu. I remember the shepherd's pie I got reminded me of food I ate in the United Kingdom - very authentic!

We were anxious to try this local spot again after it had been completely remodeled. We always enjoyed the food, but the flow of it and the decor had always fallen short. We were not dissapointed, the ambiance is comfortable, trendy, but, sophisticated enough for an occasion. Our old favorites were still on the menu and lots of cool new things. Love the crab soup. Had the scallops and my husband had the pork chop which was amazing. Dessert was excellent. Really liked all the barn board and the lighting was really unique and eye catching. We will def go back!
Nice salad at a good price, but make sure you have a lot of time on your hands as service is slow and disorganized.

Buffalo Wings generally have pretty consistent service and food quality -- I mean, how hard is it to serve reheated chicken and beer?  Well--evidently, pretty hard.  We arrived at 5:45 -- pretty early for dinner -- and were told a 20-30 minute wait, which turned into a 45 minute wait.  That should have been our first sign something was amiss.  After waiting 45 minutes, we already knew what we wanted to order, so ordered immediately after being seated at 6:30.  We ordered a chicken salad, a burger, a wrap, boneless wings, and a kids mini corn dogs.  60 minutes later we finally got our food.  Our waitress was great, and came by every 10 minutes to ask if we needed anything (other than our food), but all she could say is it should be coming, it should be coming.  We asked if the order was lost, and she said she saw it up on the screen in the kitchen, and said she had confirmed the kitchen had seen it, and that the screen shows them how long a order has gone unfilled, so they should know it had been an hour.  She had even talked with the manger.  Despite this, it took a full 60 minutes to bring out 6 items which literally have 5 minute prep time.  The chicken on the salad, wrap, and wings had all been precooked and heated under a heat lamp -- they were all dry.  They also put dressing on the salad despite asking for it on the side.  The waitress insisted on the manager coming over to us.  She asked him several times.  He finally came over as we were trying to leave, and said "what is the problem" curtly as if the waitress hadn't already told him 10 times, before, during, and after our meal was delayed an hour.  When my 74 year old mother politely told him (remember, the waitress asked him to come over, not us), he replied "did everything come out ok?" as if the only thing that mattered was did we receive edible food or not after waiting 1 hour and 45 minutes.  The guy acted exasperated, like the whole thing was out of his control.  Dude, I hate to break it to you, but your the manager.  This place is bleeding money -- if you can't get food out in under an hour, you can't turn tables.  The faster you turn tables, the more customers you can serve, and the more money you make.  Also, the less the wait time, so less customers get frustrated and leave and are less likely to come back.  With an hour wait for food, less customers are going to come back again, including us.  Sayonara Buffalo Wings -- it was nice knowing you for 20 years, but after 86th/Ditch service/kitchen went downhill, we were only willing to give you one last chance, and despite having a brand new restaurant with a brand new general manager, you managed to disappoint us even further.  We simply have too many casual dining and bar and grill options to waste our time and money with you.

I love patty melts and the ones here make me happy. yeah the place is kinda greazy and has a reputation, but I have to go once in a while ;)

OK, to be honest we thought there was a cracker barrel on this exit but we couldn't find it, so we got stuck eating here. But it wasn't *totally* shitty!

Great, local beer complimented by an excellent menu that changes based on products sourced locally. This is as good as a microbrewery gets, and the food can be described as "gourmet" bar food. Love it!!

My family and I eat here often and I have never been disappointed. The Salsa is so fresh and amazing. The Brunch is delicious and the Mimosas are only $1.  The last time I ate here I had the crab cake with creole tomato and crawfish sauce with an egg on top (don't recall the name of the item) it was SO AMAZING! My husband had the seared tuna fish salad and he said it was fresh and really tasty. Our son and nephew both had Quesadillas. My nephew told me they were the best he ever had, even better than Taco Bell (Hey he's 5). Great place for families and pets.

New owner owns a few restaurants, and upscaled the menu, but still reasonably priced. I got the bacon wrapped filet, it was cooked perfectly, and was top 3 I've ever had, and I've had prob close to 50 different steakhouse offerings before.
Also offer cheaper sandwiches that looked amazing too.
Bar offerings could be expanded a bit, but I'm sure they are working on it.

I was searching for a good hoagie place rather than doing Primo or Wawa for an evening bowling event at Devon Playdrome.  I found this deli did trays so I ordered a tray and a few other different hoagies to accomdate the group.  The woman who took my order was very helpful in trying to figure out how many sandwiches were needed to feed our total amount of people. The food was very tasty and a definite reason to stop there for a sandwich at any time.  We'll be having more bowling events and will be sure to stop back again the next time or sooner.

It's hard to say that there is a five star buffet in Reno, but I come here every summer for breakfast which is the best for the buck. This is a buffet that has great selection of food that is a bit above the average buffet. Lines can be long, but that's because everyone knows to come here. The price is average . Attentive staff. It's clean. It's roomy . What more do you want? You want more , go spend more money at a non - buffet restaurant.

This is by far my worst experience dining in NOLA. Ordered French Onion Soup, veal chop, veggie and bordelaise sauce. My chop was to be medium rare plus ... closer to medium. 

No soup showed up. Wrong sauce. And the chop was rare and an end cut. How do you serve an end-cut rare ... and is always reserved for medium well to well orders. 

Terribly disappointed and all I wanted was a casual good NOLA meal.

Second chance failed miserably! Medium rare to rare in some sections of the cut. The quality was horrific, vainy and tough. Over charred on the outside a under cooked, cold center in the middle. 

The best thing I can say is the bread was fine and the butter wasn't frozen. 

They lost a customer and a "former" advocate. Given the prices, you expect more and I'm left with a bad experience and hungry.

I have been meaning to write a review for months for this great little Tucson restaurant. My husband and I have come to love it. So few interesting restaurants in the north half of Tucson. This is a little gem to be enjoyed. They have great music. A lovely little patio. A quaint little interior. I'm on a limited sugar diet and they helped me invent a lovely muddled mint ad cucumber vodka, club sofa and lime cocktail. Incredible service. But better than that is the absolute consistency we have experienced with the Seabass and rice dish. Perfectly prepared fish at that fine point where it flakes but not one bit over done. Hard to find in Tucson. We have had many of their appetizers all which were delicious. Great place to experience in Tucson.

Another great meal at Tokai.  Chef David made some amazing creations. 
Loved everything.

We have always enjoyed this restaurant and the entire dinning experience. Last night was an example of how one individual can ruin the evening. When we had an issue with the To-Go order the manager basically told me to pound sand. We dinned in and at the time of seating ordered an entree to take home with the expectation it would be ready when we were finished. Unfortunately that was not the case and I was told when I received my bill that it would be an additional fifteen minutes before my take home order was ready because the kitchen was backed up. When I expressed my disappointment to the waiter, she sent Nanu, the manager over to speak with me. Nanu was not apologetic, did not offer concern and was certainly not  making my satisfaction his priority. I asked him to at least offer the entree to me for half price. He brought back my bill, said he charged me half for my take home order and quickly walked off. When I was leaving he was standing at the front, I told him that his actions were not acceptable and He was obviously not focused on customer service. His response was "call corporate". Wow, don't think I will be visiting this restaurant again. Management certainly does not care about the customer experience.

This is a quaint little bar just down from Bourbon Street. Just far enough from the ruckus. Let me start by saying they, by far, had the coldest beer I've ever tasted. $3 Blue Moons.....say what?! Yes, please!  

My crew ordered the backspace burger minus the fixins but RAVED about how great the burger tasted.  I had the adult grilled cheese. Equally great.  I would given them 5 stars but the kitchen was a one-man-band so our food took forever.  Granted it was the day of the Alabama/Ohio State game, but  the place isn't that large. It was well worth the wait. So much so we came back on the January 2nd for our farewell meal. This time I ordered the Backspace burger with the works. OMG! Definitely a must visit.

I went there because i heard they have good ribs. Well i walked in and the lady said "We are not open, Probably another hour". Mind you its going on 4pm. This place serves breakfast, lunch and dinner so i dont know why they would not be open. I left and came back the next day. Me and my cousin ordered two chicken wing platters. The chicken had absolutely no flavor or season. The greens i have had way better, The mac and cheese was ok but i have had better as well. Cabbage was horrid and the yams was really good. Lemon and strawberry cake was really good as well. Icing is very sweet though. I would only go back to get a slice of cake if i ever went back

Maybe we were there on a bad day because the service was very slow, short staffed it seemed. We were waiting forever just to get waited on which was frustrating when you're hungry. By the time we got our food (almost 30+ mins) we just wanted to eat and leave. I suggested this to my family because of the reviews here on Yelp and my brother has been here before to add to the positive comments but for me, my first impressions of it (service-wise) weren't too good. 

The food, on the other hand, was good and I would probably give it another go because of  it. I got the chicken pad Thai. My parents also ordered from the big bowl menu and my brother got the chicken Katsu which was yummy. The prices were very reasonable, about $44 for all of us. 

I'm open to change my review on a next visit if the service is better. Service definitely affects your whole dine-in experience.

After loving on the west coast for over 20 years, I admit I'm a sushi snob. From the quality of the fish to the rice to the wasabi, it all counts and Tuna Bar hits on all cylinders (the wasabi is freshly grated). I'm looking forward to trying the other dishes as well but I'm sure they will deliver as well.

Food is good, service is TERRIBLE. We were there for 30 minutes before WE flagged down a waiter. They never asked how everything was. Never got refills on drinks until we asked. Be prepared to spend almost 2 hours cause they are so slow.

Went to johns pass to watch dolphins and the sunset to enjoy our last night in Florida. Was hoping to go to waltzs but they were closed, so we went to sculleys. We came at around 9:15 and they close at 10 so we cut it close, but our waiter showed no signs of frustration and was very nice and attentive all night. I ordered a cup of the clam chowder which was delicious, and the kale and quinoa salad with mahi mahi. Fish was very fresh, and the salad was excellent. My girlfriend ordered pasta with mussels and she enjoyed hers as well. To top it off we sat next to the water and got to see dolphins jumping out of the water. It was a great way to end our vacation and I look forward to coming back next time I get the opportunity
Every time I come home I always need to get Taste of India. Always impeccable and delicious and you're getting so much food for your money which is great cause I always have leftovers!

I recently just got married at Shephards on May 30th of this year. Let me tell you that the only saving grace for them is Sharyn the wedding coordinator. She was amazing!! She was very thorough and everything associated with our wedding was perfect, we couldn't have asked for a better person to help us set everything up since we live in Kentucky. Now that was the only thing that went smoothly. Whenever we checked into the hotel on the 28th on a Thursday we were inquiring about all the rooms that we had booked for the wedding party. The girl at the front desk was wearing a name tag that said Valerie but come to find out whenever she answered the phone her actual name was Heather. Hmm mm. Oh well. We were checking on 3 other reservations with "Valerie" and she said that she didn't see any in the system. Do we had to pull up all the reservations from our email and read them off to her. We had reserved two additional bay side rooms and 1 island view rooms. Well come to find out they booked us for  was 2 island view rooms and 1 bay room. We had told her that this wasn't correct and we had made the reservations directly with Greg. She then said well that sounds about right, implying that Greg does this numerous times a week. Finally we got everything straightened out and were told that we needed a 50$ deposit for incidentals. No worries on that. Let's fast forward through all the other boring details and get right down to the heart of the problem. My wife's mother was paying for our room and my brother in laws room also. Whenever we both checked our credit card statements my wife had 3 deposits for 50$ held on her card and also 2 charges for 210 and some change each. So our 50 deposit turned into over 470 dollars rather quickly. We let my brother in law know about what happened and told him to check his card also. Come to find out that they charged his card over 900$. When we checked out at the front desk what we thought would be a quick fix turned into a nightmare. A quick 5-10 minute check out turned into almost an hour. Not one person at the front desk could give us an explanation on how or why these charges were on our credit cards. The amounts didn't even match up to our room totals at all is the thing. No one at the front desk even cared to explain the situation and why the charged were ut on the cards. Eventually after the hour was up everything was finally worked out, everything except for my mother in law getting charged a 50$ incidental fee in addition to all the room costs. It is now the 10th of June and still have not seen that refund back on her card and it has been 11 days. I will not stay or use this resort ever again. Sharyn was the saving grace at this resort by far and she should be commended on how professional that she was. Also I would like to think whenever you book a 200+ dollar a night king suite that you are not kept up till 2-3am in the morning because the tiki bar outside lets the locals in to party all night. Stay away from this place at all costs.

Attended a Sockeye Brewery Tastings And food pairings. Six brews and five courses masterfully prepared by chef Shipley with excellent service. The restaurant is acoustically lively; at times it was difficult to maintain a conversation with our table mates. Within walking distance of the Capitol building, the usual menu and table names plays on the legislative process and famous legislators. Tonight's special event was a real treat and we plan to return in the future.

This place has gone from an iconic Tucson institution to a sad modern day faux Mexican restaurant. Couple the average food with terrible service and you have a customer will will not be coming back. We had a group of 10 that sat for about 6 mins before anyone ever approached our table. From there everything was painstakingly slow at every turn. I had a salad and tacos. The chopped salad was straight out of a bag with minimal Mexican cheese, canned mandarin orange slices, and soaked in dressing. I could have picked up the tacos at a hole in the wall for half the price and had a more authentic Mexican dinner. Save you time and don't go.

My girlfriend used to go to college in the area and when I was visiting this was the spot to go. They serve all types if meals but this review is really for the cheesesteak. It was damn good. In fact whenever I go to Philly I feel the need to get one from here (double cheese with green peppers). It's a good look.

My boyfriend and I went here back in April for my birthday breakfast and we loved every little bit of it.  The building is quaint and cute, the service was great and even the patrons were laid back.  I got a mimosa and he got a tequila sunrise, both were well made, no 80% OJ 20% champagne stuff going on at Horn's.  For food, I got the Crabby Wife and he got the Jewish Coonass.  Both dishes were absolutely delicious and neither of us would have changed a thing, talk about filling and comforting. I'm not usually a biscuit fan, but event the biscuits at Horn's were good!  If we're in NOLA again, we'll definitely be back.

Love this place. How is this place still in business with the huge portions you get! The food is very authentic and old family style italian. BYOB which is always awesome. It's also located right at the edge of girard estates area of philly which is the nicest and safest area in the city. I hope this places stays a south philly secret.

Ok. Yesterday was the third time I've been here in two weeks. May go again today. Definitely not a dieters delight. Though they do have veggie burgers. Tried the hot dogs but my favorite is the bacon cheeseburger. Fast, extremely friendly staff, large burger (if you have a small appetite, try the little burger), all condiments are free add ons. Such as mushrooms, lettuce, tomato, pickles and more.
Staff sings to the music.

Could've been an off night, but as yelp puts it, "meh. I've experienced better." The grungy crowd stared me down when I walked in wearing business attire and sat down to wait for a friend. Once she arrived, our frazzled waitress poured glasses of water before flitting off to wait on ten other tables (four of which were outside), returning very intermittently. The front and porch doors were left open breezing 50 degree weather past us for the entirety of our meal. It was not a comfortable place to eat.

The restaurant welcomed vegetarian menu in an otherwise carnivorous town. The hummus was a little dry and my Volatoo Indian rice bowl too liquid and bland (note: I like my food spicier than your average American, but it still was below standards after asking for extra spice). My friend commented her Thai peanut sauce was also blander than she had expected. I would not re-order these three dishes.

The crowd grew as the evening continued, leading me to think live music began after dinnertime, but I was in no mood to stay after eating.
Two visits on my trip. Excellent food and service! Had the oyster Benedict and the seafood Benedict.  Awesome grits as well!
Lots of slots, you have to pay to park, the cocktail waitresses aren't cute, drinks take forever, and everyone smokes in there..... I'd still go back though

First off. This rating is for service and not the food. I have to stress that first. That being said I can't begin to say how disappointed I am in the service (or lack there of) I received tonight. I actually frequent this restaurant and have for years. Tonight I attempted to bring 7 of my friends along to enjoy dinner here for a birthday celebration. When we arrived we asked what the wait time would be. The hostess who was very nice told us 20-25 minutes for indoor or we could be seated immediately outdoor. The 8 of us were talking and another woman arrived at the hostess station and told her it would not be 25 min but 45 to an hour. So we asked to be seated outside. The hostess explained that if we chose to eat outside if it rained there would be no guarantee we could be moved indoors. We agreed and that was fine. The hostess then mentioned to the other young lady (who I would later find out was named laney) that we chose outside and she was worried about the rain. Laney told her "well that isn't our problem". During the time that I was speaking to the hostess the other young woman kept repeating what the hostess was telling me. I'm an adult and I can hear plenty well so I knew what she was saying the first time and didn't need a third party repeating it. 

While the hostess sat the rest of my party I stuck around to ask the young lady if there was a problem or if we had done something to annoy or offend her. She simply stated she wasn't referring to us she was talking about something else. Ok.
