My stuffed french toast was not cooked all the way through, and my fiance's breakfast sandwich was a mess.  I was also frustrated that my meal was served with imitation maple syrup in a plastic cup, considering our meal was $30 dollars before tip (you can add real maple syrup for $2, lol).  The hash browns were just terrible, they were slimy and tasted a month old.  The food was almost as good as a quality diner, but not quite.  The space is charming, but it seems like they have far more tables than the kitchen can keep up with.  We sat near the kitchen door and during our lengthy stay you could see the kitchen staff was barely keeping things together.  It's a shame to see a small kitchen working so hard with no hope of getting out of the weeds. The army of servers was very friendly and took our order promptly.  We had high hopes for Blue Plate, but have to say we won't return and wouldn't recommend it to others.

Not the best quality today in my arugula
Salad.  The avocado was bad (gray) and yet still served on top of the salad.  Usually much better.  Staff mis rung our order and changed it from salad to wrap.  While walking out, we were stopped and asked for $2 difference.  Not very professional nor customer friendly.

As a local, it takes a lot to get me to cross the causeway and to the beach.  However, my wife convinced me to try Basimo, and I'm certainly glad that we did.  The food is fresh, made-to-order, and unique, especially in an area filled with chains and comfort food.  I ordered the organic bagel and a smoothie, while my wife got poached eggs.  The flavor of the food was outstanding, especially the blend of pepper on the greens, which sparked my wife to comment how it'd be easier to get me to eat vegetables if they tasted like that all the time.  I couldn't argue!  The smoothie was delicious, and the cream cheese was a revelation, as was the blackberry jam, which took me back to my childhood and my aunt's orchard.

Beyond the delicious food, and a very passable cup of coffee, we were taken by the homey atmosphere.  It was like visiting a neighbor and sitting at the breakfast bar chatting while they fixed breakfast.  And they treated my young daughter very nicely, even giving her some tasty grapes on the house.  We lingered well beyond the time we would normally spend in a restaurant (especially with a 16-month old).  Who could want to rush out of such a nice place?

We had a fantastic experience, and are looking forward to our next meal at Basimo.  It is definitely worth crossing the causeway for a healthy, homemade breakfast, and Basimo delivers both with flying colors.

Had the pleasure of dining here with the parents, kids, and the wife this past Sunday. I enjoyed their brunch menu: leiper's fork, a delicious egg, tn country ham, smoked Gouda and sausage gravy opened face sandwich. It was fantastic. The side items were a bit cold (breakfast potatoes) and my mother's praline banana French toast was also cold (like they cooked hours ahead of time and topped the bananas and pralines when she ordered it). If not for this, I'd have given a five star. Also the she-crab soup that my step-father got was delicious. All in all a great little slice of heaven in the Bellevue area. Crumb de la Crumb does offer great bakery items and coffees as well. I highly recommend this place.

If I could give half stars, I'd want to give 3.5 here. It's definitely not yet at 4, but more than 3, no doubt. 

I was super excited when I found out about this restaurant. Being from Dallas, one of the big voids I felt here in St. Louis was the lack of proper crawfish, so when news broke of this place, I rejoiced. After having the crawfish, I remain cautiously optimistic. That having been said, I won't rave and say this place is amazing, because it isn't. Not yet. However, I see much potential here. I got 2 lbs of crawfish, corn, and Cajun fries. The corn was sweet and juicy and perfectly soaked up all the juice from my boil bag. The shoestring fries were crispy and seasoned just right. The crawfish was good. Not great, but good. I was disappointed at the flavor. I opted for the whole sha-bang (obvi the only way to go!) and went with mild on the spice level (my general spice tolerance is pretty low), afraid that anything higher that mild would make my nose leak and my lips burn. However, the mild was, in fact, extremely mild. I tried my fiancé's top level spicy crawfish, and even that was doable. I think they could probably afford to go more heavy handed with the spice on the flavor, and really kick it up a couple notches with the heat. I must admit, though, that the buggers that were sitting and marinating at the bottom of the bag were quite flavorful and succulent, so that was a plus. Also, mopping up each crawfish in the remaining juice also helped with the flavor. 

If crawfish isn't your thing, they have crab, oysters, shrimp, and other options. Shrimp basket was fantastic; one thing I generally dislike about fried food is all the breading. The shrimp here were crisp with minimal breading, and the flavor was spot on. Interior is nice and spacious, and there is ample spaces to park. Extra points for having sinks in the back of the restaurant, outside of the restroom area, so you can quickly wash all the crawfish juice from your hands. 

I remain highly optimistic for this place. Will I go back? 100%. Do I recommend it? Yes, definitely give it a try. I am hoping that with some time, the flavors will really develop and I will really, really be mad for the Mad Crab!

Ha, the breakfast was just okay. Granted I didn't go during breakfast time really. Except the french toast, unbelievably good for a tiny place like this. Our waitress seemed hurried.. I soon learned why. What made the experience memorable was the employees blatently discussing details of drug transactions in front of senile old customers in terms they were sure no one would understand. Apparently as soon as she was done with our table she would run home and pick it up. Wondering if customers can also score an eighth for the low, lol.

Another amazing Mexican place in Tennessee! We headed into Nashville from Kentucky, before heading back to California. Of course I needed to get another chimichanga covered in cheese dip before we headed back the next day! 
I searched on Yelp and we were close to Las Palmas! 
Once again the cheese dip covered chimichanga did not disappoint. As someone who is from a California, visits Mexico often, and has lived in Texas, I have had my fair share of Mexican food. From traditional to Tex Mex nothing beats the amazing cheese dip of Kentucky and Tennessee. 
I absolutely love the chimichangas but my younger cousins all love what many restaurants refer to as the the special. Here it is called the LP Special and is rice with meat covered in the cheese dip! I want to try this next time!
Check this place out if you're in Nashville!

My wife and I recently went to Red Mesa during a brief stop in St. Pete. Though it looks unassuming from the exterior, and the interior is nothing to write about, the food here is amazing. 

We tried the fried calamari as an appetizer, and I can't rave enough about the sauces which accompanied the  perfectly fried calamari; both the chipotle and curry dipping sauces were divine. 

My wife got some fried shrimp as her entree and I decided to go with a combination platter with a taco, enchilada, and empanada. Both our meals were PERFECT. The empanada crust could make anything taste good, it was simply delicious!

This restaurant is a must when stopping in St. Pete!

There's a lot of pizza around Drexel so I thought this place would be just like the others...it's not!  A friend convinced me to check it out and when I saw their 2 slices and a bottled soda for $5 I was drawn inside.  I had the Big Daddy Bacon, BBQ, Ranch pizza and it was one of the best pizzas I've had (and I've had a lot).  Today, I just went back to get some more and they were in the process of cooking the pizza I wanted so they took my name and number and said they'd call me when it was ready since I work close enough they're even going to bring it to me!  Service at it's FINEST!

Had a very nice first visit here. The owner Ted, was very friendly from the start and the restaurant was busy on a Friday night the beginning of Chinese New Year. We ordered the Pu-pu platter and crab Rangoon and for dinner chef specials with seafood instead of Chinese American regulars and some fried rice. Everything was well prepared. The shrimp large vegetables crisp. The chili sauce sweet and tangy. 

We will return. The owner made an effort to visit and learn our names and ask about our first visit.

I had been wanting to try Oakley's for months (since I read about it on Yelp, thank you, Yelpers!) and about three weeks before Max was born, we headed out the whole 2 miles from our house (yes, this little gem was hiding out just around the corner for the entire five years we have lived here!) to experience the fabulousness that is Oakley's Bistro.  Tucked in a small strip mall (I know, right?  Not ideal but...it works!), it doesn't have a ton of curb appeal, but once inside, the trendy, romantic atmosphere prevails.  Don't let the parking lot scare you away or trick you into thinking this is a cheap dining (as bistro might let on).

My husband and I were seated promptly on a Friday night on a cool summer evening in early August.  It was a great location with a view of the whole dining room AND the kitchen (like that!).  Our waiter (I can't remember his name but his girlfriend had just recently had a baby) was prompt, polite and recommended incredible choices from the menu.

I do remember arguing with hubs about which appetizer to get, but we settled (and by settled, I mean, I got my way) on the Lobster Waffle.  We had to try it, after all - who puts lobster in a waffle?  All I can say is ...wow.  Heaven in my mouth (I am writing this review SOLELY for the waffle, I won't lie - you MUST go there now and get it).  It came in a skillet, hot out of the oven, full of a deliciousness I cannot fully describe!  Large chunks of lobster, an incredible sauce all mixed together with some amazing veggies IN A WAFFLE!! Who knew?!?!  I certainly did not, but let me tell you, I could have eaten another for my entree.

My entree ...while good, was not as delectable as the lobster waffle (but I suppose, I may have blown the load on the appetizer!) :).  I got the Fettuccini with veal meatballs.  It was good, but a bit on the salty side and I am a HUGE fan of this particular spice, so I was a bit overwhelmed.  I thought the sauce lacked SOMETHING, though at the time, I could not place it.  I would not get it again.

My husband got the Duck and Duck and he thought it was great.  I went to try it and he nearly stabbed my pregnant paw with his fork before allowing me a (small) bite.  It was mouth-watery and delicious.  I was incredibly jealous of his meal.  

We skipped dessert.  Our bill was still out of our pre-baby budget at right over $100 with tip but I absolutely enjoyed my "last supper" and would definitely go back!!

I recommend Oakley's for anyone looking for something unique, original, small and intimate in Indy.  Great for a small group (maybe 4-8 people), a third (hello - home run, boys!) date, or a nice girls' night out.  They have a wine list that I did not partake in but was very interested, and I think that if you have the money, you should spend it here instead of a typical chain hell hole that encompasses the roads of Indianapolis.
This place gets how to do it. Online ordering, with tip included! They show up when they say they will. The food! Great sushi for a perfect price. Just love this place.

We made a reservation to go here with our children on Sunday evening solely based on the high Yelp rating. Disappointing is an understatement. The $13-15 price for three bites of pasta is absolutely ridiculous. They stated that they were meant for tasting. In that case, either lower the price or provide a somewhat larger portion. We were flabbergasted! The food overall had a good flavor but was consistently over salted.The waitress was friendly but mostly stood over by the kitchen and chatted with her cohorts. Getting her to get us a check or for more water was impossible. Definitely not going here again.
Love this place!! Amazing French toast with Caramelized bananas and great omelets as well. Very nice atmosphere and great service... Will be returning often.
Great place to bring a girlfriend, the view is pretty spectacular!

I was craving sushi one night, but it was late in Chinatown.  My options were limited, and I opted to try Mixx Asian Bistro.  I called in an order for pick-up, including a spider roll, tamago nigiri, and a few more rolls to tally my bill to approximately $30.  To my chagrin, there were no other customers in the restaurant upon my arrival... despite Chinatown being alive and kickin' until upwards of 2 AM.

Well, it was the worst spider roll I have ever had.  In fact, all of the rolls were horrible.  I've had better "sushi" in pre-packaged containers from the grocery store.  The rice was dry and inconsistent, but boy was there ever a lot of it!  The tamago was also dry and lacking of any sweetness.  I should have just scrambled some eggs myself and slapped it on rice.  The remaining rolls aren't even worth mentioning.

I was left with a bloated rice stomach, an insulted palate, and a lingering feeling of regret for flushing $30 down the toilet.

I will never come back to this restaurant.

I had an enjoyable dinner her I sat at the bar to watch the Warriors win the NBA finals. The wild mushroom with balsamic was a great appetizer and it went well with a black butte porter. The bar staff were very attentive and made good recommendations. For my main course I kept it simple with a nice burger, some of the other entrees looked interesting too. I would not hesitate to eat her again.

Not happy. When I ordered a beer and chips and dip it took 20 min and I still had no chips and dip. Finally I told the waiter to refund my money. 5 more minutes to complete that. The entire time the manager, a short haired blonde females with glasses I could hear explained the entire thing. She never said a word to me. Poor management and organization.

This place looks a lot nicer than it actually is, unfortunately. It's also priced as if it were a nicer restaurant.

I just ordered soup since I wasn't all that hungry to begin with, and it was just ok. My friend, however, ordered a full entree for $26 and she said it was subpar at best. The fries were soft and the schnitzel didn't have much flavor. It was a $30 fried meal basically. The staff also seemed inexperienced. They were nice though. 

I know we didn't have to order what we ordered. Maybe if we had ordered something else, our experience would have been better, but overall we weren't impressed.
Best breakfast in Indy. You always get something different as the menu is always changing. Go early since it can get busy. And it's the best orange juice I've ever had.

The food tastes like it was seasoned with water and the turkey may as well have been jerky. The food was well below subpar. I know this is a local hot spot but I cannot figure out why. . I usually don't mind waiting for excellent food and service, but never again will I wait 30 mins in the rain for pancake pantry. Do yourself a favor and skip it, especially if you're price conscious. Outrageously priced for the meager offerings.

I found this place on Facebook. I love a good Cuban Sandwich so I figured why not try one that is "Authentic". Beautiful day when I went. Sat outside, ordered my sandwich and was super excited. Got my sandwich looked good, but tasted awful. The au jus or whatever it was, wasn't that great. The Sandwich was bland as well as the sauce. I have had a better Cuban Sandwich at 14 West. Sorry Tata but I won't return.

Epic fail.  15 minutes after we ordered, we received the smallest 13 dollar cheesesteak I could even imagine.  13 dollars you say?  Oh yes, they charge a dollar for exactly 3 pieces of long hots, and TWO dollars for sharp provalone.  And their "traditional" size is so cute and little.  Like it is a kid size.  
Now, mind you, we are Tony Luke Oregon Ave customers.  We go there instead of Pats and Genos.  
This sandwich went in the trash.  It was greasy.  The meat was cooked weird.  It was stacked weird.  The onions were disgusting.  Now, this was at 7pm, not 1:30 AM.   Clearly the grill was not hot enough, and the cooks were not good enough or didn't care enough to fix it.  The roll was bad.  I can't believe my wife and I had to toss this in the trash and look for other food.  But we did.
The worst part? OK, the sandwich was the worst part.  But the next worst part?  We talked to the manager.  He apologized and said he would keep an eye on the guys on the grill.  But didn't offer us a re-done sandwich or a refund or anything.  He saw us throw it in the trash and did not make it right.
Tony.  We have talked to you at your stand in South Philly, and the restaurant across the street.  If this is what you think of South Jersey, stay on your side of the river.  I can get a sandwich like this for a couple dollars at Wawa.

So there isnt much great to say about this location popeyes there is usually always an issue with condiments. Not enough ketchup NEVER any strawberry jelly (because yes not everyone loves grape). But the main reason that they get such a poor rating is because i dont think i have ever been there and the staff didnt have an attitude all the way up to the manager! If you are traveling and leaving out the city to head towards Ms then may suggest another popeyes because you may get hot fresh chicken or you may just get the wrong order as i have a few times. They get two stars instead of one because when the order is correct and fresh the food is good!

Good food. Indian in Bryn Mawr, yay! I had Malai Kofta, which didn't really seem to have much cheese for "cheese dumplings" but were nonetheless delicious. My girlfriend had mango chicken (on the special bryn mawr menu) and it was delicious as well. 

I've had better naan but this was perfectly acceptable. tamarind and mint chutneys served with it were good. 

decor is somewhat cheesy but that doesn't matter. service is just fine. 

lots of families with kids there when I went. 

They deliver! and there's no fee (according to the website) so a meal + tip is pretty much the same price whether you go to sit in or order delivery. Seeing as how I usually end up spending way more than I intend on delivery food I think I'll try this next time and get better quality food than pizza or bad chinese for probably a similar price.

Also I definitely plan to go to the 9? dollar lunch buffet sometime!

Amazing!  Have tried Piezanos several times since their opening and have been consistently impressed with the quality of pizza and other food there.  The crust is chewy, the sauce is lovely with a nice spice to it, and prices are awesome.  They also have a good selection of nicely prepared salads to feast on prior to the carb over load.  This is a great new option in Tucson!  Keep up the great work.
I love their donuts!!  First tasted them in Duck, NC.  So glad they're here.  The kids working there did a great job!!  Pretty darn quick, considering they're "assembled".

Had a wonderful time and delicious food!

So friend #1 is vegan and allergic to onions. The chef came to the table and helped create a tasty custom taco that catered to her dietary requirements and she absolutely loved it! She has a taco with kale, peppers, and avocado.

Friend #2 is super picky! She had the grilled avocado entree and said it was amazing! The flavor was just great.

Lastly, little old me :) I just had the queso and chips. But it was fantastic! 

Finally the server in training and his trainer were superb! They really made our night and we can't wait to return.
Great casual brunch spot. Egg frittata was excellent. Customer service was exceptional!

Jesse's was one of the first restaurants I visited after moving to this area over 20 years ago.   At the time smoking was still allowed in certain sections and the people I was with did smoke. The place reminded me of the old Ohio bar/restaurants I used to go to with my grandparent who were smokers and drinkers.  It brought back fond memories. But back go Jesse's.... This is always my first pick for steak in Brandon.  I also love the Jesse special.  The salad and bread are always fresh and the bartender does not skimp on the alcohol.   We always went during early bird- happy hour - to take advantage of the specials.  I highly recommend this Brandon landmark.  Oh. By the way.   No more smoking in the restaurant which is fine for me and I know everyone else is happy too - except maybe those people drinking at the small bar....  Long live Jesse's.  Much better than any chain restaurant.

No attention grabber or witty introduction here, just some amazing pasta. 

I came to Moto with some friends for a bachelorette party. We arrived early and got drinks at the bar while we waited but were still seated on time. Our waiter was friendly and helpful with menu suggestions. All of the pasta I tried was unbelievable, definitely house made fresh and somebody knows what they're doing. All of the drinks I tried were great, unique and summery. I wanted to explore their wine deals/selections a little more but we were going to bars afterwards and I knew I wouldn't be having wine there. Don't miss the accompaniments for the bread, they cost extra but otherwise you don't get anything served with the bread. They will bring you more so ask for it!

I would love to come back here to have more of their heavenly pasta, Ill just have to find an excuse to come back to Nashville

Oh goodness the red curry here is addictive.  As is the lamb rack.  It is cooked to tender perfection and the seasoning really brings out the meat's flavor without overpowering it.  One of my favorite Thai places.  And it's only 5 min away!

Came in town for a friends wedding had been here a very long time ago and i hadnt realized how good this place waa until i tried it again this morning! You are going to have a wait so be prepared to wait or get there super early. I got there about 930 on saturday morning and had to wait about 15-20 mins to get seated. After having a hard time deciding between the sweet potato pancakes and the cinnamon spice i decided to go with the sweet potatoe and lets just say hands down you have to try those! Even if you aren't a big sweet potatoe fan you will love these!! I cant wait to come back to Nashville just to try these. My girl had the blueberry pancake it was still great just no as good as mine! Def worth the hype and give it a try if you are in town

Never give up the chance to eat beignets!! Beignets are French donuts topped with powdered sugar. If you're like me , and never want to share deliciois food esp beignets and don't want evidence showing you have been there (because when there's good food we are a little selfish, don't lie!! I know I'm not the only one).. don't wear black. The powdered sugar GETS EVERY WHERE!!! LOLOL.

They have a drive through here for quick pick ups if you don't want to stop inside to eat/drink. If you do plan on ordering to go, it would be a good idea to ask for the beignets and powdered sugar be put in different bags so it doesn't all melt together by the time you are ready to eat them. 

They're so hot, fluffy, doughy goodness. Everytime I'm in town I will always have to make a stop to pick some up. They have souvenir stuff inside that you can pick up, including a premix that you can buy to make some yourself at home. 

Only reason I'm giving a four instead of a 5, is because of their restroom situation. They really really are in need of a major restroom make over ! It's old, disgusting, cramped, and stinks. Do not use the restroom it will make you lose your appetite.

HOT POT!

Oh hot pot, today, when it is so cold and dreary, I really, really wish I had another of you to warm the cockles of my heart. 

When I saw all of my Yelp friends had already been here and thought it was awesome, I knew I had to come try it out.  I was certainly not disappointed.  The ambiance here is a little weird, I think it's an old Perkins or something, but that is more than made up for by the food.  I ordered the vegetarian hot and sour soup hot pot.  It came in a big stainless steel bowl that rested over an open flame to keep it warm (see photos).  This was then ladled onto vermicelli noodles, and then put in my mouth.  This was a ton of food.  I ate it all.  I also got a thai tea bubble tea which was almost like a bubble tea milkshake and was really good.    

I want to bring my husband back here asap, as I went with a friend.  I was just there last night, but if he wanted to go this weekend, I happily would.  In fact, if he wanted to go right this second, I still would.  With bells on.

Well made, tasty, good portion sizes, ready for pickup on time. Many more offerings than Tiffin, our previous go to in Wynnewood. "Medium" spice level might be a bit hotter than some are accustomed to.

This restaurant is a solid four based on the experience, service and food. 

The waitstaff was incredible friendly and they timed each thing perfectly. 

MY DATE'S EXPERIENCE
He started with the soup sampler and it was really fantastic. Together it equals about a cup of soup and was the perfect starter to his meal. Next, he had the raved about BBQ shrimp. After getting over the embarrassment of the bib, my introverted boyfriend went nuts. He really enjoyed the dish. 

MY FOOD
I'd had an upset stomach for most of my trip to NO, which is just unfortunate. This means my 'dinner' was salad (mixed greens with an incredible herb vignette) and the duck egg roll. I also ordered the fries and while they claim 'emerged in rosemary and garlic oil' I think the mean: regular old friends with a roasted garlic on the side rosemary sprinkled over top.

This place is fantastic! Top notch, couldn't find a thing to complain about if I tried.  We sat in the back yard/ garden.  It was like stepping into a Mediterranean/ middle eastern garden.  We were actually supposed to head in for dinner but just couldn't leave the beauty of that garden.  

Drinks: extremely unique.  We tried "the poet" but there were a bunch of awesome craft cocktails plus a full bar.  

Food: delicious!  You don't get access to the full menu in the yard but the stuff that we did have access to was amazing.  

Service: excellent bar, waiter and support/ management.  Really made us feel at home.  

* note: we went without our kids.  Changing tables and children friendly bathrooms were not assessed! We'll see if there a deal breaker here....
Best dessert bakery in Northern Nevada. Haven't been there for a dine-in meal yet, but cookies and pastries are awesome. Breads are ok - not much selection.

Okay first time here and I really was great every bite I took I was happy with, the wait wasn't too bad prices were good although I found it a little strange they charge for a cup of water (really?)... The woman who too my order was nice and had a big smile always a plus. The only reason they didn't get a straight 5 star was the dining experience, there just is not enough space in there I was elbow to elbow with people I didn't know and it was pretty loud they need a bigger location they really are doing fried chicken right :) I was overall really happy I won't be returning to Popeyes for the rest of my stay in Nola that's for sure this place had a great homecookin flavor!
What a wonderful little spot! We enjoyed the service and the food. Too much to finish. The Quesidillas and steak was excellent.

I'm not sure what all the fuss is about.  Went there last night and had the coconut smoothie and it was very good.  Then ordered the mapo tofu, fried pork bao and the eggplant and pork.
What a disappointment.  The tofu while a large enough portion had very little flavor!  We ordered it with pork and it had maybe 5 little pieces of ground pork.  We kept adding spices and soy to get some flavor.  Then while the eggplant had good flavor, it was a bit undercooked and also, where's the pork?  I have never seen less meat in a dish that advertised meat!  Never!  The pork bao was ok but the bao part was a bit old and I had to pick the hard parts of the dough off.  
I would not return.  Thoroughly unimpressed.
Great beer.  Need I say more.  Great food. Wonderful staff.  Generous portions.   Sit outside dogs are welcome    They provide water for your dog.  Very kind.

This was R's FAVE place during our short visit in NOLA. They're famous for their burger or at least that's what R told me. We came during happy hour on a weekday. I think it was like 4-6 PM? Or maybe it went to 7 PM. Regardless, we MADE it, that's the important thing. Because their HH is amaze-balls. There were $0.75 raw oysters, $1.50 cooked on the menu. Half off of cocktails. We ordered a few, like 5? These raw oysters were so huge, like a little bigger than the size of my hand. What an amazing deal. They were delicious too! The service was nice and attentive. Oh yeh, the burger. R loved this burger too. I think he just likes burgers in general but if you're a burger fan, you've really got to try their's out. We saw other people in tables next to us that ordered like, 20 oysters at once. Despite ordering a small number, I think it was satisfying. Their cocktails are really good too. This place is next to the Hilton and the crazy thing is that when we walked to our hotel room (yup, we stayed at the next door Hilton), there was a Luke's takeout bag in front of someone's door! Apparently, you can use hotel credit at Lukes AND have them deliver I think.

I have a hard time knocking a restaurant that makes an actual attempt at accessible french cuisine in the desert.  The dining room is beautiful and clean, the presentation and preparation of the food is of importance to the kitchen staff and it shows, and some of the dishes are really quite good.  The obvious downfall is the service, but I have only had issues on really busy nights, and always with the same servers.

The best suggestion I have for your best bet at an awesome experience is this:

Skip the typical busy nights if possible, and if not, sit at the bar or patio.  They seem to be the smallest sections distributed to the servers, and you're more likely to get attentive service here.

Indulge in the oysters.  They could easily be called among the top three freshest available in the Old Pueblo, and at $3.00, they are actually pretty moderately priced.  

For the less adventurous pallets, both of the burgers and all three salads are really well done.  One of my friends let me try their burger, and the meat was of really good quality and also cooked perfectly to temperature.

The lamb shank is delicious.  Mine was perfectly cooked, juicy and falling off the bone.  I didn't touch the asparagus or the mashed potatoes, but only because I liked the lamb so much.

As I mentioned in the last two meat dishes, the cooking any meat is done well here, and the Steak Frites is no exception.  Perfectly cooked, soft for a strip cut and really devoid of too much garnish.  It's a quality peace of meat, and they let the flavor of it stand for itself, which I love.  

The Trout Meuniere was prepared well, and if you are a trout fan, you probably won't be disappointed with the dish, though you get the impression that it was something added to the menu as an after thought.  A little uninspired and "safe" in the flavors and preparation for my taste.

Meals you may want to skip:
"Le Grand Plateau" however, can be skipped in my opinion.  I spent the money ($55.00) because if the oysters were so good, so I figured this dish that included crab legs, shrimp, mussels, scallops, and other tasty seafood was going to be just as impressive, but i was sadly mistaken.  The concept behind the dish is strong, but it's probably not a big seller, because the freshness I loved about the oysters was not there in "Le Grand Plateau".  

While you're at it, skip the Pate too.  It's canned, or at least it tastes canned, and I don't think it was any good before it made it into the can to begin with.

So overall, I really had a pleasant experience here.  I think you could too, and it would be well worth the effort.  It is a newer restaurant with a mostly untested staff up to this point, and I hope that soon the management and front of house will get into a good groove, because the kitchen is putting out some really good stuff.

Check it out if you're feeling adventurous.  If anything, you'll at least be surrounded by a beautiful setting, be served a good mixed drink or glass of wine and a well cooked piece of meat.

Great fries.  Basic bar food at decent prices.  My friend swears that she had a bottle beer refilled and served back to her here.  Still, we usually come back whenever I visit for the fries and the people watching.

Good fresh food & excellent service.  The menu is broad and I don't think there is anything over $8.  The farm fresh eggs were as good as described;I didn't have to ask for extra napkins, a plus for me:) and my toast was perfect.  I'll definitely be back with my little ones next time.  This place has permanently removed Ihop and Denny's as future breakfast choices for me.

Overall a good experience! The interior and decorations are really nice and service was good.

We had an early dinner around 5 and it was pretty empty but filled up as it got closer to 6.

We ordered two ramen bowls, two sushi rolls, and a vegan poke bowl for four people and were satisfied. The ramen was a great price point ($11) and was pretty good. Thought the flavor of the broth could be richer, but can't beat that price in this area. The sushi rolls were good although I didn't try nigiri or sashimi so didn't get a good feel for the raw fish itself. The vegan poke bowl was unique, the vegan tuna in it could've tricked me if I hadn't known beforehand!

Cute spot with good food at a good price!

I visited for lunch- The highlight of my experience was Garland the perfect bartender. He was helpful and funny Prompt without being pushy. He clearly knows service and is good at his job.

The food left something to be desired. I had the arancini. it was the right texture, but was entirely to salty. I also had the panzanella, which is supposed to be a bread salad meant to use up day old bread. What I got was a green salad with croutons.... Very disappointing!

I Think maybe the building has bad juju, since the last restaurant here also was terrible. I had higher hopes since this is backed by Dave McGroggan, but maybe they are getting complacent too!

Come for drinks and Garland at the bar, but eat somewhere else.

This is the WORST D&B I have ever visited. The restaurant was filthy, with napkins, food and other trash all over the floor. The food was cold. The waitress ignored us while she cleaned liquor bottles for 10 minutes and we had to ask for assistance. When we asked for the manager, he was rude and dismissive. Don't waste your time!

I've gotten food here many times and never had a problem with the food or the service. Daphne, one of the owners, remembers you and always wants to have a small friendly chat when you walk in.  Vanessa, who also works at the front, is very nice and funny.  The food is very good, fast  and always piping hot.  If you want a dish that is not spicy, just ask, they will make it spicy for you.  Any special requests we had, it was always done without any issues.  I never had anything in my food that wasn't supposed to be there.  I don't think they have their actual menu online, but the menu that is, is NOT THEM!!!  This great little business in the neighborhood is taking the brunt of horrible things being said about a jaw bone in their fried rice and a rat in their bathroom.  They do not have a public bathroom as it is a take out restaurant and we always get either their pork or chicken fried rice without any issues.  It is really a shame that there are other places with the same name, in and around the area that are terrible and customers think it is the same place or same owners and it is not.  I know Daphne is very upset and horrified that those incidents are plaguing her business. I have been coming here for over 12 years without one negative incident or dissatisfaction of the food or service.  Again, this take out place is in Hatboro, on County Line Road, not related to any other location with the same name.  I know the owners take pride in their business and do care about their customers.  Please give this restaurant a chance and ignore the negative reviews from other places with the same name.
Food at the Steak house was delicious, however our waiter was not very attentive and I felt rushed to order.

This place was only okay. I have high expectations for a brunch place, especially one in Nashville. I ordered a salad, which was $13 dollars. All it had on it was about 4 blackberries, arugula, two cubes of cheese, and a teaspoon of granola. No meat or bacon or anything. Disappointed to say the least. We were also rudely kicked out by the male worker in the front by the hostess stand when we were trying to purchase a T shirt. No explanation, just told he was clearing out the restaurant. Won't be coming back here and you shouldn't either.
5 stars across the board for food/dining/location/layout/service and menu!!! It definitely is a bit on the pricier side for a local joint but you get what you pay for!

I decided to give this place another shot because I know they have good quality food. As long as you go in expecting a line, get your name on their waiting list (a hostess will come around to get your name), and maybe 15+ minutes wait depending on how far back in line you are. I would not recommend any groups larger than 4 as seating is very limited. So with that mindset, you're ready for Two Chicks Cafe.

I absolutely LOVE LOVE their bbq shrimp and grits. It's the second best shrimp and grits I've ever had (the best is a restaurant in Louisville). I come to NOLA a lot for work at the Convention Center, and would try to eat here every time I come for a visit. I also really enjoy their Green Blast juice if I can splurge on a drink like that. I've had their buckwheat savory crepe before and it wasn't bad. I've heard from multiple people that their quinoa salad is very good. I think I'll give that a try soon. 

I thought this place is very tasty and deserves an updated review.

My favorite place in West Chester to grab a bite and drink. The dining area is is very nice and relaxing. The wait staff has always been very knowledgable and attentive. The food is too die for as well, I would recommend all the appetizers and pastas any day! They have installed a stone pizza oven and I can't wait to try their pizza as well!

My favorite part is the bar. They have incredible bartenders who like to talk to you, recommend new drinks, as well as ensure you are never short on beverages. The bar menu is an incredible deal and the parmesan french fries are to die for! A great place for college kids on a budget with the bar menu and an amazing place to grab a bite with friends or family

I found this place  by accident  and  had  to try it... even though I have  to travel all across town to get there  I always go back at least  once  a month because  the food  is  soo good and  spicy. I strongly recommend itif you wanna try real and good  jamaican food.

Amazingly delicious place for breakfast, beautifully decorated, every detail is gorgeous! Delicious fresh squeezed juices! We came here 4 days in a row and every single time was great!! The two chicks are awesome!!! Highly recommended.
They went out of their way to make sure we had a great time. Crawfish Etouffee was great and the drinks were fantastic.

Tonight we decided to go to Pappy's around 7pm, hoping they still had some bbq left because it was a Wednesday night. I guess we were too hopeful. So instead I used the Yelp app to find another restaurant around because I was not familiar with the other restaurants in the area. I never heard of The Good Pie, but it had some great reviews so we decided to head over there. 

We walked in, and personally  I really liked the feel of the room. Exposed brick walls with the old bicycles along one wall. Wooden tables and the fire burning oven in the open. It wasn't terribly busy, but no one really up at the front. And for being first timers here we didn't know if we were to seat ourselves or wait to be seated (no sign). So we awkwardly stand for a few mins and finally get asked how many and then told to pick a table. UH... why not just put a sign? 

Then we sit ourselves at the table of our choosing....... get our water cups and napkins......... then water............ then finally our menu! The menu wasn't very extensive but I didn't mind. I decided on the good pie. Waited for what seemed to be a reasonable amount of time and finally got our pizzas!

The pizza was a little disappointing....wayy too much olive oil. I cut the pizza in half, lifted it a little bit and slanted it so some of the excess could run off.... it was too much of a good thing. Nothing like the picture on yelp. The ingredients tasted fresh and delicious. I just wish they would've spread them out  a little bit better. 1/4 of my pizza had everything, 1/2 had just basil leaves and sauce, 1/4 had cheese and sauce. And I moved the cherry tomatoes around so it'd be a little more evenly spread out on my pizza. 

I bite in, but all I could taste was the burnt crust. That was disappointing. So I peak on the bottom of my pizza, and it was black :( So i examined the underside of my whole pizza and realize that 1/2 of it is super burnt and the other 1/2 is acceptably burnt. That was seriously the most disappointing fact.

Overall, service was okay, food was okay, ambience of the place was great. But what actually counts and makes a restaurant great was just mediocre. Not really interested in going back there....

We thought we would try roscoes based on the reviews. I was surprised how bland their food was. The shredded chicken tasted like it was canned meat and had no flavor. The tortilla chips are the kind you get at a state fair with cheese on them. I wouldn't go back but I have to say how surprised we were that they were busy. If you like bland Mexican food this is your place.

Pho so Good! I had a beef mix and a side of mixed veggies I added to my soup with rice noodles. Every element was cooked and seasoned to perfection. This was my first time ad I will definitely come back soon. FYI.......What I had was completely gluten free. It only cost $12 and it was enough for2-3 meals.

Decent food (but not fantastic) reasonable prices and what you'd expect from the wait staff....but it was so SO loud.

I don't think you should have to shout to have a conversation. Please turn the music down.

All things considered, I give this place a 3 out of 5 -- average to slightly better than average.
Been to Bab about 6-7 times now. Just solid solid, wholesome food. Love the rice soup you get. The selection of sauces are great. Meats and veggies cooked perfectly.

I went to the restaurant when I was on a business trip in Tucson based on a recommendation of a local who said it was the "best" Mexican restaurant in town. In my opinion it is not. 

The exterior of the restaurant looks nice but the inside is pretty basic. The chips and salsa were average. The wait staff were nice enough and somewhat attentive, but slow. 

The main event of course was the food. I was in a rush and ordered a beef  taco and an enchilada (boring I know). Obviously, these are not the most complex dishes to do well. Unfortunately, they were not and fell into the mediocre category. Both tasted like pabulum and frankly it reminded me of Taco Bell.  There was no flavor in either dish. 

I was really disappointed, paid and rushed out. Would I go back? No.

Horrible customer service. Ask for 12 tacos no lettuce, get them home, all 12 tacos have lettuce. Call to let them know and have new made get hung up on, call back ask for manager and she is very rude. Go get tacos and they are talking about the phone call like I did something wrong not vice versa.
Their new menu is on point, everyone that works here is super friendly! Definitely a good place for a snack and some yummy tacos

Delicious, super affordable. Nice people excellent staff sometimes the owners / cook comes out and says hi. The food is low priced there are great deals for under $5 for a complete breakfast which is unheard of but is definitely delicious. I highly recommend their sausage it's Unique and very flavory. The coffee is delicious, service is fast the place is clean the bathroom is clean.  I take a lot of business friends to this and I've taken my wife to this I've never been disappointed. Great breakfast deals and excellent food for lunch. Highly highly recommended.

I went last night with 2 friends and in short we were underwhelmed. We all were really excited to try out the new place, but left feeling disappointed. The cocktail selection and quality were great, but every piece of drink ware had an issue (lipstick, schmutz, cracks, etc). When I pointed out my really dirty drink glass the waiter just replied "ok"... not a lot of service/let me make you happy attitude. The food was mediocre at best (we had the peach pork, veggie enchiladas and fish tacos), but the guac is GREAT... I wanted to love it, but....

This place is amazing- mainly because of the 2 reasons why everyone else on here thinks so: great food & great people. 

The Moroccan cuisine is some of the best I have had in the city (the lamb was delicious, eggplant was perfect, rice perfectly seasoned & the tomato/cucumber salad TOTALLY worth it) and seriously worth the cheap price. The management is awesome & super friendly, this is definitely a business I will support & continue to frequent as long as I am around/near University City.

i havent been here in years, and was so excited to go back. unfortunately we were disappointed. the waitress never brought us bread, so we had to ask the bus boy for it. the garlic bread was cold and stale, like it had been made days before. i ordered the ahi skewers with a "shepherd's" side salad. the salad only consisted of mixed greens, with a few cherry tomatoes tossed with a vinaigrette - very boring. the ahi was slightly overcooked and dry, but i did like the oak-grilled flavor. also came with rice which was quite oily. my husband had the tri-tip sandwich, which actually turned out to be sliced roast beef - weird! the rest of our guests said the food was ok, but not worthy of coming back. the young waitress seemed nice enough, but honestly she was terrible. we will NOT be going back, it is not nearly as good as it used to be!!!!!

Owner tends to let the place get pretty warm inside before closing the front door and turning on the AC. I can't imagine how the folks working there must feel...  If ya pull up on a warm day and see the front door open, well, you know what to expect.
Best food ever and so many selections. Pot roast is incredible! It is my go to place for good food. Wish their ToGo packaging was better though!
Food just arrived, entire meal was inedible. I never write reviews but felt it was necessary to write this one.

Great Service from Scott....dirty silverware all silverware 
Pizza ok would not call it wood grilled...maybe gas grilled

This review is for service only, not the food.  I love Blake's crushed ice...I know that's a strange thing to love, but it's true.  I am even willing to wait in the drive through line for just a soda!  And that's what I did yesterday, but wow, I wish I hadn't.  There was only one car in front of me, so it shouldn't have been that long of a wait.  Wrong!  After placing my order and then finally making it to the window (10 minutes), no one came to the window for another 5, and when they did, they had to ask me what I had ordered again.  When I told them, it took another 5 for them to make the soda and get it for me.  And another 3 to get my change.  Pretty ridiculous wait for a soda.  Get it together Blake's!

Went here on a weekend night after booking through open table. When we arrived they had no record of the Open Table reservation but were still able to sit us quickly. The place was full. Interesting though - I received an email from Open Table afterwards indicating the restaurant said we were no shows. 

Service: very friendly staff. Can't say enough. 

Food: DELICIOUS. One of the best meals we have had. The salad, meatballs, gnocchi, flatbreads, and cacciotore were fantastic. Every plate rocked. 

Price: $35 pp is probably too much for everything received. This is why it is a four star review and not a five star. My value rating (IMO): five stars here would probably be $25/30 from weekday/weekend service. 

Overall a great experience. We'll only go here once in awhile due to price rather than it being more regular. Check out the Station Taproom in Downingtown for a place that knows great food/service/value.

FYI - they do accept credit cards now.

So I live across the street and have ordered pick up a couple of times due to convenience.  EVERY time there seems to be a bunch of people "working" there, all doing nothing and barely acknowledge you when you come in.  Even if they say order will be ready in 30 min, and you come 30 min later to an empty, dingy takeout joint, they 1) totally ignore you, rudely going on with their conversation  2) did not start your order and give you no indication that they plan to start it soon.  I would say guesstimate double the wait time they say.  Also, got a large cheese pizza here last time, and half of the cheese was slid off the pizza, crust so thin and soggy that it had no structural integrity for the pieces that did have cheese- so unappetizing that I didn't eat it.

However:  shitty pizza and service aside, this place has REALLY good salads- full of delicious veggies and chicken and comes with 2 garlic knots- $9 chicken avocado salad lasts me 2 meals and the oriental sesame dressing is really good.  Also, mozzarella sticks were pretty good, but those are near impossible to mess up.
After alot of drinking and your body is in need of food , this place is a must , had the baked chicken with dirty rice and cold beet salad , comfort food,your body will feel better.....

We enjoyed our first breakfast here Saturday morning.  The service was good and the food was good too. 
We both had eggs over medium with home fries. Service was quick and they were not jammed. 
We are from New Jersey so diners are in our blood. We just enjoy the diner bibe. This certainly qualifies. 
They serve breakfast, lunch and dinner. But, they close at 3pm on Saturdays and Sundays.

ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE! We had a
Large Cuban, it's a total gut buster! This is the biggest Cuban I have ever been served. Granted, I did order a large, but still, I'm a big eater and this filled me up. The Rice and Beans with a meat (we had pork) is OUT OF THIS WORLD! The pork is some of the best I have ever had. We have a new favorite. We could have easily ordered just the Rice Beans and Meat, split it, and been fine.

I am only giving 3 stars because I expected more from the service because of the well-known name and higher dining prices.  The service wasn't great.  The food was just ok.  I ordered fish.  My date ordered duck.  The bread pudding was pretty good.  We wanted this to be a more romantic outing but it was extremely noisy that we didn't really talk much.  I'll probably try again at a quieter time maybe during the day or during the week.  I've been twice...both times on weekends.

Portion size is generous. Outdoor seating is nice. Waitress was attentive. Selection of mixed alcoholic drinks was good.

Fountain in outdoor patio was non-functional. I almost deducted a star.
Best sushi I've found in landlocked St. Louis. What better review could you want?
Great food.  Great service. Great view.  Only bad thing is those pesky bums harassing you on the way in for spare change. If they were all relocated to middle of ocean, this place would be heaven.

This was our first time in Zionsville. We drove around and thought the area was super cute.

This coffee shop/breakfast place has free WiFi (yay), GOOD strong coffee and some yummy cinnamon rolls. You order at the counter and seat yourself at any open table. 
I got the veggie quiche is comes with fruit and the hubby got a breakfast burrito with chipotle cream cheese. I liked that the quiche wasn't humongous and they had quite a few veggies. The fresh fruit cup was also really good (especially the pineapple). Overall a pretty cute place. Although this place has coffee and serves food they are pretty decent at both but not something unique I would drive all the way to Zionsville for. Its more of a if-i-am-in-the-area-i-will-stop-in kind of a place. I would give it 3.5 stars if I could.

I've been going here since introduced by co-workers in November of 1979, and we ALWAYS make a pilgrimage visit on every return visit to St Pete. Today, we once again proved that this is THE STANDARD for hamburgers, smoked fish, warm German potato salad and root beer. Comparing foods in most of the SE and NE of US, plus the Rockies and SW....everybody else comes up short.  Today was no exception....it's a wonderful thing when a restaurant focuses and delivers an excellent product, day after day, year after year.  Other fads and places may come and go; but, Ted Peters' is the best across the country, bar none!

Made a reservation 3 weeks in advance for Sunday Brunch. I requested seating near the fish tank. Received a call on Sat, at Noon to reconfirm my reservation. Arrived 10 minutes prior to 11:45 am reservation. Some confusion at the front desk, then promptly seated far away from the tank. Asked about moving closer to tank, as the place was mostly empty. Was told, "this is your table." Stephanie was our "server". No smile, no greeting, just a script of you either get juice or coffee with the buffet. Then she told us Plates are at the buffet and left. That was the extent of the service. Food is okay, but nothing special. Luke warm buffet line food. Would not recommend for $30 a person, or for $20 per person.

Go to see the aquarium, which you can do for free. Eat somewhere else. If you do eat there, tell Stephanie...well, just tell her Jim said Hello.

Room smells like cigarette smoke, Dog in room 505 or 504, barked all night, No towels, no room service in two days. Clogged up bathroom sink, with someone's hair Ana no toilet paper in bathroom... slow .. very slow elevators... Come on guys you can do better then this. The Super 8 is better then this.... very disappointing...

Again, a tip o' my hat to Kelly B. for bringing this new gem in my neighborhood to my attention. What we do without you, Kelly?

As for my review? OMFG. The best gyro, hands down, I've ever had. I was a Gyro Company devotee, but I'm going to have to write them a Dear John letter and break it off. First of all, it's so stuffed with goodies it looks like a small pipe bomb. The highlight, though, is the meat, which the owner informed me he makes himself. It is so tender, so flavorful, SO fucking good. Whatever is in the special lamb sauce is amazing. I also had the eggplant appetizer, and...wow. Just do yourself a favor and start off with this dish.

Those of you who love gyros, please take some time to try Sound Grand Gyro Express. You won't be disappointed.

Food looked good but we never got to try it. We were told by the manager when we went in that the kitchen was backed up, and they were not currently taking orders, so it would be a little but of a wait. This happens, and I totally get it, I've waited tables and understand the kitchen backs up. We sat down and were ignored for about 30 minutes. We finally stopped a waitress and asked if they were taking orders now, and if it would be possible to get some waters and some menus. She was very friendly. However, the manager came back out and very rudely asked us "did you understand when I said our kitchen was on a hold?" And walked away. We waited for about another 15 and no one approached us again, so we left. Went to Zoe's Kitchen and it was great.

I had super high hopes for this place. Would probably give a 3.5 star rating. Line was super long, but the food cane pretty quickly once ordered. The food was kind of dry and the flavors just didn't quite pop for me. The prices are decent so I wouldn't protest going there again to try something else, but probably not during rush hour.

I was here on a Saturday night and probably the oldest person in here. I had a salad which was really good. I also did a flight of beers and a flight of hard liquor. I had 2 bourbons and the 2 ryes. All the alcohol was quite good. I sat at the bar, so my service was great, I can't speak about table service. The one thing about the place is it is REALLY loud. Seemed like a lot of locals were in here, but it's definitely got the trendy hipster thing going. I'd definitely go back when I'm in town again.

Small, comfortable Puerto Rican restaurant in the Gulch area. Space / decor is minimal and bright. Try to snag one of the cozy semi-circular booths if you are able. Food was fresh and tasty. Lots of interesting choices. Plantain, spinach lasagne was amazing. Couldn't fully evaluate the Mofongo Relleno given a mashed plantain shortage, but the substitute (potato???) used  as the base was quite nice. Reasonable drink prices, friendly, attentive service despite a full house.
Great, really fresh seafood. This hole in the wall is attached to a seafood market. Only place I have been where you can get fresh blackened yellowfin tuna for 16 bucks.

Yum! I'm so happy we stopped here. 
Made a quick stop from tour de America to have lunch. I got the vegetarian burro (which was a big burrito) and I asked for potatoes in it. Oh man, so good! They're tortillas are homemade and so delicious. 
I'm constantly eating mexican food.  I think burritos should be apart of the main food groups. This place has one of the best burritos I have ever had. Ever. 
I also tried the horchata which I also really enjoyed. Not too sweet, not too watered down. 
The woman behind the counter was very helpful and willing to answer questions. 
If I lived in the area I would be here all the time!
I would rate this a 5 star, but usually I leave that up to consistency.

Being a Mass Ave resident, I have to tell any visitors that Chatham Tap is an absolute must. A great sports pub showing all major soccer (aka Euro Football) matches, great food, and a unique and eclectic beer selection - what more could you want? 

Pro Tip: Get.the.wings.

This diner is above the rest! Every time I have eaten there, we were always seated by a woman (possibly owner) who seems to love her job/people; she always has a smile on her face : )  The food is very good and prices are the norm for a diner. Will definitely eat there again. Oh and by the way, the beat Phily Diner in Runnemede by a long shot!
Chilled asparagus soup with whiskey and sage bread was superb. I loved the individual loaf of bread - it looked charming. Easy place to be on your own but not feel marooned.

My husband and I had dinner at Michaels and loved everything! The restaurant is quiet and cozy nice for date night or to relax. We ordered salmon and a shrimp pasta for dinner and my husband is still raving over how good the salmon was! So we will be going back for sure :)

Pumpkin seed salsa is fabulous.  Crab and shrimp empanada will give you sweet dreams. Puffed pastry filled with chocolate yummy!  Oh and my absolute favorite margarita..the tamarind margarita rimmed with pepper....taste like a sour patch kid!  YUMMY!

Definitely a fun atmosphere. There are few places in Exton where you can sit outside in a nice environment and not look directly at a parking lot. The games are fun as well. Despite the fact that they have a huge beer list, their choice of IPAs rarely corresponds with my taste and the food is not very good. With respect to the beer, I am impossibly fussy so I'll give them a pass but objectively the food needs work. Mostly I go for the atmosphere. Would give 3.5 stars if I could.

Awesome hotel for events, especially if you're a bunch of dudes, or a couple in town to party. If you insist on staying on Bourbon Street (as we did for my bachelor party), this is a great option. You're in the middle of it all, with classically trashy joints across the street as a bonus (if you're facing Bourbon): Stiletto's, etc.

The rooms are very nice (we had a suite on the third floor). The lobby and much of the hotel are elegant, well appointed, and pleasant to the nose...a contrast to and escape from the madness of Bourbon Street for those times you're looking for a break. If you get a room with a balcony, you'll feel like the King (or Queen, as it were) of Mardi Gras.

There's a nice pool area on the third floor. It gets full so come early if you want a chair. Bar service seemed spotty but we didn't really partake (mostly BYOB and going out). Internet was equally spotty, but that's life in the hotel. The sports bar/grill attached to the hotel, "Le Booze" (YES), had good food and drink specials, and I was able to watch the Euro in the comfort of American soccer apathy. Kermit Ruffins threw a party in the suite directly below us on 4th of July, which was pretty amazing.

Only cons I can think of were the front desk check-in service, which was agonizingly slow (that could have been a quirk); and the level of noise. If you're in New Orleans to catch Zzzzs, either get an inner-facing room, or consider other options. If you're here to "rage," on the other hand, you're in the right place.

Soon after arriving we were given bread and bruschetta. The bread was not my favorite because it didn't have any flavor. I ordered the rigatoni in vodka sauce, which was really delightful. It wasn't too creamy and I had more than enough for leftovers for the next day. The restaurant was a little loud making it harder to hear, but overall great place for a date night.

My husband and I have taken our young children to the Ardmore location twice within the past month. We love it! The ingredients are fresh and pizzas fully customizable. I have a gluten sensitivity and this is one of the only pizzerias that offers a GF crust that doesn't taste awful. The staff is nice, but twice now there has been a tall dark-skinned African American man who really has gone out of his way to be kind and engaging, and is especially sweet to my toddler son. He really goes above and beyond to make sure the customers are having a great experience and its that kind of person who will keep customers coming back time and time again. They don't wear name tags, otherwise I'd write his name! Anyway, hope this location stays open for many many years because we love it here!

Always refreshing to find vegan friendly restaurants with a variety of options for us veg-heads. Loved the fact that my friend and I were personally greeted by the owner of the restaurant who explained the concept of their food (clean eating without the extra sodium and other artificial additives-in other words,REAL food). I am looking forward to coming back to try some of the other menu items. I got the Buddha Satay Bowl with tofu and it had a nice spicy kick to it and great flavor.
Backyard Bowls has fresh, local ingredients and tasty smoothies. This is one of my favorite places in town for a light lunch.

I have always been enjoying hibachi at this place with large groups of friends. Today was my first time "seat at the table with a menu" dinner and it was an excellent one. The presentation, the food quality, very friendly staff. I highly recommend Sashimi Deluxe, Tokai Sashimi Salad, Roasted duck (and probably everything else on the menu). My mom for not being a big fan of spicy foods loved Curry Seafood combo. Will certainly be going back to To Kai.

I recently went to pita jungle with a good friend of mine for dinner. We were sat promptly and our server was very attentive and efficient, I believe her name was Lacy. We ordered the jalapeño cilantro hummus for an appetizer and the flavor was amazing; however the pita bread was sub par, definitely not homemade. My friend ordered the portabella burger and raved about how delicious it was. I had the vegetable ginger stir fry with tofu and the tofu was definitely the best cooked tofu I have had at a restaurant. The manager (tall dark haired guy) came by the table and asked us how everything was and refilled our drinks, which I thought was a nice touch to the experience! All in all I would definitely recommend pita jungle for people looking for fresh food, especially vegetarians!

Decided to watch the Lightning hockey game at Brick House. First off, if you are looking for a place to watch all the sports you want, this is it!!! They have TVs everywhere and a variety of seating options indoor and outdoor. The bar is really nice, being half indoors and half outdoors (with a roof over). To top off the great atmosphere, our server Caitlyn was just phenomenal. 

We chose where we wanted to be seated and started off with the pretzel appetizer.  I am a huge sauce person, loving to try all and any different sauces. The photo of the pretzel shows the dips that come with it (queso, siracha ranch, and yellow mustard). Our server went above and beyond giving us a variety of the other sauces they have for other menu items. Our entrees came out in a timely manner and was exactly what we wanted. Being a picky eater myself, I ordered a salad and asked for a few additions which I received with no extra charge. The chicken sandwich was tender and juicy, and how can you go wrong with some bacon added?! Instead of the traditional sides, we chose the apple cider slaw for a little bit of health. Lastly we got a few Togo boxes for what we didn't finish and the server brought out little togo containers with all the different sauces. 

Service and food was excellent! Definitely will be going back soon!

Update: went back the other day and they no longer have the special fries on the menu at all and they changed a lot of the menu. They say it is because they change the menu seasonally. A restaurant called Fries Rebellion and you took the fries off the menu? They were still able to kind of make the Smack fries by putting the garlic parmesan wing sauce on fries which we really appreciated but come on now.

The other food was good. Burger was awesome. Onion soup was great but served in the world's smallest crock. Pepperoni/prosciutto grilled cheese was a lot of salty too thick cut meats. Crab soup was not bad but a little thin. Wish they hadn't made so many changes...

Kitschy bright colors, tiny room with lots of tables, and awesome Early Bird specials that include appetizer, salad, and entree in smaller portions, which is wonderful. They are not uptight and are happy to let you get in on them, even when the time for specials is almost over. 

Vegetarian menu is helpful. though I had to send back my coconut soup after finding a big piece of chicken in it.  So stir around first! :-)  I loved how finely they shredded the cabbage peanut salad, and the dressing was excellent.  His mock duck came with a ton of the seitan, when they sometimes skimp on it at other places.

Inexpensive, and we will be back when we are in town.  They seem to welcome BYOB though we did not bring anything.

Walked in on a Saturday afternoon and the aroma of the spices hit me immediately - a perfect succulent blend of scents. The buffet is two tables and a bit larger than your standard buffet. The spiced chicken was to die for. The palak paneer standard, but good. Butter chicken tasted like butter chicken (I'm not a huge fan of this dish). The goat curry was good but maybe a smidge more grease than I prefer. Channa masala was good. Everything was good and surprisingly with a kick of spice! Way spicier than your standard Indian buffet! I both liked and disliked that the naan is provided to you per table - it was fresher this way but less convenient (wait time wasn't terribly long, but one does not go to a buffet to wait!). Disappointed that the naan was of the thinner variety, which was prone to one order being more crispy rather than soft delicious bread. 

Make sure you get the $1.00 coupon from Indy coupons. The final cost was still $10.99, which is maybe standard for a Saturday but also more than I prefer (but hey, that's Carmel for you).

Location sucks right now because of construction, so make sure you go via N Illinois rather than Meridian!

Staff was not friendly but adequate-good in getting my dishes and water. I'd say thank you and sometimes they smiled or nodded. But many walked around with a curt expression.

We tried this place because of the Yelp reviews while visiting Nashville. The hot chicken was really good! The tapas were good. The strawberry swirl margarita was very good.  We tried the brussel sprouts at the request of our server who offered to take them off the bill if we didn't like them. We loved them! Neither of us even eat brussel sprouts. I don't know what kind of magic they cooked up with these things, but they were tasty! All in all it was a really good experience to start our Nashville adventure.

Best Italian in St. Louis for my money!  Visited for the first time over the weekend with my wife, son and parents-in-law.  The food is great but the service is incredible.

I can't speak enough about the service.  Every staff member was incredibly friendly, pleasant, professional and seemed to genuinely enjoy their jobs.  We brought my two-year-old son based on some reviews on Yelp that said it was a restaurant for all ages.  They were very accommodating.  They had a high chair waiting for us and provided him some crayons.

We ordered the toasted ravs for an appetizer.  These rank up there with some of the best I've had.  I ordered the spinach and prosciutto pizza.  My wife had the cannolli.  The PILs ordered the Straw and Hay and the Chocolate Fettuccine and a house salad.

Everyone raved about their food.  Naturally, as an Italian restaurant, they gave us more food than we could eat.  Another nice touch was the dinner rolls with hummus rather than the traditional olive oil or butter.

I love this place and probably can't eat Italian food anywhere else in town.

Okay, how to begin this... yes, it is worth the wait. It really is. I've been here three times, and I remember my eyes watering the first time because their pancakes are SO. FKN. DELICIOUS. So far I've tried the blueberry pancakes, the Smokey Mountains-pancakes and the Banana Bread-pancakes; the blueberry ones being my favorite (yes, that was the time I almost cried because it was so good). 

Not only is the food great, but the staff is amazing. Extremely friendly, professional and helpful; special requests is not a problem at all, and they've never mixed up anything.

Also, I love the atmosphere of this place; it's very simple but genuine; it's simply cool without trying to be cool. 

So, overall; yes, it is worth the wait.
worst resturant in the whole planet earth!!!!!!!!!!!!!!please stay away not even worth one star! found a huge cockroach in my food!

This is where I will be getting my bbq in the area, now that my favorite place has closed.  While I have had better pulled pork, it has rarely been this good in the area.  None of the food was smokey, but the pork fell apart, as did the ribs.  The collard greens were terrific (and I have heard these are difficult to prepare).  The cole slaw was pretty good, nothing spectacular.  Corn bread was not very good (full disclosure: I like my corn bread sweet and this was not).  

The service was good enough for me and was efficient.  My friend thought the water tasted funny, though I couldn't tell.  

They have a full bar, which we did not utilize.  This place looks like it would be fun to go for dinner and stick around for drinks.  I heard they have live music.

Good sized New York style slices for a reasonable price. Cheese starts at $3.50 and additional toppings are .50 extra. Lots of indoor seating, and open late for the after bar crews. Definitely the cheapest and probably only late night pizza place here in SB. Pretty good, will go back.

I'm usually skeptical when a restaurant is new and only has a few reviews, but figured I'd give Wise Guy's a shot.

I was not disappointed. Wise Guy's is good cheap and bad for you comfort food type of joint.

I got the Philly cheese steak. It was pretty good. Not a tops in Philly spot, but up their at the top of the regular Joe's spots.

I also got the Wise Guys fries. They are good fries. Then addition of melted American and cheese wiz made it better. A lot of it was on the bottom through. They could have done a better job melting it on top. The jalapeno peppers were nice. The bacon, to my surprise, was two whole strips of tasty bacon. As nice as fresh strips are, I actually wish it was more of an in bits type of deal. It's kind of hard to eat the whole bacon with the fries.

I also got the mac n cheese bites. These could do no wrong. The worst thing about them, there were not enough. And, they could have been bigger. But mac n cheese baked inside fried bread crumbs is heaven.

There's lots of good looking items on their "I don't know what to choose" menu. So much that looks good, and makes you feel just a little guilty eating.

But hey, we all need a little guilty pleasure in our lives.

Update: I had to drop Wise Guys to three stars (from four) after having their pizza. I have no idea what those talking their pizza up are talking about. I'm a New Yorker, so perhaps I am a little more picky. But, it was passable at best. I do not recommend it. You want pizza, go to Colonial.

Update 2: So, it turns out the pizza wasn't as bad as it seemed. The problem was it was under cooked. When I reheated the pizza and made sure it was well done, it was actually pretty tasty. Still no Colonial, but not bad by any means.

Placed a phone order for pick up; Jefferson's burger. This is the sad looking item I found when I got back to my office.
No cheese, two strips and barely a squirt.
Menu clearly states this item should come w/American cheese and I did not opt out.
Temp was lukewarm at best. 
Extremely disappointed.
Attached image to backup my review.

Service here is good and very attentive. They gave me input on what was good and what was not.

The pho was delicious with no msg. Jasmine tea was very refreshing as well. 

Owner came out and spent some time w us giving us insight on top tourist destinations in the area. 

Very friendly staff, good food, affordable prices.

This place is great to locate good, hard-to-find beers. Beware that picking out a random 6-pack will probably run you $30-40. However, sticking with the basics like Dale's Pale Ale or Old Chub will only run you about $14. Overall, it's an easy and convenience location for grabbing a quick pack of brewskies!

Easily the best Indian restaurant in Nashville.  I've tried almost all of them.  I've always been leery of suggesting curry restaurants to friends, but I've finally found a place that is so good, my British friends have said it's better than many curry houses in London.  And that is saying a lot!  Give this place a shot.  A bit hard to find, behind Patel Bros Indian grocer.  Every dish we had was perfectly spiced, and the dosa was great!  Oddly, they only have bottles of water to offer for refreshment, but that only enhances the mom and pop feel.  The coffee and chai (which are the only other beverages) are incredible.  They only have one dessert, a fried ice cream, but it is delicious.  Our waiter said their focus is on village dishes.  We ordered one of the specials of day, and were rewarded.


Sorry for the brevity of this post, I typed it on my iPhone.  Stop reading and go get a curry!
Food was so good! Great music, good casual or event atmosphere. Came here for a group birthday dinner. Their white sangria was amazing
Friendly service, great food. New to the neighborhood, everyone should try this local business !!

Been to Broadripple Brew Pub many times. This place is always packed! There is usually a wait, but its totally worth it. Its a traditional Irish Pub with a twist. They have many typical Irish dishes, but also have pizza and other options as well. You HAVE to try the scottish eggs. They are probably the best Ive ever had! 

Prices are reasonable, atmosphere is great, service is usually pretty good. We had an issue with our server the last time we were there, she obviously did not want to be there. Other than that its typically been a great experience.

BYOB, $10 corking fee. They accept credit card. Pretty sure its the same owner as Banana Leaf because both places are really similar. Large amount of seating and really big menu. Good mix of Malaysian, Chinese, and Thai. I think one of the most hyped things here is their Roti Canai, which reminds me of a really light Chinese pancake served with a curry for dipping. In addition, their tom yum soup is really solid, and offers a nice bit of spice for your meal. Chow Kueh Teow was like a seafood Chow Fun, and super tasty. Really great family-style restaurant. Fast seating and solid food.

I really thought about it before giving Puckett's 5 stars.  Surely there must be something to subtract a star.  Nope, the only complaint I have about Puckett's is that sometimes you can't go there when you want to because of a show and they are only taking reservations.  The food has never disappointed. The servers are friendly, although sometimes they are just too darn busy.  We take most out of town guests to Puckett's and they always want to go back.  It's perfect for breakfast, the BBQ is underrated...soooooo good, delicious salads, fried chicken to die for and you can also just sit outside and nurse a beer over some amazing fried green beans!  

One night we sat and listened to Don Schlitz perform and my husband said, "We are so spoiled." He's right...Puckett's is a treasure and we are so lucky to have such a great place.  Haven't checked out the Nashville location yet, I hope it's as good as Franklin's.

Enjoyed a great dinner at the bar on a cold February night. Fantastic atmosphere, great wine counsel by the bartender. The dinner was great and met a few locals who seem to be regulars - always a good sign! The decor is a spirited blend of over the top Madonna Inn, English pub, and holiday event.  Will definitely go back!

20 minutes and we still hadn't received our food. There were no other customers before us. It was only 2 beef tacos, a chicken sandwich and a burger...we asked for a refund and they gave us attitude but I seriously doubt they would wait that long for "fast food". Ive been served faster at sit down restaurants!

An awesome addition to the neighborhood. Love the seating outside .. but more importantly, love the bibimbap (especially in the stone bowl). I've been a few times now, and I just can't bring myself to order anything else!

Let me first start by saying this is my first ever Yelp review and I am only writing this because: THIS.PLACE.IS.AWESOME.

The food is fresh, unique combinations, and you can tell its made with love. The owner is very welcoming and is willing to accommodate specific tastes. If you are in the area, or not, definitely make it a point to try this place. 100% recommended!
