The first time I visited some recommended the Pork Milanesa Cemita and I have never ordered anything else.  It is basically a Mexican version of the fried tenderloin with a egg and other goodies.  My wife has ordered every taco and she loves each one.

Note:  Take a look at the pictures of the menu because items on the lunch menu are not on the dinner menu and vice versa.

Father's Day Brunch, this place was close to my hotel and not too packed for a big holiday.

Waitress at front asked me how she could help instead of how many in my party. Before I could ask her what else they offer besides food and drinks, her coworker saved her and took over. Quickly seated, ordered Haphazard drink from cocktail menu. 

Had shrimp & cheese grits. The grits are really cheesy, so much so you can't eat them without cutting the strings of cheese. The shrimp, sausage, onion gravy mix that it's covered in is VERY tasty and flavorful. The grits are bland but it works with the shrimp.

I liked it and will return. Service was good too.

This place needs to get it together! Ice cream machine is always "out of order" has happened at least 5 times. The worse part is getting stuck in the drive through just to find out the machine is broken again. Not going here again !

Mostly kids working that don't care about service. We waited over an hour for our pizza.  When we finally got it the pizza and potatoes were cold. The place is loud and full of drunks on a Saturday night. If you want to get drunk and eat cold pizza its a great place. I won't go back.

Love this place! Great Chinese and Japanese takeout.

It is consistent & reasonably priced.

Food quality very good and fast for take out.

Great experience to lighten up a cold-rainy day in New Orleans. 

We came in on a Saturday afternoon and were seated in less than 5 minutes. Our server was kind and attentive and the waitstaff were accommodating. 

I ordered the crawfish beignet with jalapeno aoili and a side caesar salad. The beignet was hot oozing with gooey cheese and warmed up my day. To drink decided to mix things up with an adult Arnold Palmer. I asked for regular jack instead of vodka but to my surprise, honey jack was added which made it my new favorite drink. 

The establishment itself has a pretty cozy fit which mainly allows for smaller parties in the front. I did not make it upstairs but there is upstairs seating. 

All in all this hidden gem is a great place to experience what New Orleans has to offer.

A must while in Nashville! Get there early to avoid long line! Staff very friendly. Food was delicious! I got the old fashioned pancakes with a side of bacon and eggs. My fiancé got the apple walnut pancakes with a side of hash browns and bacon. All very delicious and it's worth the wait if there's a line!!! Highly recommend and will return when in Nashville again!

So far the best tasting pizza place Ive found since I moved to AZ. The flavor, the cheese, the meats, all complement one another well. The crust is good also, however I was wondering if this place offers a thin crust because I would definitely like to try that out. I'm from CA and yea I'm a Straw Hat fan with their thinner crust but the similarities overall made me happier then a fat kid at hometown buffet in the dessert section  jk.  But I would highly recommend this place
Everything was delicious!!  Generous servings!  Delicious homemade pasta. Anthony took great care of us!!
Best guac ever!!! Love this spot I come here all the time. Really good happy hour too.

Even though UF isn't where I went to school, I do live in Florida and see zero problem with a Florida business supporting a Florida university. In fact, Gators is one of the Tampa Bay area's classic beach spots everyone should visit. Sure, it's a little touristy at times, but this is the nation's tourism capital after all so what do we expect!? The bottom line is that the food at Gators is far better than the typical beach bar/restaurant and you can't beat the location/view/access. It's a great place to go just for drinks too since they have good live bands and other events on a regular basis.
Solid 4 start. Amazing bread. Good concept. Fast and tasty. I will go again. Their bowl is quite filling. Chicken is very tasty.

The ambiance was fantastic, the food was delicious. The service was great. The reason for the 4 stars is because, when they served the appetizers they did not give us plates or serving spoons. I thought maybe this was an oversight but we ordered 3 appetizers and they did it all 3 times. Please pay attention to this.

Have you ever gone to a restaurant, place your order and wonder whether or not what you just did was a good idea? Well, it happened to me at this place. Actually, it was after I used the restroom that I became concerned and questioned my decision.

Before I go further I should explain I (obviously) survived to tell the tale. :)

See, this used to be a Church's Fried Chicken restaurant. Therefore you can expect it to be a little run down. However, it appears they kept the old greasy everything for posterity. The walls and floors are covered in grease. There's grease on the plumbing at the urinal for the love of all that's holy. My guess is they moved in and didn't even clean the place.  How it passes inspection is beyond me. As they say, if you want to know how clean a restaurant is look at the bathroom. 

The people were very nice.  I showed up about 20 minutes before closing and ordered food to go. I learned something in that they premake their fried rice. I suppose they add the meat or whatever to it as they go, but they were all out so I had to go with white rice. Of course, it was bland as you'd expect.

I ordered sesame chicken but there was hardly any sauce and no sesame.  So, it was deep fried chicken nuggets with a little sauce. The portion was large so you get a fair amount at a decent price. The flavor of the sauce was OK but the meat itself is questionable. Every restaurant buys breaded nuggets so this place isn't unique. The chicken, though, didn't seem right. It was cooked thoroughly but seemed off like it was perhaps pressed something or the other. 

The crab Rangoon that came with it was inedible. They tasted of old grease, we're dry as a bone and definitely not a good choice. Maybe it's because it was the end of the night, I don't know. But they were horrible. Sorry folks. Skip these mm if you go here.

Perhaps my experience was an anomaly. Others seem to enjoy it. Maybe I've become spoiled or expect too much. I don't think so. A clean restaurant is expected at any cost. This place doesn't even come close. 

Don't take my word on it. Try for yourself. Who knows, it could be the best experience you've had.
Unbelievable food.  Best I've ever had and it's always almost empty.  Sure the ambiance isn't great, but oh the food is so amazing!!
Food was delicious!! The wait staff seemed a little confused but all in all, it was a good experience.

Not bad! I got a burrito with salmon and it was a yummy, salty mix of flavors. Sushi burritos have a collapsability about them that makes eating them a bit more challenging, which I find entertaining. 

The burrito a rather underwhelming size (compared to the giant logs of food you get from regular burrito places) and the flavor of the fish didn't blow me away (compared to the flavors you might experience at a serious sushi place, or an expensive piece you get from a good grocery store). 

It was acceptable and satiating, but it felt like most of my taste bud reactions were coming from how they spiced and/or marinated their ingredients, rather than the freshness of the ingredients themselves. For the $10+ price, which made me feel like I was splurging a bit on an extra-exotic burrito, it didn't feel like I got much more food value than a regular burrito. 

However, I had a really nice server ! It's always interesting when the people are both charismatic and attentive. Their bowls looked larger and more impressive, so I'll see how their bowls are next time!

One of those unexpected local restaurants you always hope to find. Great staff, ambiance and menu. Creative and unusual food combinations (the filet may be the best I've had. ever). The restaurant was full and the rooms are fairly open but surprisingly quiet enough for conversation. We'll be back

We found this place by searching yelp and it definitely is a good place to eat. We come here for breakfast all the time. We either eat in or get it to go. They always have specials. We've been here for dinner once and it was delicious! I got stuffed tilapia with crab meat and it was amazing! And only $10.50! The food always comes quickly so you're never waiting long for your food which is great when you go in there starving! It's decent pricing. Also, nothing too crazy here with the menus so Iif you're looking for a good home cooked meal This is definitely the place to go. All around its a good place! Definitely check it out!

Perfect place to watch the sunset over Philly. R2L is on the 37th floor with 2 sides of glass windows. There view is on West Philly where you can see the Schuylkill River, Penn/Drexel and University City and beyond. On the south side, you can see the Delaware River and beyond.

We only had drinks there so not much to comment on the quality. The beer was cold and was 5 bucks.

Service: the service was great. The server was very polite, had a smile on her face all the time and always catered to photo requests by the patrons. Well done management and staff.
Bagels are okay a bit expensive but the sandwiches choices are really good!! Sure wish they had gluten free

I was looking for something different for lunch in the Old City area.  Let's say, I should have stuck with my cheesesteak wrap from Gianfrancos!  I found them on Grubhub and it sounded great!  I ordered a buffalo chicken wrap which had a "*" next to it indicating it was a restaurant favorite.  It also came with french fries.  Once you added the tip on, it ended up costing me $14 for delivery.  It arrived in fairly good time, but I am not sure when the french fries were hot, it was long before they arrived here.  They looked like had they been fresh, they would have tasted good, but they were cold and hard.  The wrap itself was so far from what I was hoping for.  When ordering, it gives you the option of hot or mild sauce.  I chose mild.  I cannot imagine what the hot choice was like since the mild made my mouth feel on fire!  It says it contains blue cheese and I requested extra blue cheese.  I got one small 1oz soufle cup, none was inside the wrap as I was anticpating.  This was about enough for 1/2 of 1/2 of the wrap.  I was definitely disappointed!

We went there after making a reservation for two. The menu does not have a lot of variety and the food is mediocre. I had high hopes but it did not meet my expectations. Service was good overall along with good ambiance.

I wish I could exaggerate the quality of food but I cannot the food tasted fresh and came out very swiftly I kept staring at the table next to me with this gigantic plate of pancakes... The waitress quickly informed me that most of their food is larger than normal.... The wait wasn't long they get very busy but handle it well if your impatient you can join the wait less on Yelp or call in advance

This food is dam good.  The sliders were amazing. I recommend getting the brown bag special (two sliders, fries and homemade soda). If you have a small appetite consider sharing.  Don't let the size of the sliders fool you they are filling. And don't you dare go without getting a donut.  They're the best donuts in New Orleans.

I used to travel to Japan 4 times a year and really love all the different styles of Japanese food. Sadly Reno is know for all you can eat sushi which  just based on economics drives down quality.  Japan is all about quality over quantity,  presentation and experience rule the day.   Enter Kauboi Izakaya - it's pushing the envelope in Reno's growing food scene.  

I love the creativity of the food, the flavors were spot on and the service was top notch.   We had the Poke which was the best in Reno IMO.  Sure it's a small portion for the money but again quality over quantity.  The spicy shrimp gyoza was amazing as was the pork Raman.  The Giant Squid was giant and squid, it was good but I reminded again that I am not a fan of squid regardless of how It's prepared.  
The bottom line is this is a great restaurant that is pushing the creative boundaries in Reno. It's not your cheapest option in town and it shouldn't be.  (In Japan it would have 3x the price.   ). My only suggestion is they stock the bar with different Japanese Shochu's and it will be like I am back in Tokyo.

I think capital beer is pretty ok to me. I dont have any complaints other than maybe price but that doesnt really bother me that much with this place. Ill go here once a week or anytime im craving sushi its always pretty good. Chinese food is standard. Great beer selection take your pick.

Wait here for lunch during the week Between Christmas and New Years with 6 elementary age Girl Scouts (!!).  Nonwait, great service and the server named Nico was very patient with the 6 Scouts... answering questions, bringing extra sauces, etc.  all 6 Scouts had ice cream and proclaimed Baileys Range to be their new favorite place.  This moms burger was delicious too.  Thx!
We got takeout from there tonight - a small pizza and some sides. We picked up the order and brought it home. The pizza was still piping hot and very tasty. Everything was great!

Having visited New Orleans several times, I've had the pleasure of many superb meals. Cafe Reconcile is no exception to excellence in dining. In fact, I had the best shrimp étouffée, while in NOLA and THE best peach cobbler anywhere. Ever. 
The atmosphere is warm, friendly and very welcoming. The staff were so friendly, folks you could talk to. 
I strongly support the concept of this cafe and wish it every success. I know I'll do my part to spread word about an absolutely outstanding cafe and will make a point of coming back for seconds. I may just have to swing by for more cobbler on the way home.

I ended up at this place because the "not-to-be-named-famous-restaurant-down-the-street" was too busy to wait. Squeal was almost closing but their friendly staff made room for two visiting Floridians. 

The service was great and beer selection surprising. In addition to the meats we tried the bacon Mac and cheese, and greens and certainly left satisfied. I was disappointed that the bacon brownie was not available, but I guess that's what happens when you show up late to the party.

The food here was not bad - probably better than most of the Japanese restaurants in Edmonton. However, I've never been kicked out of a restaurant. My friend and I came here for lunch recently and after our meal were just talking and catching up when at around 1:30pm were told they are locking the doors and asked us to leave. We weren't there for that long, probably just under an hour.  Ive never been to a restaurant that has kicked me out before and it's not like we were lingerers, we had just paid when the waitress came back and told us to pack up.  Anyways, that just tainted the experience for me and I won't be going back.

Just average. My wife and I were one of two occupied tables on the night we visited. The food was OK but nothing special. The prices were along the lines of Lil' Abners and Daisy Maes which ARE good steak houses. The staff seem pretty uninterested as a whole. Service was slow even though there was only one other table besides ours. I had expected better for the price paid.

Being from NY I was excited to see this place come to Hendersonville, and it is one of the few with close to NY style pizza, however as a single parent of a college student, like in NY, they had single slices! Apparently not anymore, so after this became my after work destination for the comforts of NY, I longer have a reason to come. Lots of NY style downtown that still
sells slices.

I went here with my boyfriend after a doctor appointment, we were both feeling a little blah after sitting in the hospital for so long and we were starving. This place sure did satisfy our hunger! We both ordered chili and a salad from the menu and we were able to pick our own toppings. The owner was so nice, he gave my boyfriend a free hat for it being our first time! We will definitely be back for more :)

I've been watching the remodel of this place that used to be Carrow's.  Wondered what was going in.  Stopped in to see what was different.  The inside was completely redone.  It's kind of a cross between sports bar, restaurant, and lounge.  There was a lot going on, but service was excellent.  I had the Saratoga Chicken Club, it was excellent.  Fresh chicken, lettuce, tomatoes and just the right amount of mayo on toast.  My daughter had the half pound combo.  She got it with veggies and tots.  She was in heaven.  I got another half pound combo to go which was enjoyed at home.  The to go order was brought just as we finished dinner.  Tried the mac and cheese and beans for the two sides.  When we got home had to check out the sides and the mac and cheese was the kind you'd make at home from scratch, oh so good and the baked beans had so much flavor, a favorite.  At the restaurant had to try the lemon meringue pie.  Oh mercy, the flavor was wonder with a light crust.  Nice way to end a fantastic diner.  I enjoy hot tea with my dinner and a refill was brought just as I finished my first cup with out having to ask.  Really enjoy the atmosphere, staff, and food.  Will be back.

My guy and I were looking for a BYOB and boy did we are great place. We were greeted by a friendly face and was seated immediately.  This place is small but big on flavor.  The duck fries were to die for. My Guy had the steak stir fry and he said it was delicious.  We definitely will be coming back
Delicious food, fast and very friendly service.  Just good people.  One of my favorites in town.
I really don't have too much to say about this place other than ALL their food is deliciously amazing. it's where I order from every time I order. Delivery is not that long of a wait either.

Seemed like a decent enough place while in town for business. I was interested in the Reuben but didn't come across any reviews, glad I tried this one. Most places make below average versions with either too much flavorless meat or not enough sauce, sauerkraut and soggy bread. Everything was good about this reuben from the crunchy rye bread to the cheese, possibly the best I've had.
Although it was enough for me the serving of coleslaw was quite small.
$2 taco Tuesday is amazing. We were in a hurry unfortunately and our bartender was so accommodating and friendly.  I'll definitely o back when I have more time!

What can I say but, "Outstanding".  We happened upon Chase while driving down State Street in Santa Barbara.  My husband liked the "look" of the restaurant (not our typical criteria for restaurant selection).  It reminded me of those mahogany and leather high-end restaurants of old... which somehow managed to be very comfortable and inviting.  The decor: large leather banquettes and contemporary chairs, giant mirrors, grape vines sporting tiny, Italian, white lights hanging from the ceiling and an odd collection of "sculptures" with fresh roses on each table.  The restaurant was impeccably clean.

But let's talk about the FOOD!  Fresh bread was served with butter and freshly grated parmesan cheese.  While we waited for our entrees', the waiter brought us a tasting of their white beans (fabulous) and cabbage cooked in a spicy tomato sauce (yum).  

My husband ordered the spaghetti and meatballs.  Very tasty, very Italian, very plentiful.  The homemade Italian dressing on the salad was to die for.

I ordered their homemade ravioli appetizer (giant ravioli stuffed with cheese and fried to the perfect crispness) and Insalata Caprese (Buffalo Mozzarella with tomato slices and fresh basil drizzled with a wonderful Balsamic Vinegar).  Caprese is my favorite salad, and this one did not disappoint.  

By the way, service was incredibly attentive (even bringing us fresh bread plates when our entrees' arrived).  I wish we were staying longer in Santa Barbara... I'd like to work my way down their menu!
No free drink refills. There are many other options in the food court. This is a bad business decision.

If I could give no stars I would!! Last night, I was party of a group of people who were coming from a wedding. There were approximately 50 or more people in my party! We had a number of people who were turned away because they either did not have IDs or  IDs that could not be scanned. I would understand this if the persons age was in question! Why a 60 year old women was turned away, the mother of the groom and other assorted people is beyond me! The men at the door were rude and disrespectful to us! Very unprofessional. My husband who is in law enforcement also was told his id was no good! By the way he is 56 years old! 
Most of the party left! I guess this could be referred to as a "kid" bar! We thought this would be a great place to go since the local university was not in session yet! I hope it was worth it Kelly's!!  We won't be returning!

My husband and I set a course for Cold Spring Tavern on a Sunday afternoon to kick off a week long road trip. As we approached the tavern there were so many people there that we had to pass it up. On our way back through the area the following Thursday at 5 pm we decided to give it another try. We lucked out. Now there were all of 15 people there so there was no wait. Service was fast and friendly. My husband had the famous tri tip sandwich and I had the pork ribs. Both were messy and delicious. Pick the right time to visit and you won't be disappointed.

5 star review for their brunch! We came here at 11:30 AM with a group of 12 and were promptly seated.  We couldn't decide what to order so we shared one of each of the small plates. Let me tell you everything was AMAZING and had such unique flavors I had never had before. I think their menu changes seasonally but when we went we had avocado toast, zucchini fritters, chilled shrimp, and everything bagel.  

For the large plates we split the goat bolognese (MUST GET!), coconut French toast, biscuits and gravy, and black bean avocado eggs. I had their Compere Lapin mimosa which was really good, I would rarely say worth the $12 price but this one was very much worthy.

When you want to experience real Greek food come here. They are famous for their desert case.
This place is located right in the heart of Tarpon Springs, a little Greek community.

The service here is awful and the food is even worse. I took my grandmother for her birthday and none of the employees acknowledged us for 20 minutes. After that it took another half an hour before we were brought our food (which was cold). No one said anything about how long our wait was, no apology and no explanation. When the check came there was a mysterious 10% off however I would have much preferred a simple explanation for why the service was so awful.

I used to visit SATCO more regularly when I lived in Nashville, but now that I live in Franklin, I don't go out of my way to eat here unless meeting up with a friend. Decent food at a decent price. A great place to hang on the patio on a nice day.

Pro's: Large patio, good location, ability to customize your order (i.e. "build your own taco" with the sheets where you circle the meat and toppings you want), line moves fairly quickly.

Con's: Food can be hit or miss

I've been here three times and have had three poor experiences. Once it took twenty minutes for a cheeseburger. Another time the pizza was cold when I got it, and the last time I called a few times with no answer, then drive there to see employees sitting at the tables. When I walked in they said their equipment was broken.

SB Shellfish Company is a cute little restaurant at the end of the pier that offers both inside and outside seating.  When we arrived (Saturday afternoon) the waiting list was 3 pages long; thankfully it moved quickly and was WELL WORTH THE WAIT.  The staff was very friendly and helpful in deciding what wonderful items on the menu we should order (thanks Sean)!  We ordered chowder, crab cocktail, & fried calamari.  Each entree came with to die for onion rings which were incredibly light and fluffy and I could have sworn had a slight coconut flavor.  YUM!  To complete our meals and satisfy our thirst the boys had a local beer on tap and I had a Spicy Bloody Mary.  The meal was absolutely spectacular.  The only reason why I gave the restaurant 4 out of 5 stars is because the indoor seating is quite cramped, I literally played elbow wars with the patrons sitting on each side of me throughout the entire meal.  However, the seating didn't ruin my experience and next time we are in town we will definitely be dining at SB Shellfish Co.
Pretty good food and drinks, would definitely recommend.....and I guess they deliver........,

Sunday - April 28, 2013 - 10:30 AM

I'm an evolving carnivore.  Non-meat options are gradually finding their way into my diet.  I've always enjoyed fruits and vegetables but, meat has always been a staple.

 I've heard mainly positive remarks and the promise of a Sunny Sunday prompted this suburbanite to venture into the city. HipCityVeg is a small store within a minute walk from Rittenhouse Square.

I was immediately greeted by a cheerful 20 something that eagerly described some of the customer favorites.  She recommended the $9.00 Udon Noodle Salad (Chinese black bean dressing, sprouts, arugula, carrots, cabbage, daikon, peanuts, & spicy glazed "chick'n").  My eyes transfixed to an oddly written drink - The $4.50 Groothie (green smoothie with organic apples, organic leafy greens, bananas, & seasonal fruit).  I ordered same.

The Udon Noodle Salad was very good but, was suspicious of the so-called chick'n.  Why?  It tasted like grilled chicken but, in fact, is soy and organic grains cooked on a hot stove.  The Groothie was refreshing and flavorful.  

I won't wait for another Sunny Sunday to enjoy HipCityVeg.

I just had my 45th birthday party at Marmont last night and I couldn't have been more pleased. Let me start with booking the event, Dave (the owner) was as easy as pie to work with, he helped me with every little detail. I'm a little picky, but he was patient as could be.

Casey, helped me create a custom martini as the drink special for my party,he concocted a delectable coconut, cherry, lime martini and my guest simply loved them, let me tell you Leah-tini's are delicious! Ask for one.

The food was simply incredible! My guests feasted on three courses of hot appetizers, we had jumbo garlic fried shrimp (to die for!), calamari with jalepenos (crisp, crunchy, full of flavor), steak spring rolls (beefy, cheesy, yummy), cheese fries and Dave was nice enough to add spicy buffalo wings to my party food menu for the night. Some of my guest ordered other items as well, the crab cakes got rave reviews!

The DJ kept us dancing all night with a combination of dance music, pop music and selections from a playlist I gave to Dave, I danced almost the entire night!

Most importantly the staff was the nicest most attentive people ever, the wait staff was always smiling, full of personality and eager to please. The bar staff never had anyone wait longer than a few seconds to place thier drink order. Even the security guard was nice (big dude-I wouldn't mess with him!) but he was very kind and cordial the entire night.

You know you can have great ambiance, food and music but if the staff isn't up to par it can ruin a night. I was so lucky to have these people here catering to my guests.

This was an important birthday for me, Thank you Marmont for making it special.

Melt in your mouth good. Friendly staff. Solid for this area and great price point for take out. I've never eaten in, but that's OK.  Get your sushi from Temaki, and oh yeah...tell 'em big Texas sent you.

My mother, who is 82 years old, had been here several times and raved about the food that in her words was "delicious." We finally all went together and she is right. We got the fried green tomatoes. That has never been a favorite of mine, but they had a GREAT light breading on it that sold me. I ordered the Smoke burger. It was a very good sandwich. My only complaint, if it can be called that, was that the burger was so juicy it had to be finished off using a fork because it got messy. It was a really big burger too. The prices aren't terrible. Not dollar menu pricing, but who wants that? Everyone on the staff was very attentive and always smiling. I am sure I will be back again and again.

Amazing bloody Mary! The entire menu looked delicious and I wish I could have tried it all! The atmosphere was spot on for a New Orleans breakfast, and the staff was friendly and inviting. Do yourself a flavor and check it out...you won't be disappointed!

This is the 2nd meal at this end of the wharf locals dive joint. we sat outside. You put your name on a list and its pretty quick.  You can also order at the take out window and eat at the benches over looking the ocean if you need to catch the train.

Daughter had the 2 lb crab & it was fresh & meaty.  The other two had the shrimp tacos & loved them, as they had ample shrimp & they were not breaded.

  I like the clam chowder, which has bacon in i,t  but it is not dairy free or gluten free for some in our party. :(

We told our waiter we had to catch a train & he really hopped to it in every way!! Chowder was hot, drawn butter was yummy and I liked the blue cheese & ranch too.

My special was the 3 crab claws for $14.95, no sides.  It was plenty and filled me up with the cup of chowder.  I suggest you go here sometime in your life time...its the Jewell of Santa Barbara when it comes to seafood!!

I normally don't complain, but this place was a new level of awful. I came here with my family for lunch and the service was awful. The waiter rarely checked on us, we never got a refill on drinks, we had to waive him down to finally ask for our check and then we waited for him to come back for the check and he never came back. I had to take the check up to the front counter and then he finally asked if I needed anything else. The beer was mediocre and the food was okay. It totally wasn't worth it. I sure hope they fix the problem, because they'll lose more customers. I wouldn't come back to this place.

This is a great place for a nice dinner in the French Quarter that won't break the bank.  They have two options for dinner - a traditional a la carte meal or a Table d'Hote which includes appetizer, entree, and dessert for a fixed price of $28.95.  We chose the Table d'Hote because we felt it was the better deal.  Our waiter, Tucker, was phenomenal!  Super friendly and really knowledgable about the menu.  He figured we were tourists so he explained the ingredients in the soup of day (the main ingredient was some sort of local squash that I had never heard of).  My boyfriend ordered the glazed pork chops and claimed they were the best pork chops he had ever had!  I had the seafood au gratin, which was also very tasty and filling.  Beware - if you plan to have a few drinks after dinner do not order this meal - it is so good that you will want to finish it but it is very heavy.  The downstairs dining rooms are decorated with old photographs and interesting architectural details.  The bar is set in the back and a nice place to sit and relax - order the Pimm's Cup.  You must definitely check out the upstairs while you're there!  Beautiful dining rooms used for special events, a seance room, and a balcony overlooking Jackson Square.  Our waiter informed us that anyone is welcome to have a drink upstairs on the balcony anytime the restaurant is open (they don't serve food up there though).  It would be a great place to people watch during the day.  And be on the lookout for the restaurant's resident ghost!

Marrakesh is an experience unlike any other restaurant could give you.

Let's start with the fact that you have to ring the doorbell to this place before even getting in. If that's not enough to make you feel like you're in for something unique, I'm not sure what is.

So I won't get into huge detail but the jist of it is this- 7 courses. $33 after tax/tip. You eat with your hands off of a communal plate so make sure you bring your friends who wash their hands after going to the bathroom. The occasional belly dancer may shimmy through as well.

This place is 3 stories high and I only got a glimpse of the top two. I have to say they were very cool looking and there were plenty of spaces for big groups. 

Ok, so I noticed that this whole review (which I was about to end) didn't even mention the food. The food is pretty good. I wouldn't go back for the food alone. The chicken is melt in your mouth delicious, but nothing really wows me. But it's definitely a place to take out of town guests if you really want to give them a unique and fun experience.

I live near here so I'm not sure why it took me so long to discover it, but I'm sure glad I did!  Everything is fresh and delicious, and I feel like you just can't go wrong with what you order from here.  Nothing against Bread Co, but I'd recommend this place about 1,000 times more!

Fish Taco's were good with cilantro/lime rice.
Miller Lite's were cold... Not the best, but served a purpose.

Soooooooooooo yummmmmmy!!! I always get their black bean burger with various toppings, always good. Milkshakes are very good. A little skimpy with the toppings but if you ask you'll get the perfect amount

Food is up to Outback standards and comes out quickly. Our server Jillien was simply the best and encouraged us to try some of the new menu items. We enjoyed our dinner and look forward to going again.
Same as the rest. No complaints. It is actually a pretty big locations with an open concept so makes it feel big and easy to see all of the tvs
Are they closed?? Every time we stop, their sign says open but they are closed. Bummer

WHOA! The huevos rancheros here are incredible! The self serve coffee from the pot is way better than the Daily Grinds' and the service is awesome. This is my first visit and I can't wait to come back. Also, gluten free bread! Hell yeah!
Had best meal in 10 years. Fantastic service by Chris with as promised best steak in Tucson.  Appetizers were phenomenal.  Definitely will be back, and forgot to mention live music!

Definitely the best BBQ in Jefferson county. The ribs, pulled pork and pork steaks are outstanding! I agree with some of the other reviews that their sides are not the greatest, not bad either just OK. But fuck it, the meat more than makes up for the sides.

This is one of my very favorite places in all of St. Louis. The worst meal I ever had here was still GOOD! I've tried most all of the menu and everything is really good! The Pressed Cuban is the best I've found. The Royal Grill is always a favorite (try it with turkey). The Stutz Salad is great with anything. And the ice cream.... Hey, I like ice cream. But it's not an obsession. How great can it be? Oh. Mah. Gawd. I still remember; it was the Almond Joy Sundae. It was really the best ice cream I've ever had. And the home made hot fudge; I just want to get a barrel of it. Again, it's all amazing. All the flavors, all the toppings. And the ice cream martinis might look cute and pretty, but they pack a serious punch. You will FEEL just one of them. It's all great. The atmosphere is fun. You just will not be disappointed.

We have been to Guru's many times (dine and carry-out) and it is safe to say that it is the BEST Indian restaurant in the area...by a mile.  On our first two trips we had excellent experiences, with great food, excellent help staff and reasonable prices.  The main owner also appears to be the front of house lead, and she is an incredibly nice and friendly woman, and we always enjoy interacting with her.  I think the big watch out for Guru's, is that they must train the staff to be as thoughtful and caring as the lead owner/maitre'd.  On a recent Friday evening visit, we had another staff member help us and it was not nearly the same experience, with slow service and a general "scattered-ness".  Overall, I highly recommend Guru's for great Indian food in Newtown...hopefully the staff takes the lead from the owner, so that they will ensure a consistent and memorable experience every time.

This place literally changed my life... I am a foodie first, and a Weight Watchers devotee second. I have found both a bit difficult this summer thanks to my boyfriend and his adorable children (read - macaroni and cheese).  The gang was out of town this week, so I decided it was time to get back on track. After a dedicated week of points tracking, and a miserable salad for dinner (sorry Cosi, you're just not doing it for me anymore), I was craving something more. I literally stumbled upon The Lite Choice, and thought I'd give it a shot. I was chatted up and offered samples and decided to go for a healthy option - base soft serve in chocolate covered strawberry. I was very pleased with the portion size, and the honesty that their prices are a little higher, but you get what you pay for. This stuff was absolutely delicious. Creamy, just sweet enough, no weird aftertaste - I enjoyed every bite. When I got home, I went on their website to calculate the WW points. Brace yourself.. TWO POINTS!!! This cup of creamy, deliciousness was only two points!!!! I know this won't mean much to some of you, but for me - life changing. I can't wait to go back.

Walking around New Hope, we were looking for a place to eat lunch. We came across Cumin Cafe and decided to try it. OMG, it was soooooo good. We were the first ones there when they opened so they were still setting up and preparing to open for the day. Since we were the first we had to wait quite a while after we ordered lunch, around 30 minutes, BUT, we knew it was being cooked fresh because we could hear the chopping of veggies and blending of sauces. We were in for a treat. Out came our Chicken Tikka Masala, Lamb Korma, Vegetable Biryani, Samosas, Garlic Naan, and Aloo Gobi. Everything was so incredibly delicious, fresh, and good! We eat at a lot of Indian places and Cumin Cafe was our favorite. The downfall? We live in L.A. and we're only here visiting. Great job Cumin Cafe, hope we can enjoy eating there again.

My friend visting from California and I both tried the grass fed cheesesteak sandwiches, they were definitely a lot less greasy than a conventional steak, but  kinda bland in terms of flavor and a bit of a let down for my friend who was attempting to try her first true Philly cheesesteak.. the caesar salad served with them was OK, but not too exciting. interesting cocktails (albeit $10 each) are available, I tried dark and snappy it was pretty good.. however the cheesesteak wontons are a must try in my humble opinion!!! just a small appetizer plate but they are great. waitress was very friendly, service was very good, she was full of advice for us. the interior is clean and the environment pretty pleasant.

When I started going to the Kingshighway McD, their game was to refuse you a cup and the counter, then ignore you for as long as possible when you tried to get one. That issue seems to have been addressed (largely by myself), but since then I've had naked burgers, fries that looked like they were swept off the floor, undersized orders, and most recently, long delays while they leave my burger down near the grill where it can't be seen. One of the girls walking by loudly mocked me by saying "Is this customer still waiting for his order??" None of them ever touched it. It took me 17 minutes of standing there while others were served around me before I could get the attention of the manager, who got me my bag in 10 seconds.

I don't like needless conflict in my life. I don't want to be part of this war. I am at peace with different people. I would hire them without prejudice. I am always as polite as I can be there. I honestly am.

This place is consistently and deliberately hostile. Their service is pointedly antagonistic toward anyone they don't like the looks of, and they don't care how far they take it. In the two years I've been going there, the management has not been effective in controlling the issue.

They are just around the corner from me, and it was handy sometimes, but I've finally had to give them up. It's better for every part of my body and mind never to go there again.

Has a very similar set up to all bar and grill restaurants, almost seemed liked I had been there before. Order the Nachos! I dislike black olives (no mention of olives on menu description) but still ate every bite of this delicious nacho amazingness. Steak and crab cake tasted okay, similar to everywhere else. Next time I'll just order a large Nachos just for myself.

First time here, was pretty pleased. We had a group of 7, but didn't have to wait long for a table, staff very friendly. I got a chicken Caesar salad that was delicious, and more than enough! I went with our waiters suggestion of some Margherita w/o sour mix and some citrus flavor...it wasn't all that great, could've stuck with a regular and been happy. Also, two of our party's food came out late, so they comped their orders! Very accommodating and not many complaints for a chain restaurant.
Friendly host staff... Server basically assumed women know nothing about beer and overall horrendous service for mediocre beer.

Rushed service.  Crawfish beignet was not a beignet at all but a cheese calzone with some fishy crawfish in it. 

The grits were really tasty.  The baked oysters are incredibly delicious.  Lots of garlic and butter.  Wish the bread was better. It tasted like a cheap grocery store baguette.

Hands down the best restront ever. Best food, the serious was amazing and they treat you like family. The serious was on point, your glass is never empty, and they all have a big genuine smile on their face, and shout out to our waitress Tasha grate job. The food was so good but get here fast because the menu changes all the time. Over all amazing, beyond amazing can't even describe it was god like, would come back.

Gulliftys has been around forever.  You'll find a large menu that is likely to satisfy everyone.  There is an outside deck that some folks love.  I'm not a fan for two reasons.  First it's surrounded on three sides by the parking lot.  Yeach!  Second its menu is very limited compared to inside.  Speaking of the parking lot, it's large.  Parking is a breeze.

I visit Gullifty's for the beer selection which is easily one of the largest in the Western burbs.  Just ask for the beer book and see for yourself.  The bottle selection is especially large.

If I was rating the food and ambiance I'd say three stars.  The amazing beer selection ups it to four (4).

Looking for another place to eat and after passing the Hill, I turned around to try it.   30/40 years ago the place was called Betty's and they had a good breakfast.  I stopped for dinner.
If your looking for ambiance, your in the wrong place.

Let me say up front, the food was good.   I ordered veal parm with a side of penne and a cup of escarole and meatball soup.

The soup was great so I was expecting a great entree.  The sauce on the veal and panne was good and tasty.  The veal itself turned out to be one of those ground patties.  It was ok but not like biting into a nice piece of veal.  Probably why it was so cheap. ($13)

Now the bad part.  Do you remember the noise level in your high school cafeteria?   Now put that into a 30 x 50 restaurant with a low ceiling.  For some reason everyone needed to yell at each other.  And most of the people were over 60!   Go figure!

A resort style outdoor bar with a flavorful menu of fresh seafood. Great atmosphere and fun drinks to go around. 
All that was missing was the sound of the ocean.

Wow. Where do I start. The BEST dining experience me and my wife have had in the French quarter while on vacation. Made a reservation here weeks ahead to celebrate an anniversary with my lady and first off let's talk about the spectacular customer service. First off, I sent a brief email when I made the reservation, requesting (if possible) a romantic table more secluded and away from the rest. We were seated at the only table by the corner window directly facing Jackson square, under a few romantic lamps on the wall, very cool. The waiter was even notified apparently of our celebration because he wished us a happy anniversary and we each received a complementary glass of champagne which was great, not cheap bitter bubbles. Now let's talk about the food. Wow. You want messy food, tons of stuff jammed together? You have half of the French quarter. You want a five star dinner made by an amazing chef; with tastes so widespread you are guaranteed to say wow at something new? Go to Muriel's. The BEST pork chop I've had my whole life, the best bread pudding I've had my whole life, the list can go on. But most importantly, CUSTOMER SERVICE. Exceptional. I've spent years working in the customer service industry, as well as training people in customer service, and if I had to choose restaurants to represent the level of service I expect at all times, I'd choose Muriel's and Jackson Square, and the South Gate restaurant in the Essex House across the street from Central Park NY. I've been around and know when a restaurant truly deserves a review as exceptional as their service/food. To the chef and management of Muriel's, my hat is off to you. You have a customer for life every time I am in NOLA.
One of my new favorite go to places for authentic Mexican food! The margaritas are good and the food is absolutely delicious.

Awesome little place.  Tasty GF, Dairy Free. Vegan eatery.  I got a Cran-Apple Wrap and fresh Watermelon juice.  Friendly service, clean decor.  On the pricy side, but finally diet/ lifestyle friendly food that is scrumptous!

I really disliked my pizza I ordered through you guys through Bite Squad, the new mobile app for delivery service. I ordered the White Cheese steak Pie, the crust was very hard and the mixture of the ingredients was very strange I will never order again.
Probably the worst Chinese buffet I've been to in the Indy area. Food was discolored and bland tasting. Even the prepackaged fortune cookies were an odd color.

Misto Diner, we love you. This is a family-run business, and at the top is May--she and everyone else are so incredibly friendly. 

We were sketchy when we tried this place almost a year ago (there were no reviews then, and it's easy to drive past), but everything we've ever had has been amazing and fresh. Often, we order delivery--we're told it'll take the usual 30-45 minutes, but it always comes 10-15 minutes later (we live close, so this might vary). Even with this glorious speed, everything is so freshly made, perfectly cooked, and delicious. 

My husband and I want everyone to know that Misto Diner is where it's at. We've tried just about all of the other Chinese cuisine in the area, and we haven't found anything that comes near Misto's quality. (We haven't tried the sushi, but surely it's just as good.) Our favorites: the house special pan fried noodles, all of the various fried rices, boneless spare ribs, teriyaki beef sticks, the omelets, chicken with peanuts, pepper steak, fried shrimp... everything. I especially love their chicken dishes because they're cut into narrow strips, clean of fat and other nasty things, and perfectly cooked. This includes the chicken rice soup. To make sure I don't forget--get soup! It comes with home made crunchy rice noodles and they are ridonkulous. I would pay to have those for the rest of my life. 

This place is affordable, provides tons of food for the price, and just so, so good. Do yourself a favor and try it.

I've eaten here a few times, and I like it a lot (for being a chain restaurant). 

First, the good stuff: Service is always AWESOME. The kids working in there are just so happy to be there, it's frightening. And so knowledgeable about the menu and meat in general. Bravo. I almost feel like they may be a little overstaffed, but that's probably because they are new and just hired a million people to start out with. 

The food is seriously delish, but if you don't like meat, seriously, you have no business here. I'm not a huge steak person, but I do okay with their steak tips dinner, which is very mushroomy and delicious. They also have amazingly good ribs, and the pulled pork is awesome. If clogged arteries are your thing, the cactus blossom is yum as well (think Chili's Awesome Blossom, or Outback's Bloomin' Onion - same exact thing). I think the best part is the bread they serve in the beginning, with the cinnamon-y butter. Dessert before dinner. SO GOOD! 

On the downside, it's a little pricey. Comparable to Outback or Lonestar, I suppose. But it's steak, so that's to be expected. 

Now on to my major complaint - wait time for a table. There's always AT LEAST a two hour wait, unless you go at noon on a sunday when everyone's still in bed/at church. The first time we went, we called ahead and were told to show up in about 2 hours to get our table (when you do call ahead, you're supposed to show up 15 minutes prior to your number being called). Once we got there, we had to wait an additional HOUR and 15 minutes. They said the problem was that people weren't leaving, that they were lingering too long for them to efficiently turn their tables, but it was still annoying. While we waited, waitresses were running up and down the waiting rooms (there are two huge waiting rooms on either side of the entrance, so I guess they knew they'd have a problem while building it) with appetizers for us to pick at, so that was thoughtful (and another testament to my theory that they're actually overstaffed). 

So, all in all, good chain restaurant as far as food and service. I just hope you can stand waiting. Don't even bother on a Friday or Saturday evening.

In Baton Rouge I would say this is one of my favorite sushi places, in New Orleans not even close. The service we had was quite awful, the server was complaining a lot about her shit and how they had to pay for parking themselves ($25) to work. The food is just alright. The lighting is so dark you can barely see what you're eating. It's just not that great for what you are paying for.

The food had no taste and we ended up throwing it all out.   How can you ruin chicken parmigiana?  They did.  Wilted lettuce.  Mozzarella sticks like shoe leather fried.   Horrible horrible horrible.  Gary

I lived a block away from this place for over 6 months before trying it. Big mistake!! I love the Tennessee burger and the nachos! Also has a great outside patio for enjoying a beer and burger on a nice day!

Really good food. We ordered Pad Thai with both shrimp and chicken which was really tasty. Nachos with crab dip simply delicious. Seared scallops very tender with a delicious corn and peach salad, and a dry corn cake, that I wish I could buy by a dozen. Glad we decided to come try this place.

I love Louis Pappas Resturant. There food is really good. I love their Cubans, Mojo pork and my favorite is there lemon chicken soup. There salads are yummy. I retired in February 2016 and on my way home I decided to stop in and celebrate my new life. Now, every year in February I stop by for a delicious lunch. This time when I stopped in they had a BLT special so I got it with my soup. Usually I only eat 1/2 sandwhich but this time I ate it all....it probably was that special sauce on it.

Cajun Food and Jazz!

We decided to check this place out after reading other Yelp reviews.  The restaurant was inviting and the staff were very friendly.  We decided to sit in the patio area because the music was about to start and it was a beautiful night.

There were so many choices on the menu that I didn't think I would ever be able to pick one thing.  I finally decided on Miss Linda's Cajun dish with our waitresses help.  She was very patient and explained each of the entrees.  Miss Linda's Cajun dish was fresh grouper on rice and topped with shrimp and crawfish ettofe.  The only reason I chose this over the shrimp and crawfish ettofe is because the waitress advised it was very spicy and their hottest dish so I opted for the fish with a little less ettofe.  It was very spicy but I could handle it and it was amazing.  I can't wait to go back and get the full order of ettofe next time.

The jazz musicians were great.  It was very relaxing listening to the music and finishing my wine after I devoured the cajun food.  I highly recommend this place for a great evening.  They have more  on their menu than cajun if you aren't into a lot of spice.

Definitely an excellent restaurant 
Wood oven Pizza was fantastic and definitely the best pizza in town. Prepared and tasting like a true Italian Pizza. Great wine selection. Steak was also great
Great atmosphere and excellent service. A restaurant not to miss for excellent Italian food with family or friends.
This is my absolute favorite BBQ joint. The staff is amazing and the specials are top notch.

I have been here 5 or 6 times sitting outside at the tiki hut each time. The service is excellent, and my waitress jenna, was very funny and engaging. 

I ordered a blackened grouper wrap. It was very good except maybe a little too much mayo. Had mozzarella sticks as an appetizer with a Jillian red beer. All of it was very good. 

The ambiance was wonderful watching pelicans flying around and the dolphins in the inlet. 

A real nice time, all in all.

Stopped in over the weekend with family in town.  The atmosphere was inviting and the staff was great.  Since this was our first time in we ordered a variety of burgers and split them.  We ordered The Hangover, Shitake, & BBQ.  The Hangover was my favorite.  

Ordered the regular and sweet potato fries.  Sweet potato fries a great choice and the dipping sauce wasn't too sweet.  

The beer menu is expansive, 124 beers on tap.  Their beer menu was well organized and labeled.  The bartender was very knowledgeable about the breweries and beers available.  

If we are up that way again, we will pop in.  Glad we did and tried somewhere new.
It's alright. Nothing special. I had a pasta and pizza, and my pasta was a little bit watery and very bland. The pizza I had was good for the price that I paid.
Very good service!!! Great for quick lunch breaks. The margaritas were awesome and the enchiladas verdes are a must have! Highly recommended.
Never disappoints! Love this place! I get something different every time and every time I fall in love with a new dish! Great place!

My fiance and I heard about this place from the co-owner who stopped by my fiance's store.  We decided to check it out.

When we first arrived (On a Saturday night, 7pm).  All but 1 table was taken, but there were several spots still at the bar.  Watch your knee on the rocks!  It looks great, but can scrape your knee if you aren't paying attention.  Anyway, their decor is great.  The wood doors for the tap room & kitchen are great.  The restaurant looked pretty new inside.  It had an overall clean feeling as well.

Their draft list is great!  When we visited they had 9 beers on draft (one had just tapped out).  I had Allagash White, one of my favorites.  My fiance had Flying Bitch.

Our server was both the bartender and what seemed like a manager.  Both were incredibly nice and really made sure we had what we needed when we wanted it.  The food came out quickly.

For an appetizer we both shared the Hawg Wings (Pork Shanks).  These come in several different flavors.  We chose Teriyaki. I'll be honest, I'm a BBQ fan.  I smoke ribs, brisket, sausage and more for hours and hours.  These Hawg Wings, with the Teriyaki sauce, were some of the best I've ever had.  I 100% recommend them!  Do not miss out!

We ordered up some Hangover burgers.  These come with your choice of bacon, a fried egg, hot sauce, sharp cheddar, fries and slaw.  I absolutely dislike coleslaw.  This slaw was unreal.  I'm not sure what they did to it but I thoroughly enjoyed it.  The burger was also phenomenal.  They cooked ours perfect to our liking.  The beef was juicy and had some great flavor.  Again, highly recommended!  If you're in the area, stop by and check this place out!  We'll be back quite soon for more Hawg Wings, burgers, and maybe a flight of bacon this time!
You can't go wrong here. Great food and a good view of the street performers in Jackson Square. Try the gator, fried or blackened. In fact, do half and half; you can thank me later.
Food is always good just a little pricey. It is a family owned business! Burgers are good when they have them most specials aren't that great salads good!

Used to love this place when it was Rushes, but sadly a big frustrating disappointment as Creekside. All the novel gourmet upscale items are gone from the menu, which leaves burgers, standard fare, and lots of fried appetizers. Biggest dismay was how anti-vegetarian they are; no veg burger option first two times here (they say they will add), and despite the hostess' assurances that they can "make something up for you" we got literally incredulous stares, disgusted hmmphs, rolled eyes, and hedging "I don't know"s when asking for small veg-friendly changes (eg vegs listed on the menu substituted for meat in pasta dishes; not a welcoming feeling at all. Meat-eating companions also found food mediocre and service very slow and confused. Hope they get their act together; has the potential to be great if they'll consider client feedback.

To my knowledge, Cosi's sandwiches are all pre-prepared , so I never go in there expecting to be BLOWN AWAY. Their food is EDIBLE, and that's pretty much it.

I like to go to Cosi for lunch and sit outside and catch a breeze. It's a perfect spot for kicking it with friends or as a neutral meeting place for business acquaintances. 

I like the tomato soup and the Chicken TBM sandwich, the hot apple cider, the hot chocolate and teas.

Chef's Market is always good. I've tried almost all of their offerings and have never been disappointed. I like the Salad Trio for lunch; you select 3
salads from a myriad of choices. Curried Chicken Salad, Italian Pasta Salad, Avocado and Corn Salad with your choice of house baked roll, delicious. One of my dinner favorites is Short Ribs with Jack Daniels Sauce and a choice of 2 hot veggie sides, their sweet potato casserole is crazy good but I like the roasted potatoes and vegetable saute with the short ribs. Dessert, OMG. The cakes are to die for, you will not be able to eat a whole piece. Be sure to take a look, they're in the front case.

This place is located near the Garden District. It is pretty small and my party of 6 had to be broken up into 2 tables. That is how small this place is, but that's ok. I ordered their Crab Omelette and it was delicious. Usually with my omelette, I stick with vegetables, bacon, etc. but I had to try this. It was well worth it and was not too heavy.

There is plenty of street parking, just watch out for any signs that are permitted.
Good food, good atmosphere and friendly service. Great place to watch a game with friends. Management staff is very attentive to customers and restaurant operations.
Had the 96 burger and the Iceland beer and it was amazing. Server's recommendation is pretty good and friendly. Definitely will be back again next time

As far as breakfast on a Saturday morning goes, there's no point in eating anything or anywhere else... Amish Country Market at The Feed Mill is always an outstanding way to start off the weekend for your mouth. Plus, in the 5 or 6 times we've been, everyone has been incredibly friendly and accommodating... it just makes the experience all the more enjoyable.

FINALLY made it to kanella back in march, holy crap that felt like it took forever. I was a fan of Cheg Pitsillides (I hope that's close to the correct spelling, don't feel like Googling) when he cooked at the unfortunately short-lived meze but for some reason kanella kept getting pushed lower down my eattherenow list. enough of this mischief, on to the food!

delicious haloumi, as one can expect, excellent grilled sardines (a semi-constant craving of mine), delicious lamb-stuffed, fried koubes, YUM! also, delicious stuffed peppers (no longer on the menu, maybe was a special). am definitely itching to go back and try more things, i completely trust this chef to deliver. one of the dishes we had in march was a special, and i remember it was a red meat served with a mix of braised green veg, including escarole and nettles. excellent. and he used nettles, which are a criminally underused/under-appreciated (and hard to frickin find) ingredient. i asked our waiter to ask where the chef got his but he wouldn't tell me. boo! but he doesn't know that i am not a chef or a spy. sigh. maybe anastasio's will special order some for me....

May be my new favorite Cunningham restaurant! Adorable interior (and exterior) that makes your dining experience just that much more fun. Amazing house margarita and I crave the street corn on the reg! I love to order several dishes with friends and share them all. Great way to try out different dishes on the menu without committing to one meal. I have heard of people complaining about how slippery the floor is inside? I have never had a problem with this, however does make me a bit anxious that I'm going to biff it walking to the bathroom in front of everyone.
I love their food!! Their drunken noodles and pad thai are the bomb, their curries especially green curry is delicious!
Used to love this place, but I don't know what happened. Sub-par food and not great service

Ok, I'm a slightly reluctant fan of this PF Chang spinoff. I have visited the parent restaurant several times but today was my first at this more casual chain.

The menu is similar to what I have experienced at PFC, and the prices are lower, so far me likey. How could I not try the lettuce wraps, I'm obsessed with them and order at almost anyplace that I encounter them. Here there are 2 versions, I opted for the Thai and it was good but not great, but kudos to them for providing enough lettuce to eat them with. Next time I'll the original version. 

A few entrees looked enticing but in keeping with a Thai-ish theme I selected Dynamite chicken. I liked this a lot, crunchy chicken pieces that were slightly spicy. The veggie pasty of the dish was sparse, mucho scallion but just some shredded carrots and red pepper. Sauce was almost non existent. Trish ordered her favorite here, chicken Pad Thai. I tasted and thought it was ok, not quite what the dish can be in a good Thai shop, but for the price and quickness, very acceptable.

They offer a good rewards program that probably helps bring back repeat customers. At our early lunch arrival we noticed that the place filled in quickly. This is a good choice for a fast and filling meal at a reasonable price. 4 why do I feel slightly guilty Yelps
Incredibly great breakfast. By far, the best pancakes and corn beef hash i have ever put in my mouth.

Great food!!! I order from here all the time. They have some of the best burgers around which are also 100% pure angus beef and they make some of the best pizza dough around. Also try they're soup! I'm personally a big fan of their waffle fries.

We've been here twice with our 3 kiddos. 4, 2 and 5 months. Food is always great and I love how nice the people are. Because the restaurant is never very busy, the wait staff is always very attentive. We joke that we want it to stay just busy enough to never go out of business but not too busy that they can't be attentive and quick with the food. Lol. But in all seriousness, there food is always very good.

After reviewing the menu online, I decided to check this place out with a friend.  It looked like they had an eclectic, varied menu with a nice selection of beers and wine.  Several people I know have been here before and it came highly recomended.  Unfortunatly, though, my experience left much to be desired.
     We arrived around 5 pm, at which time it appeared all of the servers were arriving as well.  We were seated promptly, however it took about 15 minutes for a server to appear.  Both my friend and I ordered the "Pub Steak" which were brought out reasonably quick.  The presentation was non-existent, simply a hunk of meat with french fries.  I ordered mine med-rare and received it well done.  The waitress did nothing to rectify this except apologize (I had barely eaten half).  
     The best part is this, I soon discovered a chip in my wine glass and upon showing it to the waitress she asked if I would like another.  I replied yes and was brought a new glass with the old wine poured into it.  Unbelievable!  How incredibly un-professional.  I pointed this out to the waitress and got another apology.
     We recieved a bill with no concessions.  No manager came to speak with us.  Nothing was done to rectify this experience.  Needless to say, I won't be visiting this establishment again.

Just got back from a five day trip to Santa Barbara and out of those five days, we found and ate at Cuernavaca three days.  They were that good.  Loved their al pastor tacos, tried their quesadilla, burrito and taco de chicharon, even brought some home.  Also loved their taco de raja con queso.  I understand they have one in Ventura and opening in Oxnard.  Would most definitely make the drive.  Would highly recommend this place to anyone visiting SB.

I use to love going here but service has severely fallen short recently. The food and drinks are still good. The problem comes with if you actually get what you ordered. Wrong drink and food given. When I come into the store to tell them of the issue I'm having they talk to me like I'm to dumb to understand what's going on. Even though they were the ones that handed me an order through the window with a girls name on it and not even close to my order. Don't be condescending toward your customers. The friendliness from this place is sorely lacking when it use to be one of the better places to go too. It's a shame.

My wife and I dined at TJ's tonight for date night and were extremely disappointed,  disappointed on many levels.  One level being the service (server 7021 on the receipt), she should never serve again.  She spoke like we were an inconvenience to her, never told us her name, and had a demeanor as if she did not care about anything.  She was short with every response and uneducated on the menu, she did not even ask how our food was that we barely touched.  Second the food was terrible.  We had ordered the calamari as an appetizer, way under seasoned, red sauce was bland and tasted like canned marinara.  I had dumped one cap full of table salt(probably 1/8 tsp) from the salt shaker into our 2 oz portion of red sauce and it barely helped.  Calamari tasted just like fryer oil with no seasoning in the flour.  I had the sausage Parmesan sub and my wife had the meatball Parmesan sub.  Terrible choices.  Meatballs tasted like a frozen product, with canned marinara sauce.  My wife ate 1/4 of her meal and set it aside.  The sausage Parmesan was even worse.  Sliced Italian sausage with, maybe peppers covered with slopped sauce and cheese, on the best part of the entire meal, the bread. When we picked up our subs they immediately fell through the bread onto the plate.  Annoying to all sandwich lovers.  Oh, the beer battered onion rings, awful.  Nothing else to say about those other than we ate 2.  Server 7021 never asked us is everything was okay, or if we enjoyed the meal and clearly from the almost full portions of food that we denied to go boxes for didn't send a message, I do not know what else would.  My wife and I will never return to TJ's nor recommend this to anyone.  This was the worst $56 I have ever spent on food.

I've always been a fan of "chopped" cheesesteaks, and have never found a ribeye style steak that compared...until I had my first Chink's.  Oh man, this steak simply blew me away.  It was meticulously prepared for me to order, as I sat at the soda fountain counter with my black cherry soda.  Then when it came out, with a nice side of hot peppers, I was in marvel at the fine preparation.  When I saw the ribeye style, I was skeptical.  One bite and I was a believer.  Chubby's is my all time favorite, but darn it, Chink's immediately is up there in the top 3 cheesesteaks I've ever tasted.

Large outside venue with full coffee and alcohol bar. I noticed others eating food but we just ordered beignets. Beignets were good (not as good as Cafe du Monde) they are $3.99 for 3. Live musicians playing and was pretty packed every time we walked by. Nice place, we'll return!

Very cool restaurant with an enclosed courtyard. Our two waiters were very attentive the entire meal, which I would definitely expect dining at a restaurant like Muriel's.  The escargot was fantastic and the soft shell crab was delicious. We had a large group and were lucky to get same day reservations. (I would definitely recommend reserving a table a few days in advance.)

Sending props out to Ben, Rachel, Suzanne and the chefs that made last nights meal amazing! "Sunday Supper" menu items, whiskey offerings and service were outstanding. The portions were generous and the ambiance = F.U.N.!!! Be sure to make a resee and go hungry! 
 (Oh, and you are welcome!!!! )

I'm still trying to convince my mom to bring us back for dinner. We went here for lunch, it was pretty busy but they had room for us. The space is historic and seems like a cross between a 20s movie theatre/20s soda fountain/40s club. I had the Sunday special which was chicken salad on a fresh croissant and it was DE-LICIOUS - and I'm not even a huge fan of chicken salad. We got ice cream after that and it was awesome. Big sundaes that were definitely worth the price. 
The whole place was worth way more than the price. The meals were under $10. It was awesome. Me and the three kids meals + big ice cream desserts came out to $38 - not including tip.
My only complaints are that they don't have any burgers (they definitely seem like they should) and the service was a little slow. I think the service was just my waitress, however, because she seemed a little out of it.
Really, seriously, get food here.

Used to be a go to for me. Tried to hit this one in the Harrah's Casino and it's the worst ever. Taking an hour to get food and getting it wrong almost each time. You'd do better to go to a hotdog vendor on the street. Sad times for this place. The franchise as a whole has fallen far from grace but this one takes the cake.

I live close enough to walk to St Pete Bagel, which is good because parking is limited. I go on the weekends for a cup of coffee and something yummy, like a fresh bagel and house-made cream cheese. Bacon and garlic-chive are my two favorite flavors. If you want something sweet, the peach fritters are out of this world. The donuts are beautifully made; it's hard to decide on just one. Bonus deal, you get a free donut with the purchase of a latte. They recently started serving iced chai lattes, so I see a lot of free donuts in my future! Stopping in for lunch? I recommend the Cuban sandwich. But I don't think you can go wrong with anything on the menu. They are always busy, but the line usually moves pretty quick. It helps if you know what you want when you get to the counter. There are a few tables inside and outside, if you want to sit and eat. The staff is always friendly and it's obvious they get joy from seeing people enjoy the food. Visit St Pete Bagel Co and your mouth will thank you. Happy eating!

We went on Sunday noon time.  It was pretty packed, waited about 20 mins they accidentally lost our names so quickly gave us the next available table.  Overall service was great!  Food overall was really good not too greasy which most diners foods are.  Love the waffles and potato tots!  Although fried chicken was not crispy enough!

Went on a Friday night and man was it busy! We waited at least 45 min for our food and when it came it was mediocre at best. I ordered the GF crust pizza and hubby ordered a buffalo chicken sandwich which he said was solid. Server was friendly just seemed super understaffed for how crowded they were...

Kien Giang is pretty good (but not as good as Miss Saigon).  A good sign that its a  good Vietnamese restaurant is that its always packed solid.  Their Pho is a bit salty and has more taste than Miss Saigon (its better).  But I would say that just about everything else on the menu, though cheaper, is not as good as it is at Miss Saigon.  Their rice paper rolls and bubble tea (powder based) were huge disappointments.  The rolls' pork tasted off and you have to make a special request for the peanut sauce. And my vermicelli dish was just mediocre.

It drives me crazy that they don't take credit cards because I never carry cash on me and its a pain in the butt to have to make a special trip to the next door atm at Kroger's.

The staff are not very friendly (except for this one guy) and definitely not attentive.  It took them 5 minutes to get a menu to us, another 5-7 minutes to take our order, another 15 minutes to get our drinks and another 10 minutes to bring out the orders.  SO SLOW!!!  And it took the guy forever to come back with the peanut sauce which I asked for for the rolls and for a fork and they were so absent minded that when we went to pay for the bill, she took the money then started cleaning tables before she gave us back our change!

Its not fancy or anything, but the food is authentic, delicious and cheap.  Sometimes I wonder how clean the kitchen or backrooms are, but whatever...

Bottom line: food is mediocre/ pretty good but cheap, service is slow, staff is inattentive. Its too packed and noisy, which I think is the reason for the slow and inattentive service.  Attracts a lot of local Vietnamese and poor college students, but  for an extra 2 bucks, I'd rather go to Miss Saigon and have a close to perfect experience.
Excellent selection of meat and great quality. A little pricey but you get what you pay for here. The southwest tritip sandwich is amazing and they have a wide variety of rare meats.

Stir fry and fruit are amazing. One of Bala's gems but definitely need to count calories when eating here. One plus is the charging lockers for cell phones. One downside is the noise. This is one very noisy spot and not optimal for dining in. The food is fresh, the staff are nice and I love the customer experience. Fruit and salads are good, a little pricey but good for kids. 

A favorite indeed.

Ordered village burger and it was ok at best. Didn't blow my mind for a highly rated burger. Drinks were decent but normal priced for center city. Wouldn't go back, but overall wasn't too bad. Shake shack is close by! P.s. our waitress wasn't impressed by our shamrocks attire...lighten up!

Went there for lunch and got the ribs, baked beans and fried corn on the cob. The meat was tender and fall off the bone juicy and delicious. The baked beans excellent. The fried corn was good but I prefer boiled corn. The staff was friendly and the service fast. I'll be back to try more items.

The wait is long and it is crowded, even late at night. I came in past 8 and waited over 30 minutes for a seat when it was cold and windy out. I would give it 5 stars if not for that seat! The Rock Crab is worth it, however; fresh and sweet with Caesar salad and a cup of hot lobster bisque on the side. The crab cakes are OK and so was the shrimp and scallop pasta.  The server was friendly, fast and helpful. She substituted the regular soup for  the bisque! 5 stars for her! A little pricey but a nice place for fresh, simple seafood fare.

UPDATE as of 2/28/11: CLOSED permanently! 

Yum! Definitely try this place and you will not be disappointed!!!! It's also super fun to sit outside on their large patio and listen to the waves crash as you sip on a nice pitcher of cold beer and bite into your delicious pizza!!

My girlfriend and I stopped there around 11PM on a Saturday night. The place was completely dead and we were the only people in the restaurant, so we figured we would get a better than average meal and service, based on many of the yelp reviewers.

The server was somewhat prompt and friendly, quickly taking our drink and meal orders. We were pretty hungry, so we ordered the hummus right away. It came out with some warm pita bread and a bunch of raw vegetables; the presentation left a lot to be desired, but it was decent.

Then came our main course. We ordered a pepperoni pizza with roasted garlic to share; in addition I ordered a chicken Parmesan sandwich, and my girlfriend ordered the Cajun chicken pasta. And this is where positive remarks can no longer describe the experience.

The pizza had a Chuck E Cheese cardboard crust that was rather unpleasant to eat. The sauce could have been good but there was so little of it, we couldn't really tell you. Pepperoni was OK, but the roasted garlic was cold (probably from a jar), tasteless, and piled high. Absolutely disgusting and unacceptable for almost $20. 

Next, I tried the sandwich, which was not a chicken Parmesan sandwich at all, but rather some grilled chicken from the freezer section chopped up into squares on a giant French roll. Again, there was almost no marinara sauce and cheese was scarce. Another big disappointment.

Finally comes the Cajun chicken pasta. I only tried a bite of the strange substance, which appeared to be comprised of the same chicken from the sandwich, an attempt at Alfredo sauce, red onions, and pickled jalepenos. It looked like something that comes out of your body, rather than something you put into it. The almost room temperature, overcooked pasta and overwhelming taste of raw onions soured my palette enough to get the check and head out ASAP.

What really put the final nail in the coffin, however, was the fact that my girlfriend became sick for two days after eating there, spending a good portion of our vacation in the bathroom. I would not recommend this place to anyone who values good food or sanitation.

A good BBQ spot at an affordable price on Street Rd.  My wife and I decided to give this place a try after reading the rave reviews.  A few things to keep in mind before trying this restaurant out.  The restaurant is in the Best Western hotel, not even in the front, you need to awkwardly head to the back of the joint to find the place.  At first glance it looks like a little dive bar.  We visited at 8:30PM on a Saturday night so our experience may have been out of the norm.  We actually missed the turn because the sign is so small it's easy to miss.  Worse, if you miss the turn you need to drive at least a half mile if not further to turn around (if you're headed towards Feasterville-Trevose that is).  

We were greeted by Julie.  Our first thought as we watched her run both the bar and attend to the floor was, seriously?  This place with such great reviews is being run by one person?  Julie is actually a true gem, personable and went out of her way to get everyone's name that comes into the place.  If you do meet her ask about her trip to Chile but wait until after you've eaten already ;)

As for the food.  I really wanted to give this place 5 stars however there were just too many things that went wrong.
