It is ok. We don't have much choicein our small town,  so it's about aa good as it gets. The bad part is they know it, so they typically don't care if you're happy or not. Food can be hit or miss. Service is mostly miss. Prices are high for the quality of food and service.

I've been a regular customer here for the past 10 months. Today, I decided this to be my last visit to this place. The service staff and the cooking staff are not polite. They kept staring at me and my friends while eating. It worth mentioning that this is all you can eat restaurant; however, in order to make us feel full quickly, they decided to put a quantity of rice double the size of the sushi. When we left some rice, they decided to charge us for it. They were not polite by telling us you're ordering too much quantities and that's why we concluded that they put too much rice. The girls serving was talked to us in a rude way and one of them used her finger tips to point to us while talking. I will stop coming to this place again
Great service and the food is great too. Have eaten here several times and I am impressed. They will go out of their way to accommodate you.

Epic is definitely an inadequate description of this place. Mind-boggling, miraculous, incredible, amazing - we're getting closer to being accurate. 

After we realized (via Yelp) that they were open on Monday, this has been our Monday night spot, every week for the last several weeks. We try to get something new every time, although that doesn't always happen because sometimes we'll spend the week yearning for just one more order of gnocchi or another piece of perfectly cooked rib eye. Today I feel comfortable enough to write a review because we have literally eaten through about 80% of the items on the menu and I can tell you - it's absolutely flawless. My personal favorite is the gnocchi on the menu (the gnocchi special, although a potato gnocchi in Gorgonzola, which is entirely different from the gnocchi on the menu - is also amazing) and the ribeye - but every other item I've tasted (and it's been most of the items available) has been impressively good as well. 

This place is a good as it gets, you'll leave dreaming of coming back for more!

The food here was excellent. I had the two egg breakfast and the eggs were tasty along with the sausage and English muffins. The waffles are great as well. They are shaped like the fluer de list symbol that is prominent in New Orleans and were served warm with a selection of syrups. The service was quite slow. Not sure why because there were more servers than customers. Overall great place for a morning breakfast in the city. Highly recommended!

This is called a South Philadelphia hoagie....!!!!! If you want a grand experience with fireworks blasting come to Ricci's!! My dad brought me here as a young girl (he made me the Foodie I am today, lol) after school me still in my Catholic school uniform and we ordered the best hoagie ever....

The wait is quick and everyone just forms a line and they make your hoagie assembly line style. My favorite is the lady in there she looks like Sandra bullock she is very nice.... 

Hoagie roll is soft and toppings fresh.... 

RICCI never disappoints but get there early because they close like 3ish.

The best sushi I had was a place by the bay in Baltimore years ago. Ever since, I always compare my sushi experiences with that place. I have been to quite a few acceptable sushi places, including a few here in Nashville. Not one compared to my experience in Baltimore, until now. This restaurant is amazing. It is clean, crisp, and modern. The sushi is the best you will find around Nashville. Many places use so much sauce to add flavor that the fresh taste of the roll disappears entirely. Here, fresh and flavorful go hand in hand. The rolls were made with careful thought as to the texture and flavor. Neither were overdone and resulted in the sushi rolls of your dreams. What? You don't have those dreams? Well stop by here and find out what you've been missing.
Best wings I have found in Tucson. Never dined in, I always had take out. Always been great! Habanero wings are the best if you like heat. If not try the sweet Asian.

This place is fantastic - I really can't say enough good things about it. The owners are lovely people, and the food is utterly delicious. We had the jerk chicken wings to start, followed by the taste of the islands (curry goat, oxtail, and jerk chicken, plus rice and peas, plantain, and a salad) and the curry chicken. Everything was delicious, beautifully spiced, and the meat just fell of the bone. I'll be dreaming about those wings for days to come!

My husband and I visited with my 18 month old daughter, and the owners couldn't have been better with her, bringing her a puzzle to play with, and generally making a fuss of her - she loved it! There were a mix of families, couples, and groups in the restaurant when we visited on a Friday night, and a generally lovely atmosphere. The decor is crisp and modern, and the music was great. They also have TVs showing sport, including cricket to my husband's delight (we're British - he misses it, I don't!).

All in all this is the sort of family owned restaurant that you really hope does well. It's convenient for the convention centre, and whether you're looking for a place for a quiet dinner or fun with a group of friends, I think the delicious food and warm welcome would fit the bill. Loved it!
Huge fan of Local Taco.  I pretty much always get the special on the board - it's always something interesting (Lobster tacos with spicy butter sauce and local arugla?  Sure!)

Last day in Nashville so we had to walk over to the Pancake Pantry.  

It was raining out and we arrived around 8:20AM and the wait was about 20 minutes.   Not too bad.  Once we arrived, the line was more than double after 5 minutes so we had good timing...and the rain stopped after 10 minutes so all was going well.

A Guy came out as we got close to the door and asked people how many in your party.  There is a small vestibule you can sit in right before they come out and get you when your table is ready. 

We ordered the medley with pancakes, cherry pancakes and kids pancakes with chocolate chips.  They ask if you want the trimmings on the kids pancakes since they cut them into the shape of stars.  

The wait for the food was about 20 minutes;which was a bit surprising considering we ordered almost right away and got out food after another table of 4 got their food first arriving after us.  

We all enjoyed our food but the pancakes had a bit too much baking powder flavor to fluff up the pancakes.  Overall, it was a good visit and would go again. The prices were reasonable and the staff was friendly.

The staff was friendly and the service was fast, but the food was mediocre at best. I ordered a simple double whopper combo. The fries were cold and stale, the edges of the bun were hard, and the vegetables on the burger were warm and wilted like the burger had been under a heat lamp. Overall it wasn't totally inedible, but I definitely expect more for a fast food place that charges almost $10 for a combo meal.

I'm not sure how much you can expect when going to a place like this.  I feel like I've been to twenty parties here within the past year.  Its not terribly clean, but not out right dirty either.  The staff isn't rude, but they're not friendly.  Games that are supposed to dispense tickets seem to have a mind of their own.  And if the roll of tickets runs out in the middle of printing up your child tickets, you're SOL.  The pizza is pretty decent, considering.  And I like that they have a salad bar.  The prizes that you can "buy" with your tickets, I feel, are a bit sub-par.  But my 4 year old is always ecstatic to get that glow in the dark spider, or "super-eraser".  I'm not familiar with their prices for party packages, but I dont think I would plan a party here.

Went here for brunch and it was really excellent. My partner had the waffles and they were amazing -- especially the cream/marmalade topping for them. I had the fried chicken biscuit which was also wonderful. The chicken has an amazing honey glaze with a subtle kick that really makes it so good. The only drawback was that our waitress was not the best. But hard to dwell on that when the food is so amazing.

Visiting from San Antonio and I had researched some places to try while in Tucson. This was THE place at the top of my list and we were not disappointed!  We visited on a Tuesday for breakfast and when we arrived it was busy. I ordered the Breakfast Sammi and it was delicious. The English muffin and eggs were perfect and the Preps potatoes are amazing!  The Smoked Salmon Beni was served perfectly. The service  was friendly an on point!  We wanted to try one of their pastries but they sold of them before we could.  This place is a 'MUST' try!!

Seminole Hard Rock Casino is a great entertainment venue best times vary according to your own luck. I enjoy the food and drinks while I'm there; Frequently I've been invited to a jackpot party even months after the original jackpot win. Gambeling isn't as addictive as one my think with some good critical thinking and the right selection of games; for example, Baccarat or roulette you could certainly leave a winner and revisit with better enthusiasm!  I also enjoy some good perks as an elite member along with charity tournaments so don't listen so much to all the sour comments get out there and create your own energy . Life is about paying it forward. Try googling Earnest Cobb of Detroit his theory on slots is revolutionary for those who are aware of Average Daily Translations records of play and payouts from random number generator slots . Select , Project ,Expect and Collect. It's all there. Experience the magic at Orient's 301 Seminole Hard Rock Casino of Tama

I'm not sure I can write a review to adequately convey how truly excellent tonight's meal was! 

We started with the shrimp crepes and the gumbo, and had the black drum with shiitake mushroom sauce & my husband had the seafood "bayoubaisse".. Followed with a chocolate cake that was to die for, and some fantastic house made sorbet! 

Every course was perfect!  

The ambiance was lovely, the service outstanding!  Thank you David and Yana!

Thank goodness we discounted the negative reviews, despite how well written and convincing!

Going back tomorrow for brunch!

On a better day I think Han Dynasty probably is worthy of a 5 star review, but I think we went on an off day. All of our dishes were extremely salty or over seasoned. Not so overpowering that we couldn't eat it, but just enough that each small bite had to be chased down by a huge mouthful of rice. 

Service was good. It was busy but we were seated immediately. The only gap was about 15 minutes between appetizers and main courses. 

The Dan Dan noodles was not the sesame paste type that I am used to, but a more beefy noodle and spicy type. It had great flavor.

Both the dry fry pork and the water spinach were tasty but too salty. When were took our leftovers home, by the next day the vegetables had absorbed the rest of the base and was too salty to eat. Had to throw it out.

Great potential. Would give this place another shot.

Extremely over priced. We are that the New Mexican place around the corner and got a margarita, dirty martini, two beers, fish tacos and quesadilla's for $45, than we got here which was one glass of table red wine off their tap that was not good, two beers and a meatball appetizer $37.
Delicious food, the best beef patties I have had in a long time.  my only complaint is the never have Roti and the expired juices.

So, I've been to SatCo a million times, it was a college favorite for my friends and me. But, after purchasing a sharing spree voucher for a tailgating pack,I have found a new love!! For 25 dollars I was able to feed my very large and hungry family for my daughter's birthday dinner with no mess and no cleanup. I don't know how they do it, but their tacos were still so fresh and delicious after being transported from Satco to my house. (We don't live close) My dad commented on how great the steak tacos were and how tender the meat was. Fajita steak is typically not super tender. The queso was even better than I remembered. Also, they gave us enough chips and salsa to feed a small army. Seriously, I had a chip, salsa, and queso bar for my work friends the next day! I would definitely pay full price for this anytime. It was a great value!

Mother's Day Brunch was NOT what we expected. We were party of ten and able to made reservation for May 7, 2016. They only had special menu for Mother's Day. 
Unfortunately, food and the service both were sub standard. Waffle special had typical pop up waffle that you get out a toaster with three mixed fruits and very little whip cream for $15. I had better waffle at Bob Evans. I eat meatball omelette which had a few cut out meatball inside a skinny plain omelette. 
The decor is nice and the location is great.

This place creates new addictions with every trip.  First of all, they put amazing samples of breads with olive oil and aged balsamic vinegar.  I could craze along the counter all day, and be a very happy man.  I have to say that their olive bread is to die for.  After loading up on the carbs, you are ready for something refreshing.  The salads are beyond exceptional.  The ingredients are dripping with freshness, and feels like farm to table while you wait.  If you are looking for a sandwich, the Cubano is just the ticket.  The first time I went in, I asked the cashier what she recommended because I was having a hard time deciding.  She told me that her favorite, without a doubt, was the Cubano.  So, I gave it a shot.  Now, I need my fix at least once a week.  I think there is an addictive agent in that sandwich.  It's probably in the bread - ya know, the bread that they have calling and enticing you from the top of the display case like a seductress.  Oh, did I fail to mention that once they get you in their grip, you're soon turned onto the pastries and goodies in the display case???  They have so many to choose from, and each one looks delectable.  They even have vegan and gluten free, which I was skeptical about, but very happily surprised.  I would be totally neglectful if I didn't mention the AWESOME staff.  They are genuine, fun, and really ensure that you have a positive experience.  No matter what mood you walk into Our Daily Bread in, you leave in a great mood.  So, if you need/want a new addiction in your life and to be treated like the most important person around, Our Daily Bread is a stop for you.

I know food trucks have come a long way, but I was still a bit wary about eating here. Once I got a good look at the food though, that went right out the window! The place is a little hard to spot when driving, so just look for the 'Rusty Nail' sign that leads to a bar sharing the same parking lot. 

Recommend:
Sonoran dogs
Tortas (very buttery goodness!)
Tacos 
Burrito Jr.'s
...ALL were excellent!! 

I usually get a little irritated when a place receives a high rating for subpar Mexican food, but not this place. Everything was so flavorful, tender, and fresh. The employees are another asset to this place. They are very friendly, fast, and obviously do a great job of cooking. When we were done eating they wrapped up our food in little meat department packaging for us! I really appreciated that extra step. 

They play music in the seating area, and there is a flat screen TV. The open tent seating area is kept very clean after each table leaves, and they have an awesome salsa bar with just about every condiment you can think of. I usually drink my salsa before I start to gauge a restaurant's salsa making capabilities, and I must say, this place makes great hot and savory salsas! 

Drinks were soda out of a can (bottle Pepsi), and cash only~!!! I'm excited to have a new place to haunt.

I like food trucks. 

I like food trucks that have Poutine. 

I may just be a little biased here, but ALAS, I have found poutine in New Orleans.   For those of you who don't know what poutine is, it's actually a canadian dish originating in quebec.  It is composed of fries, with cheese curds that are sprinkled on top and they melt into a gooey mess as brown gravy is poured onto it.  It's a heart attack in a cup.

Back home in Canada, they have a a lot of different variations of poutines, and there are specialty poutine shops. I often think about poutine, so I was especially excited when I saw it on Foodie Call's menu as they were setting up.  I was so excited, I couldn't wait and I ordered it immediately, I had to wait about 20 minutes for the poutine because they hadn't even started up their burners yet.

Although it didn't taste like home, the poutine was still good in its own New Orleans way.  A little bit of seasoned fries, gravy with debris, and cheese curds.  Cheese curds weren't quite melted into a gooey mess, they were still sort of square and not totally soft.

Plus side, I know where I can poutine for my cravings, I just have to chase this truck down, and now I also know where I can get cheese curds in this city.  As we all know the grocery stores don't carry them.

The oysters are fresh, large and delicious! What a great find. We were staying at the hotel across the street, so we stumbled onto this place. Decided to be adventurous and get the Swamp platter. I highly recommend it. Everything was good, especially the frog legs!

My niece is in Broadway Dreams and she is very hardcore into counting calories. This place was a dream for her (they have a board with calories for everything) she literally ate here everyday for a week and I'm not kidding! I didn't mind because the food is DELISH! Pizza, sandwiches, soups, salads, anything you can think of! I don't really leave reviews but I just had to because of the manager Natalie. She knows what customer service is! We had an issue with our soup one day and threw it away (tasted like it was the bottom of the pot of soup it was end of the night when came in) We came in the next day told her it tasted funny and we were thinking we'd maybe get a free cookie or something.. No she comped our ENTIRE MEAL for 3 people! Super sweet people and great customer service! My niece loves the turkey light sandwich plus the best oatmeal raisin cookie I've ever had. I'm back home in Richmond, VA and missing one already :(

The food was decent tasting but came to us cold. We actually got our entrées first and then got our appetizers. The waitress was horrible with the service. Another customer or possibly friend of hers was more helpful to us getting our drinks and getting us things that we needed or even checking to see how we were doing. We don't think we'll ever return :/

This is a place that, for me, has been hit or miss.

When they hit, they hit a grand slam.

When they miss, it's the biggest miss ever.

In all fairness, their food is ALWAYS above average to VERY good.  Their pizza, especially, is stellar, and the burgers aren't bad.  Salads, while a tad pricey, are very good indeed and generally worth the money.

But the issue is with the service.  It's terribly inconsistent.  I've been there and had absolutely wonderful service.  And I've been there when you pretty much had to tackle a server to get ANYTHING.

So, based on that, they get a 2.  If I'm with friends and they want to go, I'll go there and not complain.  But I'll not make a special effort to go there.

I couldn't be happier with the Riviera Mansion - I am so glad we had our wedding there! First, it is so unique and cool - everyone raved about the space. It is the perfect representation of Santa Barbara...part mission and part glam. It is absolutely gorgeous and Breanna and the rest of the staff are all so easy to work with. I fully recommend the Mansion!!

Breanna is lovely and was always totally available to answer any questions I had, and she and the chef were so great when we sat down to do the tasting. The food was exactly what we'd hoped it would be, and they worked with us to make the menu perfectly us. I also really appreciate that the Mansion was so amenable to what we wanted to do décor-wise - we brought in tables, which meant a LOT of work for the staff, but they did an amazing job! And, speaking of the staff: I'm still getting comments from my family about how awesome the staff was - how attentive and nice they were. 

I'm so happy we had our wedding at the Riviera Mansion - it was perfect!!

I've been here more times than I can count. The food and service are always great. The dinner menu can get a bit pricey, especially if you order drinks too, so I mostly come by for lunch. I love the atmosphere during lunch on weekdays because it's never super crowded and it's a great time to relax and have an actual conversation with a friend without having to yell over music or other people talking. I've never been anything but pleased with Momos though, so I'm still willing to pay out for dinner on occasion. The Mahi Mahi and scallop risotto are particularly fantastic. Highly recommended, and they are almost always on groupon, if you want to try it without investing a lot of money.

This place is terrible. I ordered delivery through Grub Hub. The grilled fish tacos were cold and soggy. The enfrijolados were ok but cold! The salad was mediocre and wilted. I would not recommend ordering from here to anyone.
Got a flight of red wines (Pinot Noir, Cabernet and a Meritage.)  Not too impressive.  They are new so I will go back.  Right near the Speedway.

Good thing I bought a rubber cover for my key board, so as to keep the drool off.

Man, this place is a classic for breakfast.  My first impression is when it's filled with locals at 9am on Sunday that it had to be good.  I had the green corn waffles, and they don't need any syrup they are that good.  The chorizo was excellent as a side.

Very busy and rightfully so.  Service is quick and attentive.  Can't wait to return.

Awesome lunch!!!!! I haven't been here since they moved from their old location--- I've been missing out!

Walked in and were seated promptly by a sweet girl. Ordered water and breadsticks with marinara sauce. Bread was fresh and piping hot!!! Their menu is huge and meets all price points. 

Ordered kids cheese pizza (kids eat free Wednesday nights)- pizza looked AMAZING and my daughter loved it! It was huge for a kids menu item. Perk for having leftovers another day. 

I ordered their steak and cheese sandwich- it was huge and delicious. Served with a side of pasta. I was full after eating the sandwich and brought the pasta home for leftovers. 

My mom ordered the Italian stallion sandwich- which she raved about and was also huge. She ate half and brought home half with her side pasta. 

Our server was really nice and prompt with refills and service. I can't wait to come back and try more off their menu!!!

No bad.  I stop in from time to time for lunch when I am at work.  They have a good lunch special, two slices and a can of soda for like $4.99, cheaper than most lunch options around here.  I've only ahd the pizza thus far so if I ever try anything else, I'll add an update.

Regional chain that does breakfast and lunch right. The kids love the French toast and I omelettes and I am a big fan of their lunch. Chicken soup is phenomenal. Solid sandwiches, nothing too crazy or complicated, good service and even better food.

Best place for take-out breakfast around Roxborough/Manayunk area. I say take-out just because Mels is very small (like 3 tables or so and a very small counter.) So I usually call and order in advance and pick up my breakfast sandwich 10 mins later. My go-to is the simple bacon, eggs and cheese on a long roll. This sandwich is HUGE. If you're not too hungry, this can easily be shared. They put LOTS of crispy bacon on it (which is an A+ according to me). The prices are extremely reasonable and everything I've tried has been excellent. I would definitely recommend Mel's to anyone in the area looking for some good breakfast food.

Just ate a teriyaki chicken lunch bowl that was terrible. The chicken was full of fat and loaded with teriyaki and the white rice was sticky. I had to ask for a knife to dissect the chicken to be able to eat some of it. I will be surprised if my dog eats the leftovers that I bring him. Additionally, had to ask several times for water refills and it wasn't even crowded. Should have stayed with the cabbage salad only. 
Never again!
Great, laid-back atmosphere, terrific food. The ahi was good quality, as were the hummus and curry dip. We're going back for the peanut butter sandwiches.

I'm a huge fan of Mellow Mushroom!  I've been to at least 3 different ones in Atlanta, along with one in Winston-Salem, Raleigh, and Greenville, NC.  We love their pretzel appetizers, caesar, greek, and pepperoni pizza.  And the beer selection is always great.  But for some reason, the Brandon location has struggled on service.  The waitress we had was "out there".  We had to constantly remind her of drink refills.  And then we sat and watched our pizzas sit on the shelf for 10 minutes after coming out of the oven...while she ran the take-out register and chatted up the bartender.  The food was just as good as other locations...but the service...c'mon...customers visiting a pizza shop don't have high expectations to begin with.  I've had wet sponges with more personality.  They've got the food quality and kitchen staff...get rid of the service problems and this Mellow Mushroom will be the best in the pizza business for the Tampa area.
Breakfast burrito was good, very filling and at a great price! Service was super quick and I was out of there in less than 10 minutes.

We celebrated my daughter's 18th birthday here and we had a wonderful time.  We rented out the back room and Katherine (the event coordinator) took care of our every need.  The food was delicious (my husband is still talking about the mushroom soup!) and of course the cake was fabulous.
Good food, good service. Never an issue. Never a bad meal. A+ on price too. Pancakes are very good.
Great vibe, great drinks. Try the Only Child, a fancy take on a rum sour. Menu looked good but I didn't eat. Wish I did though...

I've been here more times than I can count. Their beef Lo mein is my favorite. Great crab rangoons. Fast and friendly! I usually order on my way to pick it up and it's ready by the time I get there 8 minutes later.

I went here per a neighbor's recommendation to get some good seafood during a recent visit to New Orleans.  I am amazingly thankful for the recommendation as I haven't had seafood this tasty in quite some time.  It was totally worth leaving the touristy areas to get some great seafood.

To start off, I had the raw oysters on the half shell.  Normally, I'm not a fan of warm water oysters.  But these were delicious.  The oysters were very fresh and shucked perfectly.  Even the husband, who refers to raw oysters as horse boogers, ate them and was impressed.  

As the main course, my party shared a basket of fried oysters & shrimp, as well as some boiled shrimp, crabs, crayfish, corn, garlic, and sausage.  Needless to say, we had quite the feast.  

I prefer my oysters raw, but the fried ones were pretty darn good and juicy.  But the boiled seafood is where it was at.  The shrimp were succulent and I appreciated the fact that the heads were left on.  The crayfish and crabs were good too.  One member of my party was impressed that we were given so many female crabs.  Apparently, female crab roe is a delicacy.  I tried it and it was OK.  But to each their own.

This is the best pho I've ever had.  I travel for work and I try pho every chance I get.  That being said, the best is when I come home and go to Pho An Hoa.  Best broth, tender meat, lots of noodles and  fresh veggies.

Color me convinced.  I hadn't looked at their prices online before I called up to place an order and it's probably good that I hadn't because I might not of called.  

My wife is a chef and used to run a bakery and is NEVER EVER satisfied with any cake I get for her birthday. ("I might as well bake my own!") So when I saw the good reviews I thought I'd call and see if they sell complete cakes for birthdays.  They do, and they are pretty freaking delicious.  

I got the 6" Chocolate Cherry cake (can't remember the cake name) for $75.  That's probably double the most expensive cake I've purchased for a family birthday party, but to be fair it was easily twice as good in every way.  To be crystal clear, I'm a complete cheapskate and what I got was worth the price.  This place is first class.  The box looks great, the cake looks great, it tasted even better than it looked and for once, my wife was more than satisfied with her birthday cake.  I wouldn't come here every day, but if you want to impress someone you love, you can't go wrong here.

We went here with very well traveled clients used to fine dining.  Cafe Ponte was exquisite.  Every course was outstanding.  The service was impeccable.  For fine dining in the area, Cafe Ponte is the place to go.  For fine cuisine the prices are quite reasonable.

The atmosphere and clientele at Coffeebar shifts with the hands of the clock, so don't let the fear of being the wrong "type" keep you from frequenting this spot, just wait an hour -- your people will show up. There's less posturing here, less imitation, than the likes of Hub Riverside, Bibo Record, or Old World Coffee; and more families, which can be credited to the location (nestled into a residential area), the selection of treats and decaffeinated drinks, and approachable staff. The open kitchen layout adds to the already home-y vibe. 

You can really settle into your seat, shamelessly, like a La-Z-Boy, without the pressure to see and be seen, making it an ideal workspace for students and telecommuters; though, if you choose to look up from your screen, there's bound to be a cutie somewhere. Evenings at Coffeebar are casual, too, but seem to attract couples (of all ages). I've overheard first dates, Mom & Dad "date nights," and had my own heart-to-heart dates with a close friend. It's a good place to meet up with someone from Tinder. Not that I'd know anything about that. 

Unlike other coffee shops open after dark, there are nights that you can walk in without the noise of amateur entertainers. Not that it's necessarily bad noise! There's no weekly schedule of open mic, trivia, et. al, which encourages a larger crowd when events DO happen, some recurring ones that come to mind are the latte art contest and monthly wine tasting. Speaking of the latte art contest, it's so nice to see baristas from different shops engaged in friendly competition. One time, my Coffeebar barista recommended the Hub! Now that's a healthy local economy. 

PS: The drinks are good! but more expensive now that Old World, Magpie, and Blue Whale are open...hoping that the "friendly competition" doesn't provoke gentrification, leaving Starbucks as the only joint with an affordable cup (and that would be saying something, right?). Maybe Reno needs a Dunkin' ;) Try the Lavender Latte, Matcha Latte or single espresso!
Not bad, not so spectacular either. A local version of panera bread, and slightly better. Salads are good, a few east coast sandwiches.

Horrible customer service from......no other than Alam the manager.  Then to top it off they didn't put the lid on but instead just placed it on top! I grab my coffee and turn around to leave and of course pop goes the lid and hot coffee pour out all over my arm hand and legs!!  Sorry alam but it's time to find a better career maybe pizza delivery boy?!?

Fast, friendly, delicious!!! Welcome to the neighborhood!!!

Standard American Chinese dishes. Made quickly, served hot, and yummy! Been here twice since they opened a couple weeks ago. Dining in is available, I think they have 8-10 booths, similar to a burger joint. No tables and chairs. It would make a great lunch stop, it's a relatively small place. 

Egg rolls are great, you can tell they are made with fresh ingredients. Not greasy, or mushy. The chicken batter is crispy, not soggy. 

Prices are relatively low compared to other Chinese restaurants in the area, but does not limit the quality.

To start off, this parking lot is a nightmare,  I saw multiple near fender benders during my attempt to get served at this Wendy's.  I was craving some chilli on a brisk fall morning and thought I'd run the through the drive thru and get a cup of Wendy's Famous Chilli.  I went during a time at which you can usually expect places to be a little slower.  The inside didn't seem to be packed but the drive thru was backed up almost nearly to the street.  I attempted to patiently wait for service to get the Chilli I craved, however, after 15 minutes of waiting there was still three cars between me and being able to place my order, let alone get to the service window to get my food.  The chaos in the parking lot was starting to increase as the line to the drive thru was blocking off the exit to the main road so I decided to simply turn off before being committed to the drive thru by the concrete curb that serves as a barricade between the rest of the parking lot.

Every time I'm in the area, I go to Makiman. Compared to other sushi places in the area, I find them to be one of the best. My favorite is Pete's roll. 

Although the service is not great, especially because the place is usually empty. But if you're just coming in to eat then it's not a deal breaker. 

They also have a lot of different rolls to choose from and the  decor is really nice and modern. 

If you have room for dessert then get the fried ice cream.

I love Mexican food and I think that is one thing the St. Louis area lacks,  good Mexican food. My husband and I tried this place for the first time last night and felt very satisfied. I'm a chips and salsa snob and have to say this place has the best chips and salsa around. Warm chips and delicious, not-too-spicy salsa. We also ordered the chorizo dip which was divine. My husband ordered the steak and chicken combo fajitas--they were great. I ordered the steak fajita chimi--it was okay. I didn't care for the beans and was a little disappointed about that because I usually love the side of beans. I also had a medium margarita which was a little strong,  but good. We had an awesome waiter who was attentive and friendly. 

Someone wrote a review on here about getting the Groupon, which we did and I'm so grateful for that! At the time I purchased the Groupon,  it was $28 for $45 worth of food. Great deal!! With all the food we ordered: chorizo dip, medium margarita, fajita chimi,  and steak/chicken fajita, our check was $45.30 (but of course, I just paid $28 using my Groupon). If you do purchase a Groupon,  make sure it is for the right location,  they will check.  Also, I don't think the Groupon can be used for tip so have extra $ for your server.

The Good:  The decor was great, fun tables where you remove your shoes and sit on cushions on the floor.  The food was great.  Samosas were VERY tasty, garlic naan was good, but it's hard to mess up garlic naan.  Ok.  Now on to 

The Bad:  The service was pretty miserable.  Very slow, inattentive, and a not particularly friendly or engaging waiter.  Five minutes after we ordered, he came back & told us "The kitchen just informed me that we are out of dal."  One of the most common Indian dishes.  He should have known that when he started his shift.  And it wasn't as if they had just run out -- there were only about 3 other occupied tables.  And this was EARLY on a Friday night.  And they didn't bring us a chutney tray until we asked.  It took forever for him to bring the bill, and forever for him to take it once we'd put our credit card down.  And they kept turning on these HORRENDOUS flourescent lights (this was at night and made it feel like a Seven-Eleven), albeit only for a few minutes at a time.  

While i MIGHT return for the food, i would hesitate due to the memories of the service.  I'll probably go back, though.  Maybe it was just an off-night, service-wise.

This anecdote well summarizes my experience.  A friend and I had lunch here.  When the waiter came over to the table midway through our meal and asked perfunctorily "How's everything?" both of us replied, "Frankly, everything is very salty!"  "A lot of people have told me that," our waiter replied.  "Well," I said, "Did you ever manage to go back to the kitchen and tell THEM?!"

Typical bar with bar food and clientele. Slightly above dive bar level, but not swanky by any means. Service was good. They had a DJ and the music was louder than it needed to be, but wasn't deafening. The drinks were good and they have different specials everyday, but were out of a lot of beers because their keg was broken or something. The food was decent, but nothing spectacular. The mozzarella sticks look a lot better than the way they taste, but the Mac and cheese balls and brisket sandwich were good. What did annoy me (and always annoys me anywhere it happens) is when I ask for a side of ranch and then get the check and find out I got charged for it. I get that it's not a lot of money, but it's ridiculous when an establishment is that petty that they need to charge an already paying customer who ordered a decent amount of food and drinks for a condiment to go with their bland food. That is what happened here and I find it to be a turn off. Oh, but don't worry the ketchup is free for those of you who like to violate your food with it...

The food came out fast, great ambiance for dinner and a very helpful waitress. I got the pepperoni pizza as it had high ratings and wasn't disappointed! My husband got the spicy ham (you can't split toppings so we got our own...leftovers:) which he said the toppings kept slipping off.

I would recommend. Fair prices, good service, tasty brick oven pizza.

By far the best Afghan restaurant in Philadelphia. My friends and I went there last night and we all LOVED what we ordered. I had the Sansom Kabob, which was perfection. From the meats, to the grilled tomato and onion, to the rice, each part of the dish was tastier than the last, every bite was full of wonderful flavors, and elegantly presented. I've had a lot of Afghan food at different restaurants and also home cooking with my family, and this is one of the best Afghan restaurants I've been to anywhere. Honestly, it was one of the best dining experiences I've recently had. The service was excellent and the ambience was charming and had a tasteful, traditional flare. The restroom was so impeccably clean: always a reassuring thing to see. I was already planning my next visit before I even finished my plate, and I can't wait to go back!

Such a disappointment in my book. We arrived about 12pm on a Sunday and were seated in about 3-5 minutes. That's about the only good thing I have to say. It took our server about 5 minutes to arrive at our table. He took our drink and food order. I lied, I have another good thing to say. Our food came out insanely fast. I ordered the Strawberry Crepes and a side of bacon. The bacon was delicious, cooked well and nice and thick. The crepes on the other hand were a huge let down. I'm sorry to say that Ihop's are better. My crepes were bland and lacked any filling. The powdered sugar and strawberry topping were non existent. Our server NEVER came back to the table until we were completely done and that was just to drop off the check. Never asked how everything was or even offer a refill. Breakfast is my favorite meal of the day and honestly, I've had better and could have saved money by going somewhere else. $4.50 for a side of bacon is a bit extreme, and $8 for the main meal with no additional side items is pretty steep. I can't recall a breakfast joint where I spent $32 for so little food (pancakes, crepes, 2 sides of bacon, & 2 drinks). I may be willing to try it again and maybe have a better experience, but it won't be anytime soon.

I really like this place. Reasonable prices for the large portions. I love BBQ sauce, I put it on everything, so I really like places like this that have BBQ sauce readily available in many different flavors. I've had 2 sandwiches, both were delicious. I've tried a bunch of different sides too; all were good.

It has never been busy. Been there for lunch and dinner, and both times it's awkwardly empty; maybe 15 tables at dinner, and 3 at lunch. Not complaining though, because that just means more attention from the waitress. I just hope it stays in business.

This was my first time at District Donuts and the hype from my friends made me really excited to try it.

First- I lucked out with parking in the lot attached. I think there are around 15 spots back there, and it's a little tight. 

Second-I really like the atmosphere of District Donuts - it was like this urban hipster (in the absolute best way) place. 

Third- umm...YUM!! The donuts are so creative and Ssoooo good. I had a jelly donut and my friend ordered the tiramisu. Both were awesome. My friend's tasted exactly like the dessert. It was awesome. 

We also ordered coffee drinks. I got a delicious vanilla latte. It took a little bit of time for the drink to be made, but it was actually nice to enjoy my donut in the restaurant. 

The line seemed was not that bad when I got there around 9:30 on a Saturday. It goes fast :)

Overall thoughts: yum. I'll go there again for sure.

Ended up here on a Friday just as a walk in.  We were able to get seated immediately (which isn't easy for Media) but were brought into this tiny room in the basement with no windows and so full of tables they have to be breaking a fire code.  The food was really good, but we couldn't really have a conversation because the sound from the 16 other people shoved into the 10 by 10 cement room was so loud.  

I'd definitely go back because all four of us had outstanding meals but insist on not sitting in that room of lost souls (or just people without reservations).

Visiting Edmonton for the weekend and we decided to go for some good ol' bowling. We got here and right away was met with a person who either decided right away she didn't like our group or just really hates her job. We immediately felt like an annoyance to her already long day even though we just got here. We kept having some technical problems with our lane so that really didn't help ease our situation. The 2 stars is solely for the bar staff and our awesome server.

As mentioned by other Yelpers the food, location and wonderful decor are standout but what sets Clear Sky on Cleveland (CSC) apart is Service with a capital S.  

My mission was to hit the CSC happy hour and then catch a show at the Capitol theater across the street after driving in rush hour traffic from Orlando.

I looked at my watch as I crossed the threshold and it was 5:58 with happy hour ending at 6 pm.  The host directed me to the bar for the fastest service and the server quickly placed my order of drinks and appetizers.  For the record happy hour is 2-6 pm and they offer drink specials and half priced hummus, falafels and naan (flat) breads.

We got there just at shift change and as we sat at the bar, Kayla took over as our server.  I was a little concerned because of the previous server's efficiency but Kayla is a star.  She is the perfect combination of efficiency, helpful and is charming - just fun to be around.  She helped describe menu items, she offered info and when I made a bad choice (she had provided info but I had already made up my mind) removed the item from my check.

Here is what we ended up with.  They have 8 naan flat breads and we chose the sausage and broccolini as well as the mushroom and herb.  Both outstanding choices and I could not pick a favorite.  We also got the hummus which was excellent but very filling.

I ordered the cottage pie and it was not to my liking.  I think they could have a better title but it was more like a stew as Kayla had mentioned with a lump of mashed in the middle.  It had a lot of celery and did not match my Irish idea of cottage pie.

So here is the break down:

Pro
-Great food - lots of apps as well as entrees, burger, sandwiches and flatbreads.  I think there are a lot of appetizers and picking several apps is the way to go especially with groups.  There are many interesting choices.
-Good wine - generous pours even at happy hour and the wine is good quality
-Interior decor and al fresco dining is modern, clean and interesting.  The bathrooms were spotless and decoration of the stalls is fun
-Happy hour offers food and wine at really great prices
-Service and really caring about the customers.  After I ordered an item and sent it back they comp'd me a piece of pie for dessert.  I mean I felt bad for sending something back and they went over the top to make it right.  I dine out a lot and this is exceptional

Cons
-There is a concert venue across the street.  It was quiet when we got there but I saw the place quickly fill up and the crowd cleared out right before the show.  Plan accordingly for the best service. 
-They have a lot in back and there is on street parking with meters until 6 pm.  Again with the concert venue I could see parking a block or so away and walking.  It's worth it.  Ruth Eckerd uses the Captiol Theater for smaller venue shows.  

We have another trip planned to Clearwater and I will go out of the way to dine at Clear Sky on Cleveland once again.

Really cheap? Pretty fast delivery? Open late? Yes to all three.

Is the food good? Not really. We were either outright unhappy (one dish went into the trash untouched) or just unimpressed with China Star. The fried rice was nothing special, and the egg drop soup was totally bland. Probably there are better Chinese takeout spots around here.

This is a great date place. I really enjoyed the atmosphere...they had a live jazz playing and it was dimly lit on the inside. They also had a porch outside which we really enjoyed for people watching and relaxing, not to worry...you can hear the live music from the outside too :).

I ordered a Farmer's Market Gimlet to start off with, it was really good, not too sweet and garnished with Rosemary.

We got the mussels as an appetizer. That was honestly the BEST part of our meal. Order the mussels! You won't regret it, they were delicious! Served on a hot plate, still sizzling.

I ordered the meatballs bolognese...it was ok, honestly the pasta was a little over cooked and I felt it lacked in the seasoning department but it did not take away from the experience, the mussels were still on my mind :)

We also ordered the BLT salad with blackened chicken. I cannot say enough good things about that salad...the chicken was basically herb crusted, the mustard drizzle was just the right amount of tangy and spicy and it complemented the tomatoes and fresh mozzarella...then there was the bacon...I do t know what sweet glaze it had on it but it was delicious! 

We will definitely be returning and trying out more things on the menu...and of course ordering the mussels again!

Stopped in for some late dinner and sat at the bar. The bartender was more interested in preparing to close than waiting on us. Food is OK. M
Nice daily specials. I live in Springfield and have eaten there s few times. I have had to send food back twice which I rarely do. Nice sports bar if I was rating only that it be 3 stars.

It lives up to its name! I had the Dad's Green Chili Burger and fried pickles. My wife had the Gateway Burger and fries. Plus we had the $1 ice cream cones. Everything was amazing! Get in the car and go there now!!!

Let me tell you, this place had the potential to be 5 stars. We REALLY wanted it to be our spot. Our normal spot Salty Rim Grill recently closed and we were looking for a new spot on the water to be our new regular go to. 

At first this place had all the makings to be that spot. Beautiful view, food was really good, drinks were tasty. But the service. My god the service was sooo bad. We read a lot of reviews about how the service sucked but you never know maybe it's just one person right? Wrong. 

EVERYTHING took forever. From sitting down to being greeted, to getting the food, to getting more drinks, to trying to get our bill. Which btw we bought a voucher on Yelp which not only did the waitress not know how to do but neither did the manager. Oh yeah and it took 15 minutes for the manager to come out after the waitress said she had to get him for the voucher. Then I got the bill, it was wrong. We waited forever again and finally I went inside. I found the waitress and waited for her while she ignored me as she entered bills. Finally I get her attention and tell her the bill is wrong. She says to me "did you tell your waitress?" I go "you were our waitress..." wow.  Saw the manager again so flagged him down. He finally fixed it and I had a conversation with him. Told him about how the food was great and so was the view and we were hoping to make it our normal spot but the service was so bad we won't be coming back (did I mention there was almost no other customers in the place?) He said he appreciated the feedback but just made a bunch of excuses. New staff, he was in the kitchen, etc. listen it could just be an off day but he didn't even seem like he cared at all. Never tried to make it right. Nothing. 

So there you have it. Like I said food was great, good view, they had a live band which was good. But horrible service is a deal breaker. We won't be back. Too bad, so much potential. But you HAVE to care about your customers.

PS. Get some umbrellas on the patio so we don't have to melt in the sun. I don't mind it as I love the sun and heat but my wife and son really felt horrible by the end. Maybe that's cause we were there so long waiting for service...

This menu was extensive and unique, not that there weren't traditional items on the menu, but everything seemed to have a good little twist to it.   We ordered the pasta rustica and the lamb burger with fries.  The braised beef in the pasta was tender and delicious.  The whole dish was made of simple ingredients, but they worked perfectly together.  The lamb burger cooked medium rare was one of the best I've had in town.  My girlfriend doesn't care for lamb burgers much, but she had about a third of this one and said she'd order it again for herself.

Overall great atmosphere, great menu, large portions, and a good wait staff.  We'll definitely be coming back

Arrived at 8:30 on a Sunday night and sat at the bar.  Ordered an old fashion and St Elmo Cola.  The St Elmo only requires a splash of the cola that is served with it.  Had the french onion soup and it was fantastic.  The onions melted in my mouth.  For dinner I tried the 6oz filet, melt in your mouth delicious.  I tried the cheesecake and it was similar to others.  Loved the conversation with the bar staff, engaging and relaxed.

This is a hidden gem off Maryland Way! Food is good. Daily specials certainly are attractive (Burger & fries 6.99, .75 wings, 6.99 Philly cheese, etc...) Service is always friendly but sometimes slow.

This place never disappoints.  Fresh veggies, meat, sauces, noodles or rice.  The home made bread is addictive, so be careful or you'll fill up before your food arrives.  And don't forget to tip the chef.
This is the worst restaurant in tampa waiters are rude they don't answer you properly they pretend that we are buzy but they are not never suggest to anyone

Very disappointed this time. Been coming here for years!! Salmon and steak portions, reduced more then half. Salty Salty!! If you have High cholestrol, watch out!  Fried rice was bland... 9 people 2 eggs in that large of portion! Really! So asked to put in another egg, charge $2 for 1 egg!! Still no flavor! Could not understand our cook. English was terrible. Our server was very good! So prices went up and portions and quality went down... very sad. Was a great place for Hibachi at one time.

Pretty good place for dinner, with lots of selection and variety. Their sushi offerings are pretty extensive, and the quality is not bad. They also have hot pot available, soft tofu (though I heard it's not so great), and lots of hot dishes. The fried chicken wings are great!

Wouldn't mind checking it out again sometime
I am so thrilled Sushi Sho has opened in St. Pete. This is far and away the best sushi experience in the Bay Area.  Try everything and leave a very happy sushi eater.

The only reason I went was because I got a coupon in the mail and the ad boasted lots of seafood. Even with that I should of stayed away. This may seem like a lot of food but I took a little bit of each. I didn't try any sushi because they only had about 6 different kinds and none of them looked appetizing. Shrimp dumplings were gross. The pork dumplings were undercooked. The chicken on a stick was bland. Pork ribs were bland as well. There was something called chicken fingers but in actuality they were chicken feet. I'm not joking, chicken friggin feet. Lo mein was gross. Blue crabs smelled like someone took a poo in it. Stuffed clams had no taste. Shrimp balls were odd. The spring roll was just ok, the pork egg roll was gross, I didn't even finish it. The sui mei was so horribly disgusting it tasted like someone farted in my mouth. The chicken wings were bad because they had some kind of weird batter on them. Even the snow crabs weren't good and even though I got some as soon as they came out, by the time I got back to my table they were cold. I don't even think there was shrimp in what was supposed to be fried shrimp, n no cocktail sauce to speak of. And even though they had stuff to make a salad, I couldn't find any salad dressing. The only good thing I had was the nilla wafer pudding, but I'm sure you can buy the same thing in a store. This was my first and last time here. Do yourself a favor and go somewhere else, or eat a can of dog food which I'm sure will be more enjoyable. If they served this garbage to inmates it would be considered cruel and unusual punishment. I should of just stuck with my usual place, Hibachi Grill and supreme buffet in Cinnaminson which is far far superior. That's the way a buffet should be handled.

Decided to give this place a try after I was craving a good cuban. My go-to Cuban spot is Big Stein's down the road, but wanted to try something new. They definitely have a lot of options and is a a very cute restaurant. I got the lunch special which was the Hot Honey Turkey wrap (pressed). I was kind of confused when my bill came out to $10 when the lunch special was $6.99, but I'm assuming that's because I got the soup as my side. The soup, by the way, was cold. It's just an assumption that my soup would be hot, because well it's soup so that was disappointing. I will give this place another try for breakfast - seemed like they had a lot of good options and its served all day. My wrap was good but didn't have enough turkey.

HORRIBLE! this place gives meaning to the word crap! This place is in a great spot next to the airport. I work next to the airport and mentioned I was going there to eat and everybody tried to talk me out of it but I went anyway. The food was dry and tasteless and the place needs a good cleaning. Stay away...far away from this place!

The ambience is nice and there are several small touches making the service nice.  I had the veggie quesadilla with zucchini and it was good,  not super flavorful,  but still good. The salsa is tasty!  
The beans delivered with the meal in one little bowl to a booth of 6 people is strange and no one even touched them.  Either deliver with the chips and salsa and more than one bowl for booth of 6 (easier logistics to share) or skip.

Not good at all ... Ate there 2 weeks ago on Sunday ... Ordered 2 pounds of Alaskan king crab .. $60 per pound and there were disgusting and freezer burned ... We also ordered a bunch or other seafood ... Blue crabs ... Snow crab... Bill was just as much as eating at Barclay prime ... And we had no drinks !!! I will never eat there again ... Even if it were free ... I would not go back ...

Good food but when they are busy they take forever and if u call and complain they say the food is on it's way. Took and additional hour after that! Food was cold and the customer service was horrible needless to say I stopped ordering from here.

I have been here twice, and both times I was really impressed with the food. I ordered the same meal both times, the grilled chicken grande burrito. It is amazing! Also, the rice is fresh and really good.

A Gaybourhood institution! used to be a lot more fun... now rather tired.  

The food is rather decent, though a pit pricey.  I do like that one can order a salad with a burger rather than fries.  The guacamole is an embarrassment, but as a whole everything is OK.

It's the server that will make or break the experience.  There is this one chap that has been there for ages and I reckon it's because he gives the guys who frequent the place something to salivate over.  I for one am more impressed with my server's work ethic than looks.  

One one occasion, I asked for more napkins... didn't get them, another time needed an extra fork... not happening either.  Never got a refill on Iced Tea.  I once had to even ask the other server for the check because apparently he didn't feel like getting that for us either.  

If you get any other server, you'll have a decent experience as none of the others have as much 'tude.   Still, there are better places out there.
Loved the food, drinks and ambiance. Very good service too. Tableside guacamole is outstanding.  Salsa different and delish. Sauces were wonderful as well. Will visit again!

Came here for Collingswood Restaurant Week; I had been to another Sabrina's location years ago but hadn't had the chance to try this one.  I ordered the vegetable spring rolls-great crunch and flavor, the braised short rib over risotto-large portion and meat was cooked nicely but the risotto was slightly bland, and the mini churros-so delicious and perfect size to end a large meal.

This place has a huge menu and while we were there tons of other kinds of food kept coming from the kitchen. I definitely want to come back and try their breakfast options!

Had lunch here today, while working nearby!  Just a simple pulled pork sandwich and some potato salad... and I left HAPPY! Service was awesome... really friendly staff, and it smells like carnivore heaven in there! 

The pulled pork was good, lots of flavor and very tender. The potato salad? OMG! Some of the best I have had... creamy and tart, and sweet.... just yummy! 

I will be going back.. when I am not time constrained... because I want to eat at least one whole rack of their ribs all by myself! And try some of the other assorted goodies on that menu!

Wonderful stuff! But you don't want to go there... trust me. If you don't go... there will be more for me!   :)

highly recommended!

Top Tomato is right near where I work, so after trying the rest of the pizza places within the three block radius of my office, this is my main go-to spot for pizza because it's the best I've found! The slices are large and they have a lot of variety in their offerings.  I love their red top pizza (sauce on top, cheese on bottom) but I've also had the Mediterranean pizza (spinach, feta, chunky tomato sauce, mozzarella) the Jersey Tomato pizza (chunky tomato sauce, mozzarella) and the plain is great too! I haven't tried a lot of the menu items besides the pizza, but I have had their italian and also tuna hoagies and they are great.  Not on a traditional hoagie roll but it looks like they may bake their own rolls, which are delicious. 

Also, the staff is very friendly and I've been there so much they greet me and know what I order.  

I am not sure about the reviewer who thinks Top Tomato is more expensive than NYPD - I go to NYPD too and I'm pretty sure their slices are a tad more expensive - but not enough to really matter.  It's Philly and you'll generally pay $2.50 -  $3 for a plain slice and more for one with toppings wherever you go.

Stopped in here on the way back to DC, after reading the reviews on Yelp. I always look for great places to eat outside of chain food restaurants. I have to say, my tummy was very pleased!!! I'm a big French toast fan and I have to say, they nailed it!! The eggs were scrambled and cooked to perfection. I loved the home fries that were flavored just right. 

The service was excellent! Very friendly and food came out pretty quickly. Prices are very reasonable and the settings of the restaurant are nice as well. I would highly recommend to others looking for a great breakfast spot!

Can't say enough good things about Famous Dave's restaurant. Their menu has a wide selection, their atmosphere has a good vibe, their prices are very fair, and their staff is excellent. Our waitress came out and gave us a sauce sample (which had a very cute presentation) and since it was our first time there, we even left with a complimentary bottle of their barbecue sauce. Definitely take the time to stop by Famous Dave's!
Meh. I think maybe Tampa bay just doesn't have great indian food? Is that why there's such good reviews? I've been here for the lunch buffet a few times and am just not impressed. It's just ok.

Food was great. Service was poor. I went for my Dads birthday and we were rushed out the whole time. The server literally took the menu from my hands before asking if I was ready to order. Not expected from a fine dining restaurant.

There was a time I would have given Tryst 5 stars. Food was good, drinks reasonably priced and the house music best in town. During a recent visit July 7th the shift manager and wait staff had such the attitude - I found them to be pompus, arrogant and outright repugnant. The menu has erroded over the years from interesting to "safe". I guess the owner has lost his european flair and this now "just another place". Save your money and go the  champaign bar next door. Interesting food, great wine and champaign selection, attentive service and you can still enjoy the music from Tryst - its only 20 ft away.

If you are making a Mexican meal this is the best store for it. The meat is reasonable and there are so many things on sale here. Don't go by the ads on this place for sales. There are far more sales that they don't publish. I mean one month I got four stick of real butter for $1.49 a pack  This is my favorite place to shop. The only reason that I didn't give it five stars is because I think pulling their deli was BS.

Maybe it was just me - but nothing about my experience here was worth repeating.

From reading the other reviews, I guess it's better if you're ravenous!  But there are much better places that showcase St. Louis cuisine and are still within walking distance of all the downtown venues and Arch  

I'd head to Washington Ave. downtown, or head down to Soulard / Benton Park for better eats.

I want to LOVE this place. Like full on just F'n LOVE it.
Here is what I do love about-
The pepperjack cheese sticks, The sriracha dipping sauce is just the right kind of spicy and damn good. The cheese sticks could stand alone but that dipping sauce makes it one of my favorite appetizers in all of Reno.
Their burgers are outstanding. Juicy, flavorful, cooked to order, one of Reno's best.
The fact that it used to be Carrow's actually makes it cooler to me. Maybe I'm just a nostalgic fool but I like that it's been remodeled and not just tore down.
The beer selection is really good, like that they focus on local brews.
The crazy hunky bartender that looks like he could be Jason Momoa's brother. He is funny, engaging and damn fun to gaze at. Hubba.
I want to LOVE IT, but I just can't.
The service is just too hit and miss. Some visits (I've made about a dozen) the service is outstanding, others have been horrible. Almost like there is no middle ground.
The chicken Caesar salad can be really good but sometimes the chicken is drier than the playa in August.
And as referenced in a few other reviews, the prices are a bit high for the type of food they serve. 
So, it's a solid well deserved 4 stars instead of the 5 I want to give but can't bring myself to.
But hey, now they have room to grow!

Don't bother stopping in here - I did you the favor of trying it out and am here to report our visit left a lot to be desired.

We tried the first two breakfast burritos. I'm pretty sure they are microwaved.

My bf commented the coffee tasted like a hotel coffee-really watery and bland. I ordered a cafe au lait and it was probably the worst one I've ever had. Taste and Calvin Fletcher Coffee Co make this drink the intended way, and it is a completely different beverage than what I was served here.

Two women walked in after my boyfriend and I had been seated for 5-10 minutes and their food was brought out before ours was.

This place might as well be a starbucks.  Very disappointing.

I love wine, so this is a favorite spot for me.  I have met a date many times here during happy hour for a glass of wine (or more), accompanied by some classy appetizers.  If you're a fan of wine and cheese, this is the spot for you.  I never have a full dinner here, but it's a great place to sip a glass of wine, have delicious fancy snacks, and chat with friends. The atmosphere is hip.  When you get a two person table, it also has a romantic and intimate vibe, which makes it good for a date.  Highly recommended!

Something about being drunk on bourbon screams eat fried chicken at the end of the night. The first time I had it my friend was force feeding it down my throat at 4:00 a.m after I had thrown up a daiquiri from this same establishment (don't be like my please). I knew it was good but the second time around and I ordered my own plate I realized how good it actually was. They have these sauces on the table and the orange looking one was sooooo good drunk me wanted to take the bottle back with me to Texas. The biscuits were so good my friend literally ordered a whole box. I honestly can't wait to get back to NOLA and get some more of this goodness.

If I could rate a business 6 stars, I would! This place is wonderful! Some of the best coffee I've had, with the largest selection of regular and sugar free syrups!  The owner is incredibly sweet and nice, and offered to make me another coffee if I wasn't 110% happy with my flavor choices!  And, this place is priced fairly as well! My fiancé and I will be flying home in 2 days, but we will definitely be back tomorrow to enjoy this wonderful place again!
The only reason I give this 3 stars is because of the ambience. The drinks were poorly made and muddled and the staff communicated poorly, making ordering drinks difficult and off-putting.

After reading the previous reviews I decided to try it out and was surprised by how disappointed I was. The staff was great, very welcoming and friendly, however the food was not. I ordered the Gabagool grinder with fries and a side salad. The salad was fine, but everything else was very dry/hard. The meat on the sandwich was very tender and tasty though, so I took it off the hard bread and tossed it in my salad. Unfortunately, I was not impressed, maybe it's because I got takeout? Regardless, I will not be returning.

Are you kidding me. That's how this review is starting out. "Fast and easy service for curbside" is a joke. I was out there parked in a curbside spot for 20+ minutes PAST my "order ready" time. I had to call them for them to notice my car parked out there to tell me "oh yeah it's ready!" HA. My food better not be cold. Once the girl brought my food out to me, all I got was an "we're really busy" and walked away. I'm sorry, but what? That's all you're going to offer? Not even a free drink or a "I'm sorry?" Absolutely DO NOT recommended coming here.
Perfect fried chicken. Yummy mustard greens and beans. Mac N Cheese was bland. Will definitely go back next time I am in New Orleans.

Yum. Everything we ate was so good. I highly recommend the shrimp and grits. So good. The oysters were amazingly fresh and a great deal during happy hour. The onion tart was a really interesting, different type of appetizer. Salads were fresh and high quality too.

Good atmosphere for friends, family, happy hour after the big game, or for date night.

Great place with good service. Highly recommend.

First time eating here. Food was great - sandwiches and sides. Tomato basil was super fresh and rich- delish. Very fresh, cheesy, customizable. Even a BYO-salad for healthier options. Staff was super helpful with options, menu, checking in on us at the table. Great experience. Will definitely be back!

First time here.  Do NOT be discouraged by outside of building.  Place is CLEAN inside and the food is GREAT!  My husband had the tilapia, rice and peas, & plantains.  I had the jerked chicken, carrot rice and cabbage.  Both meals were wonderful and the service was exemplary.  Servings were plentiful, price is good and, again, the food was great.  We will be back again and again.  Excited to find this restaurant.

This review is based solely on food.  I'm Mormon, and Mormons don't drink (theoretically). But let me fill you in on a little secret-- not drinking means you indulge in food that much more because really, it's all you have to cling to. 

Village burger, duck fat frites WITH cheese sauce.  Pickled beets with ricotta and olive tapenade. Perfect in their simplicity, each and every item.

Service sucks but I liked the food so much I don't really care. It's the size of a tuna can in this place and it's a bar so I wasn't expecting super attentive service, but it was borderline obnoxious.  Perhaps when you aren't tossing back drinks and racking up your tab the server isn't too pleased you're taking up a table? I can understand.  I'm guessing on the weekends it's out of control, but on a weeknight it was tolerable and we didn't have to wait for a table.

Could do without the appetizers that were a bit greasy and nothing great but, fish first courses were both great- a shrimp one and one with hamachi. The lamb curry was good- but more of a gnocchi dish than meat focused dish. Pepper pot ok.  Every few minutes someone tried to take our dishes away. First the bread and our bread dishes- even when there was still bread on them- we had to stop them. Then, our drinks- which weren't finished and throughout the meal they kept asking if were were done and trying to grab our plates. Very weird. Still, enjoyed the food.

great breakfast place. never been here for lunch or dinner but for breakfast it's very good. They have great bacon and the prices are reasonable. Always have the food out quickly too which I like. Its always busy for a reason and its spotlessly clean. 
My step father had the chicken fried steak that he said was the best he's ever had. The biscuits and gravy were excellent. 

You can't miss for breakfast!

This is one of the nicer and cleaner McDonalds I have been to!  They even had a couple of touch screens that allow you to order and skip the normal line.   The bathrooms and seating area is clean.  They also still have hazelnut iced coffee, which some locations have discontinued!  The only thing is that the cinnamelts we ordered for breakfast were kind of dry and not very warm. :(

I wrote a review last year and want to update it.  This is my second time getting a cake here and both times I have found that Evelhyinne was a pleasure to work with - she was kind, accomodating and willing to work within my budget.  The cake she made was amazing.  I was really so happy with how my order turned out, and it was very reasonably priced.  My son loved his cake and cupcakes.  This place is definitely a hidden gem.  Thank you!

Average sushi. Horrible service. Just ordered on Uber eats and the food took 30 minutes longer than estimated. Essentially took an hour and a half to get my dinner. When I called the restaurant to check on the order, they were not helpful at all.

Reasonably priced, laid back, easy. I prefer my tacos with corn tortillas, so really these are burritos with flour tortillas (if you wanna get technical).  Good sangria. Loved the buffalo chicken taco innards. Nice people.
Good food. Good service. Nice people. Fat guy portions. What more do you need? I had a salad and everyone else got sandwiches and burgers. Good stuff!

I ordered from Chef's Market for a small corporate event. I had the whole process and menu confused, but they(Debbie) worked with me as much as she could to get something that was perfect for my event.  The sandwiches, chips, and salad were all great, and the gourmet cookies got rave reviews.  I couldn't be happier with the service, helpfulness, and quality of this organization and its products.  

*highly recommend"

The cakes are delicious but extremely over priced. I've had better cakes at better prices and I don't find this place to be worth the money unless you are going for specifically the environment. Coffee is also very overpriced. Gorgeous interior though. If there's one thing you do try, try the Caramel cake.

I went in as a fan of Chicago-style pizza, which 312 advertises itself as specializing in.  Maybe I'm not fully versed in the details of Chicago-style, but I was slightly disappointed in a few details.  First, however, the ambiance and service were great.  I arrived about 6pm on a Tuesday and found a place to park right on the street outside.  My waitress was charming and attentive, so no problems there.  I ordered a deep-dish 10" cheese & pepperoni, expecting to eat half there and take the other half home.  My waitress warned me they take a while to cook - app. 45 minutes.  Which it did. Good thing I wasn't starving.  When the pizza came, there was plenty, but the sauce...oh, the sauce!  Tomato sauce dripping from every conceivable spot on the pizza, overwhelming the taste of the cheese and even the pepperoni.  And the crust was surprisingly hard, as if overdone.  But it was definitely thick with cheese and definitely filling.  I still have yet to eat my leftovers so my opinion may change slightly, but I doubt I'll be coming back.

Oh, and the price - $20 for a 10" one-topping pizza.  I bit the bullet because it sounded so good, but my total bill was almost $30 and definitely not worth what I got.

UPDATE: Apologies for getting a couple of factual items incorrect.  I went back and re-looked at the online menu to get my facts straight.  It was indeed a 12" pizza, and the price was $17.  With an iced tea, tax, and tip my total bill came to right about $30.  Probably not out of line, but less than satisfied with final product as indicated above. I apologize for any mischaracterization of the value.

Love Makiman. I come here at least once a month and have never been disappointed with the food or service. It's not some posh or swanky sushi bar, but the sushi is some of the best in the city (I eat sushi 1-2 times per week). They've got a huge variety of really great fushion-rolls. Must try: NE Viking, Cap'n Crunch, Sixers, and Caterpillar. It's surprisingly affordable for the quality of the sushi, and it's a BYOB. What's not to love?!
Great food and owner is a nice personable young man.  Highly recommend this restaurant.
50's diner and sports bar, good breakfast for normal prices. This place is packed as hell on sundays so expect a short wait for a seat.

I don't know or care to know about the restaurant side of this place.

All I want is my bag of crawfish, (maybe some mushrooms, corn, and potatoes) and to scuttle back to my hotel room, where I will eat them all while watching "say yes to the dress".

I keep going here, I keep loving it, I keep wanting more. 

I know you locals say there is a season to crawfish, that some months they are better and other months you want to stay away. But I am from the frozen north, from the land of the ice and steel grey skies. I will eat any and all mudbugs that you feel are lacking.


That is all.
Unbelievable market with Italian wines, homemade pastas and a great grocery!
An ok place. Music is nice, calamari was not the best, but the piña colada was great...
Our family of four really enjoyed the atmosphere and food here.  Our waitress was friendly and efficient, and the baby back ribs and sides were delicious.  We will be back!

Love this place! The sushi is delicious, so fresh, so yummy! You can bring your non-sushi eating friends, their noodle bowls are delicious too. The service is great, and the stuff is friendly. I love that I don't have to drive into the city for great sushi.

Beautiful, modern facility with a ton of options other than bowling. Instead of a rehearsal dinner for our wedding, we did a game night with our families here. The event planner for the space gave us two lanes at a discounted rate with food options. Everyone had a great time enjoying the lanes, bar, chess table and foosball.

First time to try seafood crepe and it was delicious, loaded with shrimp  and crab meet , and dill on the top giving it a different experience, definitely recommend it for breakfast and lunch,y wife had the belt eggwich and she said it is full of flavors and delicious.

I was impressed the minute I walked in, and I left even happier.

Very clean and modern inside, not the usual drab interior of a local Chinese restaurant. The service was very attentive and nice, and we ordered quickly.

The Food? Very good quality, I was very happy with my dish and appetizer. Since I'm a fan of Chinese food, I always order hot tea, and it was also good.

This is one of my new favorite local restaurants!
This is really good food. I've had better in New York City but this is really tasty. I got the combo meat salad. Hard to beat five bucks for dinner.
Great local Mexican with real, real horchata. Had a really good carne asada gotta with great salsa, all 3 heat levels.

Chop Stix is like a mini PF Changs...similar food and quality, nice atmosphere, great servers, food comes out fast. The happy hour from 3-5pm is awesome, great appetizer prices and adult beverages. As of this review, local hotel guests receive a discount. The servers and cooks are very open about changing up the menu for your dish. The food is really good.

I leave very close to Mood and it is one of my favorite places in West Philly. The Salad Chaat is my fave and it's even better when you add chicken. The rice pudding they keep in the fridges opposite of the counter is killer.

We went to Farmhaus last weekend for probably the 10th-15th time.  As always, the food was amazing.  The mushroom salad was very tasty and the breakfast was as wonderful as always.  It is definitely one of my favorite meals there-or anywhere.  

In the past, I would have given Farmhaus five stars and moved on.  

However, after we sat, we were informed of the chef's tasting menu-a new addition since the last time we had been there.  All was good and the menu looked great.  Out of our party of four, we definitely had 1-2 people interested in this tasting menu, particularly because their morel mushroom pasts could only be ordered off this menu, not the regular menu.  
The problem is that Farmhaus insists that each person at the table order a tasting menu if one person does.  Well, not everyone wanted a tasting menu!  We had a person with us recovering from the flu and he inquired whether he could split a tasting menu as he had little appetite and just wanted a bite of food.  Nope, each person had to order their own.  So we had 2 people who wanted the tasting menu (at over 50 dollars) and two who did not.  Any flexibility?
