Our waiter was helpful. He broke down the menu for us, said I asked tons of questions which I do, and he answered them very well. Hubby picked a N.Y. Strip and I picked the grilled jerk swordfish w papaya rum butter sauce. 
Guess what happens shortly after that?  Electricity went out! That's never happened to us at a restaurant. Ok. What's next? We just chilled a bit. We received table lamps, and the menus were lit.  Everyone had their calm professional demeanor with us. I'm sure they were really freaking out to death. Much of the surrounding businesses were out from the storm. Someone said someone hit a light pole. No idea. Florida is weird. It could be the case. Lights came on 15 minutes later, and food had not stopped coming out so I guess they were fine in the kitchen. Cool!
Management was so professional. Went to every single table, apologized for any inconvenience. I thought that was really nice that they did that.
While we were waiting, we were still able to see the fish swimming in the tank. There was light there. Weird feeling to have no electricity, but it worked out fine, and there were no mishaps.
Our food came out soon. my hubby's steak came with truffled mashed potatoes, & he changed the veggie option to coconut rice. It was perfect. Seriously, it was juicy and flavorable, and the right temperature and color.  My jerk swordfish was very good with the papaya rum butter sauce. I think it's more of a salsa to me w cubes of cut up papaya. I would ask for extra if I were you. It's that good. I was concerned that the jerk seasoning would be spicy, but w each bite of the sauce it was perfect. My waiter also said, if it ended up being spicy, he would make sure to make me a new one. He was really good and helpful. My dish came w coconut rice and red beans. It was a plate which I could not make at home so it proved to be an excellent choice. I washed it down with a "tanked"cocktail with tropical juices, mango rum, and bitters. Perfect.
We were celebrating my birthday weekend. Hubby let my waiter know about my birthday, and after we finished our entrees, my happy birthday dessert came with salted caramel ice cream and lava cake. Yes that was perfect too.
Afterwards... ahh, we had a great dinner and great service, we had to kill time at the restaurant. With the pouring rain, it was fine, we checked out the cave. You don't have to eat at the restaurant to see the fishes. Just go through the cave. There are so many picture opportunities. Everything is bright and pretty. The sting ray is smiling from the ceiling. I guess he likes the edges. The nurse shark is small.  It looks like it's like a stuffed animal because of its shape. Check out the irridescent colorful fish and the see through school of fish family. All the descriptions of the fish are there. You will not have to guess.
Before you leave, you can see if there's a band in the bar, or watch some sports on the flat screen tv. Lastly, shop for some Guy Harvey apparel, or make an appointment to swim in the tank.
This is a great place for a nice occasion, or just a night out. Children are welcome and will love the fish tank. You don't need to sit to close, with sitting a bit further you can better see the top of the tank. I am happy to have finally checked out Rum Fish Grill. Food is tasty, service was great, and fish tank, and Guy Harvey art was vibrant and fun.
Wonderful fresh flavors!  Best Brunch in Philly hands down - don't be afraid to try the specials - I have yet to try something here that I have not liked.

I was a little skeptical at first. There have been to a few bakeries in Indy over the last couple of years that had great decor but mediocre desserts. I am happy to say that The Cake Bake Shop is different. I tried the millionaire cake and a brownie and they were both delicious. Thank you for being an authentic bakery!

Poke Bowl is great. It's small and there's no normal seating...just bar stools and a small counter. But the poke is top quality and personally crafted like a Subway sandwich shop line. You can mix and match items in each of the categories and create your own perfect combination. The staff was nice and the place was super clean. Be careful about extra ingredients though. I asked if I could add a little of this and a little of that and my poke maker was happy to oblige but I later learned that I was upcharged for all of those extras without being told.

I had heard Iris can pour you up any number of specialty cocktails, so I was disappointed the bar did not have the ingredients for my drink of choice, the bourbon cobbler. The mixologist had a little something special up her sleeve though and poured a creative, yummy apricot bourbon substitute beverage. All in the group of seven were pleased with their cocktail selection, with the exception of the dry martini. The food, however, was a bit a let-down. 

As what I'm learning is an unfortunate theme in this town, it was a bit expensive for the quality of the meal. My eggplant lasagna was warm at best with very little flavor to it. Fortunately (or unforuntunately, depending on how you see it) I had gorged on the cheese plate(s) and was already too full to have more than a few bites. My fellow diners agreed their meals were okay but not would probably not come back and order again. 

Conclusion: I would come back for the charming ambience and creative cocktails, but not stay for dinner.

Wonderful restaurant! My husband's pumpkin ravioli was perfect, not too sweet, the ravioli cooked exactly right. My lamb shank was falling off the bone delicious. Our waiter was informative and attentive, and easy to hear and understand in a small crowded restaurant. We enjoyed every bite! New to Philly, we appreciated the confirmation call when they reminded us that the restaurant was byob. If I'm ever in Philly again and would definitely go back to Kanellas.

Reeds American Table is to die for. I've been several times now since it's opened and had most items on the menu and everything has been wonderful. For the quality of food and price point, Reeds is probably one of the best restaurants in St. Louis. Try the beef and the pork belly (YUM!).

Definitely a decent taco place. I got the fish taco plate for $8 which includes 3 fish/shrimp tacos (I substituted 1 chicken), a 16 oz drink which includes their horchata or fresh pineapple/mango smoothie, and rice and beans. The corn tortillas are definitely the best part of the meal. They're thick and soft and so yummy. The fish tacos are pretty good but the chicken was a little bland. Beans and rice..  eh. 

Overall, the tacos are pretty good, not sure if I'll be coming back with so many other choices. It's about $1.50/$1.60 a taco. 

There're more tables inside than it would seem and also some picnic tables outside but don't sit out there! Between loud noises of the tire shop and the mosquito that was biting me, I wish I had been inside with the a/c.

Food is great! I was impressed with the many healthy options,I had a hard time choosing what to pick!

Only thing, customer service was a little off, waiters did not seem very connected with customers, which was strange to me since they just opened. 

Bottom line, I recommend.
The service here was friendly and fast. The mini Cuban was delicious!!! I highly recommend trying this out for starters if you've never had Cuban before.

Very busy, popular and loud.  Place is a little dingy for the prices. Not much atmosphere. $5 beers, main dishes $ 16-26.  Food was just OK. We ordered 5-6 plates of food and there was nothing I had I would want again. $16.50 "Fried chicken" ended up being a bunch of thin chicken fingers hot spicy sauce. Not good especially for the prices.  Could have gone to Mickey D's for same.  Hate that they tack on the tip for you and put a spot for an additional tip.  Not impressed. Wouldn't be missing out if didn't come back. Much rather eat at Lee how fuk around corner. Have been to much better around Chinatown. Disappointing.

Excellent steaks! I had the ribeye with the gorgonzola crust. One of the best steaks I've had in years. Garlic mashed potatoes were delicious as well. Get there early - the placed packed out. Well worth it.
They only take CASH...NO debit cards. Bummer! Needless to sau, had to turn right around and leave. Next time I will have cash

Bravo sits in a fun area of Wayne--right off Lancaster Ave, which can be pretty busy at the dinnertime hour, on a slightyl less busy street. Parking is still something to consider before 6:00 when you have to feed the meter, but all in all, it's still a good experience.

The pizza is good. It's a little on the greasy side, but overall, good cheese, good sauce, good toppings, good crust. Good stuff, not excellent. The restaurant itself is very well maintained.

Lots to do at the Hard Rock. Both the Lounge and Cafe are great. I enjoy stopping on the casino floor watching the action. Also there is a large variety of food available at the buffet, make sure you check it out for the weekly special.

I was visiting from out of town and excited to try Herbies. It was such a sad state of affairs. As a former St. Louisian, I am very interested in making sure businesses are thriving. This restaurant is doomed. The waiter was nice but everything took a ridiculously long time to receive. My friend ordered a French Onion Soup and it came in a coffee cup sized portion and apparently was bland. My other friend and I got salads that were unmentionably average. Then it took literally over 30 min to receive our entrees. My first friend ordered the veal chop and it was actually good. My other friend ordered the salmon and it was ok and appropriately prepared. I ordered the roasted chicken after bragging to the waiter that I am a roasted chicken connoisseur and he highly recommended their roasted chicken. I am not exaggerating when I tell you it was smaller than my fist (I am a petite woman). The drum stick portion was smaller than my pinky finger. It was actually very cute but ridiculous for $28. It was over cooked, dry and basically I got about 3 bites of actual chicken. We had to complain because I thought it was a joke. The waiter explained that these chickens are 28 days old when they are cooked. So they are basically baby chickens. If they gave two in a portion I could have understood the cost. When we complained, they offered another one to eat. It took at least 15 more minutes to receive this one and the waiter offered to wrap it up because it was obvious we were ready to get the heck out of there. We talked to the manager and he had no interest in our story. I'm mostly just sad that this restaurant was so bad and will likely not survive.

This is my favorite place to get sushi in Reno! It is reasonably priced especially considering the quality. Be warned that they love their hot sauce here so if you aren't really into spice, order without.

The staff is friendly and attentive to your needs, and the chefs are nice and always greet you. The Jalapeno appetizer is the best especially when they are not too spicy. This is the place that I bring people when I want to show them the best all you can eat.
Visiting for work and came to try the black spaghetti,  amazing,  order it,  trust me it was delicious.  I will be back next time in in town.

Taste of Havana is basically a food truck in a small store front in Broad Ripple. There are 2 tables for those lucky enough to get one. There's also a bar with a few stools, but I have a feeling that most folks grab their food and go. And that's a bad decision on their part. If you don't stick around and visit with the owner, Jorge, then you miss out on a big part of the Taste of Havana experience. He'll tell you that the best Cuban food is in Miami and Broad Ripple. And that there isn't a decent Cuban restaurant in New York City. He should know. He lived there for 3 years. If you stick around long enough, he'll also pour you a shot of Cuban coffee which he claims is far superior to Italian coffee because they always burn it. Anyways on to the food. I had a regular Cuban sandwich. Excellent bread, ham and cheese. The pork was good too but I think I would've preferred just a little more spice in it. The pickles and mustard round out a perfect sandwich experience. I would highly recommend Taste of Havana. Go for the food. Stay for the atmosphere.

Nice location. Good service. Okay food. Good deal for a nice place-- $28 for 3 small plates and a glass of wine. I appreciated the ability to try several things-- but the food could have been better. I felt like everything was a little too salty-- but it was imaginative and beautifully plated. No regrets. I had the brown butter spaetzle and broiled oysters. My favorite thing was the City Park salad with romaine and baby red oak leaves and little pieces of apple and bacon and stilton. The BBQ shrimp looked great. The husband had chicken livers, turtle soup and citrus lacquered pork belly. His fav small plate was the chicken livers. He said they were top notch.

Recommended as a great local place to get Mexican food and a new startup that needed support.  We were not disappointed.  The tacos were excellent and reminded me of tacos I've eaten in Austin, TX (the highest praise possible for tacos!).  Very reasonably priced with high quality ingredients.  Obviously appreciated by locals, which is my favorite way to find places to eat.

Great customer service. Awesome fried pork chop, it's a must order item in the menu. Food is served quickly and has a mix menu from Indonesian to taiwanese to chinese. A must recommended restaurant to eat at.

Hands down, the best tri tip sandwich you will ever have!! i have been coming here for many years with some of the best camping in southern cali nearby.  the vibe is amazing especially over the weekends when people get together listening to a dude hitting a empty jack daniels box as a drum.  great day drive from LA !!

I took a friend to this Korean spot because she was curious about Korean food.  Bimbimbop was inedible, fried chicken with panko was not a real chicken filet, but akin to chicken McNuggets, or mystery meat.  The wings were just OK.  This was an awful meal, and I think my friend will likely skip the Korean food for a long time to come.
This pizza is great! Moved to the Main Line from Chicago and this has been my favorite pizza so far. Flavorful with a delicious crust, good service and friendly staff.

My sister and I have visited Tarpon Springs three times (once a year), and Hella's is always our destination for lunch.  The service is spot-on, and the food is great.

I have had their gyro, which is tender and succulent and full of good flavor.  I also have had their cod, and it was a pleasant surprise - I never knew that cod was that good.  My sister has also had many of their dishes and really liked them.

One hint, get there early - otherwise you will have to wait for a table.

Highly recommended.
Best Chinese in the area! Quality delicious food, speedy service and friendly people work the counter. I've been getting my Chinese from here for years and have never been disappointed!

I had lunch at this small and very simple restaurant. Lunch specials are under $8 and include a small bowl of soup, an egg roll, rice and your dish. I had the curry beef that was just OK, the beef itself was spicy with curry flavor but the bell peppers were barely cooked. The portions are good and considering the price it's a great value.
The food wasn't hot, we ordered the "El Jefe" Nachos, both the shredded chicken and beef weren't hot, and the meat was dry....
Great flavors, wonderful taste and consistency.  Staff is terrific. You can't do better.

The last three times I've gone herr my steak has been over cooked by two grades and the wait staff were mediocre at best.  We called ahead for seating and arrived 5 minutes early for our time, we then had to wait 25 extra minutes for them to put our party of 6 in at a 4 top with chairs on the end.  It was extremely uncomfortable.   I will not be returning.

The food here is great! I had the meatloaf, my hubby had the medium wings which were really hot so he would go mild next time which is not the norm, but the homemade blue cheese was so fantastic! My son had a French dip with fries which was good too. Service was great it's not busy and very casual. I love it here!

So glad Urban Village took our reservation for 10 people for Father's Day lunch! It was the perfect place for a big group with different tastes. Some of our favorites included the Wildey Wheat, black IPA, rye IPA, Kelly pizza, village salad, and shaved salad.

Special shout out to our wonderful server Erica, especially for carrying over countless 4 oz testers (we loved this option to be able to try several beers each). We'll definitely be back!

They're good enough but their prices sometimes make me cringe. They're good.... but not that good. They have one delivery guy who never fails to deliver pizzas that it looks like he plays Frisbee with them on his way from there to my house. It's definitely better than more than half the places in the area and we've never had anything that was less than delicious... Even if it came to us looking like it made it through a war on the way here.
I like eating there because it's cute but not fancy.
 Phone girls are nice too.

I've eaten here several times but today was pretty great. Corey my sever was exceptional, he was very attentive and quite knowledgeable in regards to the menu. I had the coffee cured filet with burgundy mushrooms and potatoes all was wonderful. I can't speak for the entire staff but my sever was the best.

The best sandwich in the Reno/Sparks area! I've been eating there for at least 15 years and it's always the same, KILLER! Michelle and the other staff are THE BOMBDIGITTY and you'll be hard pressed to find better, more friendly and relaxed staff. The pricess are a little higher than some other sandwich shops but they are worth every penny. My favorite sandwich is the yellow sub with sprouts, but I also love their wraps and soups. I can't imagine anyone not loving this place.

I can customize my rolls?!? YAY! I'm pregnant and the waitress was so nice and patient with going over all of the cook rolls.  In addition to their available cooked rolls, I added whatever I wanted in them- mango, avocado, sauce, tamago egg... I called the shots.  

I love that their ceiling is really high and that their location is in a not so busy area. I will definitely be coming back for more after I give birth to try out their raw fish.

Cosi made a really DUMB move this week. I went in for my usual Orange-cranberry squagel bundled with a grande coffe. First I noticed that there were no orange cranberry ones and only 12 bagels in total (at 8AM!). So I chose a cinamon Raisin. Then I went to register and asked them to bundle with a coffee. I was tokd they were "cutting back bagels and promoting flatbread sandwiches) and they no longer bundle with coffee. SO I said I wasn't happy but to give me the coffee anyway. The price was 45% (!) more than last week! Then I looked at menu board and saw that the 1/2 salad and 1/2 sandwich combo (a healthy alternative) was not there. "We don't do that any more I was told". I WAS told that this new "menu" is only at 15th & Locust, 12th and Walnut and 4th & Chestnus (MY usual location) but I could walk to 9th and Chestnut or 18th and Walnut and get the "old menu". No staff person explained the reason and I saw lots of other customers who were surprised and not happy and said they wouldn't be back. REALLY dumb corporate decision, which I hope will change soon before they lose MANY more long time customers at these three locations.\\
I did not enjoy my food here. The fish was fried so hard I couldn't eat it. My rice taste like some boil n the bag rice. I was not impressed at all.

The pho is EXCELLENT and so is the service...but it's not the tidiest place in town.  The walls are pretty dirty, which is surprising for a newish place, and the floors are often not clean.  Regardless, it's still my go to pho spot.

Cafe deluxe was awesome. This used to be a laundromat back in the day, and now they've established a quirky little breakfast spot. We got some kind of breakfast scramble with meats and various other veggie ingredients. We ordered some flour tortillas on the side which were huge. 

The egg scrambles were huge portions, so after we got our fill, I made us two huge burritos to go. 

Cool place, nice people, and great coffee.
The Habit has hands down my favorite Onion rings ever! they are cooked perfectly and they pair perfectly with the ranch sauce. My hamburger was good but i was fixated on my onion rings.

We ordered take out: Sesame Chicken, Lemon Chicken, and Chicken Chow Mein (yes, we love us some chicken!). I was definitely in the mood for some delightfully-bad-for-you-hole-in-the-wall food, and this far exceeded my expectations. 

First: the portions are ENORMOUS. Seriously. I've eaten Chinese take out in several different states, and this was striking. They packed in as many chow mein noodles as the little white box could handle. Complete with enough meat to last me 4 meals (and my boyfriend, 2 meals). 

Second: mouth watering glorious explosions in my mouth. The Sesame chicken was so crispy and sweet I was in Chinese food heaven. The Chow Mein noodles were thick and flavored well, and definitely left me wanting more. My boyfriend enjoyed his Lemon chicken, but I didn't actually try it myself. 

Third: amazing price for what you get. DO IT.

It was perfect for a take out movie night in. If I lived in Reno, this would be my go to.

The restaurant is in the casino which is understandable but some more signage outside would help. The place looks a bit gaudy and outdated but nice and clean. 

We had good service with drinks and appetizers. However, we got there at 7pm and it was 8:11pm and we still hadn't been served out entrees. Tables behind and in front of us were served and those people came after us. We asked for the manager and told him to charge us for our drinks and apps so we could leave. He then told us that or entrees were ready and he would only charge us half price. It was another 10 minutes and then a different server brought them out and we just told him to pack them up to go. The manager came back with the entrees packed in a bag and said they were on the house. He then informed us that because my husband ordered a bone-in chicken dish, it takes 26 minutes to make the meal. That is still the longest 26 minutes I have ever experienced. 

I don't believe the ambience or the food is worth the price.

One of my favorite spots for morning coffee. The device here is excellent. Such a cute place to sit back and relax. I've had several of their hot and cold beverages and my favorite is the white chocolate mocha on ice. Delicious!!!  This business will be seeing a lot of me.

My husband and I were visiting Philly from LA for a conference. We grabbed a chicken club and curry tofu wrap for the airplane ride. Even though we ate it a couple hours later, the flavors were still on point! I'd love to check out Hip City Veg again in a situation when I had more time.

Beautiful, classy and very old school Italiano decor.

Service is prompt, music is great (i.e. Sinatra, Dean Martin) and food was delicious!

As a bedrock of the Safety Harbor community it is terrible that this Cosby is tearing down more than 20 legacy "live oaks" in order to pave in a parking lot. Those trees are a vital part of the personality of Safety Harbor and since Choice Hotels purchased them they have proved they do not understand how important community support is for t
Fun little place. Great burgers and the basket of fries is enough for the whole family. They also have great deals during happy hour but haven't been in yet for that yet.

nice place for gatherings and hanging out. Friendly staff. 

Food was OK. Not bad, not good, it just sat somewhere in the middle.

Don't let the amount of reviews turn you away!  This place is a gem! Went there after looking for kitchen lighting at Ikea on a whem. I had the papusas (pork), horse steak (not horse meat) which came with tostones and rice and beans, and complimentary empanada (beef), the homemade nachos with a spicy dip that they serve to everyone, and complementary flan. The papusa was a warm tortilla like an arepa but flat and filed with your choice of fillings  (cheese, pork and I forgot the other) it was a good. Next the beef empanada had a soft outside (not like others I've had with a crispy outside) and wonderfully seasoned beef inside.  The entree came next I will tell you I was already full. The steak was nothing to scream about but it was good in its sauce with peppers and onions, rice (yellow rice, they do have white)and beans(black or red ) and the tostones. The tostones cane with this white sauce I've never had usually use to having them with a garlic and oil sauce,  this dip was excellent and even better in the steak.  The tostones cooked perfectly crispy edges and soft inside ( I ate all of them)! Then the smiling chef behind the counter said how about dessert? My response no way! He responds I have something special for you!  Our comes the vanilla flan! I kid you not this was the best flan I've had! Creamy, with just the right about of sweet caramel along the top and bottom. It was sinful! You want to give this spot a try! Great customer service! The smile on the head chef is amazing! They were all so personable. Clean,  great hot food made to order, everything came out piping HOT! Budget friendly and you'll have enough for lunch the next day!

I really like their vegetable korma.
Apparently, they offer delivery close by, but you need a 35 dollar minimum.

Im kind of glad that Im not the only one not singing Posto's praises.  While there wasnt anything horribly wrong with my lunch there, it really was a laclkluster experience for the pricetag. The service was minimal and I got the impression that I wasnt cool enough or European enough to be there. The salad and sandwich was tasty enough, but just not great. I was so excited reading the sammie descriptions, but then the actual product just kind of fell flat.  If you want a real sandwich served with a smile, go to st james!

Lilly's Café doesn't need my four star review because the place is always packed with happy and satisfied customers.  Best part of Lilly's Café is the always fresh ingredients used in the meal.  Great atmosphere and great quality food.  Nice change of pace from your typical Asian culinary fair.
In this Mexican food heaven on earth why would anyone eat here is beyond my comprehension.

We love this place! From the open air setup and outdoor seating to the deliciously unique rolls and friendly wait staff... this is my friends and I's South Philly go-to. Though they're busy we can always get a good table on a Friday night.

The special roll is always a hit and my personal favorite is the Remy roll. The vegetarian/ vegan sushi is also amazing! If that's your thing... ask them to make you an avocado and sweet potato roll with benito flakes. 

What's really special though is their seaweed salad. This is no average run of the mill seaweek, and nothing like the typical you get at sushi joints. Their seaweed is FRESH and served in mellow vinegar and lemon. Absolutely delicious! Even my apprehensive friend was Wowed and loved it. The only reason why we didn't give Izumi 5 stars is we figured there are even more insane sushi spots we have yet to try... but for now, this is our favorite =)

I've been having a hard time finding a good brunch spot, until I found Jones.  Unfortunately for me, Jones is a 3 hour drive.   So I will not be frequenting it - but one can dream.

We sat upstairs, which I recommend - a little quieter & you can watch everyone below you.  We were there around 11:30 on a rainy Saturday, and were sat immediately.  Service was fine, and fast.  Decor is super cute.

I had the French toast with tater tots.  Tater tots, you ask?  Yes, because where I'm from, they are not quite ubiquitous.  My Philly friend (aka tour guide) also had the French toast, and my husband had the avocado sandwich with fries.   The French toast was thick and tasty, and probably the biggest piece of French toast I've ever seen.   I enjoyed the tater tots.  My husband liked his sandwich and fries, but the fries went cold fast.  

Perhaps a second location in DC or Boston is needed?
I've been going to this Wawa pretty much every week since they opened for business. Service is good enough and gas prices are competitive with the area.

Oxymoronic name to begin with and I asked do you serve sparkling water with your Espresso and the lady said sometimes, clearly I didn't go in that sometimes! The cheap ass Quality Inn had free Breakfast that had more choices than this 'Breakfast' place :)

Espresso? Meh!

If you walk outside and look to the left you may find the breakfast place you are looking for :)

Kudos to the nice looking spot but it gives some sort of a fake vibe! Doesn't jive with a coffee shop, oh well.

Okay, so I tried this place because a co-worker gave me a coupon for buy 1 get 1 free for AYCE sushi from the valpak booklet.  Since I hadn't yet heard of Sushi Minato, I immediately Yelped it and saw nothing but great reviews.   I personally keep a 1-5 star sushi restaurant rating in my notes on my phone and I always love adding a place I've never been to - so why not ?  With a heck of a deal I had nothing to lose! 

First off, if they serve apps with AYCE sushi I always start with the seaweed salad.  They gave a good 5 to 6 bite bowl that was the perfect amount.  It wasn't too sweet and was lightly dressed.  Other places can tend to make theirs super sugary, so this actually tasted and felt healthy.  We did order the wontons (3 pc), they weren't anything to rave about - stay clear from ordering these as they were extremely greasy.   

We arrived at the restaurant about 5:15 straight after work to get a good spot at the counter on a Friday night.  My date immediately ordered the Mountain roll to start - it was made very promptly and it was delish,   The avocado was super green and ripe - never brown.  Everyone sitting at the counter asked the sushi chef which roll that was and they ended up ordering the Mountain as well.  The crab salad topping was so light with very little mayo which is a big plus in my book.  Since the Mountain roll was really good, I had to go with the house Minato roll because I love rolls with lemon slices and it's usually a good idea to order the signature roll.  There wasn't an overwhelming amount of rice on any of the rolls and the pieces were just the right size.  All of the fish was super fresh and was never mushy or bland.  I can't remember the names of all the rolls we ate, but a few of them incorporated fresh herbs such as basil, cilantro, and/or basil sauce.  The two herbs I'm completely obsessed with lately - especially cilantro.  I had the sushi chef make me the Cinco roll without cream cheese.  It had lovely chunks of tuna on top mixed with cilantro, it was so fresh but a heaping roll which filled me up quickly, so after that I stuck with mostly nigiri and Donald Ducks.    

All in all we had a good experience.  The sushi chef was very friendly and smiley and good at what he does.  I couldn't say "mmmmm" enough while I was eating and I was very excited to find a good new sushi place in Reno.  Everything was made right away and we never had to wait long.  

I will definitely be going back!
It s cheap drinking and average bar food at best. The service is hit or miss but its still a great place to go to watch a sporting event. I normally stop in when getting my car serviced next door.
Great food, one of bet places to eat in apollo beach.  Gyro is amazing and they have gluten-free pitas too!

Chase is marvelous. The romantic ambiance is great for an intimate dinner date, and the food is pretty good too. The lighting is a bit dark, making it hard to read the manus

But the food was lovely. I had a great chicken parm. and their bread is great.

My only complaint is that the wait staff was a bit slow. We had to wait for a long time before our food came and it was a while before we were brought the check and refills on drinks.

We visited this location a total of four times in a two month period while we were staying in the area. The food was good each time but the service was vastly different each time. The last time we almost left. This is something the restaurant needs to work on with their servers. If our last experience was our only experience, I would have only given a two star rating.

We went to this place a couple of times already, then one day we had a $25 off gift thing from resturants.com

Boy was that a big mistake, one of the owners (jamaican guy) was so rude and blunt about how he did not approve of it and how it would cost him money if he used it. We left without ordering after getting his diss about it. He began telling us how the other owners wanted it but not him. (great for us)

We came back hoping the same man would not be there (he was) and then one of the servers said they were closed. It was 9:30pm and they closed at 10pm. We just wanted a slice.

We shall never return again. The pizza is just dough with toppings you can get anywhere, so get the "Walnut St" stick out your butt. We went to NYPD pizza around the corner to get our slice.
Best ox-tails in the area..! Great ropa viejo, picadillo, bollitos, etc. Cafeteria style makes it more fun...!

Ted Peters is darn good, famous mostly because it's been around longer than most Florida transplants. Yes, smoked mullet isn't bad, having said that though it IS about the only way they are edible. And if anyone who owns a smokehouse knows, it's not exactly something you say an hour before dinner - hmmm I think I'm going to smoke me some mullet!! I digress, me personally I do prefer the smoked Salmon, or even one of their burgers as they are friggin awesome too. The potato salad is not my style, having said that though it is not bad at all for the style that it is. (I'm more a NY Publix potato salad guy even though I don't care for NY - figure that out!) The only reason I did not give it 5 stars is the old real estate adage "location location location!!!" It's just plain not convenient for anyone not from south Saint Pete, St. Pete Beach or Gulfport so although the food is great being handicapped I only make the drive every few years. Having said this without having to add a smokehouse they could easily add a Park Blvd location which would expand their business drastically even drawing in some from as far as Clearwater one would think. But who knows, maybe the owner likes dollars more than hundreds! :)

I love this place. Everthing I've tried there has been so good. I love the food, ambiance and cooks. The hibachi chefs include everyone in the fun. The only complaint I have is they are not opened early enough for us to go during week. If they were open earlier than  4:30 during week we would go more often.
Absolutely terrible service. Went through the drive thru and waited OVER 15 MINUTES for my food. Absolutely unacceptable. Will NOT be back!!
The BBQ shrimp is so yummy. I always I want to eat all of the buttery, garlicky and peppery BBQ  sauce with the French bread. Fortunately for my waist line I only ate half...so good!

I'm not a particular fan of Mexican food. However, I received a gift certificate for Red Mesa and decided to try it out. I was very impressed! They give you chips and salsa to start. The chips are freshly made but not overly oily and the salsa is mild. I absolutely in loved the grilled mahi dish with Mofongo. It was the perfect balance of sweet, savory and acid. We ended the dinner with the guava empanada that comes with a side of vanilla ice cream. So delicious! Apparently Red Mesa has been around for many years and is very popular in the Saint Pete area. I highly recommend!

If you wish to gamble for free, you will need to bring a non gambling traveler to drop you off and they find somewhere else to hang out as there is now a $10 fee to park. Never have I been to a casino with a parking fee and that includes some that are much nicer than this one.

Very few good penny slots with low minimum bets.

Nonsmoking is a joke as there is not enough separation between smoking and non smoking areas.

This place is amazing. From the outside, it doesn't look like you would want to eat there, but don't let that fool you! The inside is cute and cozy. The food is plentiful, cheap and delicious. The Texas Margaritas have me drive across town just to have some. Seriously, don't let the fact that it is inside a sketchy motel keep you from stopping. It's authentic Mexican food. Not too spicy, but really tasty. I will literally drive 30 min just to have some tacos and a margarita here.

Went back to have lunch here the other day and was nicely surprised that we could order very tasty breakfast dishes.  The Shakshuka, eggs braised in tomato and pepper stew, with a strong cumin flavor, were certainly a good way to start our meal, the soft-cooked peppers making a perfect accompaniment for the runny eggs.  We ordered the appetizer combination plate, including well-known meze favorites.  Especially good were the crisply fried fava falafal balls, other meze were quite ordinary, like the lackluster tzatziki.  Not at all to our liking were the mushy, bland dolmades (stuffed grape leaves).  The grilled pork was correctly done, served with a small salad.  I was glad to see a pretty good lunch crowd, the lunch prices, after all, are very good.  Looking at the dinner menu, including goat stew and rabbit, I imagined the food to be more focused and also more original in the evening, while the lunch choices did not surpass average, including the desserts of galaktobureko (with tired phyllo) and a pudding with lots of rose water.  The service is knowledgeable and friendly and the atmosphere of the restaurant bright and inviting.
From service to taste this restaurant had it all. Their mahi sandwich was cooked and seasoned perfectly. Their drink selection was vast and test

Amazing! Incredible service to match fabulous food.
Shrimp and grits were out of this world, but we all tried each other's dishes. Can also vouch for bourbon street breakfast (served with bourbon to dump all over your pancakes) and oyster Benedict too. So so good!

My family and I were in Nashville for the first time and needed some BBQ before we were out of time and had to return home. This place was next to our hotel so we tried it. The ribs were the best: Tender and juicy and great flavor. The sides were also very good. Probably Not the best BBQ in Nashville but Satisfied the last item on the list.

The food here is fantastic. We had the lunch combo - a half sandwich with salad and soup. The vegan vegetable soup was superb, as was the lime cilantro dressing with the salad. The sandwiches (grilled portobello and roasted turkey) were both excellent. The staff were friendly and we loved the relaxed atmosphere. Go.

This review is for the lunch Buffet:

I'm not an Indian Food expert, but really enjoy it from time to time.  The lunch buffet has many options, and everything I tried was wonderful.

Service was excellent and very friendly.

I don't remember the last time I had such a good meal for $8......... that's right, $8 for an outstanding lunch.  Wish i was going to be in the area tomorrow as i'd be delighted to go back.
Love boat is very nice! I really enjoy this place. Definitely want to come to try other stuffs, too!

This is my favorite place for COFFEE. Rembrandt's has excellent coffee. Their lunch menu is excellent as well. I have not had dinner yet but am looking forward to trying because the lunch menu is so good. 
Staff and service are great. I am there often!!

You guys, I finally made it to Milktooth!  I have to say this place is amazing and I don't think my review will be any different than anyone else's.  So I'm just gonna get my complaints out of the way now so I can move on:
1.  You're almost too popular because I had to wait, outside in the rain, for an hour to be seated with my party.  (But I keep a commitment so I did it)
2. I don't like the disorganization of the coffee area or the prices of such. ($4 for a tiny cup? Come on, it's morning and mama needs some energy) also, I was practically shunned for asking for some cream and *gasp* sweetener for my iced coffee.  I'm a lady who knows what she wants and I really try to lay off the suga, so gimme my Splenda packet and we'll be ok.  

On to the good stuff.  Despite how busy they were, service was great.  I almost didn't feel cool enough to be there.  Everyone in their locally made apparel and handlebar mustaches, but I had on my best Hayes & Taylor shirt and crammed myself in anyways.  Of course I tried the bacon.  Do you consider that bacon?  It was half the size of a small pig, but none the less it was delicious!!  I had the pigs in a poncho to eat.  Soooo amazing!  That avocado cream sauce was just the perfect topping and the pickled veggies! I dream about being caught in a rainstorm wearing a poncho like that... 

I'll be back, and for my own selfishness I hope you are less busy :)

This was excellent. We came for dinner and got conch croquettes, crispy dirty rice arancini, hamachi, broiled shrimp, semolina gnocchi, and curried goat. Everything was good, but the arancini and curried goat stood out for me. The arancini was somewhat unexpected, as it was a last second throw-in to our order, but the flavor really jumped and the dipping sauce it came with was excellent as well. 

Obviously, though, the main event was the curried goat. The meat itself was outstanding, but the gnocchi and the sauce could have been a great entree on its own. (To some extent, it overshadowed the semolina gnocchi, which was also very good, but more plain.) 

My wife also loved the broiled shrimp, and while I liked them too, I'm more turned off by having to do the work of peeling them.

Overall, an excellent dinner, and I was really torn between 4 and 5 stars.
Soda Fountain Square is closed as a restaurant space and is now an event space through Sqwires.

Great locally owned and operated restaurant. The staff is very great at helping you through the menu. They are right in the center of all the action Clearwater Beach has to offer. When we have friends or family in town we usually take them here and sit on the 2nd floor good views of the beach and pier. Their food and drinks are great and I think reasonably priced.
Food is excellent, Small and quaint, only a 20 min wait at 7:00 on a Saturday night. The only complaint was it was way to bright in there.

Overall experience was unpleasant at best. Seated 20 minutes beyond our reservations, server barely checked on us over the hour and a half we waited for our food. Once food actually arrived, risotto was undercooked, Brussel sprouts were over cooked and missing side dishes. Notified server with no reconciliation until we mentioned it again. Finally got a pseudo-manager who's first priority seemed to simply get out of the situation as quickly as possible. We reminded him that we still had not gotten part of one of our dishes - he assured us that would be taken care of immediately. During this time our original server could be seen openly having a confrontation with multiple people and was subsequently removed from our service. A new server was appointed at which time we had to start over explaining the issues with the meal and still missing items.
Needless to say after nearly 2 hours we we just wanted to go! Part of meal was comped but will not go back!

It's become the place you go to before a game in south Philly.  I have always had a good experience here.  Crab fries are a staple.  Lobster white pizza is always great.  Mussels in white garlic sauce, yes please, I will take all the bread you can give me to eat this delicious broth.  My favorite of all time at Chickie's is the McGooby sandwich.  A great roll, with chopped onion and pickle.  They then top that with steamed and peeled shrimp.  On top of that goes some crab fries, and on top of that goes the patented Chickie's cheese sauce.  It is a great balance of cold and hot in a seafood sandwich.  Can it complete with the lobster rolls of New England, maybe... I would like to think so.

My service has always been great here, and there are always beer specials to be had.
The menu is great but unfortunately they are inconsistent with food prep. I've had great food, then cold food, then undercooked food all for the exact same dish.
Ate there tonight with my guy. Good food and good service.  Clean restaurant too. We will be going back again.

We were traveling through Franklin and decided to try this brewery after reading reviews on Yelp. This place was a great find and exactly what we needed for our overnight stay in the area. The beer is outstanding (one of the best Ambers I have had and the pecker wrecker is a must try).

This is going to be long, sorry...

Beautiful views if you have a window seat, other than that you are either facing the restaurant or too low to see the views. We made a reservation a week before so understandably they couldn't seat us at the window but it was a Wednesday night and there were raised/better view booths open the entire time we were there. IMO, seat your reservations at the best possible tables esp for birthdays/anniversaries.

We arrived at 7:27 for a 7:30 reservation. The hostess asked us to sit at the bar while they were getting our table ready. We sat at the bar no problem, great views, cool ice block, views of the sous chefs, lots of things to look at and talk about. Bartenders were attentive and friendly. We each ordered a basic drink. About 7:40 the hostess came over and said our table was ready. I asked should we close out our tab or can we just transfer it? I asked knowing she was probably going to say they will transfer it but I used to be a bartender and did not want to stiff this guy on a tip. She said "leave your drinks here and your waitress will bring them over." We thought, oh how fancy. Thinking they didn't want us walking around with drinks in our hands. Meanwhile we walked by 3-4 people with ripped jeans, white sneakers, some interesting attire.. My husband said "I guess they don't enforce the dress code"

We were seated and waited, and waited, now our drinks are about 15 feet behind us and we have not been greeted by the waitress. Some time goes by and I turned to the look at the bar and saw the bartender going to grab our drinks and then with a confused face looking around the restaurant. So my husband jumped up and grabbed our drinks from the bar before he dumped them out. It was just an odd encounter that really nobody is at fault but we would have happily brought our drinks with us. A few minutes later our waitress comes by and asked us if we want bottled, sparking, or ice water. We opted for the ice water.

We decided to go without appetizers since we ALWAYS fill up on appetizers too quickly. My husband ordered the 20oz Ribeye w/ potatoes and I ordered the Crisp Pork Osso Bucco. We also ordered mac n cheese to share. Both entrees were very good! The mac n cheese was pretty good, not as good as those potatoes, yum!

Here's where we get to 3 stars, the overall service. The waitress came over pretty quickly after the food was dropped off, I think I had taken one bite and asked how everything was, "good" we said. We didn't see her again for a lonnggg time. Well we saw her running by us about 25 times, but she never filled our water or asked if we wanted another cocktail, or if we needed anything at all. Now I am all about not being bothered but just come by and check our water glasses. My husband's glass was bone dry for about 20 minutes and I let him have the rest of mine. I am not one to wave a waitress down... She seemed really busy. We have been to a lot of restaurants (Butcher and Singer, Barclay Prime, Waterworks, Sotto Varalli to name a few) and all those places have a person that goes around and fills water glasses, and clears the table of extra stuff (unused wine glasses, take bread plates, etc). This person didn't exist or they just never came around.

I was just surprised that a few details were overlooked. Am I being picky? Yes, bc I am writing a Yelp review. Am I losing sleep over this place and wishing we didn't spend $165? No. I just want people to know that if you are expecting over the top service you will not get it here. You will get a cool atmosphere and good food. So for me that is worthy of 3 stars. :) 

TL;DR - Must reserve a window booth or you are missing out, expect decent service but not exceptional, food is good but nothing that I can see us craving to have again like my husband and his Delmonico at Butcher and Singer that I never stop hearing about....haha

This place is great! They always have fresh sushi and creative options. I love trying all the new rolls they always taste great! It's also byo which is wonderful!!! It's got a great atmosphere and the servers always treat you wonderfully. Highly recommend for sushi.

It was an ok experience. I was there last night and you would have thought they were closed. We drive by thinking oh we will go there but then were like they are closed. Well I was hungry so I decided to call and make sure they were closed only to find out that they are open and asked what time they were open they were so rude and never answered what time so we went home dropped off people came in and they were open so we went. When we did go we didn't know that we were suppose to sit ourselves so we finally did and then the waiter took forever to come. We were about ready to get up and leave when she finally came and got our order. So we ordered our drink but when we asked for a few more minutes to look at the menu and we did it took a very long time for the waiter to come back. We ordered and it took quite a long time to get our food considering we only ordered a hamburger and chicken sandwhich. We finally got our food which was decent to say the least and then took more time to get our check. If we go back we need to make sure that they actually are open they need lighting on the outside.

Obsessed, I average about 1 visit a week.  absolutely my favorite froyo place around, I will tell you why:

- Close to my house. I live 0.4 miles away and its the perfect neighborhood spot. 

- They let you sample by yourself, little cups sitting by the froyo. I've been to some places where they literally have to run from behind the counter and serve each sample to you and your mates and it takes forever/annoying. 

- Flavors are robust and delicious and taste like theyre supposed to. They always offer soy options. My favorites:  Nutella, Cinnabon, Almond, Pistachio, Cake Batter, Rasberry (and add hot fudge)

-They rotate the flavors all the time! like weekly maybe even

-Service is fine. It seems to always be a young girl in there with really fly nails

-They offer a reward program to earn free froyo and different specials thoughout the week like "student discount" etc

After my first couple years of college a friend and I noticed that the incoming freshmen had, well, little heads.  I'm not sure why, but they absolutely had little heads.  Maybe they had not begun to expand as a result of the absorption of knowledge or as a result of other "mind expanding" things that happen in college (allegedly).  Anyway, from then on, freshmen were dubbed "littleheads."  As in; "Hey, here comes some littleheads, lets eff with them!"

Anyway, when we stopped in here for a late dinner the place seemed to be populated with...littleheads.  Dining, serving, etc.  This impression was not helped by the fact that past of the lighting in this place is accented with blacklights.  Certainly an unusual choice.  It took me a moment to figure out why the couple in the back had such oddly glowing teeth.

So I opted for a small pizza, I think it was the "Caruso Supreme" or something.  It wasn't very good.  I tasted my wife's chicken parm and it was probably in the 3 star neighborhood.

Overall, Caruso's was a disappointment.  Interesting, but a disappointment.  Seems like the place where the local college kids go for a "nice dinner out."

We wanted to love this place, it is very cool looking, the food smelled great, but the service really needs work. I say that the food SMELLED great because we actually never got ours. Had to flag down a waiter just to get water, then finally got our bar and food order in, only to have our waiter disappear and never return.  We  sat there nearly an hour with only water, and could not get anyone to help us, so we decided to call it a night and head to another favorite St. Charles restaurant.  To be fair, the place was super busy, but it won't stay that way if the service is bad.  Seems like it could be a fun place.

What this place has is a good idea (simplicity), the hip atmosphere and a great staff.  I give the staff who work there 5 stars.  They were friendly and helpful and if I were ever to return, it's because of them.  The coffee was decent.  The donuts were okay.  The chicken was dry and too much sauce that didn't help with the chicken.  But for $25 (2 coffee, 5 or 6 donuts and half a chicken), I think I can get much much much better coffee, donuts and chicken from elsewhere.

It's a diner.  You don't go to a diner for gourmet food (despite what The Food Network, etc. would have you believe).

As far as diners go, this place was no better or worse than any other diner.  It does kind of feel like not much has been done to it since the 70s or 80s.

I was stuck in the nearby hotel/industrial area and needed breakfast at 5:30 pm and Indy's fit the bill.

My hostess/waitress was extremely attentive and took great care of me.  She even noticed that I had a laptop bag and asked if I needed to sit near an outlet.  As I prepared to leave she asked if I need a coffee to go which was a nice touch.

Coffee was fresh brewed (rather than having sat in a pot all afternoon) and my breakfast arrived quickly.  Eggs, bacon and pancakes!  

Food was delicious and cheap. Service was outstanding.  I will go there again.

If your in Nashville, you must go to the Pancake Pantry. The line is not a myth! We were able to wait inside, but others were outside and around the building. "I'm a picky pancake eater and these really were worth the hype. Despite the long line, you do get good service and you are not "rushed" to clear the table for the next guest. 
You really can't go wrong with anything on this menu.

Fatty's Pub is the best place to chill inside or out (which i prefer - it has an awning, lotsa flowers & ceiling fans as well as a giant screen TV).....everything on the menu is delish but you must try their skinny buffalo chicken cheese steak (if you can finish as i usually take 1/2 home) & their cocktails are fabulous!!!

MOST IMPORTANTLY YOU MUST SIT IN COLETTE'S SECTION IF YOU CAN FIND A SPOT AS SHE IS THE BEST WAITRESS ANYWHERE, BAR NONE (no pun intended-lol)!!!  WE DRIVE 25 MINS JUST TO DINE @FATTY'S & IT'S DEFINITELY WELL WORTH THE DRIVE!!!

This place is great. Service brought us extra cherries for baby without asking. The fried seafood and drinks are the best. I love norleans! It's like Vegas with great food everywhere here hoooraaaaye.

Probably the best Italian in the West Chester area that has a full bar. This place has grown so much over the years, from a small BYOB to expanding and becoming packed every night (so make reservations). Because of the popularity, they use every space available and the result is a somewhat cramped and loud atmosphere.

The food isn't the best Italian in the area but certainly holds its own. It's a little on the pricy side but they put a lot of care into everything they do and make dinner an experience. You'll get started with complimentary bruschetta and bread. For appetizers, I'd recommend the grilled seafood which comes with calamari, scallops, and shrimp. They've also got a good assortment of antipastos. The meat and pasta dishes are all solid, a mix of American-Italian dishes and a few things that I've never heard of. The only dessert I've had is the key lime cheesecake which is delicious, but pricy for what you get. At the end you'll get offered some complimentary Limoncello shots as well.

They also do a lunch buffet during the week. It includes pastas, salads, and pizzas. Probably the best deal around. 

Service has always been good, the only reason it might seem slow is if they're getting slammed, but I wouldn't say that's they're fault. 

Overall, if you don't have a bottle of wine or want some nice cocktails or a beer, this is the best spot to go if you're in the mood for Italian. It's better than Teca, but I'd recommend Core de Roma over for food (BYOB). Either way, you'll get a good meal here:

For airport food you can't get much better. It helps that this is tucked around the corner in Terminal E so I think many miss it. 

The service was fast, friendly and attentive. They played a mix of different Irish music from traditional to U2 and others. We had the fish and chips and they were quite good, very well cooked and flaky and relatively lightly battered.  Had a Guinness of course too:). 

Note that the online menu on the restaurant's website seems to be missing the entrees, like the fish and chips. But there are several snaps of the menu on Yelp you can check out.

Best choice in the Terminal.

I love their pizza.  Everything we have tried there is really good.  Their food is so good, that InRiva hosted my baby shower last year and they were great.  I did not quite get their menu at first, but after visiting several times, I love it.

Must try!

Excellent ambiance, great keeping of tradition on meats which are excellent. I was expending a bigger bill than what I got. Happy to find a new favorite steakhouse in New Orleans. Sit in of the booths, you won't regret it.

Checked out this new sushi spot after hearing good things and I'm glad I did! The fish was clearly very fresh and the portion sizes were generous. The seasoning was excellent on the dishes. The J&J Specialty Roll was really good and I highly recommend it.  All in all, a great experience with delectable food and lovely ambiance. Will definitely be coming back!

What an amazing little gem of a restaurant!!!  The food is AMAZING!!  I had the perogies!!  My brother had his bday there and the service was impeccable!!!  This is our new go-to restaurant!!  Keep up the great work Paul!!!  You are so talented!!!

Was really disappointed when I received my tofu Provençale this last time.  Both the potatoes and tofu came out incredibly dry...no olive oil to be found on the plate.  Their Provençale had previously been a blend of olive oil, herbs, tomatoes and garlic sautéed to perfection.  I've always asked for this dish without onions.  Today the olive oil with Herbs de Provence, garlic etc. was completely missing.  The waitress told me she had no idea why they did that.  It was just dry fried tofu with a bit of tomato and herbs. I was so disappointed that this excellent dish had been botched.  She took it back and returned with what tasted like a lesser olive oil and nearly raw garlic added to my existing plate.  I guess I won't be returning, which is too bad because I adored that dish.

How does ANY pizza place not serve a pepperoni pizza?  The pizzas they do serve are good, some more adventerous than others. Their salads are good too. But they don't serve the most popular pizza topping in America.

I probably would have given them a better score but I ordered a bacon and egg biscuit and didn't get the bacon. The biscuits are so-so. I've had more flavorful. My coffee was a little on the weak side.  The young lady at the window was very nice and had a lovely smile.  Not sure of the exact address but they are right off the interstate and I could see the Cloverdale tower with the name. Very busy place.

Although I have only been here once, I have to say my first time was amazing. It isn't really diner food per say. I think it is geared more towards a Jewish palette. I ordered almond encrusted french toast with eggs over hard (which no one cooks right) and saugage links. The french toast was incredible. My eggs were cooked as best they could which is fine. The waitress was as sweet and attentive. I really want to go back there sometime soon.

Tried this place during my lunch break after finishing my workout on a Thursday. The diner had a cozy, hidden feeling to it in the shopping plaza its attached to. Service was quick and friendly and the food came out in a timely manner. I ordered the chicken fried steak skillet; it was delicious especially the fried steak which had a generous portion. The gravy also tasted good, the potatoes/hash browns it came with we're kind of bland... nothing special but they weren't bad by any stretch.  Prices were fair for the quality/amount of food I received. Will be visiting in the future to try their other dishes out.

I am not sure why Ru San's has such bad ratings on Yelp. I guess it really depends on a variety of things, including the day you went in, how parking was that day, how your service was, and who was the chef that day. 

Either way, we have been to Ru San's twice and used Groupons both times and loved our experience. I am not sure if I would return here for a full priced meal just because Nashville has so many options, and some of them cheaper than Ru San's but for half-priced these guys were great. 

We loved their appetizers, especially the avocado-shrimp nacho looking thing (I cannot for the life of me remember it's name). We also really enjoyed their calamari. 

The sushi is great. They have a lot of friend options and regular sushi options. Their speciality rolls are good too. 

We have never run into a problem with their service. The first time we went there, we were in and out in a matter of 1-1.5 hours. The second time, we were using a Groupon and usually you cannot use it for alcohol but the waiter let my boyfriend use it for his beer anyway. That was cool of him!:) 

TIP: I would park with the valet at Sambuca. It is the easiest way to find parking at the Gulch and worth the dollar tip.
Amazing food for amazing value. Wonderful blend of flavors, very friendly family run restaurant. If you want some amazing food at a great price look no further.

District Donuts is awesome! The donuts are the best thing to get. They are very reasonably priced considering the amazing flavors you get. The Pecan Pie donut was fabulous. The sliders are decent--a bit pricey at 4.50 for one. Overall, the place is a hidden gem. Definitely recommend visiting.

Went here for a dinner date with my fiancé on a Sunday, glad I reserved it because all the Colts fans came pouring in! The only thing I didn't like here were the rude hostesses who, when we checked in, told us we needed to be done by 6pm. Rude! Once we got seated everything got better. Our waitress was nice, attentive and had good suggestions. We ordered the lamb porterhouse which was great, but the Izzy Style NY Strip was even better! Best steak I've ever had. The cracked pepper flavor and seared crispy texture on the outside on this steak did it for me. For sides we had garlic mashed potatoes and asparagus, and appetizers we had grilled slab bacon (very thick cut!). The drinks here are expensive but worth it bc they are fancy and on the strong side. I had the Limoncello Todd Collins. Definitely recommend this place to everyone (just ignore the rude hostesses)!

Slow service was the rule of the day. The food wasn't particularly noteworthy either. The fresh squeezed orange juice has more pulp than juice. If I wanted to eat an orange, I would have ordered one instead of a glass of overpriced pulp. The waitress with the neck tattoo was interesting, but I'll probably try somewhere else next time. The Capri always has good food and timely service...

Avoid the steak. I have eaten their twice and found several pieces of it were mainly fat or grisle. One time I complained to the manager and he said it was hard for them to tell the difference when they grilled it. The other meat items are more reliable although I am no fan of shredded chicken either. My friend had the vegetarian bowl which looked better. Other ingredients looked good and were tasty.

Being a clean eater that strays away from meat and gluten makes it a little difficult to go out to eat. Finding someone to dine with at a vegetarian restaurant can be difficult so I often find myself saying "I'll just get a salad" when going out to eat with friends. At Blue Sage there were many options for me and I couldn't have been more pleased.

Before I get to the food I would first like to compliment our server, Charlee. She was very kind and well educated on the menu. This is important because I can't eat gluten and get very nervous when dining at a restaurant for the first time. She made my first experience at Blue Sage fantastic!!

For starters, she offered a delicious UNSWEETENED raspberry iced tea, which is almost impossible to find! We also got an appetizer, the Tacos Verduras. The amount of texture and flavor piled high on a homemade blue corn taco was more than satisfying. I split this with a friend but was tempted to put in another order as my meal. 

Instead of doing that I went for the miso pumpkin soup. The miso broth was jam packed with flavor and even developed a slight creamy texture. The soup was hearty and had medium, bite sized chunks of cauliflower and pumpkin which was accompanied but the punch of flavor possessed by scallions. I was In love. 


Overall, I was extremely satisfied with the service, flavor, portions and prices. I am so excited to go back to Blue Sage and try more of their menu!

Recommended by a local, and packed for lunch by them, but overall not a do over. Very very loud and noisy, so conversation was difficult. The Reuben sandwiches didn't grab your tastebuds, and neither did the brisket sandwich. The latter was juicy and tender but no flavor over and above the roll. I would expect, from a place with these ratings, signature sandwiches that made your mouth water for another visit. Much prefer my wife's smoked brisket as a meal, then leftovers, leftovers, leftovers.

What a pleasant  surprise.  We just happened  to be driving  by and say a small crowd seated at outdoor tables. We figured  "Why not try it?". The service  was first rate and the  food was fantastic! My new favorite place.
Good food and service. The Lox bagel was very fresh! Enjoyed the ambience of the cafe as well.

This place is a diamond in the rough. The combo of  pizza and Chinese may be off putting at first but they do everything right for a good price. The General Teo's pizza was both savory and sweet with a hint of heat, the balance of flavors was spot on. Also, try any of their Chinese dishes and you will not be disappointed. The beef soup is one of my all time favorites. If you haven't tried this place you should. Don't let the shabby exterior fool you, this place is worth it.

I love the ambiance in this place, the purple walls, great ceiling light fixtures, memorabilia, red (faux) leather seats.  Great vibe.  

My food was ok, not excellent.  The charro beans didn't have as much flavor as I'd hoped.  The Tamale was good however the masa was the mushy corn/mealy type not the authentic tamale I'm used to and love.  The beef taco tasted fine but in looking at the meat it was a greyish blob that looked like half a hamburger patty, a little strange.  Again, it tasted fine but not what I'd expect in a place like this.

The red salsa had a good kick with good flavor.  The sala verde was way too thick.  I love salsa verde and this was a big disappointment.

Service was good.  

It was a decent meal but I've had better and that's exactly how two stars is defined by YELP but that seemed inappropriately low.  I am in the same boat as reviewed Don S. and I wouldn't bother returning.

Great place to eat - recently renovated and the inside looks awesome. The staff is friendly and they treat you like family here. Breakfast, lunch and dinner specials are hard to beat. Love and strongly recommend Black Horse Diner if you are looking for exceptional food and service in Mount Ephraim.

Came on a Sunday night.  Not very crowded but very loud in the upstairs dining.  No worries sound panels are on the way.  Very creative wine list and menu.  It seemed that managers were  the servers, perhaps new hires are coming.

   Now the food, dont miss the fried cornbread worth every bite.  Also the cauliflower is worth it.  Didnt love the pork thought it was a bit over cooked.  loved the farro.  Enjoyed the scallop risotto too.   All in all really liked this place but think it can continue t improve.

Met some friends for coffee/snacks here on 5/30. First, it's in Broadripple so parking is a nightmare.

First - this place is just a little too precious for my taste. Everyone in white ruffled aprons and glitter on all the food. It's very juvenile for me and not really interesting as much as irritating. But that's a personal preference. I will say that the bench seating inside is extremely uncomfortable.

Coffee drinks were good and the lemon bar I had was tasty. My friends each had a scone and said they were good but lacked flavor.

So....I'd probably go back here again if someone suggested it as a meet up spot...but it is unlikely I would go here of my own volition.
I love this place!!  Everything I have had was fantastic!  Went on a Friday night and it was packed. Great atmosphere,  and service.

New to Reno and wanted to eat downtown but had little time to research.  I rarely look for restaurant recommendations from yelp and glad I did.  Everything in the yelp reviews are true.  The Mexican Shrimp Ceviche was to die for. I will be coming back!

Oh my goodness. My first meal here was amazing. The food was impeccable, the drinks were delightful, the atmosphere warm and welcoming. But nothing compares to the kindness and care our server Steven showed us. He took his time with us and this we enjoyed ourselves even more!

First the layout of the place. There is a bar/dining area,off to the left is a kitchen, in front of that is a enclosed area with a separate entrance for take out and around back is the beer garden.I sat at the bar and had a few beers and ordered a mini pizza and a small antipasto to go.I have to say I have never seen so many employees in a place of this size. As I sat at the bar I saw dozens of pizzas going right by me on their way to the dining area. They looked awesome, crust perfectly browned, some I could see the cheese bubbling.So when I got my order back to the hotel room I was shocked, the pizza was not cooked, the crust had no color and the cheese was barely melted,on top of each slice was one scared little piece of pepperoni  .I was very hungry and ate two slices and it was so bad I threw the other two away.The salad was good so at least I was full.
I dont know what to say,everyone was ordering large pies,I might have been the only mini of the night so the kitchen said lets really screw this one up.
Words to the wise, if you have a take out order check every part of it carefully before you leave  , my mistake.

Somewhat of a hidden jewel of a place that people like to keep to themselves, because it's definitely one of mine.

I had the Chicken Quesadilla & Sangria and both were great on all levels. The flavors, smell, presentation, and the polite service would definitely get me back here in a heartbeat. 

You might want to find some time in search of parking though.
Been coming here forever!  They are the best!  Yummy salad bar and pizza as well as other Italian dishes.  Busy but friendly service.  Kathleen is the best server ever!  Can't wait to go back!
hands down the best pizza in st louis. get the chicago style supreme, you will not be disappointed...

Burgers were good - not great.  Fries are ok at best but they give you a very large portion for the price. Although, if I'm going to pay $7 for a burger, I might as well pay $3 more at another restaurant for a burger that's great and also not a fast food burger.

Just ate there for lunch.  Excellent food and service.  The restaurant is owned by a husband and wife, and she took the time to answer my questions about the menu.  She recommended that I try the shredded chicken, which was flavorful and spicy, but not heat spicy.  I also had the hot and sour soup, which was very traditional, fresh, with the right amount of kick.  Left a tingle on the lips and palate, without leaving any unpleasant burning.  Even my 11 year old daughter  loved it.  She ordered the pepper steak and the wonton soup.  The entree was excellent, with good flavor, tender steak, crisp onions and green peppers.  The wonton soup was pretty standard but good.  The restaurant is definitely worth returning to, and the fact that it is a family operation, with owners who care and who want you to feel welcome,  makes it that much better.
This place really sucks to be honest. Been here ten minutes got cursed out twice didn't even get a drink order.
This is our FAVORITE restaurant, rarely do we go out to eat anywhere BUT here. Amazing menu, value and food. The wait staff is kind and helpful and the chefs aim to please.

I love Ube and Green Tea!  Went with a big group and we all got something different.  All of them were delish!!  The owners were so hospitable and welcoming.  So happy to have Ube soft serve!! Thank you!!

I never write yelp reviews. BUT this place deserves a review! Italian owned, all noodles made in house daily, and great staff make this my new favorite Italian spot! The tiramisu topped off an amazing dining experience! We will definitely be back! Ask for Anthony!

Delivery is my specialty. lol. I love ordering-out when I'm way too busy at work. Either late lunch or dinner. I have ordered the veggie dumplings fried and steam. It is really good. My fave is the Beef Cho Ho Fun extra spicy. They are just as good as Chinatown food. I've had many other menu items from here and have never been disappointed.

From String Beans in Garlic sauce to Fried Chicken. The only thing is the delivery sur charge. lol. $1.50 is not much to ask but if your a good tipper then that just sucks.

This would be a highly recommend place to order take-out. I get my deliveries to Brewerytown and they are pretty quick.

Really delicious food and pretty quick service considering the wait to sit was an hour. Don't worry about the wait though, for $15 you can get bottomless mimosa's or bloody Mary's while you sit outside before you get your table. Chicken and waffles and Katherine's Po Boy are the only things I tried but it's definitely a place I'll go back to next time I'm in town.

I really love Cafe Pontalba.

Located at the corner of Chartres and St Peter Streets, overlooking Jackson Square, St. Louis Cathedral, and the Cabrildo Museum - Cafe Pontalba is a wonderful spot to take in all the action.

Cafe Pontalba is classic New Orleans. Floor to ceiling French doors with a large ornate marble and wood bar, with dark wooden floors. It also has extremely clean & well maintained bathrooms, which isn't always the norm in town.

Wait for a table overlooking the square. You won't be disappointed. These tables sit in the French doors, which are open rain or shine.

We love to show up there after the Noon rush to have cocktails, eat appetizers, and watch the show. Tourists, musicians, the homeless, wedding parties, physics, jugglers, a guy painted silver acting like a robot, and artists.

The cuisine is also classic New Orleans, but aimed at us tourists. The wait staff is very friendly and don't mind if you dawdle.

You have to put Cafe Pontalba on the "must do" list, when you visit the French Quarter.

Totally enjoy this place.. Food was great in fact my fat a$$ was back an hour later for more .. Seen a review here complaining because it was crowded well when you have great food and its a tourist area guess you'll have that.. But during the week not so crowded..

This restaurant is in a strip mall so don't expect a skyway. We stopped on the way back from Tampa airport and were pleasantly surprised at the quality of the food and care of the server. We ate 
outside in comfortable chairs and enjoyed the entire breakfast experience.
My favorite NY style pizza in Tampa so far! Even the crust was yummy. Love the ambience and the staff were friendly and helpful. Definitely a fun place to go for dinner.

Right up there with the best NJ diners. The portions are huge, the staff is friendly, and the prices are beyond reasonable. They are open 24 hours too, nothing bugs me more than "diners" that close. Love love love this place!

They get 2 stars for the 2 delicious desserts we ordered after a disappointing bland meal. We wouldn't have gone here ourselves, but we received a gift card and so we wanted to give it a try. 

First of all, it took a while before our waitress took our order for drinks. I felt slightly ignored. 

We went on and ordered the calamari as a starter which was just ok. For our main course we ordered the Buddha's feast (vegetables), the Mongolian beef and the honey chicken. I thought it was one of the worst American Chinese foods I've ever eaten. There was no flavor to be found, and the beef was overcooked. The vegetables were ok, though they used too much ginger for my taste. 

After we finished our main course, it took ages for our table to be cleaned up. We wanted to get to dessert to get rid of the blandness of the main course! 

We eventually ordered the banana spring rolls and the caramel cake. Both were good! 

After dessert, our waitress was nowhere to be found (again!). We had to ask someone else to bring our check. 

Would not come back here. I'd say there's better American Chinese food at the mall!

There are lots of people waiting in line! But it's really clean place to eat inside. I had really good experience ordering online, using coupon code and just waited for pick up! That will save your time!!

We walked up to the counter and the lady said there was a long wait. We decided to go for a walk down Frenchman and return a little later. When we got back there was no line and we ordered. We had the Gator bites and Creole potatoes. Was it fancy? No. Was it good? Yes? We were actually surprised how good the food was coming out of this little shack. Maybe it's not for everyone, but neither is New Orleans.
Nice atmosphere, good food & service, very enjoyable lunch.  I also liked that they have gluten free options.

Michael Solomonov does modern Mexican with local ingredients, in a colorfully decorated, inviting dining space with a lively bar area. The food is excellent, the servers are friendly and attentive.

Happy hour is a great deal. It goes from 5-7pm every day for $5 margaritas, $3 draft beer specials, and $6 Guero specials-- I had myself a marg, and it is a very stiff drink, so perfect if you've had a tough day at work or just want an early start to the night.  

Good guac is difficult to find on the East Coast, but Xochitl is known for its fresh guac with cotija cheese, prepared tableside with mortar and pestle. Chunky, delicious, and it's got a little bit of a kick to it if you let them add the red peppers (you can always request that they leave them out, but they don't make the guac overwhelmingly spicy).   

If you're getting guac anyway (and why wouldn't you?), note that the "El Sabor" special is offered daily, and it's a steal as long as the entire table has enough of an appetite for it.
