For $32, each person gets the guac, along with an appetizer and an entree (no menu item off limits). We weren't hungry enough to for it when we came, but the next time I know I'm coming to Xochitl, I'll try to plan ahead a little better to take advantage of this prix fixe option. 

For an entree, I got the Salmon marinated in achiote (a reddish seed with a bit of an earthy flavor) served over poblano crema,fava beans, and yuca tots. The fish was perfectly cooked... juicy but with a little bit of crispiness on the outside, and everything else was also tasty. 

Alas, I wish I had saved room for dessert. But there are several reasons to go back again, so perhaps I'll get to try the Postres another time.

Lazy, unorganized and unmotivated staff here as I am currently waiting in line. No falafel for 5 minutes before it was noticed and a call went out to make more. Oh, I must mention that it is 3:32 in the afternoon on a Sunday. The best part of this experience is none of the 5 people working could make the Naf fries which are a regular menu item because it would take 40 minutes. The pita looks and smells fantastic but the experience with the staff has completely turned me off. This place is despicable! Will go back to my regular falafel joint.

Update: still sitting in Naf Naf grill watching multiple food safety violations with touching non food items and then food with the same gloves. One employee came out to dining room and gave somebody a hug and then rested gloved hand on a railing and then back behind the counter to continue making peoples orders without changing gloves or proper handwashing. Wonder how long I will sit here and enjoy this comedy show of a food establishment.

During a recent visit to Central Indiana, friends took us to an Italian restaurant not far from their home in Carmel. If you're looking for a taste of Tuscany, Convivio, is the place to go. Located in a strip center, (What restaurant isn't these days?) Convivio has an open airy feeling with high ceilings and tables that are far enough away from each other so that you do not have to yell to have a conversation with your dining companions. Upon arrival, were promptly seated and our drink orders were taken. Our drinks arrived along with an order of warm focaccia and olive oil with tomato and herbs for dipping. 
The menu covers all the bases, including veal, beef, chicken, and pasta dishes along with a variety of pizzas that you will not find and your local pizzeria. The house caesar salad has just the right amount of dressing with the right number of croutons. Anchovies, which are available upon request were flavorful and not oily. Two of us had the Tonnarelli alla Puttanesca, which came in a spicy tomato sauce. The dish had just the right amount of heat and saltiness from the capers. Special orders can be accommodated as one of our party requested the shrimp prepared in a garlic butter sauce, scampi style. The shrimp were large and cooked well. The other person had the Tagliatelle el Convivo. All the pastas came out al dente with just the right amount of chew. 
Dinner was capped off by the four us splitting an order of homemade Tiramisu which was a perfect end to a wonderful meal. Our server, Kathy, was excellent. She explained each dish and attended to our needs without seeming to hover. Dinner for four people with two adult beverages was $131.00. I would highly recommend Convivio for dinner with friends or that special occasion.

For me, the most important aspect of a Mexican restaurant is the salsa. If a restaurant doesn't have good salsa, I won't return, but Alderto's has some awesome salsa. They have a few different kinds, including two verdes. My favorite is the creamier verde, which has a bit of a spicy kick. It's not the best salsa in the universe or anything (which I'm still on a hunt for), but it does the trick when I have a craving for some Mexican food. So far it's the best salsa I've tried in Reno!

I usually order the shrimp burrito, and it comes loaded with shrimp. I'm always impressed with the quantity of shrimp in the burrito for the price (less than $5). 

One of the cashiers here is a sweetheart and provides excellent service in a very softspoken way. 

I will return! Actually, I already come here like twice a month.

2.5 stars. I really wanted to like this place, but damnit, they failed.

Not awful but not worthy of the current 4.5 star rating. And the food was meh for being a New Orleans southern restaurant. 

Here's what we had:
App: crawfish etoufee - very tasty, no complaints about this except the price ($7 for a little cup!)
Soup: Gumbo - this was okay but they got the gumbo's mixed up and gave me the chicken one instead of the seafood one
Main: bf had "A Taste of Soul" Platter - Filé Gumbo, Red Beans & Rice, Jambalaya, Greens, Fried Chicken, Catfish Strips, and Bread Pudding, collard greens, while I had: Stuffed Bell Pepper  - A green bell pepper stuffed with ground beef, shrimp, spices, and seasonings, baked and topped with our light home-style brown gravy, with red beans/rice, and mac/cheese
shared the bread pudding for dessert

BF really enjoyed his entree, while I found everything about mine to be lacking. BF's was good because all the fried seafood was low in fattiness, had a nice cornmeal crust and was light on oil. Mine sucked because the stuffing in the bell pepper was just whatever, and the mac and cheese was embarrassing - it had the texture of being reheated leftovers (overly mushy noodles and hard cheese) and tasted like almost nothing, box kraft is better. And it was not hot like the bell pepper. The cornbread was not warm either so I didn't get to enjoy any nice crust on top. 
Bread pudding dessert was hot and delicious, though it had nuts so it automatically became all mine. This was the best part of the meal.

Beyond the food being less than impressive, at least my dish, the service was pretty lacking. It took a looong time for a server to get to us, while a neighboring party sat down later, ordered and received their food before us. Another neighboring party had super crappy service too, and even asked for a comment card, and of course did not get one. They could have walked out and not paid, given that they had to actually flag someone else down and ask them to please take their money so they could go, those words literally.

So, I say there is a lot of room for improvement here.

Ok - Colts day game and 20 minute wait which is understandable - but not when I counted 32 tables empty in the main dinning room areas.  Seriously - they can't schedule enough help to service the tables they have?  Someone needs to look at this manager and ask how many sales he/she sent to the restaurants next door?  BTW - Walked across to Champs / packed and seated immediately.
The quality of the food and speed of service isn't consistent with their downtown location. Sashimi pieces weren't cut all the way or were ripped. Also the bowl of rice was dry.
This is some of the best pizza I've ever had. Amazing atmosphere, really friendly wait staff who make you feel welcome and at home.

So I got the MEMO about the 50 cents oyster @ Happy Hour...and during our visit to NOLA...we were so eager to go to eat as many oysters possible at a steal deal price!

Arrived around 4ish on a HOT (week)day. We both were tourists..wearing shorts, t-shirts and sandals just like MOST others in the bar (happy) hour area. The hostess was friendly but the waiter was just a plain @$$ ...pardon my language here.

Yup, we got the head to toe look and he walked around and talked to us with his nose pointing to the ceiling, oh, come on!! We didn't care really... all we wanted were just some fresh oysters and great beer to wash away the heat.

We ordered a dozen of the oysters and the duck liver and rabbit pate $8 with two glasses of beer (we later got a second round of beer).

The oysters came out slowly.. we almost finished our beer when they arrived. They looked grossed and not cleaned well. I understand it was 50 cents each..but they shouldn't cut corners on cleanliness especially while serving raw food plus they are a fancy restaurant..how do you expect us to come back for the pricier dinner if you can't even clean the oysters well?

We were thinking to order a couple more dozens but the fact that we tasted the debris from the oyster shucking process in each oyster PLUS the unappetizing look of the small shells sticking on the oyster' shells.. we just got turned off!

The pate was excellent and we loved the pickled cucumber etc and the warm toasted bruchetta that came with it and $8 was certainly worth the priced. We licked it clean!!

We were planning to go to Luke for a couple times during our NOLA visit and even considered going there for dinner (we watch food network and top chef masters) BUT our not-so-great first (and only) happy hour experience @ Luke left none to desire to come back.

Our total tab including tax and tip was about $40... they get you on the alcohol..

The pate is a 4 to 5 stars..the oyster price is also a 5 stars, BUT the snotty service and lack of cleanliness didn't make the cut..so I'm giving Luke a fair 3 stars.

Last night I paid 50 bucks for me and my girlfriend to go to a show. They sold so many tickets, it was probably a fire code violation. I tried unsuccessfully for over 30 minutes (no exaggeration!) just to get a drink, gave up, and went home.  I want my money back! 
Last night left a horrible taste in my mouth.
The original and teriyaki wings are awesome, and the menu is so eclectic, love it! The servers are nice, sometimes the wait is a little longer than I like so I recommend ordering ahead of time.

This place is awesome. It's right on the pier and it's not a fancy schmansy type of seafood restaurant which I love. I hate hate hate touching my food without utensils so when I go to a seafood place, I want to go to one where I can get dirty and not feel judged.  My boyfriend and I got a whole crab and whole lobster.  They came with some sides and with two drinks it came out to be about $95, which is decent for the size of our fresh, steamed crustaceans.  The menu/prices are written on the chalkboards above the bar area.  The atmosphere was great and the service was good. I would definitely come back and recommend to others.

There are much better Mexican joints to hang out at in Philly.  Wound up here on a Friday afternoon, thanks to Steve Starr having the brilliant idea not to open his beer gardens until 4 PM on Fridays (huh?) for some drinks and light food.

The beer list is decent and the happy hour margaritas are only $2.50 (which probably is worth a star by itself), but the table-service and the food wrecked the experience.

We were there for about 4 hours from about 2:30 PM to 6:30 PM - a group of professionals looking for drinks and food with money to spend.  From the time we ordered our first drinks until the time the waitress bothered to come back and check on us was over an hour...we were so thirsty that people were going to the bar by themselves and paying cash...and hungry...we were ready to order food no one in sight, that it was sad.  One of the women with us, who had waitressed in a prior life, actually considered pulling the girl aside and explaining to her how much she was losing in tips.  And it is a tiny dining room and the place was mostly empty until about 5 PM.

The food barely rose above Chipoltle-quality, although it was relatively inexpensive for Philly.  The guacamole was very spicy, but that didn't mask that the avocados didn't taste fresh at all.  The tomatoes in the salsa were bland and mushy.

Won't be back.

There is an abundance of fresh seafood options in Santa Barbara. 

My gf and I like SB Seafood Co. because the food is fresh, the atmosphere is awesome, views of the harbor are excellent, and the service is friendly.

Seating inside and outside are a bit scarce, but if you are lucky enough to get one of the 4 outdoor tables, you will have an amazing view of the harbor and pier. 

Daily specials vary. 

We went big for dinner last time ordering Maine lobster and Alaskan king crab.

This time around for lunch we tried to order light. 

We started with the lobster bisque and a couple of oyster shooters.

The bisque was pretty amazing. The shooters were on par w/ Brophy's which were very tasty.

For the main event I ordered maine lobster roll. Pretty bomb...loaded w/ lobster meat I split it with my gf. It came with onion rings and cole slaw. 

My gf ordered the fried oysters, calamari, shrimp, and scallops. Pretty delicious. The calamari were a little over cooked and chewy though. The rest were well executed.

Santa Barbara Seafood Co. is a nice option on the pier, and is definitely a nice spot to grab good eats when a seafood craving is in order!

I heard the food was great here and was looking forward to trying it out.  I liked the food, so five stars... until I felt a hair in my mouth that wasn't mine.  Maybe it was the cooks? Upside, I nearly finished my food, downside, I nearly finished my food and then got a cold sweat wondering how many more strange hairs I had consumed.  Took waaaaay too long for the food to come to the table as well. People who showed up after us were already eating.  Waitress didn't seem to care about how long it was taking to get our food. And when it finally came, about 45 minutes later, not so much as a "sorry for the wait."  

Smart business says when you have people waiting as long as we did, comp something to soften the blow.  Or, at least show some shame by offering an apology. They get a pass on the hair because I didn't say anything... until now...
Fast, fast fast pizza! 180 seconds and they are calling your name, wow! The Red Vine is the classic, fresh mozzarella, cherry tomatoes, basil and parmesan. Salads were and ready Togo.

Didn't live up to expectations.

We were excited based on all the positive reviews, but Luke sadly didn't pay off.  I started off with a mint julep which tasted like bourbon water. Zero mint or sweetness to it.  For dinner I had the shrimp and grits which was very tasty, but the portion was so small.  It was sized more for an appetizer rather than entree.  When I pay over $20 for a dish it needs to be somewhat filling.  Creme brulee for desert was good.

I would not go back.
Had a taste of halo halo, it was yummy and satisfied my craving... A perfect summer treat!!!

Worth the hype! Had a fantastic dinner. The secret ingredients, as always: great, uncomplicated food and great service. I had both at Luke.

First, the waiter, Ryan, was excellent. The kind of waiter whose recommendations actually mean something. Easygoing but very attentive.

Second, the food. Oysters, duck and rabbit pate, Luke burger, and bread pudding to finish. I was Thanksgiving full, but I couldn't stop eating. Everything was on the money and a great treat on a rainy NOLA night!!! Highly recommended for dinner (breakfast was okay, but not memorable).

We really enjoyed our meal here. Inside staff was great and attentive. Young gentleman doing hostess at door could use some additional training on customer service and friendliness. He lacked both. 
Mac and cheese was to die for!absolutely mouthwatering. The Pork belly was ok, would prefer a bit more crunch/crispness. Crab Gnochi was good as well, although a bit cold when it arrived.  Aurora Nealand was performing with her band royal roses, they were outstanding!

I love the layout of this place.  There's a typical pizza shop on one side to pick up something quick and a restaurant side if you're looking for waiter service.  The food is good with no items that stand out.  Most of the cheesesteak/hoagies are around $6 - $7, with a $1.75 drink, you gotta meal for under $10.

One plus, BEER!  They have an ok selection of 6-packs.

DELICIOUS! I heard about Katie's on Diners, Drive-Ins  & Dives a while back. My husband and I thought we'd try it while honeymooning in NOLA. SO glad we did! We had 2 half salads, 1 Scottie's Special with fries, and 1 Hot Roast Beef and Gravy with fries. All I can say is YUM!!!

If you can't find a parking spot on the street- which we couldn't- there is a parking lot just for Katie's patrons on Telemach St in between Iberville St and Bienville St!

What a gem!!!!! I love a good shrimp taco!!! These are definitely an authentic shrimp taco. Im usually not a huge fan of corn tortillas but these were actually very good!!!! I love how you can select your own toppings and the pickled onions were such a good choice. The jamaica was good too. Staff was very friendly as well. If I lived in Philly this would be my good to place
Awesome noodle bowls. Chicken wings and brussel sprouts were delicious too. Nice drink selection with good service. Only downfall is it is very tiny.
Walked in the door and was treated very rudely so we turned around and left. Don't care to eat at a place when the hostess is the first person to great you and is rude
I'm from San Francisco and I'm impressed with this place. Ambience, cocktails, food and staff are great!

Great food. The menu changes and it's unique. I'm glad these guys are expanding to center city as well. Duck fries are good and I hate fries in general. Plenty of brunch options. The place is a bit crowded and seating isn't the best. But the food is great so that makes it worth it!

been here a handful of times. pretty average food overall but they have one item in particular that's pretty delicious: the Truck Stop.

don't let the overtly unappealing name stop you, this burger is really good. read the menu if you want a description.. all I can tell you is I honestly thought it was delicious. 

if you're the owner of lucky belly, please change the name of this wonder burger. What about "The Doubledecker"? it might not be a perfect name, but at least it doesn't conjure up such gross imagery.

Worst service ever. Waited in a nearly empty restaurant for 15 minutes and were never acknowledged by the staff. Right before we walked out another group walked in and were immediately seated. The staff walked by us several times but never asked to seat us. Maybe we were a threatening grouo with the 3 year old, visually impaired young man, mommy and granparents. Farm life.

These worlds greatest food!! Obviously Hillary Clinton has good taste! Always a wait but so worth it. I bring all my friends here and no one has ever complained. People will remember you there and are always friendly!!! I live for it every morning :)
This was my favorite shrimp and fish taco place in philly. But they changed their taco bread and sauce and now I can't even force myself to eat there.

Incredible food! Incredible service! Incredible bartender! I ordered a pizza, which was delicious and bigger than expected. I couldn't finish it. The bartender made drinks using a piece of wood that he smoked with fire and then fills the glass with smoke. The atmosphere was relaxing, and the music playing matched. Trendy spot. Perfect for a date.

Coming from SoCal, we have been looking for an authentic taco experience. We stumbled upon this hidden gem recently and it did not disappoint.  Great, flavorful carne asada, tasty salsas and real horchata! Even the tortillas are made fresh! Stop by!

I discovered this place when it was under different ownership, and there may have been 3 owners during the time I have gone there.  Went there yesterday for lunch.  The place is cleaner than I have ever seen it, hence the 2nd star, but the food is strictly blah.  We had pulled pork as a luncheon special, one had baked beans the other coleslaw on the side.  The pork wasn't bad, seemed to be a whole Boston butt cooked on premises, but they ruined it with lousy commercial barbecue sauce, too salty, too nondescript.  Coleslaw, the same, right out of a can or container, too sweet.

I think I can safely say I won't be returning anytime in the near future.
Great restaurant. Open 24 hours, and they always put the most toppings on my sandwich. i love it.

Wife and I decided to give this a try we are from Southern California and we are mostly use to those kind of all you can eat Korean bbq decided to give this spot a try and It was great and service was awesome only downside is that it isn't all you can eat. So it can get a bit pricey but overall food was awesome really hit the spot for being homesick
A little pricy but well worth it. The honey wheat bread and twisted shrimp are excellent.

Fantastic dinner for our last night in New Orleans!  The food was delicious and the staff went above and beyond in every category. Our preteen and teen decided it was the best restaurant experience of the trip.

A few month's ago I wrote a "just OK" review of St Elmo's which is owned by the same people as Harry & Izzy's and located right next door. So, when I was back in Indy I wanted a "do over." Unfortunately the wait for a table of 10 was almost 2 hours so they were kind enough to make reservations for us at Harry & Izzy's their sister restaurant.

My party and I sat outdoors on a beautiful night. The food was excellent. We all shared appetizers including the famous St. Elmo's shrimp cocktail. This time the shrimp were firm and while the cocktail sauce was strong it was not overpowering. I also shared a 20 rib eye with a friend and it was delicious. I would be remiss if I did not add that the service was excellent.

I ordered from this place a couple months ago and was blown away - it was super good. I ordered from here last week and was soo disappointed. It wasn't good at all. I got the fish family combo. First off the salad was old and turning brown. The beans looked like vegetable soup. The yellow rice was orange. I ended up throwing the whole thing out. I'm giving two stars instead of one because it might have been an off night.  One time is all I need - wont be ordering from here again.

I hate places that advertise with a coupon, but then have special conditions.  Did the Drive-in with a coupon, "buy one, get one free, up to $8".  When they looked at the coupon they said they would only take the coupon if we bought an $8 combo, which was the most expensive item.  NO-GO.  Went to El Pollo Loco instead.

Great Food, Organic & Gluten Free Options readily available. Casual Atmosphere that helps transport you to the Island of Hawaii - even if it is just for an Hour during Lunch. Friday night Hula shows are also a hit with Young & Old alike. The service is excellent, You can beat Free Hugs from Mama or the Owner, Teresa! ... I'm now craving popovers. mmmmmmmm

Cute little local coffee house without it being a chain. The coffee is delicious and I love ALL of the bakery items.  I just wish it was larger because oftentimes I cant find a seat and have to leave instead of staying and enjoying the ambiance.....but I don't want them to move because the location is perfect!

Why do I always forget to take pictures here??  argh!  

Actually... there's a simple explanation for that.  I forget to take pictures of the establishment because I'm so excited and distracted by the smells and decisions that need to be made.  I signed up for their emails YEARS ago and now every single week I get an email that tells me what their soups and salads are for the week, as well as what their hot special is each day.

More often than not I go for the turkey sandwhich.  You won't find processed deli meats here... it's real, fresh tasting turkey and they ALWAYS have cranberry sauce on hand for it.  yum.  It's a build your own sandwich type place, similar to Fife n dekel in Edmonton, if you're familiar.  The veggie toppings are pretty standard, and they also have various mustards and spreads available for you.

One of the hot specials this week pulled me in.. it was the perogies.  I'm a sucker for a great homemade perogies, and I just knew they wouldn't be serving me cheemos!  I can't say I was disappointed, but I'll admit that they were not as good as I hoped they would be.  Just a tad bland.  But the sausage that was served with it really made up for that.  SO GOOD.

Once in a while they have a meatball sub special that seems to be really popular.  I'll have to try it out.  And maybe I'll remember to take some damn pictures!!

Born n raised in Brooklyn so Roti and Caribbean food in general is a regular part of my diet.  The lack of good Caribbean restaurants in philly is a recurring disappointment.  that being said I was happy to find this place. The Roti skin is flavorful, not too doughy or chewy and just the right amount of flaky.  The chicken inside was well seasoned and for only $6 you definitely get a good amount for the price. I've had it twice so far and definitely plan on returning next time I get a hankering. 

Haven't tried their baked goods yet but I have my eye on their currant rolls. 

Also, Roti is traditionally made with the meat left on the bone so please ignore other reviewers complaining about that. It adds to the experience as you also get to enjoy the sauces that the bones soak up.

I will let the one rude employee slide. Service otherwise was unremarkable. What I find utterly unacceptable is that the exit at the rear of the dining area has been blocked by a trash receptacle, blocking egress in case of a fire or other emergency. I am certain this is a violation of fire and safety codes, even by Tennessee standards.
Los jefes is a hidden gem in Metairie. Best Mexican food you can find without going to south Texas. Margaritas and enchiladas are my favorite.

Perfect lunch spot. Fast friendly service. Food is pretty good. You can be in and out in 20 minutes. Great prices. I get the 1/2 sandwich and soup lunch special that comes with fries and a desert item and it costs less than $10
The Georgia Peach Pancakes are one of my favorite things ever... (the coffee needs work, but just head over to Fido next door for that!)
We had the daily special . Great quality food and service . And kids are welcome which is a plus Will be back

Long-time fan of Ralph's here.  I adore sweetbreads, which are not on every Italian restaurant's menu.  So i go to Ralph's for sweetbreads.  I think the mushrooms in the dish are canned, but the sweetbreads are perfect, with a light sauce and are a huge portion.  I'm also crazy about their Fettucini Alfredo, which is the real thing, made with pasta, butter, parm and cream and nothing else.  My partner always orders spaghetti and meatballs - he's not a foodie and that's what he likes.  Since I order 2 entrees (so I'll have leftovers tomorrow), we don't get out of there cheaply, but I love the place.  And yes, it's a good place to bring visiting firemen - old-time ambience, attentive service, and Sarcone's bread.

This is one of my go to places for a good lunch. Always receive good aervice and the Reuben sammich is off the hook. It's the Rye bread that does it. Oh and they serve Pepsi which gets them an extra star in my book.

Friendly and acomodating. Great food. Waitress was attentive and when she did not have an answer she went and got it. The food was excellent and fast enough.  Great location! Will definitely come back.
Pizza was perfect. Walked in and the restaurant smelled freshly cleaned. Very nice people behind the counter too.
Mediocre pizza, terrible service, pizza showed up folded & squished, single most painful ordering process I have ever experienced.

Maybe it was just a bad day, but our recent experience and first time at the 29th street location was a disappointment.  Previous visits to the 22nd street location were always positive.  The waitress was pleasant.  The food, however, was not.  We were not offered the standard peppers and onions; the chips were stale and mostly small, small chips; my whole talapia was burned to a crisp; and the other meals were just passible and cold.  There were no other patrons in the restaurant.  Overall the quality did not match the prices.  "All good things must come to an end."

Blondie's makes me wish I still worked downtown. It is a great addition to Washington and I've been (mostly) impressed the two times I've been. First just for drinks late on a Saturday. Other than 2-3 other small parties, the place was quiet. I was really surprised considering how busy everything else seemed to be. The decor is brilliant - cozy, comfortable, and practical. It's a mix of normal dining tables along with armchairs and sofas. Since we weren't ordering food we were able to relax by the fire. Nice!

I was also there for lunch on Saturday and the food was delicious. I tried the veggie sandwich and the turkey, green apple, mayo sandwich. Both came on a plain popover which made them impossible to eat with your hands. They were closer to an open-faced sandwich. Which leads me to my first complaint - the paper than they cover the plates with. Makes no sense at all. The sauce from the sandwiches quickly made the paper soggy and since I had to eat with utensils I was carving up the paper along with my sandwich. It was really annoying and impossible not to do. But that's an easy fix. The veggie was world's better than the turkey and this is only the second time ever I've raved about a veggie sandwich. You get either chips or fruit as a side and the chips come in a generous portion.

My other complaint is service was really, really slow. Slow to order, really slow to get our food (even though, again, there were only 3 other tables occupied), and we never did get our check delivered. We eventually went up front to pay. If service is like this during the work week, I can't imagine who would continue to go here.

Big bonus points for playing TCM on the TV's. But not cool that they have two bathrooms, both of which are unisex. Please make one a boy's and one a girl's. I hate using a public restroom after a guy. Gross.

But overall I love this place and it seems to work equally well as a lunch spot or late night hangout, which few places can do.

I was very impressed with this local food hub.  My fiancé and I were staying the night in Carpinteria for our Valentine's Day weekend, and I wanted to make sure that I took him to a scenic and delicious spot for dinner. After scouring Yelp for places with good reviews, I finally decided on this little place. I was so pleasantly surprised not only with quality in food, but also the friendly staff and ambiance.  This location is definitely the perfect place for a cute date night or even family event. The seating area gives you the option of porch seating with cozy chairs and heaters, or outdoor seating with picnic tables and a really cute grassy layout. The food was amazing and I would definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants to try something new!

Yes, it's true, the best tacos in Tucson are here! The staff is also very friendly, I love that there's a chips and salsa bar, and the watermelon-cucumber juice is to DIE FOR. You definitely can't go wrong ordering three tacos with a side of the Mexican rice. I will definitely be back!

I've been eating here for years and it never disappoints. They can get pretty busy so be prepared to wait or order ahead of time. I haven't tried anything other than the Cuban all the way with a side of sauce because it's so good I don't want to try anything else. 
The salad looks like the sub without the bread and it literally spills out of the Togo boxes they come in. 
The portions are huge here so come with a friend or a big appetite.

I wanted to try this place for a while and all I can say is that it was worth it.  Had the meat and cheese apetizer with freshly made bread, the meatballs where delicious and the fresh pasta. I can't wait to go back and try the pizza. The staff was great from the valet parking to the waiter. 
We got seated in this separate room like a party room with a nice decor that made me feel like if I was inside a cellar.
Well done!
The best Mexican food in Reno. Greeted and waited by Abel the owner was very nice!! We asked for combo Fajitas and the Apalancate dish with 2 for 1 Patron Margaritas, well worth for the price.
Tasty! Get the special sald with the grilled hot chicken! What a " semi-healthy" treat.
It's very cute. Really outstanding service. Not too expensive. And the food is really good

Wow, I've been hearing a lot about this place and I'm happy I finally did decide to stop in. It was super busy for a Wednesday night but it was so so yummy. Definitely worth the wait. The fish tacos were delicious, you won't be disappointed!

Great Mexican food. BEST queso. Clean environment, fast good service. My favorite thing is the nachos, with rice on them. Chicken is really well cooked and seasoned. Usually always fresh food anytime of day.

Seasons Pizza is usually pretty good. Up until this order, I ordered a grilled chicken salad along with my co-workers lunches at 11:30 am hoping for a 12:30 pm delivery. Their lunches arrived on time but mine was missing. I called and asked about it and they said they would send my order out now. About an hour later it arrived, the salad container had opened and spilled into the bag and the co tents where a mess. Also you can tell by the amount of condensation that the food had been sitting for a while. 

In the end I waited over 3 hours to throw a salad in the trash.


UPDATE:

Not a minute after I posted this a service rep called me and asked about my order. We talked about the foods tardiness and the salad order. Throughout the whole conversation she was very polite and sincere about the entire situation and saw to it to fix it with a store credit. I am not one to ask for anything but this was great service!

John and Caya are just an amazing couple and it is no surprize that Urban Eats is just as amazing as they are!  Everything they do, they do to their very best and that includes dancing.  They are two ot the best dancers in St Louis.  So do yourselves a BIG favor and check out Urban Eats the first chance you get!!! Uhmmm.....dance and eat.....now that a concept to think about......

I went for an early dinner (5:30 pm) on a Saturday evening to celebrate my daughter's birthday. Four adults in our party. The wait to be seated wasn't long even though the place was pretty crowded. However, the wait for our order to be taken and for all the food was much longer than is should have been. The food was good, nothing spectacular, but tasty and the portions were large. The pan fried dumplings were very good and well presented. The egg rolls were not crispy, as I expected, but were very good and came with a delicious mild sweet mustard sauce. Son-in-law had the Buddha's Delight, which seemed fresh and appealing. My chicken fried rice was fine, I've had better but still it was nothing to complain about.  The real problem came when we asked the server to bring the check. Since my son and I were hosting my daughter and her husband, we wanted to split the check between us. Then the server told us that their credit card machine was "still" down (as if we were supposed to already know about it) and that she would have to run it by hand so she could not split the check because it would be too complicated and would require her to figure out the tax herself and that it would take too long. She then brought us four separate checks, expecting all of us to pay individually. So I took two and my son took two and gave her our credit cards. Again, the server told us we couldn't do it that way. My son politely insisted. We weren't asking her for a miracle, only to run the cards by hand as every merchant did before the days of electronic credit card readers. Finally she said that she would "try" but it would probably take too long.  She was quite rude about all this, with no apology. We had not been warned ahead of time that there was a problem with the credit card machine. It wasn't until we had already had our meal that we were told of the problem. We should have been informed about it at our arrival. In the end we were able to work it out but she was quite ungracious about the whole thing. Between that and the long waits for our appetizers and meals, I can't recommend this particular P.F. Changs.

Was so happy that I was referred here by a family member! This place is the true definition of South Philly. This place is owned and run by 3 generations of the family who are always there. We showed up with 2 large bottles of wine, ready to enjoy a nice long meal. 

To start, we got the stuffed artichoke after reading the previous reviews - was just as everyone described, delicious and savory. 

I had the filet which was cooked perfectly, but skimped a little on the sides (asparagus and potatoes). I say your best bet is to go with a homemade pasta dish for the full experience!

I admit, I'm biased for this restaurant. But this is comfort food, people!

My husband and I stopped in on a very busy Saturday night... We walked by and I instantly craved the bread and sauce. We were seated within 15 minutes, and the service was very good all night. My salad was perfectly crisp and refreshing, especially after walking a few blocks in the heat and rain. I had ravioli and my husband had rigatoni; both were satisfying and just how we remembered.

We had room for dessert, a surprising occurrence, so we split the Tortoni - Wow! Other than the glob of canned whipped cream, it was awesome! The macaroon crust was flavorful without being overpowering. The almond ice cream complemented wonderfully.

If you are looking for the most authentic Italian or the latest thing, look elsewhere. But if you want a tried and true Tucson tradition, come to Carusos and sit on the patio.

Delicia was great! Their cocktails are handcrafted and delicious - try the Fire & Ice! They made vegetarian accommodations for me, and it was wonderful. I definitely recommend this spot for a perfect date night or night out with friends. It's a nicer place with a down to earth feel. I'll be back!
this place is great. i was there for a burger for the second time and was amassing.service was great and food come out fast.this guys know how to make a great tasting meal.am coming back for more.

My family and I moved to the area several months ago and have been searching for a  great pizza place and have come up short until now.  Our neighbor suggested Pizza Mizza.  We gave it a shot last night and we are thrilled.  This place is much more then your run of the mill pizza joint.  The quality of the food and menu selection is outstanding.  My wife and I loved the fact we could order a great glass of wine and a cold beer while the kids enjoyed their dinners from the kids menu.  Love the patio and love the fact that they deliver.  We are definitely looking forward to our next visit!

For those that are mesmerized by St. Elmo's I highly suggest trying this place for a different vibe and larger menu.  St. Elmo's is old school steak house with limited choices. Harry and Izzy's has softer edges with great food. Of course, they have the famous shrimp cocktail but also things like calamari with a chili sauce condiment as a starter. Steak is on the menu, but not king. Delicious wood fired pizzas, fresh beet salad, half a roast chicken are just a few gorgeous items that I've tried which have been wonderful. I much prefer Harry and Izzy's to St. Elmo's, though, if you have never tried St. Elmo's it is important to go at least once for the history and respect  of a tried and true steak house.  Almost forgot to add that their creme brûlée just can't be beat...nothing crazy, just straight up eggs, cream, sugar, vanilla turned into heaven.
To be honest, the food is good, not awesome. But the people are friendly and I can't say no to a hot bowl of pho in the middle of a hectic work day.

WOW. Spectacular food!! 

Hosted a large private dinner party here in their private room. Although we were only given two waiters- the food was absolutely phenomenal. Highly recommend the filet and fish dishes! Looking forward to going back.

This place is good, it's not great. Service is fast, efficient and friendly for sure but the overall experience is lacking....something but I can't place it. I ordered a cheeseburger med-rare with truffle fries and a black & white milkshake. Since all of these combined is pretty much my favorite thing I ever I was more than willing to hand over the $12 for the opportunity. Okay, now the food:

1) The burger. It's not like the burger isn't good, because it is. It's just not...I find myself saying "Five Guys". I admit I don't have the most refined of palettes so take that with a grain of salt. It came out more medium than medium rare and it's somewhat small. I can tell that it's quality meat but I like my burgers juicy and this one just isn't quite. The bun is also a huge factor for me in a burger and I just don't like this style. (Id dock Good Dog for the same reason. Love the meat but the bun just doesn't cut it for me). 

2) The truffle fries. Omfg. The best part of the meal. The fries are amazing. I'd probably just pop in and buy them on their own. And at this price I don't see myself ordering truffle fries from any other establishment ever again.

3) The milkshake. Boy do I love me a Black & White. This one was just too chocolate-y for my liking. It tasted much more like just a regular chocolate milkshake which in and of itself isn't such a bad thing except for when what you really want is the holy, blended harmony of rich heavy chocolate and light as air and sweet as pie vanilla. 

All in all, the proximity to my workplace and the fact that it is, well, actually good belies that there will surely be more 500 Degrees in my future. I might tweak a few things like ordering the burger rare and can you get extra cheese? ;) I wouldn't be surprised to see this spot updated even before the next work week is out.
Sterilized .. commercialized.. canned.. what more can I say?  Wasn't impressed with the beer or cocktail menus..

Nice little Boston-themed seafood house. This is one of my go-to places when I'm too lazy to cook and want a place where I won't feel out-of-place eating alone. Almost all of the food is good, but they do the fried stuff especially well, from shrimp to oysters to the fish and chips. The "chips" (fries) are among the best I've ever had--great texture and seasoning.

Guaranteed to have Sam's and Sam's seasonals on draft at all times, but otherwise an extremely no-frills beer selection. Great for watching any Boston-based teams play on TV. Addition of a sushi bar adds a very East-Nashville quirkiness.

The coolest part of La Va is their Israeli brunch specialties.  Every Saturday, they offer the Jachnoon (pastry with side of boiled egg and tomato sauce), which supposedly takes 12 hours to cook.  Other Israeli specialties include the Buraka (snake-shaped pastry with variety of fillings) and Shakshuka (poached egg in spicy tomato sauce).  Other than that, the cafe is mediocre.  They don't like people planting themselves with laptops for too long, the bathrooms aren't very clean, and the furniture is kind of dingy.  Nontheless, its worth it for trying Israeli specialties during a Saturday brunch, especially if the weather is nice and you can get a spot outside.

Excellent food. A nice change from all the Cajun/Creole (although I love it too). Nice French inspired menu. Zucchini roulade was crazy good. 
Lovely, CLEAN atmosphere, wonderful attentive service and the local lore was fun!

This was one of two Besh restaurants that I visited during my time in New Orleans, and neither disappointed (see review for Restaurant August). Came here for breakfast and ordered the eggs in purgatory, which were fantastic. Perfectly baked eggs in tomato sauce with duck sausage. My friend ordered a stuffed omelet which was fluffy and delicious. Atmosphere of the place was lovely and bright, and our server was very attentive. Great experience.

LOVE! Lilly's has been my favorite lunch spot since high school! The chicken Caesar salad is my absolute fav! They have all fresh ingredients and several delicious sandwiches as well. You can also order for pickup. I will definitely be back for years to come!

First time here. The service was awesome! The young ladies working today have clearly been trained well they were very professional, and always anticipated my needs I didn't have to ask for anything. Had a blackened chicken burrito which was great the chicken was a little dry which is the only reason I didn't give 5 stars.

I think if you read about this place before going, you'd realize that it is meant for large parties, weddings, dinner meetings, etc. I would not recommend coming here for a nice casual dinner because it would give you too much opportunity to tear in to the places out-dated feel, decor, and staff. Instead, go with a large group, order the basics that can't be messed up, and enjoy a place big enough to house you all comfortably!

I come here with an alumni group each year and the reason we keep coming back is that it's dependable; has adequate, free, and easy-to-get-to parking; and can fit us all at its bar and dining room. They also provide the cake and cheese tray for us for a small fee. It's not cheap, nor is it expensive. We get prime rib and chicken Oscar as entrée choices and get good feedback on the food. Personally, I think it's okay as well, although I've never tried the prime rib. Again, this place isn't fancy, but it is functional for large groups. 

The wait staff are generally friendly, as are the bartenders. "Treat others as you would like to be treated" type of folks from what I could tell- can't really fault them for that...

Dinner at Marti's the day after Memorial Day.  Nice hostess and attentive bartender.  Half price wine by the glass during happy hour.  

The dining room is nicely decorated with super soft leather seating.  The wait staff was on-point but the meal took a long time to arrive.  Asked to change out veggies on the main course, waiter had to ask the chef if that was ok.  Chef say no, didn't want to compromise the dish!  I thought the chef worked for the paying customers, not the other way around.  Meal was ok, nothing special about it.

There are many great dining choices in NOLA.  This is not one of them.
This is one of my favorite breakfast/brunch places in town. Friendly staff and amazing food. If you didn't bring cash that's okay there is an atm on site. The atmosphere is rather homey.

There was a great variety of food.  We went during lunch and there were items from ceviche to carved meats .  One of the best mac and cheese I have ever tasted.  Everything tasted really good.  There is a big desert section that includes a gelato station.  The buffet is very reasonably priced.

The pretty friendly employees appear to be so ashamed of the pink slabs of mystery deli meats --- What is "prosciuttini"?--- and bland white cheeses that they try to obscure your view of them with a giant poster on the glass of their refrigerator case. Bread is baked there, it appears, but it is like a big cottony hamburger roll; not appetizing. Peculiarly flavorless food.

First time trying this place, and I'm only writing this review hoping that the owners take notice. First with the bad: their hash browns are terrible. Its as if they tried to fry instant potato flakes. 
The good: everything else. The service was personable, and efficient. The rest of the food was as expected from a diner. The french toast was possibly the best I've had, but i am partial to cinnamon which they incorporate into the dish. 
Fix the hash browns!

(I never yelp, I downloaded the App just because of my experience here). Truly atrocious service. From being rudely told to wait outside in the rain for our reserved table - which was set, they just didn't want to seat us - to the server rolling his eyes and scoffing when he wrongly gave one of our party fries with cheese despite her allergy. They also complained about the tip we gave, not actually interested or apologetic for our experience. There's so many good places to around with excellent service - steer clear of Three Muses

I have passed by this place several time and dined at the Binford Cafe next door to it so I thought I would step out of my Hank's Smoked Brisket and Fat Dan's comfort zone for some Black Diamond Barbecue.  I was highly dissapointed that they were out of Brisket so I tried the rib tips with hot barbecue sauce, mac & cheese and greens.  For what I paid I felt like I got a really small portion of tips that had a great smokey taste to them but were over done or older.  The last tip that I ate was on point though.  It was very tender with great smoke flavor.  The hot barbecue sauce was spicy and flavorful without being overly hot.  The mac & cheese was just plain old mac & cheese.  The greens were very good and exactly how I like them.  I tried a friends baked beans because he kept raving about them and I will say they were pretty awesome with tons of brown sugar flavor.  All in all they were A-OK but for what I spent there I would stick with my other two go to's.  I may stop by again to see how the brisket stacks up though.

This place is a gem. As a native Calgarian who has recently moved to Edmonton, I was on a hunt to find authentic Thai food. What I found, iis that not only is this better than any Thai restaurant in Calgary, but it's the most authentic Thai food I have had outside of Thailand, where I have traveled to on several occasions.
My significant other and I LOVE Numchok Wilai, and have taken several of our friends here, who have resoundingly agreed with our assessment. Their green mango salad is a perfect balance of sweet, sour and spice. Their Pla Ra Plik (fried whole pomfret) takes me back to seafood restaurants in Phuket. The Thai basil with seafood has a generous helping of seafood, and although not truly a Thai dish, the stuffed chicken wings are delicious. As an extra bonus, their prices are extremely reasonable for their portion sizes. Thai food tends to be served in relatively small serving dishes for customers to share in a family-style manner. Numchok Wiliai's serving dishes, though small, are at least almost double the size of Viphalay (a very popular Thai restaurant in Edmonton), and their prices lower as well! To top it off, the owners are extremely sweet and polite. Service is efficient and fast  without being overbearing. 

I'm not sure why this place is not teeming with people each night. Perhaps the odd name turns people off, but truly it is a gem.

It's a typical asian resto that every americans love. I don't think my chinese friend will even try it here, basically because their food is not authentic and more of a western taste in it, i.e. Sweet. I tried their soup, which is not in their menu and it's acceptable. I'd come back here for the soup and not their main entre.
This place is awesome. Best salad I've ever had! Haven't gotten past the signature salad to be able to try anything else on the menu

Solid pub right outside of rittenhouse square. Been once before for drinks but this time came back to test out the food. Ordered the app sampler and filet sliders. Definitely hit the spot. Great flavor on the wings. Quesadilla was really tasty. Wasn't a big fan of the cheesesteak rolls. We also ordered the Mac and cheese. It was delicious - super cheesy and melt in your mouth good. Eat it!

I've been here a few times.

The first time I just came to check it out and sign up for a player's club type card and get free bonuses for the sign up, comp dollars, freeplay, etc.  Later I went for the Vineyard restaurant, then Pancho and Willie's and to check out sports bets for the Superbowl.

The most outstanding feature of Western Village (hereafter WV) is the decor.  If you're on psychedelic drugs, probably stimulants and maybe even high, you're going to lose the top off of your head when you walk in.  The lighting is the boldest, brightests, bluest onslaught you will probably ever experience.  I read in another review that the place is owned by the Peppermill.  That makes a lot of sense.  If the Peppermill is a 7/10 on the decor's overstimulation factor, this place gets an 11.  I've honestly just never seen anything like it.  It blows the Metreon to bits.  If I needed to stay awake for at least 48 hours straight without coffee, I'd go here and I would succeed.

Like the Peppermill, WV has large, high def video screens playing picturesque scenes from throughout the world, sometimes bays, sometimes cityscapes, lots of natural landscapes too.  It's actually a nice touch, classy as it can be while still being high tech.

For my sign-up with their birthday club, I got a 25 dollar food comp, the best sign-up of any casino in the Reno/Sparks area.  It was what they did in lieu of tracking.  And they sent another one every birthday.  That is very, very cool.  With the advent of their tracking club for slot play starting November 1, 2010, I'm not sure if they still do the birthday club.  

I've used the food comps at the Vineyard restaurant (excellent, great values) that has since become Pancho and Willie's (excellent also, great values, but only Mexican food so a little less interesting).  The best margarita deal in town is here.  You get a pitcher of blended margaritas (and the alcohol can be tasted) for only 6 bucks.  Portions were enormous and entrees ranged from specials of like 7.99 for a full meal to most being 11-13 dollars.  This was true for both restaurants.  You may have to wait a little bit to get in, but service is prompt.  The young women working there are really shy and made me uncomfortable.  It's like they came from incredibly socially conservative cultures recently or have been hit on far too much by sleazy older guys.  I'm a guy.  It's really okay if I talk to you a tiny bit.

I've also been to the Marina Cafe.  Not very impressed.  The food was something I could have gotten frozen and it might have been better.  Service was a bit slow.  I don't expect to go back.

The sportsbook, like every other sportsbook in town cannot compete with Cal Neva (which exists in many other casinos and has at least one satellite location on Pyramid highway).  Cal Neva has better lines and better odds than every other sports book.

I haven't played much here, but they have the typical bar video poker, table games and slots like everyone else.  They also have tvs throughout with sports events, a pretty impressive number given their space, in fact.  It seemed fairly typical.

I haven't stayed in the rooms, but I would note that they are not physically connected to the casino/restaurant floor.  You might be walking 200 feet to your room.  For the elderly or in really inclement weather, I could see this fact being a legitimate issue.

I mostly treat this place like a great value restaurant as that's what it has for me.

It's very close to the Sparks Marina so that's worth considering if you enjoy walking, shopping, fresh air and maybe doing some sailing lessons.

This is my second time dining here for brunch and I highly recommend this place for any occasion. The brunch menu and buffet consists of a great variety of breakfast and lunch entrees as well as some desserts. The endless mimosa is a nice perk they add to the $33 brunch. Make a reservation for sure, especially if you hate sitting at the bar top. The staff is friendly and extremely accommodating and I will most definitely return here in the future!

We found a pretty good line but took it as a sign that what was inside must be at least decent. Decor, service, and food was a pleasant surprise! Good carvings of tri-tip and briskit, a wide variety of dishes, and GREAT gelato. Also, a great deal during the week.
Homemade ice cream!! If there is a long line don't let that fool you it moves pretty quick definitely worth the wait.  Be Patient, if there's a wait it's for a good reason.

So chipotle is so amazing! I feel like everytime I think about going, gods killing kittens! Why? This addiction is evil!! Lol. Anyhow I love this place for all their organic meats, the chicken is amazing, the Barbados is even better, what mood will I be in next week when the carnitas is going to end up in my burro?

Decor is awesome, the place is well laid out, and they always have some good tunes playing. 

You ready for the bad part?
Ok, so my only gripe, is how these bastards don't mind a HUGE spoon of rice and beans but then they go in with the tongs and shake out half the meat!! WTF! don't skimp on the best part! 

P.S. I always tell them to add my sauce to a cup on the side!! And I slather my burro in it as I eat! Get the hot, it's insane good.

Nuff said.... K bye!

We went with Jackson's recommendations and were pleased with all of them! From his fav Eggs In A Jar to Beignets to a nice bottle of Champagne. Amazing combination of flavors. Gave them one less star for a lag in their attentiveness to service. The host eagerly sat us without menus. Then a server handed us off to Jackson who did well but was slightly distracted by his other duties at times. Tighten that up and you've got 5 stars! Thanks for an amazing last day in NOLA! We'll be back for sure
Everyone was really nice and this restaurant was so cute. Loving the tin ceiling, carved woodwork and floor tiles
Jambalaya, bbq shrimp appetizer, oysters!! All delicious!! Bread is freshly heated and super delicious. Location is central on Bourbon so you really feel the party atmosphere.

Ordered wings and basket of fries. The wings I got the Hot flavor. 
The wings were perfect. I was pretty upset about the fries. It was stale and cold. We asked for fresh fries and it still came out even harder and added more seasoning to it. Usually everything is always so perfect. 
I'm assuming it was just a busy Sunday and they just couldn't keep everything super fresh? :/ 
In place for the cold fries, they did give a free dessert 
Thank you.. we will still come back on a slower day.
The most friendliest Chick-fil-A I have ever been into. They are quick to get your order done and the mangers are always interacting with the customers.

My friend and I decided to catch up at Ooka last night and enjoy some Habachi cookin'.  Lets just say it's been a while.  We got sat at the big table of 8 with 1 other couple with the big grill between us.  Our waitress brought us some really awesome miso soup (tofu-less?) and salad with fresh veggies, and really amazing ginger dressing.  I pretty much inhaled mine.  As the token vegetarian, I was a bit bummed that Ooka hasn't embraced tofu the way that a lot of asian cuisine has.. so i ordered the veggie meal.  My friend went for the chicken.  I was really impressed that when the chef went to cook, he made all the veggies first, then the meat so there was no possibility of 'contamination'.  While I'm not that strict of a vegetarian, I appreciate that sort of consideration.  

Our chef was fantastic.  He made us laugh, we were in awe of his skills, and the food was delicious.  We had plenty of time to catch up and hang out and relax.  The meal really was a high spot in my week.  It was a bit on the salty side though, which had me drinking lots of water all night.

I only wish i had known that the restaurant was a BYOB.   I had many bottles I could have brought... but now we know for next time.
Awesome fried Okras, pudding and smoked chicken. Place to be if you like BBQ(who doesn't) .

Unbelievably great service and the food was spectacular creating an overall great experience.

The ONLY problem I had is that I took the time to write to the general manager and didn't hear anything back.  That's bad form, but, I'll assume he's just busy rather than he doesn't care.

The wait staff sure cares.  Each of them know their menu, they offer suggestions, and they help each other out.  You don't see many places that wait staff will swoop in like a well choreographed ballet to cover each other.  

The squid ink pasta was fabulous.  I actually had them prepare it with a red sauce and add some extra seafood to it.  That means, the chef was both creative and flexible, both of which I look for in my dining experiences.

All good from start to finish.  

When I'm next in Nashville, you can bet I'll be back to Moto!

I wish I could give 3.5 stars because I liked this place but it doesn't quite deserve 4. I loved the atmosphere, it felt like an old school Tucson cowboy place (which it is, I think it has been there since like 1949). The crowd was cool, kind of again an old school Tucson crowd. Not old people, per se, just cool unpretentious people. Waitress was nice, food was good...but not great, It was hot and seemed fresh but it was kind of...gringo Mexican food. And I'm a gringo! I don't know, I told the dining partner as we left "I liked it, I'd come here again, but maybe I wouldn't rush to come back here anytime terribly soon" and he agreed.

We were at a bar called Rusty Nail. Only food was a food truck called Foodie Call. It's 8pm and all I know is I'm super hungry. They didn't take credit cards. By now, there's no excuse not to take credit cards. Not only is there Square, there's a ton of other credit companies that do mobile. So I had to go get cash and pay the atm fee. Ok so I go get cash, purchase my food which are wings and fries. I realize they don't give me any sauce for my wings. Now, wings ALWAYS comes with some type of sauce whether it's ranch or bleu cheese. I ask for ranch and he tells me it's an additional charge. I've used all my cash to buy the food that I could've easily paid with my credit card. I ask if it's possible to just give me ranch with no charge and he says no. I walked away pretty disappointed. Did not take credit and couldn't possibly give me sauce for free which is probably one cent per pour. Yep. Sorry. Bad review.

Samurai is the best sushi in Nashville. The fish is always fresh and the rolls don't fall apart. The restaurant is small so you may have to wait for a table but it's worth it. Try the Vandy Roll if you're a fried roll person, it's amazing.

This strangely popular restaurant was packed from the day it was open -- it had been opened several months before I went because every time I considered going, it was packed! I finally went on a night mid-week and it was not busy at all. 

Now, I am not a fan of fried, greasy food, which seems to be their specialty, but I am not discounting their rating for that. This is the reasoning for the low rating...

Although the servers were indeed scantily dressed as per the theme, my server was not very knowledgeable regarding the menu, the dishes, or even how to serve. The food took shockingly long, arrived less than hot, and dripped with an unexplainable amount of grease. The beer was fine, the  mixed drinks were weak. 

It took a long time to get the check, during which I watched a pair of roaches crawl out from behind the napkin holder, along the wall. Yes, the same napkins I used to wipe my mouth and hands with.

I love this Place.....It always conjures memories of the Eagles song lyrics for Hotel California "Mirror's on the ceiling ; The Pink Champagne on Ice (I don't know why except Opulance) They may not have a progressive menu nor in any way do they dabble with molecular wizardry but they food is consistently great! You will never get a bad crab cake or Prime Rib.  The Shrimp cocktail and Oysters are always fresh and ice cold.  The Waiters and FOH are professional and always take ownership of any problems. The customer is always right (even when wrong)  I had a small birthday party there Sat with two kids an 8 and 6 and they were Amazing! The food and service never missed a beat. They got the kids food out quickly and paced the adults as well
It seemed like 4 or 5 courses at my request but in the end all smiles around. The soft-shell crabs are Whales now and well worthy he splurge, The desserts particularly the mudd pie and chic mousse cake are stellar.  The room is among the most elegant in Philly and even though the dress code is relaxed I feel comfortable in a sport coat 
on Saturday night but would go without one without hesitation  Even the owner thanked us for having our special occasion with them. A must visit and as my eight ]
year old told the waiter...the #1 Steakhouse in Philadelphia per US air Magazine and Zagat...haha

I come here on a pretty regular basis to eat healthy food, which basically means chicken or salmon and vegetables. I ignore the rest of the menu. Chicken is pretty good as far as chicken goes in a chain restaurant. Asparagus is good as well. Sit at the bar if Shane is there... he is outstanding!!!

I was worried I was going to walk into a restaurant with a presumptuous staff but I could not have been more wrong. The waitress was able to make fabulous recommendations and our food came out amazing. I wish the prices weren't so high but this was the perfect romantic restaurant that I thought Tucson was lacking. I would recommend it to anyone wanting to have a nice night out and has a few bucks to spend.

The Char Kuey teow was terrible.  The flat noodles were disintegrated into little oily brown bits and the tofu was dry, semi burnt and greasy.  We left half the dish uneaten. The Mee Siam was Pad Thai basically,  not the Mee Siam I remember from Malaysia.  In general not authentic and poorly done.

We have been here many times and we just love it. The steak is the best I had so far in saint Louis area. The crab cake is the must order every time when we get here. Service has always been great. Would certainly recommend this place.

Great waiters and delicious food! Highly recommend Tre Lune for a family dinner, or a date. Really love the pictures all around the restaurant. Do wish the gelato serving size was bigger, but the tiramisu was nice and big. Great lasagna, family loved everything they ordered. Even the pesto they brought at the start was yummy (I'm not a fan of pesto, and this tasted different).

I went here for a corporate dinner. Like the northside Harry and Izzy's, there's nothing really "wrong" with this place except their steaks are not USDA prime. You can look up the difference in price between USDA prime and choice.

The issue is that other steakhouses in its price range use USDA prime meat for its steaks. There is a definite difference in quality between prime and choice - it's not a gimmick. Prime is significantly more tender because it's better marbled - there is more fat interspersed in the lean meat.

For the prices they are charging, they need to serve prime.

Recently dined there on a Friday evening.  It has a lovely ambiance and pleasant service, but the food was OK, at best, for the price.  It started off well enough with a lobster-bacon bisque, but the salad was average, and the bourbon embellished filet mignon was a bit dry and chewy.

Its the first place I ever got drunk (Fun Times) so I have to give it a 5 lol its a little small but on a Friday/Saturday who cares! Its fun nice people hot bar tenders ;) and a great place just to have fun alot of my best drunk story's start with "So I left murphs" lol

This restaurant is a gem! Delicious cuisine, and excellent service. I had the Vegetable panang masala and it was delicious. I would highly recommend trying this place. The restaurant is quite busy on the weekends so I prefer to go on a week night. Although, they do accept reservations.

The sole reason this review is 3 stars instead of 2 is because of Jessica. Wish I could give 3.5. Dinner on a Sunday night at 4:20 PM took 90 minutes. We sat at the bar. Ordered the Vermont Breakfast & American burgers. Our medium & medium rare burgers were both medium well  :( My husband was so hungry, he didn't want to send it back and wait all over again. Burgers were still OK & had great flavors. We waited almost 30 minutes for milkshakes. Jessica was amazing handling a busy bar counter- she saw that our wait was long & went above and beyond to make our shakes herself. Shakes were tasty!! Jessica was personable & attentive to every customer at the bar as well!! Will probably return, but not anytime soon.

Happy Hour here is outstanding. $5 drinks and $5 select apps. Our favorite was the squash blossom quesadilla. The chicken flautas were okay and the goat cheese empanadas were tasty. Their signature margarita comes from a machine--which was offputting. However, they do not skimp on the tequila as one would think! Order it and enjoy.

Usually love this place and it's my go-to sandwich shop when I'm in the area but today was disappointing. I got a ham sandwich and in between pieces of ham there was some sort of liquid, sticky white stuff. Wasn't mayo.. Idk but it seemed weird. Took a few of those pieces off and went back to eating. Then came across multiple pieces of spoiled lettuce. They were black. 

I was so disappointed because I'm so used to the freshest of ingredients when I come here. I hope the situation is rectified because I love the staff and the food! I'll give it another shot soon and we'll see what happens

I love this place.  We have been during the week for dinner and loved it and of course we stop in when ever we can on Sundays for the tri tip sandwich from heaven.  

Quick tip - you get the golden ticket for the sandwich from the bar :)

Had a quick dinner with a friend and it was awesome in & out in 40 minutes...we are able to have our food, eat it, and get it packed up and out the door a sap without any issue with the food taste...it was amazing well-prepared well l-season...awesomeness. I had the pepper chicken amazing, amazing, amazing...next time I come to Philly I definitely would stop here!!

*Forgot about this, I had to deduct a star for food delivery. It was not timed so that we (2 people) had our food at the same time...basic waiter rules!

I stopped by there today with my boyfriend before he had to go to work. I've lived in West Philly for almost a year now, this was my first time coming in to order. I had heard great things about the Mood, and even had a friend bring some food home for me to try and I loved it.

The man behind the counter was very nice and acknowledged it was our first time there and explained what chaat was, how it was made and how he could make it for us. He said if we didn't like it, we didn't have to pay. I wish I had enough $$ to give him a great big tip! It was DELICIOUS! Mine, and my boyfriend's plate too;D Cashews and yogurt and fruit and veggies and grains and beans and crunchy things and ever so perfectly spicy!

I want to make the Mood Cafe a regular take-out and eat-in for me. So impressed!

What a great place.  I had the pleasure of eating here a while back and sure enjoyed it.  They happened to have all their bottles of wine 1/2 off the night we went so we took advantage of that.  The service was top notch and the food tasty.

Sometimes what you really need on a Saturday night is to sit at home, watch tv, and order an astounding amount of sushi. This is what I did recently. 

I can only speak about the vegetarian items, as I do not eat fish. I liked everything I ordered (mango, oshinko, avocado, cucumber) except the avocado and peanut. There seemed to be too many peanuts in the roll and/or the peanuts were not chopped finely enough... something just wasn't right. 

A great addition to the neighborhood!

Absolutely awesome beer selection, including plenty of local and top national craft brews. Solid gastropub menu. And if you ever wondered why there aren't any 25-35 year olds in Carmel, it's because you didn't look in The Pint Room. There they are.

The one big disappointment: no al fresco option, so will have to dine & drink elsewhere in prime Monon and IPA weather.
For a quick lunch within walking distance of the office you can't get better.  Great food, nice folks working here and quick service!

Maybe it's too much to expect but a pleasant staff would be nice.  I had an awful experience today with Nashiir. Some individuals should take a step back and realize working with the public might not be for them.

We always go here for lunch on the weekends.  The food is always great and I love a well crafted cocktail so it's always a win with us.  I had some kind of blackberry margarita the last time I was there and it was ridiculously amazing!!

The best part about this place was that the waiter was very attentive to our needs. 
On the other hand it was very breezy because all the windows were open, which is okay, but the fans were on also, so I was freezing. 
I wanted to order a salad, but all they had was Cesar... so if your going to eat a Cesar salad you might as well go all out because Cesar salads aren't what you call healthy... 
So I end up splitting some red beans and rice with sausage plate with my friend... and It was like a heartache on a plate. Very good but oh so bad.... 

On a positive note my drink was strong (kettle one, splash of cranberry with a twist of lime) 
and they had the LSU vs Gators game on so I was pretty content. 
Although I probably wouldn't go back again.

Love it. Food is always on point, service is great. We usually always eat at the hibachi side but tonight ate at the dine in side. I think we will do that more often unless we are with a group of people. Lunch is always cheaper of course but also have early bird special i believe the hours are from  430-530 so a little cheaper for hibachi meal and have sushi specials then as well. Crunchy shrimp roll is always good.
What's not to love about this place. Fresh EVERYTHING and the wine selection is awesome. If you love Italian, you have to go to Mazzaro's - No place like it ANYWHERE..

Hair in chicken tenders and really soggy twisted chips. Haven't seen server in awhile to tell him...

Update-they did take my meal and drink off ticket.
Friendly service topped with great tasting food. Big portions of pasta dishes. Plenty to share.
Just as good as the other Five Guys I've been to but I hate that a single is "little". I always forget and get too much food

OK food... HORRIBLE customer service!
One weekend I ordered 4 extra large pizzas (totaling $65 WITH a coupon) and when we received our order it was completely wrong.  I called to report the issue and Adam (who claimed that he was a manager) said that he would "take care" of my order next time.  He also asked me to take pictures of my pizzas (which I did).  The following week I called Pizza Guys to place my order.  Prior to placing my order, I informed the girl of my arrangement with Adam.  She responded with "Hmmm... hold on and let me figure that out".  Adam came to the phone and when I reminded him of our arrangement, he took my order (which was the exact same order as the one they messed up on), he told me that the total was $88!  When I reminded him again of our agreement, he then stated that he can "discount my order significantly" bringing it down to $60.  I told him that I was not satisfied with that.  If I had them correct the order the first time, I would not have paid for their error then, so why should I pay for it this time?  Adam told me that was the best he can do... even as a manager!  I asked who his boss was and he stated that she was standing right next to him.  I asked to speak with her. He placed me on hold for about five minutes only to return and say that she sent him back to the phone and tell me that the best she can do was to bring the cost down to $55. Come to find out that this was the OWNER! She did not even have the decency nor respect to come to the phone and talk to me.  Instead of trying to correct their error, they acted as if I was just trying to get some free food! I have NEVER been so insulted nor experienced such poor customer service!  I will NEVER order from this location EVER again!  I even spoke with Director of Operations regarding the issue and although he apologized and asked for another chance, I told him that I would not feel comfortable nor would I put it past that staff to put something in my food!  In my opinion, customer service is just as important as the quality of food I am purchasing.  Again - I will NEVER order from this location again, and if you think that customer service is just as important as I do, then you won't order from them either!
This is the best lobster roll I have had in St. Louis. Truly incredible food!

The Smoking Meatloaf sandwich was bomb!!!  Spicy enough to make me sweat and served on a jalapeño cheddar roll that was perfectly crispy at the edges.  The side salad was made with crispy fresh greens, not the standard iceberg lettuce, and included some feta and dried cranberries too.  Based on other reviews, it looks like this place has stepped up its kitchen offerings. 

I didn't get to try the beers since I have to get back to work now, but the selection looks impressive. Jen the bartender provided excellent service despite being very busy, and I liked the rugged Western bar and decor.  I would definitely come back next time I'm in Boise.

This pains me to put, but as of late the food has been subpar for the price. Edleys truly was one of my go to spots for BBQ and a great place to take friends that are visiting from out of town. 

Our last visit we ordered the Tuck Special and pulled chicken. The brisket was pretty cold and it was missing the red and white sauce. It was very busy so I gave it the benefit of the doubt. My finances food however was very very dry to the pint soaking it in BBQ didn't even help. The cornbread was great like it always is and the vegan desert we tried was pretty good just very sweet. 

I gave it three stars really because it is said to be the best in Nashville and there are so many other places that I have never had one issue with. But for the price and the lack of care recently with the food it really doesn't live up to its name anymore for us.
Horrible service everytime. I have to teach the employees how to make a proper acai bowl. They obviously can't keep or train employees.

I loved this place! It's great for a quick, inexpensive, and tasty meal. I ordered a chicken street taco and a fish taco and loved both of them. This is one of the best places I've eaten at in Tucson. The staff was friendly and helpful as well. The only reason I wouldn't give it a 5 star review is because the space is small and it was very crowded so finding a seat was tough and it was loud.

Went with girlfriends for happy hour in the bar.

They have in the bar (durirng happy hour) one- or two-bite hors d'oeuvres for 75 cents to $2. Marvelous concept!

I had a fried oyster, grilled shrimp with aoli, stuffed mushroom, pork and veal meatball, trout-stuffed red pepper with onion and caper, pickle/olive/cheese skewer, pureed asparagus on bread with crabmeat, mussels, and bacon-wrapped dates with cabreles cheese.

For all of this, it was $7.

They were all fabulously tasteful, and really made a total meal for me. I would, however, omit the pickle/olive/cheese skewer, as they were as-is, not treated in any way. Just disappointing. And the pickle was a mini sweet gerghkin. Rather boring. I'd also give a pass to the pureed asparagus on bread with crabmeat, simply because the menu didn't say pureed (so that texture was an unwelcomed surprise) and the crabmeat was quite sparse.

There are beer specials and drink specials during happy hour, as well -- as one might expect!

It was a great outing with good friends, fabulous food and a great server who helped us through the whole mass of options!

Yum yum. This is a cute little place located in the heart of broad ripple. We came about an hour before closing. We got 2 regular Cuban sandwich's and the rice, bean, pork mixture. The staff was friendly. The restaurant is clean and I love the decor. 

The food was really good. The sandwich was so filling I had to take the other half home. I could have went w the mini. We will be back for sure.
This is a bar not a 4+ star eatery. Know that going in. Food so-so. Loud and noisy. We endured lunch
