So if you want to wait forever for the wrong meal go there but I will never spend another dime there ever again.

We were originally going to Cafe du Monde on recommendations from friends, but the line there was a block long. The line here was just to the door, and with the tables pretty much all filled, everyone was getting orders to go, so the line moved fairly quickly. We were able to snag a couple of bar seats just as our order came up. My Iced Chicory and Coffee was wonderful, and matched the beauty that were the beignets we got. They came to us hot, sugary and ever so yummy!

Well they got rid of my fish sandwich only have fillets so I properly won't be back again. $17 for a fillet for lunch was much more then I expected. Completely disappointed!  Food good yes but not what I came for. This reason two stars. People get a fish sandwich back in the menu!!!!

Just had my third meal at Mt. Fuji and the family enjoys the high-quality, well prepared food and the friendly service. We are Mt. Juliet residents that very much enjoy ethnic foods.

There's this one irritating thing about Mt. Fuji. Actually, it applies to other ethnic restaurants too, but it was particularly irritating at Mt. Fuji because it was loud. It was the twangy country radio station. Our waitress was likewise irritated and gladly brought the manager over, who grinned about his inability to change things.

Ethnic restaurants are best when they offer an experience along with the food. It would be wonderful to have tranquil flute or beautiful Japanese music playing in the background. If not Mt. Fuji, then Fulin? Wasabi?

I love Tony Romas ribs, but I will never return to this location.

My last experience here was horrible for more than one reason. We sat down in a very packed Tony Romas on a Saturday afternoon and we waited and waited for a server to come by. The place was really busy so we sort of understood, but it got to the point where we almost got up and left.

Finally, a very angry server stomped up and asked what we wanted to drink. No hello, no sorry, no eye contact. It was super uncomfortable. She pretty much forced us to make a decision on the spot about what we wanted to eat and after we ordered, she avoided us like the plague.

She had one large table half filled with kids and one of them asked for another milkshake. She was holding a bunch of dirty dishes and as he asked for the refill, she stormed over to the drink area right behind our table and THREW the dishes into the sink. It was so loud and it startled me. I can't imagine how the kids felt. How embarrassing.

After a mediocre meal and continued empty glasses we asked for the cheque- and the manager. All of a sudden, she was nice and said she would be happy to grab the manager for us.

Another server came up to the table and said that the manager was just on a phone call and she was a senior server and could talk to us. I was not buying it. I had seen the two servers chatting at some point during our horrible meal and assumed they were friends and she was now covering her friends butt.

Nevertheless, I told the problem to her in detail and she apologized. That was about it. No discount, no "please come back", no accountability.

The worst part about it was when we were walking to our car, we saw the manager standing outside with a group of servers smoking. "On a phone call"?

Right.

This place definitely lost our business.

Been to Cosi a few thousand times and the Signature Salad is a favorite.   Went to this one and they tried to tell me a white dressing was the one that goes with that salad.   When I told them I didn't think that was right, they argued with me.   Seems odd that every other Cosi in the world uses a different dressing.   Maybe they were out and just didn't feel like making another batch?  It didn't taste good  and I didn't go back.

I love coming to this sushi spot! I believe that Arigato has better quality sushi however not by much, and Ichibans price point is much much better. The counter sunk tables are an awesome touch, and the guys behind the sushi bar really enjoy talking to you if you'll let them.

Brunchies is just what we needed in a Lutz! This is the perfect spot for breakfast or brunch. The guava stuffed pancakes are delicious and more than enough to share.  You can't go wrong with any of the omelettes.  Brunchies also offers a selection of mimosas.

We love the food here! We don't make it over this way often but when we do we love to stop in for a bite. The restaurant comes off as fancy, so we eat in the lounge and order our food from there, especially since we usually only eat the appetizers. The spinach dip is absolutely divine! We also get the chicken tenders tossed in buffalo and they are amazing. My husband also likes the calamari a lot, but I wouldn't know since I don't eat seafood. If you stay at the hotel or are in town, it's definitely worth eating at - even if just for appetizers.
By far the best Jamaican food I've ever had. Costs a little more than others in the area but worth every extra penny. I had oxtail, Mac and cheese, and rice and beans and everything was delicious!

Didnt think it was worth the huge line that formed outside the place while we ate.  Eggs ordinary, bacon actually very dry and crispy, blueberry pancakes not that extraordinary.  All in all, Id come back, but if there was the huge line outside, I'd recommend to find someplace else because even though the servers are prompt and efficient, the whole experience was very, sorry to say but in my humble opinion, not memorable.

I absolutely love thai food and have been here with friends before. Their food has been decent as far as I can remember. However, recently, my boyfriend and I went in with a groupon and they were absolutely horrendous. We ordered the duck avocado special and ordered a side of rice because it didn't come with rice. When we received our dish, the avocado was not ripe and tasted like cardboard. They took the dish back and said all their avocados were like that. So we ordered another dish that came with rice. Not only did they NOT apologize, but they refused to comp us for the side of rice we only ordered because of the duck avocado dish that we couldn't even eat. 

We'll never eat at this location again. The point of a groupon is to bring in service so we can go back again...they absolutely failed at that.

Worst brunch I have ever had!!! Waited one hour and ten minutes for our food. Our server said that they forgot to fix one of our orders so my food stayed in the window until they fixed the other plate. Everything on my plate was over cooked and cold. I showed her the pancake that was so hard you could here it crunch when I bit into it.She said she would comp my plate but when I got the bill it remained on it.
Meh...food is ok...can barely see any ocean, even if you are standing.  Skip it.
Comfy reclining seats. Didn't go there for the food...movie theater was enjoyable. Clean bathrooms! Suggestion - buy a new broom to clean up the theater.  Broom was dirty. We will come back again.

Delicious pad Thai and pumpkin curry, I will skip I
Thai iced coffee and get a Thai iced tea next time

Excelent! Food is wondeful, hot, and fresh! The sushi is far better than your average asian cuisine buffet! We got seated fast despite looking busy and the place was clean and the staff is on point with their service! Definitely a diamond in the rough since it really isn't in a great looking neighborhood! We will gladly be back here in the near future and we cannot wait to bring our friends and family!

This was my first time at Manhattan bagel and I most admit I haven't had service like this in a while. The cashier Iliyas customer service was very pleasant. I didn't let the cashier know this was my first visit. I was given coupons (which I love) and told about their deals and also how I saved two dollars on lunch. My food was awesome and I like that they sell turkey bacon. I would recommend others just as I was recommend by my sister to try MB out.

Chatham Tap has the best nachos in town, no question. This restaurant has a more classic pub feel and always has a soccer game playing on one of the few TV screens. It is normally pretty busy and loud and the service can tend to be slow. Usually the staff isn't over friendly but just there to take your order and deliver your food. But the food is delicious! The have a great assortment of appetizers, salads, sandwiches and of course drinks!

I went here on a date with a groupon and LOVED IT! It's got a nice cozy atmosphere - great for groups or dates. The menu is large and the waitstaff were attentive and knowledgeable and super friendly. We ordered two appetizers - seaweed salad and spicy tuna salad and both were excellent. We ordered a few sushi rolls - The St. Louis Roll was really good. Got some plum wine which went nicely. Our groupon value was 30 dollars and we ended up going over it. The place isn't super cheap, but not overpriced. It's quality and I would love to go back! I just wish they had more choices without crab, but I bet they would make things special for you if you asked.

7/19/17 10AM
Pulled in to find the parking lot half empty and silently thanked Jesus! Middle of the month, early in the day went in to find no line, no one sitting in the chairs and no one at the receptionist's desk. It's like the heavens parted and there was a ray of sunshine on the receptionist. 

We were there to get my mother's handicap hang tag renewed and since she's very handicap she was able to sit while i went from one place to the other with no issues. Just showed her license and pointed to her. 

The receptionist was very nice, did some typing into the computer, printed out what we needed, we stepped over to the registration desk and the woman working there was nothing but polite. It was completed quickly with no issues and we were on our way. 

While this was probably a total anomaly that they only had a few customers while we were there but even going when it is busy it's tolerable. The other reviewers obviously don't remember the days of sitting in DMV for HOURS back before it was privatized or they went in with an 'I'm pissed at the state bcuz i have to renew my registration' attitude. The workers have never been nicer and efficient.

With a fresh aroma hitting as soon as you walk in the door, this cozy neighborhood joint is bustling with a constant flow of diners. The food is simple, authentic, and delicious. A nice break from the usual heavy NOLA fare.

Amen to Andrew K!!  Finally someone else besides me recognizes the pure joy that is Imo's Pizza.
A St. Louis institution if there ever was one!!  

Imo's has been around for a long time and has only improved with time.  Their pizzas are a super thin, crispy crust and they use a creamy provel cheese (something that everyone else in the country doesn't know about...which makes me wonder, exactly WHAT is provel cheese???), regardless it's tasty.  I also usually don't eat much meat, but the pepperoni here is to die for.

You can even order this online & have it sent to you anywhere in the country.  Damn dangerous if you ask me.

We were at Oakleys Bistro last evening, Feb. 12th. This was our 3rd outing there and I am still not impressed with the restaurant. Their bar drinks are on the expensive side, but only average in quality. Our total dinner bill for two people, including two cocktails was $100 not including gratuity. 
We were there to celebrate my wife's birthday. She ordered the Sea Bass which she said was quite good. On the other hand, I ordered the Wild Boar Rigatoni which was just on the adequate side in terms of taste and quality. The sauce and rigatoni were good, however the "wild boar" was barely edible. It tasted old, was overlooked, dry with a rubbery quality that even the sauce could not improve. Quite disappointing, especially given the price. The lettuce wedge salad was also underwhelming and truly overpriced. I know this is an expensive restaurant and don't mind paying prices when eating out, but I expect better quality for those prices. 
On the plus side, my wife was presented with a complimentary dessert which she said was excellent. Our waiter was excellent, never hovering yet was attentive at the appropriate times, allowing us to enjoy the meal. 
Because we were there with two other couples I decided not to return my meal and ask for something else because I didn't wasn't to delay things or call attention to our evening, but I truly was dissatisfied with my meal. Oakleys is not high on my recommend list even though others seemed to enjoy their meal, given that this was my third visit there and still feel the quality is not up to par with the pricing. I have given Oakleys a weak 3 stars.

This is one of the coolest places for a happy hour or a fun Saturday afternoon in Tampa.  Kind of a pain to take a left turn into of you're headed northbound on Dale Mabry, but otherwise, cute and friendly waitstaff who totally rock, and decent prices as well. Keep up the good work guys!

We were looking for someplace new for lunch and I found Snarf's on Yelp.  A lot of good Sandwich and Salad choices.  I had the Prime Rib and Provolone.  Really good sandwich.  The Staff was really nice.  It's a  place I would go back to.

I love Razz 

Beyond great American cuisine, Chef Razz demonstrates excellent customer service, always making a point to stop by talk to the table, and make sure everything is perfect. 

It is especially a great place to take customers or host meetings. Razz had two private rooms, one with some audiovisual capability. We've hosted Christmas party's with a DJ and 75+ people, and other times just standard groups of 8-10. They arranged menus, or in the case of the party buffet style, to fit our needs equally well. 

Outside seating is available, and nice on summer evenings. Many nights Razz has live music. (Jazz etc.)  Bar area is small, but classy.

First of all the interior is nice, really intimate. If you get a chance check out the upstairs lounge that overlooks the street!

SO, to the food... We started with the Poke. I thought it was pretty good, a lot of interesting textures and bites but a little to acidic. The hazelnut and ricotta ravioli though blew my socks off. Only came with 5-6 of them but they were fantastic and rich.

For an entree we shared the Salmon with artichokes, and potatoes. Though I heard the Fried chicken is a marquee item, I felt in the mood for something slightly healthier. The broth served underneath the salmon was delicious and the salmon itself was cooked to perfection. I wish it came with crostini's or something to soak up that tasty garlic-clam broth!

Definitely need to come back and try new dishes AND for brunch. The ricotta ravioli and Salmon are 'must-gets'.

Comes to my job all the time. 
I was hungry. 
I didn't want to leave and lose my good parking spot. 
It was not too bad. 
Big ass burritos for cheap and quick. 
I really want to try the Frenchy Toast but next time.

Not impressed. I figured this place would have amazing food because its a Stephen Starr restaurant but it was just eh. We had the mac and cheese (good), piergoies, and the lobster roll. The lobster roll was small, and just OK. Nothing here "blew me away".  The decor was nice, the service was great and my apple pear smash drink was delish.

We have eaten in the restaurant several times, with 2 adults and 4 kids the bill with tip generally comes out around $70. The food is ok and the kids like it. Shakes are good. Generally the waitstaff is friendly and helpful, but it's hit or miss.

Today was enough of a bad experience that I will not be going back. I called in an order for pick-up. The manager answered the phone, began to take my order, then had a two minute conversation with someone in the waitstaff without saying "excuse me for a minute" or anything to me. That wasn't bad enough yet though. After I placed my order, she said it would be ready in 10 minutes. I let her know that I wouldn't need it for 30 minutes, which she replied to saying that orders go in to the kitchen as soon as she enters them and can't be changed (this is a very small restaurant with little staff, keep in mind). As I was asking her to cancel the order so I could call back later to re-order, she hung up on me. That's enough. No reason to tolerate a rude manager for mediocre food. I hope this place finds better staff or closes so that something nice can take it's place.

FYI... Wayback Burgers is right around the corner. 429 W Butler Ave, Chalfont, PA 18917 (267) 477-1786

Very cool place. I just bumped into the Bistro. I grabbed a couple of wraps and had to run. They have a lot of kitchen items, sauces, infused oils, and a ton of other things including a great coffee bar. 

I need to come back when I can hang out a little longer. 

The wraps were fantastic!  The people are very friendly. 

I'm totally coming back!

Excited to see a new restaurant in Reno. It looks great on the outside and it's really nice inside. Went here for lunch. I got the quarter bird with the slaw and beans as my sides. They offer sauces too but I didn't use them. The quarter bird comes with a breast and a leg and it was really well seasoned and juicy. Overall great lunch with quick service. The only thing I noticed was a lot of staff walking around and a guy tried to pick up my palate before I was finish. 
I would defiantly come here again for lunch or try out there good beer selection for dinner.

I found the food here decent, but the headache of weaving through the ever-expansive line stretching out the front door is not quite worth the heady taco experience. 

The main issue lies within the compact entrance which leaves little to no room for people to migrate into a manageable clump. Instead, we piled up like herded sheep around the register, then piled out the front door. Luckily, it was a mildly warm, sunny day so most of the crowd felt rather patient. However, I do NOT recommend coming here at peak brunch hours or evening dinner hours near weekends. My friends and I arrived at 12:30pm Saturday prime time lunch. We were able to sit with a lovely individual, but our food took app. 45 minutes before it came out. When I asked a staff member, she told me they were backed up from the whole lunch crowd. So, definitely order an appetizer (I recommend the queso) if you're waiting.

The outdoor seating is quite sidewalk-chic, if you know what I mean. Lots of large picnic tables and plenty of room for pets. They even provide dog bowls if Fido needs a drink of water. The picnic tables, I would say, are also their greatest downfall. Unless you're ok with sharing room family style (which we were), you might prefer indoor seating or taking it to-go.

Food was...less stellar than expected. I had the Korean BBQ and Brisket tacos.The meat was quite tender for the brisket, and I found the pickled red onions added just the right amount of sourness. I was disappointed by the Korean BBQ, a decent but lackluster mixture of chopped cabbage, carrots, and a slightly marinated bulgogi-ish meat. The star of my meal was the fried green chile mac n' cheese. Absolute cholesterol-inducing perfection. This made the meal worth the crazy line.

I would say, if you haven't had Tex-Mex in Texas, give it a shot. If you have, this might not be the best wait.

What a poor excuse for a restaurant, and I already expect hotel restaurants to be expensive and mediocre but the prices here were ridiculous and not posted on the menu. 

I asked if there were any other options on the breakfast menu for kids and he said they do things a la carte, like eggs, bacon, fruit....one of the a la carte things we ordered was three eggs....we paid $5 for the first two and then $3 for the 3rd. What's that about? And $5 for a drip coffee? The most overpriced coffee chain doesn't charge that for a venti. 
In the end we paid over $50 for 1 order of croissants (2), 2 miniature danishes, a small bowl of cold oatmeal and 3 slices of bacon and 3 scrambled eggs. 

We should have just braved the cold like we did for every other meal when we were staying at Hotel Monaco.
Best sushi in Tampa if you like authentic sushi. There aren't a ton of fancy rolls, but it is meticulously executed with perfect rice and quality cuts of fish. Really happy we found this place.

Sadly, this Chambersburg staple on Roebling and Fulton has closed after 25 years and is now located on Parkway Avenue in Ewing Twp.

I visited the Ewing location for the first time recently and was disappointed in both the atmosphere and the menu.  I'm not sure you'll know what I mean by atmosphere unless you're from the Trenton area and are familiar with the Burg or should I say, what used to be the Burg.  Anyhow, the new location has a lovely decor, it just has a very different feel. About the menu, again - it's different.  They could have at least kept the menu the same, right?  The menu is smaller and missing some key items I once enjoyed.  

Moderate prices for menu items, while dinner specials were a bit higher in price. Portions were on the small side, as I think I was able to count the number of penne in my side of pasta.  On a more positive note,  we had a party of eight which can sometimes be a problem on a busy Friday night, yet the service was still very good. Now a BYOB.

We've gotten from here a bunch of times while over at friends' place. Can't compare it to other places local to it, but overall, it's a winner. We've gotten a variety of soups, apps, entrees, and combo platters, from both the Chinese and Japanese sections of the menu. Everything has been tasty, though I'd give their wonton soup 3 stars.

Have been staying here each year for a number of years. They have a renovated section that is so much nicer than what I have experienced in the past.  It is crisp, clean, quality (thick, absorbent towels), extra plugs built into the nightstand. The bath is equally upgraded.  Was a pleasant surprise

Oh god someone tell yelp they need to include the option of negative stars.... Just got back from this place and it was SO bad... We ordered, they forgot about our order, we told them, they didn't speak enough english to understand, and just gave us something else.... That only took about 75 minutes. Do yourself a favor and go to Panda Express. It is 100X better.

Oh, and don't even THINK about the boba, it's not really boba, and the milk tea taste like water and imitation sugar. I think the only reason it's brown is because they put food coloring in it.

I honestly didn't have the highest expectations when I heard a Panda wannabe restaurant was going to open up in Isla Vista, but I never thought it would be this bad. I gotta go brush my teeth now, perhaps it can wait until after I throw up though. I really hope I can throw up...
Absolutely love this place and they have the best buffalo chicken pizza around. No one makes it like they do. It's not a fancy place, but if you want to guarantee great pizza, go here.

Jersey Shore meets Reno. 

Surprisingly fun and great dancing (the band was going off, great dancing, strong drinks).

Some interesting people watching too.

As for the food, skip it. tried a few apps friends ordered and no one was enjoying them (they actually screwed up fried calamari)

Not a destination place, but ok if you're walking by looking for a place with good food, and if I remember correctly, decent drinks. They do serve nice portions and it was tasty. Service friendly enough, if not a little hurried.

I only came into this Friendly's to get a "Friend-Z" (basically a Blizzard). The restaurant was very spacious and the ice cream area was incredibly clean. I used to be an ice cream girl at Friendly's when I was in high school, so I know what a pain it is to keep that sticky crap from getting all over the place.

My Friend-Z was delicious.

I'll be back!
Solid sushi and sashami. Has become my go-to take-out place for raw fish and rice.

My husband and I stopped in today for drinks while waiting for his oil change. I had rose and he had the "can't hold water" which was a blackberry lemonade whiskey drink followed by a vodka sprite. Our bartend was very friendly and attentive even with other larger parties there! Although we didn't order food, all of the food that came put looked and smelled amazing! The burger/ fries, cheese platter, and buffalo califlour all looked amazing! We will definitely be back!

We had the Monday night special 2-4-1 fish n chips. It was good. Two big pieces of fish in a fluffy but crispy beer batter, crispy fries and even a side of coleslaw. The coleslaw could've been dressed a bit more. The tartar sauce was really good. We each had a soda and the 2-4-1 special and the vanilla custard for dessert and the total was under$20. The custard was soooo good too! Friendly and fast service, clean restaurant and dozens of tap beers make this a place I'll definitely come back to try more!

We love labella's!!! My husband and I have been going there for 7 years and we can't get enough. They have amazing pizza, especially the NY style slices they have ready at the shop and great chicken wings! They have gluten free products but I can't say it's their specialty so stick to what they know best. 

It's a family owned shop where you actually meet the family . You know it's great when people are greeted by their first name.

Great food, awesome service. In the heart of fat city in a colorful building. I originally thought it was the lame hot dog place that used to be there, but upon closer look, I realized it was a new place.


Very highly recommend!

First let me mention that I came here on a recommendation so I came in with high expectations.

Ordered the fried rice lunch special with Asian BBQ wings: $7.95 (included a drink).

Meh. 

Maybe it's me, but I'm confused on the appeal. Fusion? So... what you mean is Americanized Asian? (Or is "fusion" the fact that I can get mashed potatoes and fried rice under the same roof... where I'll hear John Mellencamp playing overhead and Mexican music coming from the kitchen?) 

That being said, I won't crave the rice... and don't see myself coming here during a lunch break again unless friends suggested it.

Excellent meal. Excellent atmosphere.  Friendly staff. We stopped in on a Tuesday night for dinner. We easily found a couple seats at the bar. The bar staff were friendly and helpful. The wine and beer selections were a mix of Florida local and afar. The bartender was knowledgeable about the menu and the each meals ingredients. The kitchen easily made a modification to a meal for me. The tuna tartar was amazing; flavorful and pretty. Our meals were delicious.

This is by far our favorite neighborhood restaurant for date night, family gatherings and special occasions!  Classic Italian BYOB so fantastic value, excellent service and delicious food.  Must go!  Never disappoints!!

All of the employees were really enthusiastic and attentive. Good beers on tap (Stella, Victory, Flying Fish..) If you are going to split a pizza between two people, I would get an appetizer too. Pizzas are a good size, crispy thin crust, good sauce, we had the margharita. Calamari was crispy and delicious. Prices are reasonable, spent $50 for two people, I'd go back and try more of the more unique pies!
Food was so amazing! Andy made the best Guacamole... his food and drink  recommendations were spot on! We will definitely be back... hopefully we will be lucky enough to have Andy make our guac!
Fantastic outdoor dining in Montecito. The patio is amazing, service was great, menu phenomenal.

Awesome pizza & food!  We order all during pool season!  Fast delivery & accurate orders!!
Anchor Pool Store

I was skeptical about this place.  I have a gluten allergy so there weren't a lot of options for me.  Don't order a mojito its all syrups and they don't taste that great.   I ended up getting the mahi mahi, I was surprised at how fresh the  fish was.  It was really really good.  I went for lunch on a Saturday and they had guy playing music, he was really good.  Overall I was impressed.  But with only 2 options to eat that are gluten free I don't see myself coming back to be honest.  Unless I just want salmon or mahi mahi.

I came here for a brunch with my aunt. It was so quaint. My aunt has allergies, and the staff was very careful about making sure everything was ok for her. I had the quiche Lorraine and it was delicious. My aunt had an omelet and was very pleased. We each had a raspberry scone - omg. Served warm. Get it. I also got two cookies to go - ones flying out later that afternoon and knew I would want a snack. I'm a cookie snob and they bake everything fresh here. I had a peanut butter chocolate chip cookie and the chocolate crinkle I think they called it. Both so soft and fresh. The chocolate cookie was almost like a brownie. Yum. Enjoy!
The waiter Chris is a true craftsman at his trade the food is very good as well. The view is to die for just a great time and place for lunch or dinner!

Very cute and lovely restaurant with a wonderful vibe! We celebrated our anniversary here the other day. We tried the yucca fries, fried plantains, stuffed piquillo peppers and the tres leches cake with peach icecream! My faves were the fried plantains and dessert! I thought the fries could use more seasoning!

Vibes: quaint country home

Tasting notes for brunch:
-Shrimp and grits: well-salted shrimp in cheesy grits with cubes of ham and pepper in a red, savory broth. Egg on top is fried with crispy edges. Comes with two slices of either potato or whole grain toast. Potato toast was browned on both sides, a little on the dry side, but not bad for mopping up grits and broth. 

Impression: food is alright, nothing spectacular, a bit disappointing. On top of a 50-minute wait, I can only say this place is okay. It was slightly redeeming that the staff was aware of our long wait and gave us a dish for free.
Breakfast- good view, good service, food was just ok. Listening to the street musicians was a major perk of this place.

First time visiting The Block and it was great. We walked in a little before happy hour and ordered food and drinks. The food was terrific. We got the chicken wings, ribs and flatbread (all off the happy hour menu)! It was delicious. We ordered a round of beer and then I ordered a cocktail for drinks. They were great too. We were just bummed to receive the bill and notice that none of the drinks were on happy hour. Maybe our problem for not asking but sad that the bartender didn't let us know. We paid more for three drinks than we did for the food. Overall, it was great and I highly recommend it. I would just advise to pay attention to specials if you are trying to dine for "HAPPY HOUR" prices!

Hands down the best donut place I've ever been to.  Who would have thought they would make your donuts fresh and only when you placed the order?  It sounds like their hot flavors are rotating so the day I went in they had appolonia spice, vanilla lavender, and indian cinnamon.  I wish I could have tried them all but they recommended the appolonia spice as the "one I have to try" if I were only going there once.   I wish I could have tried their non hot donuts which also seemed very popular.  So I tried the appolonia spice and their moist fried chicken, one of the best fried chickens I've ever had as well.  This fried chicken and donut meal made me a happy camper before I left Philadelphia.  Foodies may come to Philly for the cheesesteaks but they should consider coming for Federal Donuts!

As i told the chef, Julie Buhler, "This is the best f**king sandwich i've had in a long time". By sandwich i mean, The Stoner which inckudes
Steak, lettuce, tomato, goat cheese, saracha, and ranch dressing on a hoagie roll. Fresh, savory with that bite of saracha that grabs you enough to gain your attention. The menu is small but serve both breakfast, lunch and dinner that has enough choices for vegetarians and meat lovers alike.

Affordable, fresh and definitely not the norm and friends THAT is a good thing. It is an old garage transformed with artsy decor and minimal flash.
  
So my friends if you want something that is definitely not the norm but worth a try...Get there soon. You will not be sorry.
 
https://www.phatbites.com/menus/

I love Five Guys.  The burgers are outstanding and the fries are good.  People will disagree but I think this burger is probably the best in the NOLA area for the price. 

It can get a bit pricey though but if you are there with someone you can save some coin.  You only need to order the smallest fry and share.  They dump so many extra fries in that wonderfully greasy bag that sharing is truly caring.

Right now in Harahan it gets REALLY busy.  Hopefully when the Mid City location opens it will slow down a bit!

Get over there and check it out.  Well, unless you're one of those nazis that only support local and freak when a chain opens in the area.  Because then you won't be happy since it's a chain.

My Wife and I bought E-tickets from nyephilly.com for a nice evening on New Years Eve.  The valet folks was attentive and polite. We arrived about 8:50 PM and the doors were to open at 9:00 PM.  We purchased "fast pass" tickets which we hoped would reduce the wait outside.  As we stood in line there was a obvious confusion in the crowd about where the line was for VIP, Fast pass or general admission.  Finally by word of mouth we found the VIP/fast pass line and got in around 9:35 PM.  The general admission line was not even moving which made me think they must have not got in till after 10:00 - 10:30 PM.

Unfortunately, the coat check area was holding up the lines which was greatly understaffed. There was only person working frantically to get people's coats checked.  As we finally made it into the club we are impressed with the layout and decor.  According to the tickets we bought they were supposed to have open bar from 9 -1 AM, food (buffet / horderves not sure which one) and Champagne to toast at midnight.  My wife and I had approached one of the two open bars with a minimal wait since most people were shuffling in at that time. We ordered our drinks and started walking around to get to know the environment.  No food that we could see or smell at that time though out the evening.  As the night progressed the club was packed as expected.  Unfortunately, this made waiting for a drink about 20 - 30 minutes.  Again the bars were way understaffed with little organization for crowd control.  At one of the bars they stated that they ran out of Jack Daniels early on. 

DJ was good and kept people dancing through out the night.  The crowd was friendly and respectful. The general admission crowd was left standing all night unless you could sneak into the VIP lounge area to grab a seat.  Absolutely no seats available for general admission which sucked.  At midnight the DJ missed the New Years Eve count down by 20 seconds (not a huge deal).  We left shortly after.

To say the least, we would not return due to lack of seating, no food or champagne as promised on the tickets, and bar time waits.  

Overall Rating: D+
Never Again!

One of the best things I have eaten in University City. My mom said it was one of the best things she has ever eaten period, which is not normally said and HUGE compliment. I ordered the hai street chicken and was definitely not disappointed. The textures were perfect, crunchy from the veggies, tender from the chicken, and soft from the rice. The flavors of all of the components were PERFECT! I am going back tomorrow and recommend that others try this place out too!

I couldn't tell the difference between this one and the one at Cerritos, but this place had alot more room. The one in Cerritos always felt crowded. Oh they have bathrooms here, I dont' remember one at Cerritos?
Absolutely out best dining experience in New Orleans.  The food was terrific,  the service from Paula was off the charts wonderful.  We will be back tomorrow.
I'm now giving district donut a four star because their donut lacks. The donut itself is too dense. It has good flavor but if they were to make the donut dough softer I would give them a five star.

I love LaVa! It has basically become my second office. They have free wifi, which is great (although it can be hard to find an open outlet sometimes). The food is delicious - I recommend the shakshuka or the burekas. They have $1.25 refills on hot and iced coffee, which is great if you're staying there a while. They also offer a discount for members of City Fitness.
Horrible ass place!! Can't ever get shit right. Machines always done,fries always old and cold. Worst McDonalds I've ever been too, never in my life will I go here again!!!
Nice place for breakfast or lunch any time of the day.  However,  there was no soup in the men's or women's restroom today. There was a roll of paper towels on the zinc instead of the dispenser.
Senior citizen heaven, the place is packed & the average age seems to be 85!! Excellent food, try the Authentic Chicken Grek Salad or the Bleu Cheeseburger.

MexiCali is the proverbial apple in the Garden of Eden...you want it, but you know there are dire consequences for having it. For having "Cali" in its name, it's rather disappointing (because California has some dope ass Mexican food).

What I Ordered: Cheese Quesadilla. Nothing special. Literally tortilla and some shredded cheese. Extremely overpriced for what it is.

Verdict: The food is okay at best. The only reason I gave it three stars is because my roommate, ironically from L.A., claims they serve a pretty good burrito. Haven't tried, and I don't want to try. He might be delusional. Or hasn't tried the slice of heaven known as El Taurino/King Taco. Also, their service is a joke. The lady manning the cash register looked at me with disgust when I asked for some corn salsa on the side. Also, they have one cook. Orders get backlogged. Food takes foreverrrrrr to come out. So if you're feeling Mexican food while in Philadelphia, you'll be much more satisfied with Don Memo's Food Cart, or even (dare I say) Chipotle/Qdoba. I'd recommend to try it just to try it, but leave it at that. No gastronomic love affair stems from this place.

My daughter and I went here for Happy hour on a Friday. We sat inside because it was a warm day. But we were seated right away. The server was friendly and knowledgeable. I feel awful I don't remember her name. She gave us tips and suggestions for what was good. We were pretty hungry so we ordered off the tapas menu and had a main course. We started with Mediterranean olives and trio hummus. That was the best hummus I've ever had! The pita triangles that came with it were fresh and soft. We also tried the dolmades that were bigger than I've had, but tasted delicious and lemony. We also tried the garlic lemon chicken with pine nuts. Also fabulous. As was the sauteed mushrooms. So needless to say, by the time our chicken wraps came, we were full. We didn't finish because we wanted to try the walnut Baklava; that we split. I do believe that is heaven's signature dish. Three perfectly sized baklava triangles laid on creamy scoops of vanilla ice cream. It was flaky and with just the right amount of sweetness. I didn't think we could finish the entire bowl, but we really, really had too. It was too good not to! If you have never been, the hummus and pita are a must, as is the baklava.

This morning I read the previous Yelp review on this restaurant which encouraged me to pay them a visit today. The food is sooo good and the staff are very nice. I had the original pancakes, scrambled eggs, turkey bacon, grits, toast and a tasty Mimosa. That is the best turkey bacon I've had. My waiter suggested I add some brown sugar to my grits and they tasted great! the prices are very reasonable. I will definitely be back. They just opened in May so please patronize their business!
Good specialty tacos. If you're looking to fill up, I would recommend the quesadilla. Fun soda selection. Inside is nice for a fast casual restaurant.

I'm so quick to write reviews for places that are horrible, I feel I need to write for a place I enjoy.  Walked in here and was mmediately greeted, I'm talking smilies and waves included.  Super fast service, and my burger was perfect.  Manager made rounds, asking how things were, and thanked us for coming in.  Definitely a great lunch experience on a glorious Friday!

Review would be for cocktails only - overall this place is just not my jam.

They try really hard on the ambiance and it comes off as very GQ and high end. Some people may really like and appreciate it, but to me it just came off as trying too hard to be trendy and hip. I'm all for atmosphere but if I'm taking out my phone to use the flashlight to read the menu, the lighting needs to come up a little bit.

If you are into mixology, sampling different high end types of liquor, or like exotic combinations and innovation in your drinks, and don't mind the prices you'll love it. My drink was good, but it's not worth it to me (and I wouldn't stop in for more than one) at $10-14 a drink.
I treated myself to the triple berry stuffed french toast and it was amazing! Service was friendly and fast love the gift shop glad Iive close by everything taste homemade.

Husband and I decided to try this place out! It's absolutely adorable! Very inviting atmosphere. We started with coffee and beignets which were delicious. I got egg whites and turkey bacon and railroad potatoes. My husband got pancakes with scrapple and two over easy eggs. Everything was enjoyable! The only "down fall" was our waitress. Though she was nice, she made us feel rushed, by not telling us to rush every 5 minutes and bringing our check to us directly after getting our meals. In fact every single time she came over she said don't rush. Other than her, the place was adorable and we would absolutely go back!
Food was great. Line took FOREVER!! Not exactly sure why. There were only about three families in line in front of me, but I waited in the line for 20 full minutes!??

My family takes me here every year on my birthday. I love this vintage Tucson restaurant. I usually order the rigatoni parmesan - the portions are generous and I always need a takeaway box. The restaurant building is admittedly a little rough around the edges and the food is predictable but those aspects are part of the charm. The patio is so quaint... Love the lights strung throughout the seating area as well as the fish ponds. Caruso's embodies the the unique Tucson restaurant scene. Chain establishments can never capture the personality and quirky ambiance of places like Caruso's. I feel good about Supporting Caruso's and hope it will be a part of the 4th Avenue scene for many years to come.

I am still sitting at the bar as I write this and all I can think is "Yum!" I had the bison burger (pb&j I believe) topped with pesto, smoky tomato jam, creamy tangy goat cheese and peppery arugula. It was so incredibly tasty that I didn't even mind that the burger came closer to medium rare than medium. Don't get me wrong, I love a good medium rare steak but I prefer my burgers to be slightly more cooked. In any event it tasted scrumptious so no complaints from me. Good service, good food. Highly recommend.
The food was really good and the staff was very attentive. I enjoyed the ambience as well!  I had the gumbo and it reminded me a lot of having a bowl of gumbo in New Orleans. Definitely going back :)
Excellent service and food was delicious. We will return. Husband had fillet tips blackened and he is still raving about it!!
The food is 5-star.  I do miss the eggplant and tofu, and barb-b-que pork dishes being dropped from the menu.
Food was great.  quality beer and wine list. Love a little place that isn't overly big.  I think there is only 40--ish seats.  Highly reccomend it over other touristy spots
Food is ok for a Hospital. Some of the staff are nice, others are rude. Overpriced but have a " captive audience " meaning patient families. Plus hardly any place nearby to eat.

Not your typical touristy place.  Not far from the French Quarter.  Plain decor, very friendly staff who are fully engaged in making their place a success.  Innovative dishes- asian seasoning of american staples.  Nicely presented.  Eating here just made me smile.  Restaurants are tough business.  This one definitely deserves to succeed.  Many established places will charge you more and give you a less enjoyable meal than you will get here.

Great beer selection. We went there for a friends birthday. This place is minutes from my house but I never think to go. We ordered the calamari, Meh. No flavor. Could have used seasoning in the batter. We ordered shots and when they brought them over I thought they were kidding. They were tiny. Wasn't impressed. Service was great and they seem to have good drink specials throughout the week. Not sure it will be in our rotation, but I would give it another shot.

I know it's a steakhouse but seriously they could do a better job with the fish offerings. Mine was basic and only adornment was half the contents of a fruit cocktail tin dolloped on top of it. 
The bread was cheap, stale and microwaved to try to put some life into it. 
The cheese/mashed potatoes was just packet mashed potatoes, dry, with melted cheese poured on top.

Food was great, the music was awesome, the service was not so great. Jake Landry was preforming and he was really awesome! He engaged with the customers and really made the evening enjoyable. The food was delicious as always!! But the service left something to be desired. Our host seemed uninterested in our table and it took a while to get our food and drinks even though the restaurant was virtually empty.
The sushi arrived warm and tasty. I got the sassy roll, the Godzilla roll, dragon roll, eel and cucumber, and shrimp tempura roll. They were all tasty and it's cheap.

My husband and I went here on a whim after brunch for Valentine's Day. We had the beer and chocolate pairing flight- it was oh so good! My husband LOVED their IPA and Extra Easy, I enjoyed their Southern Witt. The people working their were very nice and helpful. I would recommend this place for a first date or date night out, regardless of age!

Horrible from start to finish . We got seated in a back corner and forgotten about, when the waitress finally came over she got the drink order wrong . We ordered appetizers and dinner . Dinner came but no appetizers and she apologized and stated she forgot to put them in and would do so but we declined as our meals were already here. I ordered my granddaughter grilled cheese with apple slices and she received applesauce . Food was very bland , ordered the chicken special with
Stuffing , mashed potato and vegetable. Chicken had so many small bones throughout I stopped eating it . Stuffing was so greasy and tasteless, mashed potato was cold. Service was lousy, food was lousy and place was dirty and smelled strongly of mildew . Will never return .

The food was the best that I have had in New Orleans. Service was outstanding!! Try the chicken, burger or if you like fish they have lots to pick from. The fried Brussel sprouts we great. Can go wrong with this restaurant.
Love this place for a quick steak dinner. Their prices are affordable and quality is great. Good value here!

This is about my 4th visit here while staying in the hotel. I always say I'm going out to somewhere else, because of all of the good restaurants nearby. But after working out, I usually just want to shower, and walk downstairs for dinner...so I end up here.

After having eaten the typical bar food all of the other times, I tried the sushi tonight. I was better than I expected, especially the spider roll. Now, we're not talking high end sushi restaurant quality, but substantial better than pre-made grocery store quality. And the Edamame serving was quite large.

Most of the food on the menu is way overpriced, per the usual hotel menus. However, the sushi was really reasonable. Around $8-$10/roll, depending on the complexity.

While I'm sure I'll keep telling myself I'm getting out is the hotel for dinner when I'm here, I'd definitely settle for sushi here as a backup.

Their portion size is good. Aside from that, the food was almost flavourless. If you like very very bland tasting food, which some folks do, this could be a great spot for you. However, I ordered my friend and I the veggie panang curry which tasted like sweet butter which is extremely weird,, the pad Thai was actually flavorless, not even butter flavoured, and the curry fried rice wasn't too bad so that's the reason for the two stars. Three orders costs about 35.00 So with tip 41.00 and super disappointing. A new place opened up off of. 56th and Busch that kills the flavour game. But I'm sure somewhere else in Brandon will do.

This place moved to 9303 50 street over 2 years ago.  For fun, I tried out the new location, which admittedly is a step up from the old location  But the old location had excellent nooner pizzas.  I ordered their special soup and sandwich.  Not much in the sandwich and the soup was out of a can.  More of a trucker style of food I suppose.  Saving grace was the beer.  They have various sizes for sleves, pints, etc. It Is a rather blue collar or no collar crowd with a few old bikers.  Nothing special inside but cosy.  Had one tv.  More for locals, not something you would just want to try out of the blue.

Very poor quality as a hotel restaurant.  
We eat at a hotel restaurant even its food is mediocre and everything is overpriced, because we expect to be treated really nicely by well trained staff.  Well, the experience at this hotel restaurant was very unique.  We (five of us) stayed at the Hotel Monaco to celebrate my birthday, and reserved Red Owl Tavern based on many good reviews.  When we arrived at the tavern, we were taken to a table for four.  We told the gentleman that we were a party of five and we had a reservation.  He told us that he would bring a chair.  So, one of us sat on a chair that was placed in an aisle.  We then saw the area in the back where a group of five or so just left.  So we asked if we could move there.  The waitress told us that those tables were reserved.  I told her that we too "reserved" a table for five not four, and it was my birthday.  She told me that she would "see what she could do."  Soon, a lady came to our table and said, "Those tables are reserved."  I told her that we had made a reservation for five.  She said, "Sorry, this is only what we have" and patted on my shoulder and left.  My husband was upset, but I said it was OK.  I decided not to let this ruin my birthday.  After that, however, few things went right. They brought pasta with cheese even though I asked the waitress no cheese due to my daughter's allergy.  So, my very hungry daughter had to wait another 20 minutes for her pasta with no cheese.  We had to ask why the bread, the side, and my father's dish were so late when other dishes were already at the table.  When the bread came after a long wait, it had butter on it despite the fact we told the waitress my daughter was allergic to dairy.  My 81 year old father's dish (Caesar salad with chicken) finally came after everyone finished their food which was more than an hour after we ordered all the food.  While all these things happening, we saw the area we had hoped to move in order to have more room which was "reserved" completely empty.  Toward the end of the meal, a couple of people were seated at one of the empty tables.  Our waitress was very apologetic.  She was never rude.  She took the pasta, Caesar salad, bread, off the bill, which was nice.  Would I like to dine at Red Owl Tavern again to deal with all the stress, especially for a special occasion like a birthday?  Absolutely not.  I hope the general manager of the Hotel Monaco (Mr. James Adamson) will make more effort to train people at the restaurant at the Hotel.
They make a good spicy Bloody Mary, but I wasn't super impressed by the food. It's just okay.

This has become our go-to pizza location in Media. The Greek pizza is AMAZING when done right. We always order the extra-large size, which seems to be equivalent to other locations' larges. We love the boneless wings, but have to dock a star; everyone we order them extra crispy, you can never tell. They have a solid 6-pack beer selection, a nice eating area, and generally quick service. Definitely recommend!

The Good:

Boozy Float - draft root beer (hells yeah baby), Myers rum & vanilla ice cream.  Makes me purr.

Outside seating that isn't in the middle of the sidewalk!

Big juice burger - delicious. And when I told them to make it as rare as legally possible, they obeyed.

Possibly the best fries I've had since traipsing around Texas.

Great! BBQ sauces - loved the tangy and the spicy, although I really couldn't tell which was which.

The Bad:

Margarita with salt - I did say without salt, because bleh to salt on my margarita. The large quantities of liquor made up for the salt taste. 

Service was a bit slow, but it was a Saturday afternoon - true they weren't packed, but they also weren't rocking their A-game.

The Ugly: 

Ha, the other patrons! Drunky McDrunkerson was Cra.Zy. throughout our curbside brunch. Entertaining, but exhausting to watch. Not sure what the waitstaff could've done to restrain this chick (other then flag her, maybe?) - still. We'll be back.

My new favorite place!!! Yelp says they open at 8am... sign says 9am... we arrived about 8:45am... the owner came out and waved us in. Very nice! Beautiful restaurant..simple, clean,  kind of a cottage feel to it. Fresh flowers on each table with small candles. A romantic breakfast. We both ordered the same.  Biscuits and Gravy with Eggs. The biscuits are large,  crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside..oh...and the gravy was divine, lots of sausage, very tasty! Eggs were cooked to perfection and the potatoes were tender and seasoned with paprika..yummmm! We ordered an Peach Fritter to share.  OMG! Four small crispy balls covered in cinnamon sugar. Perfectly decadent, they arrived in a martini glass with a strawberry. Beautiful presentation! Not too sweet, just a nice blend of sugar and cinnamon and peach. The coffee is a local blend.  Very very delicious! I would have drank a third cup but all that food....I was stuffed! The chef, Michael came over and introduced himself and let us know that it would be just a few minutes before the biscuits were done. Everything is fresh made by hand, from scratch. No mixes, or pre-prepared foods. Our service was spot on! I was comfortable,  and pampered! I'll be back to try some of other items!!! I can't wait!!
The BEST Sunday brunch in the world! Save room for the crepes

went out with another family and since our other option was chillis which i frequent and love i decided to go ahead and try this place out.
servicee was very fast which was great, im assuming since it was pretty empty.
food was ;ehhhhh very mediocre. ive had better guac, chips and fajitas in other places.
dont think ill go back to any of these chains...not terrible but not worth going back

I was thrilled to find some *actual* New York style pizza so close to home!  The pizza is great and garlic knots are great - especially with some beer.

The only issue I've really found at both Racanelli's I've been to (the CWE location as well) is that I have never waited less than 20 minutes for my order - even when just picking up a slice. :( 

I'm hoping the wait times will improve because the pizza is great!

I keep coming back because the food is good.   But I need to knock off one star because there just a couple of things that irk me.  They can fix it, but they need to pay attention.  

When you order a sandwich.  It comes with fries. Many people don't like fries.  But I can't substitute with fried yucca.  Even though the fries and the fries yucca a re priced the same as sides. 

Makes no sense.  I hate things that make no sense.

Then there's the 50 cent charge for a tiny little side of sauce.  It's tiny.  And I can't help but feel they're nickel and diming me. If someone just ordered two full meals and needs a little extra sauce, seems to me they shouldn't charge.  And if they are going to charge, use a little larger container please.  

It's my pet peeves.  But I'm my opinion, it's things like these what's holding this place back from being just good to being great. 

Good tastes great though.  Come check it out.  Hope you like fries.

Try the pecan crusted drum. We were are a party of four. Three had the fish and all rated it delicious. I had the duck breast, which was perfectly prepared. Bits of duck and rendered duck skin in the dirty rice accompaniment.

I have had many Ahi Tuna entrees, from Cape Cod to the Keys and J. Gilberts is by far the absolute best. It was fired grilled with a sauce that left me wanting more.  I tried my friends scallops that was cooked perfectly and melted in your mouth.  If you are ever in St. Louis, Columbus Ohio, Kansas City, go,  it is a sure win. The sides were green beans with pecans and Brussels sprouts. Awesome! Our server Joseph was awesome. We went back 2 nights later and I had the same Tuna.  It is that good,

The only thing I tried today was the mixed berry bingsu (shaved ice). You get a cup of it for $4.99 before tax, and has a nice layer of snow like ice with a berry sauce and sweet cream swirl. It was light, refreshing, and just the right amount of sweet. The bingsu comes in chocolate, mango, and mixed berry. Would definitely recommend.

Can't say enough good things about this place. My husband and I were visiting the area and wanted a nice spot for dinner...the Red Pony was the perfect spot! We sat outside on the 2nd floor, which was beautiful, but the whole place had a great atmosphere. Our waiter, Chase, was super friendly, attentive, and had great suggestions for everything from appetizer (the grilled bacon was to die for) to entrees, drinks and dessert. My husband was lucky enough to get one of their steak burgers (they only make 15 a day!) and he said it was the best burger he ever had. We will definitely be back!

Man this place was fire !!!!! The devil eggs to start off were fabulous!!! And for a meal I got the red beans and rice and they were just spicy enough but not to hot !!!! My wife got the macaroni and cheese and I tried some and have to say that it's probably the best I have ever had. Also I tried the roast beef pot boy and it was great too. Drinks are great and great atmosphere just all around a great place to go. Come see Jeff when u come in he was great as well. Also my buddy had the the oysters raw and he said they was really good as well. Must try this place out

By chance we enter Federal Donuts while out walking on a Sunday morning, unaware that we have stumbled right into the 11:45 event horizon separating exotic doughnut time and fried chicken (and exotic doughnut) time. The air is tense with anticipation, and fear. A morbidly obese couple is forced to wait outside with their doughnuts until the fried chicken distribution begins. They eye us with suspicion and whisper between themselves: "Are they trying to parlay a doughnut order into preemptive poultry? Surely they would be shot by the guards!"

The official behind the counter explains the details of the chicken rationing to the addicts in line - each adult is permitted to place one half-order consisting of four pieces: split breast, thigh, and drumstick. A 400 pound man trembles with sweat. A stern young woman in jackboots walks the line for fried chicken orders, handing out tickets. No one is smiling except the children, seemingly too young to know better.

Fearing retribution from the chicken junkies we limit our order to doughnuts and leave. The doughnuts were excellent. I can't imagine how good the fried chicken must be.

People are hard on Dinardo's for the decor but we didn't go last night for decor... we went for blue point crabs and they were great!  We each had 2 jumbos that were steamed and seasoned perfectly.  Started with plump mussels in a red sauce we finished with a spoon! Every member of their staff was friendly and attentive.

Tastey pastry.  Similar to a funnel cake. The only difference is the dough folded instead of spread out. Only eat when freshly made. And do not worry about the powdered sugar... It will end up everywhere
This place is really good. The popcorn Chicken is amazing along with everything else we got. Definitely coming back!

My fiancé and I have celebrated our 10 years Anniversary at Vetri. We were greeted and seated promptly. The staff were amazing and so were the dishes. My fiancé and I enjoyed everything (we even did the wine pairing) and we were not disappointed. I love how the staff explain each dishes and the taste (and fragrance) of each wine. We had a lovely yet romantic evening at Vetri and it is a must go for any romantic outing. Thank you to everyone at Vetri for making our night memorable. (April 5th, 2016)

I used to live around the corner from this place about 10 years ago.  It was great place to grab a quick six pack and go.  The beer selection is incredible, and they carry a little bit of everything in the store.  I like that you can mix up your selections in a six pack.  Definitely for the beer connoisseur.

Stupidly, insanely good vegan food. That is all. 

P.S. Had the Philly and Chicken Ranch sandwiches.

Very nice and fresh food, atmosphere is nice, real clean tables. Chargrilled Oyster were ok, Chicken Hibachi was real good. The crawfish rolls were the bomb love them.  What top it the most was the service; quick and prompt food didn't take long at all.

I was at Sage the other night with my Fiancée and it was awesome!  I had the blackened shrimp and steak penne (spicy and quality) and she had an interesting scallop special. These were big boy scallops also, and we're over shrimp risotto.  We finished up with the best $2 dessert ever and will definitely be back!

This place is quite brilliant! The value and quality of the food is unmatched in SB. I have tried many of the menu offerings and haven't been disappointed yet. The salsa bar can get pretty gnarly due to the insane volume of selfish customers passing through. I am knocking it down a star for that and for the musical chairs that you sometimes need to play when it is busy.

As a native Chicagoan, I am a huge pizza snob. I generally try to stay away from pizzas in cities without a large population of Italian immigrants because it's usually pretty low quality pizza. However, the pizza that I ordered from this place was actually pretty good, even if it did have chewier and heavier crust than what I generally prefer. My one criticism is that this place needs better salad dressing - a plastic pouch of kraft dressing doesn't do it.

I can't say a single bad thing about this place! Chef JJ's is the best place to eat in town. They continue to surprise my husband and I each time we have been in. We loved our last experience so much we became season ticket "holders." You are missing out if you don't put this place on your dinning list. 
Side note: Gift cards to this place make for a fantastic gift!

La Collina hosted a special occasion party/dinner for us in the bar area. Group was about 25 adults and about 8 kids. We couldn't have been happier with the entire process and how the event came off. Dario and team were gracious and helpful in customizing food and setup for us. 

The staff - wait staff, bartender, and Dario were a pleasure to work with and very responsive throughout the evening. 

Our guests loved the variety of options - pastas, chicken marsala, roasted peppers, clams casino. 

Nobody was left waiting for a drink. The pours were a little big, which is not something anyone would every complain about. 

A few people here complained about the valet, but he was great. Parked our guests cars in the back so as not to tip off our surprise guest of honor about the surprise. And moved all of the family's cars to the front, started and warm on a cold night. 

La Collina is an ideal location for a special event or private party. Central location near 76. We had guests coming from Jersey, Chester County and points north. Great service, good food and a warm atmosphere with character. 

Thank you for making our party the special event we had hoped it would be.

"For a fun, music-filled day in the sun Shephard's is the place.   I've been here 5 times in the last 6 months and I live in Chicago.  I visited in April, May and the Labor Day weekend.   Each time it gets better and better.  Why?  I always arrive to find parking waiting for me (OK, not on Labor Day weekend), an ice cold Mojito, some peel and eat shrimp, fun people at nearby tables and dance music.  Oh, age range of people is probably 25-45, I've never seen any children here and sadly to say, the crowd is not very diverse.  However, the crowd is a nice mix of locals and tourists. 

Shephard's bands (which play 7 days a week, I believe) performs from 11:00am-11pm; at end of season that changes to 2pm-11pm.  But do not despair because the INDOOR club at Shephard's opens up at 10pm so the party continues on. 

During the day, when you're hungry while sitting in the sun...just wave the waitress over and order up lunch.  Later in the evening for a real dinner you can either dine off the menu at the fabulous restuarant they have inside or enjoy the buffet which always includes crab legs and an array of fresh seafood. 

If sitting in the sun and getting your tan on is not your cuppa tea, just stroll over to the beach front for a swim.  Or jump on a boat and go parasailing.  While you're waiting for your parasailing launch boat to arrive, cool off in the gulf bay and chat it upwith the folks anchoring their boats near the fun. 

By now, after your parasailing, dancing and dining.... the sun must set.  And what better place to watch it than here...breathtaking.  If you go to Shephard's and don't enjoy yourself....check your pulse, then see your doctor! 

P.S....Anyone remember Tone Loc?  The "Funky Cold Madina - Wild Thang" guy?  He was the featured act at Shephard's this Labor Day weekend 2006.  Check my profile for pics!!!

What can I say, I grew up with Krystal and White Castle. Whether it was late at night after being out for the evening or on the way to work in the morning nursing a hangover it was always great comfort food. Why am I saying what it still is.!

They've added little chili cheese hot dogs to their overall crystal menu which are just as enticing as a regular Krystal burger. I know, I know this is not a burger, burger but it's a Krystal burger. Come on you gotta know these things and love them. They are what they are and they don't pretend to be anything else.

I accept them for exactly what they are and appreciate them for their healing and comfort food feeling that they give me. I know everybody doesn't feel the same but this is the childhood memory that I have been able to carry on throughout my entire life. I enjoy them as much today as I did when I was a child. The addition of the chili cheese pups are just a bonus.

I understand crystal may not be for everybody but, it is open 24 hours a day which makes it very convenient. There's only two of them in town which makes it very inconvenient depending on where you live. But for some of us, it will always be part of our unhealthy diet. I pride myself on not eating fast food but this is the one I frankly just refuse to give up. I don't indulge in it that often but when I do I sure appreciate it for just what it is, nothing more nothing less.

What's a girl to do? Some things just never change no matter how old you get, lol!

I loooove it here. This is my go to diner for about two and a half years now. I love the food and the waitresses are so great. I think I have only been disappointed once when eating here. The foods great and I love the atmosphere.

Just grabbed a beer - was going to have a snack but the person next to me was doing business and every other word was F _ck!!  Now I used that word often -- has a great ring to it and it's one of my favorite words ... drives the pint home quite well . However they were a little over the top and the bartenders fell into it encouraging the discussion- lots of loud trash talking -- Happy Hour Prices upstairs but not at the main bar - didn't tell me but shared with other customers that came in after me. Disappointing at best.
While not my favorite type of food I must say it was very good.  The service was very good.  If your looking for a change of pace give it a try

Two stars only because the server did his best. Ordered the mushroom Swiss burger... Asked for it medium and it came out well done. Server was great- he took it back and brought me a new burger. The meat tasted over processed/ground. Half the burger was cooked medium and the other half well done... They must be having a problem with their grill because my friends bison burger was the same.

Food was mostly good - mussels were good as were the shrimp tacos and the mahi. The service and the attitude were bad to horrible. Not only the waitress but just everybody at the restaurant staff seemed disinterested. GOod location but avoid it if you can till they work out kinks of a new restaurant. 

Waited 15 mins after sitting down before even a waitress showed up - her excuse did not notice a party of seven in the middle of the restaurant. 

Three stars are generous.

First, this is NOT an authentic Korean BBQ restaurant, despite what the sign and the menu says.  Avoid the beef, it taste like hot dogs (unless you like that flavor).  Anything pre marinated does NOT have an authentic Korean flavor. I'm of Korean descent.

Second, the service is subpar, they do not actively exchange the grill plates and they aren't attentive to  grilling your own food.

The restaurant also doesn't have proper ventilation for grilling, the dining area is extremely smokey.  If you are not feeling well or having difficulty breathing, your health might be in danger, be careful with older adults and folks with breathing difficulties.

I personally had to excuse myself from the table to make a visit to the restroom and my guest had to leave the restaurant.

Bottom line, stay away!  The best part of the experience was the free mints at the door to mask the awful flavor and the relative fresh air of the parking lot outside.

Come hungry and early. It get crowded especially on Sundays where people come after church. Get the buffet meals so you can taste a little bit of everything. The staff are so warm and welcoming and the food is so good especially the fried chicken and gumbo. When you sit outside and eat expect flies or bugs flying around because it attracts food but it is part of the experience especially in the south. Will come back again definitely.
Amazing pad thai!!! Fresh flavorful and oh so good!!! Massaman curry and fresh summer rolls are great too!!!

This place was really good.  I was confused when they started building one so close to the Izzo's; but it really was very different.  They had several options as far as you could do nachos. tacos, a burrito, a quesidilla or a salad.  I think the prices were more reasonable than Izzo's and the staff was way friendlier.  My food was pretty good although the queso tasted a little different than what I'm used to.  The decor was cute.  I'll be back!

Last night, I cheated on my long-time Thai lover Chiang Mai.

CM, I will always love you and I will be back someday.  I just don't know how soon that day will be.

Siam impressed me, there's no way around it.  The portions were insanity.  

Two of my friends and I opted for a family meal and when the waitress asked if we needed anything else all I could think of was a second table!  Sweet and sour pork, pork fried rice, mongolian beef, almond chicken, white rice, egg rolls, pork with seeds, and a sizzling rice soup crowded our table as we sipped away at tall glasses of Thai-iced coffee.

A special aside note on the coffee: As my friends and I sipped away they heckled me over mine being darker than theirs.  The waitress overheard this and brought me extra half-and-half in case I thought the coffee 'might be too strong.'  That told me just how much she cared that my meal was exceptional.

The food, oh, the food.  I grew up eating a steady intake of all matter of southeast Asian cuisine and Siam was like eating in my mom's kitchen again.  The flavors were full and bright.  I found myself wanting to eat more and more, despite my belt silently protesting by digging into my expanding stomach.

The service was spot-on.  The servings were bountiful.  The help was incredibly friendly.

Siam Thai, I look forward to many more dollars spent and many more good meals taken in.

PS: When they say something on the menu is spicy?  They aren't kidding.

Our server was OK, I sat there with an empty glass but when our food came he did refill it. I got the southern fried chicken sandwich and I wish they seasoned it more because all it tasted like was grease. The pickles on it gave it a nice crunch and tangy taste. The fries were nice and crispy.

Probably a great stop for breakfast, but I came for a late lunch. Food was good, I didn't know all the variations they offer, the Nutella stuff looked delicious; good music playing, staff did a fair job, but the facility wasn't very clean. Looked as if it had not been cleaned since the breakfast shift, floors, tables etc. 

I'll be back most likely, for breakfast next time.
I took my girlfriend here and she got food poisoning lmao but the food was bomb tho ‍

Food came out cold. Cappuccino was ok. Server was able to add smoked boudin to my farmers omelette for $4. Given the other reviews i expected more. Service was slow. I'm sorry I fell for a tourist trap.
By far one of my favorite restaurants in the Bay Area. Consistently delicious, great service. Order the mushroom bisque... It's a must. Love this place!

Quality delivered with disdain.

The sushi is good and the Saki selection is great but its brought to you, eventually,  by people that clearly have better things to do. The lunch buffet is great and it minimizes your reliance on "the wait staff". 

The atmosphere is nothing to write home about but the music... The music is bumpin Banal blather that limits your ability to hold a conversation without it devolving into a combination of shouting a charades. That said lunch is better but once the sun sets the boombastic buffoonery begins.

I was really happy with this place. After going to Camelia's for breakfast the morning previous and getting rude service, this place was a haven. We had a nice server. The food was brought out fast and my coffee was refilled with a smile. 

The food was decent. I had no complaints about it. I had an omelet with hash browns, kind of hard to screw that up.

Went here yesterday around noon with my beau for some breakfast. I've been going here for pastries since highschool but only had their real food once before. I read some reviews on here and was worried, but they must have read yelp and improved where they were lacking. 

It was busy but we found a table right away! This was a miracle since we drove by three places thinking we would eat there, but the lines were out the door! So we were ecstatic to sit immediately.

Everything on the breakfast menu looked good, we ended up ordering a Denver omlette and eggs Benedict with ham. I do have to say their prices seemed a little high...we were starving so we didn't care that much, but around town the prices are a dollar or two less.

Both our meals were very good, the breakfast potatoes were very awesome! Crispy on the outside and soft enough on inside. Good flavor too. I also love that meals come with a mini pastry. Mmmmm!

For drinks we had a water and a coffee. The coffee was promptly refilled, the waitresses had good attitudes. 

One thing that cracked me up was their descriptions on their menu. It frequently said "this is great" or "best blah blah in town", "the best" or "so yummy" it just sounded like an afterthought, like "oh we should put canned positive words and phrases so people order this." a more authentic way to boast would be having the servers pick a favorite dish and putting "so and so's favorite breakfast" or like what squeeze in does, have a legend where a symbol represents most popular dishes. I frequently ask servers for their recommendations so im not opposed to what they wrote per say, but it made me chuckle.

Will continue going here. We enjoyed our visit!!

Anyway, enjoyed our meal here.

Really enjoyed my time at Pub & Kitchen.  Server was fabulous.  However, I got stuck in the very back and it was like an ice box with the air blowing right on our table.  Luckily our server was kind enough to move us to the main dining area where it was much more comfortable.  

Food was very good.  Pulled pork sandwich was tasty.  Nothing that would blow you out of your shoes, but nonetheless, good!  Fries were also tasty.

Overall, I would definitely come back!

Love this place! Great food, great wine! Trying the bacon jam and the brussel sprout appetizers are a must for lunch or dinner. If you go for dinner the steak is a must try. The salad and sandwiches at lunch are all good. The hamburger is so fresh it moos with every bite.
Moderately priced The Block is a nice meal treat. Great atmosphere and staff ample parking behind the building. 
The Block is Yummy!

80s themed food with a slant towards gin cocktails? Yes, please, sign me up! Unfortunately, my visit to Juniper Commons fell short. I've enjoyed all of Kevin Sbragas restaurants in the past and frequent them often but this seems like a misstep. 

The space is large and open with rust and gold hues dominating the interior. The service was good, friendly and attentive. The cocktails were tasty and the menu gin heavy...so far so good. The issue came with the food and I felt, in the end, I would have been better served at the local diner. For $80 before tip, we sampled a cup of lobster bisque, the deconstructed corned beef "sandwhich," the brussel sprouts side and the bbq ribs (5 small ribs.) The highlight was the charred brussel sprouts and that's not enough to get me back. The ribs were overcooked, the cole slaw accompaniment tastless, and the overall dish overly priced ($26!) Nothing wowed me at all and for the price tag I wanted something to be great. Right? 

I'll still enjoy Fat Ham and Sbraga but don't think I'll return to Juniper Commons.

I NEVER send food back, it happened tonight with the pizza (not NE, on the regular menu) and a friend sent back the beer cheese soup. Tried it before she did,  after taste was like plastic. I'm not usually picky about any of these menu items. Still left with a $13 tab after 2 beers and no food.

If you are looking for a hearty morning carb-fest, look no further. The Pancake Pantry is the place to be for light, sweet, perfectly buttery pancakes like you've never had before. 

Just looking at the menu made my head spin. I never knew there were so many ways to cook up a pancake! In addition to your standard buttermilk cakes, you have your healthier potato or buckwheat cakes or your super thin Swedish or crepe-style pancakes. Then there's my fave - the almost dessert for breakfast cakes: blueberry, sugar and spice, and chocolate chip, to name a few...I could go on but it makes me hungry all over again. I had a stack of blueberry pancakes, and not only were they delicious, but they were perfectly filling without being overly heavy. I ate every last bite and didn't regret a single one!
