Located in Trolley Square, across from Catherine Rooney's bar and the Logan House, Cafe Verdi offers you the option to sit down and eat or just pop in for a slice of pizza or calzone. They moved a few suites down, which threw me off a bit last night. The ambience is different inside - less pizza in a strip mall and more, "Hey! I get it....this is supposed to look like an Italian grotto." The food is always amazing. I never stray from my chicken alla griglia - two huge breasts of chicken with steamed broccoli and spinach. Last night, we had the polenta and eggplant stack (cold eggplant with mozzarella and roasted peppers) appetizers. For three discerning Italian palates, we were very happy. I had a pizelle for dessert, which my Mom had in her purse from a trip to see her Italian first cousin this weekend. No, I am not joking.

Wishing a happy, healthy holiday season to the family and staff of this priceless Italian eatery located in Newtown PA.

Always greeted with a smile, always a great meal.

Nice to be recognized and know what your food likes or food needs/requirements include. 

Hands down a wonderful go to for self, for family and for entertaining of friends and family.

I have only been here for one visit since I don't make it up to this area of town often, but this will certainly be high on my list of places to go when I am in the area. 

My visit came on a Friday night, and it was packed. Parking was made very easy in the free parking garage just go north on 1st Ave from Main St. (the intersection of Pint Room), and you will see the garage on your left immediately. There was a hostess that said she could seat us in the dining area of the place, or we could have a look around the open-seating bar area. We got really lucky and grabbed a table as another group was leaving, but trying to get a table in the bar area on a Friday night looked like a game of chance, as it was busy the entire time. There wasn't really a lot of standing room, so if you don't get a seat you might just want to put your name on the list for a table in the dining area.

I wasn't there to get food, which is good because it took me long enough just to decide on a drink from their enormous beer list. They have it broken down into categories of beers, and they cover the majority of the spectrum. The majority of their beers are on the safe side of things, but there are certainly some adventurous options on the list as well.  Don't quote me on this, but I am fairly certain that the beer list includes the name of the beer, the price, what state it is from, and the ABV %. It'd be nice to have an IBU rating, but even I will admit that I think that might be pretty ambitious for a list that long. I love that the price of every beer is listed by it. I'm amazed at how many places just have long beer lists without ever showing a price until you get your bill.

Our waitress did a great job relative to how busy it was. The guy who came over to clean our table after the last group left was not so much in that category. We got beers filled quickly and our waters stayed full the whole night. Our server even knew a decent amount about the beers they served and she was able to remind someone at our table what they had they last time they were there by just the description alone. One thing that is really frustrating at a place like this is when you finally make a decision on the one beer you want the most, and then they server goes to get it only to come back and say they are out and need a second choice. I know with a place that likes to rotate taps and gets in limited quantities of some beers that it happens, but the waitress didn't even take the time to cross it off of the beer list on our menus so the next person who sees that option and orders it will also be faced with coming up with a second option with no time to think. 

It was a little loud in here just due to the number of people, but it wasn't so bad that you couldn't have an easy conversation with the people at your table. The majority of the people here were young professionals, and the crowd was that of people who wanted to go out and get some drinks and dinner to catch up with friends, rather than to just go out drinking and getting wild for a night. There are quite a few TVs in the bar area, so all of the games you could want to watch will likely be viewable here, although it is much more of an upscale bar than a sports pub. As I said before, I wasn't here for food but everything I saw at surrounding tables looked delicious and I would like to give the food a try sometime, which I will likely be back to do in the summer when longer bike rides take me up to the Carmel area and I need a pit stop along the way.

At 9:30am on a Saturday, when the rest of downtown Santa Barbara is pretty quiet, this spot is packed - and for good reason!

The line to order wasn't long, just a few people. We waited a few minutes and were able to get a table - meant for 4, but we got enough chairs to squeeze 6 chairs around it. 

THE COST: $29 for three small bowls.

Note: The "Small" is still a decent sized bowl! We were afraid what the "Large" would have looked like. If you want what would be, say a "Large" at Pinkberry, then get the "Kid's Size". The "Small" did keep us full for several hours!

* Island - 4 stars
This is more heavy on the berry/tart flavors, and the toasted coconut on top is a treat!

* Cocoa Almond - 3.5 stars
Definitely sweeter, between the chocolate base and the banana. This would've been too much sweet on its own if I weren't sharing the Island with my friend!
Food was delicious, some items came out cold but other than that everything was great!

5 stars for Doylestown Thai food.  If you're looking around for thai food in this area look no further.

I've lived in NYC and San Fran and have eaten quite a bit of great thai food.  This place is as good as thai food that you'd find in San Fran and NYC at a non-upscale thai restaurant.

The service is great and very child friendly.  Parking in downtown can be a little difficult at times but worth it after you've eaten the drunken noodle, chicken with green beans and the massaman curry.

The pineapple fried rice was delicious but the drunken noodles were the best.  All the right flavors with a touch of heat.  The pad thai was a little too heavy on the palm sugar and too sweet for me.  I prefer my pad thai with more fish sauce, chili powder and egg.

The massaman curry is quite nice and will be going back over and over again.

This place is a BYOB and I would recommend a bottle of Riesling and some beer.

They do take reservations if you want to call in advance.  After writing this review I've talked myself into going here tonight with my family.

I can't wait for Thai deliciousness in Doylestown of all places.

Where else in the area can you visit a steampunk-decorated coffee shop? Nowhere as far as I know! We were in the area so I stopped here and got some coffee drinks to go. I enjoy Kahwa espresso so I was pleased to see that's what they serve at Grindhouse! They seemed to have a wide variety of desserts in the case and they looked scrumptious but I've been eating healthy lately so I managed to resist.

Speaking of resisting... I have to admit, the whole time, I looked around nervously, waiting for perhaps a Scientologist to attempt to assimilate me. This is downtown Clearwater after all. However, everyone here seemed OK and I've not joined a cult so life remains good. I look forward to returning!

AWRSOME breakfast place. Service. Food and prices..... suggestions  Montana plate, Bananas Foster French toast, cheese grits. 

Make sure you get here

I had the grilled Mahi tacos and my husband had the Spinach Balsamic salad with Ahi Tuna. We also had the buffalo wing appetizer. Wow. I am blown away with our experience here. The food was smoked to perfect and beautiful plating. It was definitely a fine dining dinner for only about $16 per entree. And I also got their moscato that was delicious!

Went back to HipCityVeg today for lunch. It was packed (weekday at 12:30pm) but they were quick to take orders and keep things moving. 

I just wanted to post on Yelp again to thank the manager (I believe) for such great service today. I ordered the udon noodle salad as I had read rave reviews. Unfortunately, the salad fell flat. It was tasteless and just bland. (My parents had the buffalo Bella and crispy HipCityVeg and both were so good! And sweet potato fries were soooo amazing - crispy on outside and soft on inside) 

I decided the udon salad wasn't worth eating, so I went up and asked if I could have something else instead. The manager honestly actually cared that I didn't enjoy my salad and BOTH replaced it with the philly steak (my choice) free of charge, but also remade the salad so I could give it a second try! He thought that perhaps the fake chicken hadn't been marinated well and the salad was light on the dressing. This second version was MUCH better - much more flavor. I think my first salad was missing the dressing. I still prefer the sandwiches and I think the salad was a bit oily (I know, you can't have it all!). However, that is just first class customer service and I applaud how the situation was handled. Thank you so much, can't wait to be back soon!
Great place! Really crowded at night! The service was excellent. They literally said "we can cook it however you like". The food was good and exotic. Would definitely go back!

Alright, just finished a basketball tourney and my daughter wanted ice cream and I wanted a hotdog, checked yelp and this place popped up, wasn't far so we thought we would try it, drove by and place was totally packed, out to the street, debated then decided to do the wait, took maybe 20 minutes to get thru the drive thru and get our food, was totally worth it! Peer pressure made me get the double cheese burger with everything on it my daughter got a Reece's extreme, the cheeseburger was very good, one of the better ones, her ice cream was HUGE and very good, we both split some fries which was awesome. If you are even remotely close you really should stop, it is well worth it
Excellent soul food. Everything was delicious well seasoned and cooked to perfection. Best greens and black eye peas I ever had.

I've been eating here since I was two years old! I learned how to use chopsticks here and I've seen the staff all grow up along with me. This place is by far the best Thai food I've ever had (and I've been to Simply Thai, Dusit Thai, Smiling Elephant and all those other places). 

For appetizers, the tiger tear salad, chicken satay, and tom yung koon are the bomb dot com and I never leave without having one of them.

They have the best pad thai and chicken panang, so be sure to try it sometime. The seafood curry, while pricey, is worth it for the large medley of seafood you get. Stay away from ordering native Thai hot unless you want a red ring in the morning! 

Please don't pass this hole in the wall up. You'll love every bite of whatever you decide to order. I've never had something I didn't like.

Quite possibly the best Indian food I've ever had, certainly in the top 3 experiences. Food is spiced to order and met expectations perfectly, especially if you have a hard time finding real heat. Staff was friendly, helpful and attentive. Even the leftovers tasted great!

Try the sexy naan!

Best food, best atmosphere!  I will never pass by another Joe's Crab Shack! I could live on the Crazy Good Crab Dip.  Servers are very good, hostess station is friendly upon arriving and leaving.  Food came out in a timely manner and was delicious!

I've been sitting at the bar waiting for someone to ask me what I'm having. I waited a good 5 minutes and still no one asked, yet everyone else around me was being served. It wasn't busy at all.  I ordered the pineapple rice and sushi and it was the worst thing I had ever had. The service sucked and so did the food. The sake cafe on Magazine st. is much better.

Makiman is good, but a bit pricier than other sushi places in town if you don't have some kind of deal. I've had various fish and vegetable rolls, which have all been decent, and the vegetable tempura is good. Service is average.

Twice now, I've run from the cold to squeeze through the door of Pabbit. It's been a nice refuge these last couple of freezing cold nights. 

In short,
The burger is better than Monk's. 
The fries are a close second to Monk's. 
The gnocchi are way too salty. (I still need to try the pierogies.) 

I love having a large pint of cider and a burger so that's probably what I'll stick to if we return again. I might also work my way through all of the $3 bar munchies.

Our server was wonderful! So polite and nice mannered. The food. Oh. My. Goodness. Enough said. Portions are a great size! Prices very affordable. I had the jambalaya and catfish bites and the food was moist and well seasoned. The bites were so light and flaky and hot!! The cornbread is sooo fluffy and warm still and moist. Visit this place!!!

I had a late dinner 9:30pm due to a last minute decision. The food was delicious and well seasoned. The only problem is while patrons are still eating the employees sweep around your table and feet. I understand you want to go home but this issue needs to be addressed. Other than that all went well

A hidden gem. Don't judge it by the location in a small strip mall or its appearance. The food was incredibly fresh and delicious and prices are very reasonable. Ate here for dinner based on other Yelp reviews and was very pleased. They even took great care to accommodate a dietary allergy. We will be back.

Just okay. It seems that the crab is all they know how to do as myself and others have tried other menu items just to be disappointed every time. The only decent appetizer is mozzarella sticks. The crab cakes are bland but somehow still overly black peppered flavored. I guess the French fries are the best non-crab food item they have.

We visited Eats! during Creative Loafing's Tampa Bay Burger Week to try their $5 Juicy Lucy Burger. This Wednesday evening was fairly busy, but we quickly found a table with a view of the World Series game on several televisions. But because this is a small restaurant, I imagine it does fill up at busier times.

Having enjoyed their Mac-N-Cheese at the annual Yelp event in April, I was delighted we could substitute that for fries on one of our orders at no additional charge. Because the burgers were delicious. I'll rave about them first. Mine was cooked more than my requested medium well, but was simply so good that I was able to completely ignore the overcooking. The fries were also very delicious. But the highlight of my meal was that homemade Mac-N-Cheese! The bowl was huge - more than plenty to share between the two of us. Piping-hot creamy pasta, covered with bacon & a thick layer of cheese - glorious. Sooo good!

Our server was very attentive but not over-bearing. She was friendly & helpful, sharing her opinion of a couple dishes that had caught our eye for future visits. But, we also appreciated that she wasn't terribly chatty. Later in the evening, we saw a sign on the ad board about 70¢ wings on Wednesdays, and hubs almost ordered a few to take home for his lunch, due to our server raving about them. Even though he ultimately didn't order any (only because he wasn't able to finish his burger), we are definitely returning for those wings, as well as a few other entrees... And that amazing Mac-N-Cheese.

The restaurant just reopened today from a 2 1/2 week renovation. The restaurant over went a complete transition. The look used to be casual dining with a very busy decor to a classy upscale looking restaurant. Don't worry about the prices, the restaurants is affordable. 

Great semi open kitchen so you can view the cooks in action. There is a glass to keep the noise from entering the dining room. 

Apps are around the $10 area and you can get many main course for $14 - $16. 

The food and service is top notch. There are many dishes to choose from. This has now become my wife and I favourite Italian restaurant in this price range. 

The reason I am giving it 4 out of 5 stars is because they spent the money on renovating the restaurant but our bread came in a broken wicker basket. One of our menus was very worn out around the edges. Not a big deal but don't cheap out on the little things.

A country town feel inside of New Jersey? Go figure! A gift shop full of knick knacs that your paddywhack cousins adorn their walls with at home. A solid breakfast menu that is perfect for a quick stop or a take out on the go. Enjoyed the service and the escape.

Plush is a huge place, kind of gives a vibe of an college apartment party with all the different rooms/areas that different groups congregate to; with an added bonus of being a music venue.  Shuffleboard on the floor and ping pong tables upstairs.  Cool.  

The beer list is pretty long with a nice mix of microbrews and prices were very reasonable, pints topped out at $5, with cheaper 9oz options if you want to sample more of their beers.  

The kitchen is open late, and the food is tasty, although judging from the appetizers, food wouldn't be my main draw for coming.  The grilled cheese sandwiches are mini and good for sharing, the spinich/fig/blue cheese wontons were a great mix of flavor, but the wings were wimpy.  It was nice that the whole menu is served all day.

I hate knocking places on service if the goods deliver, but Plush seemed very understaffed.  They have 4 bars in the place, which were moderately crowded, but took way too long to get a drink, the orders would be wrong, and then the beer would be completely flat.  What?!  

It's a great space, I'd come here for a show, but without the music, Plush would have to tighten up its game for me to come back.

What can you say?  Typical Applebees that seemed to be well-run and had friendly staff.  Food is consistent and predictable.

The Tuesday night burger deal is a good one -- any burger on their menu for $6.99.

If there was a 12 step program for ice cream addictions, this place would probably distract me from completing the course... Anyplace that still serves Richman's Ice Cream has my business whenever I can get there. Although I never have tried any, there's a menu full of good from the fryer and grill. The cheese fries must be a favorite since I saw a few orders being eaten on my way in. 
The ice cream prices are a bargain, and the serving size is enough to make you stuffed and looking forward to your next visit. 
They've been around for awhile, so its good to see a quality business still in the area.

Well after reading that this is one of the Top 20 Italian Restaurants in the Country, we went with some rather high expectations. And let me say they far exceeded those high expectations. My wife Donna, whose is a much harsher critic than I am said "Best Meal I ever had in SJ" then added, "Maybe better then the meals we had in Italy"

The Fennel Sausage and Broccoli Rabe app along with the roasted artichoke hearts with Mozzarella and tomato were truly amazing. simple ingredients and amazing tastes. For our pasta course we had the Spinach Gnocchi that was delicious . and the Pesto, that was as good if not better than the pesto in Cinque Terra Italy. For entrees Donna had the Orata which she raved about and I had the Bistecca Enna which was amazing 

If you are looking for Chicken Parm or Meatballs or American Italian Food, than this is not for you. But if you want simple authentic Italian food like you would order in Italy then I say book a reservation right away because you will not be disappointed.
I've been going to Alex's for a long time. Just good ol' BBQ. Nothing wrong with that...

I like this place because you can go with your non vegan friends and they won't be like ewww. I go here every single time I visit philly and it's definitely my go to if I have a sweet tooth or am missing the flavor of chicken!

Bad service. I've eaten inside there a few times and one time they sat us near the back then left the patio door open the whole time except for 5 minutes after I asked them to close it then it was propped back open again. Another time just not attentive and never came to our table. I've attempted to get carry out from there twice. The first time they lot my order so I had to wait 20 minutes after my pickup time for them to actually make it. Second time I called them and was put on hold for literally fifteen minutes- they never answered again. I just went to restaurant (still on hold), asked to speak to the manager and showed him the call before I hung up. They had plenty of staff and only 3 tables besides 1 group of 3 at the bar. Eventually they found the phone muted by the bartender who acted like she had no idea. The manager apologized (not the bartender) but nothing was done- not even my appetizer comped. Very disappointing. There's plenty of other places in the area with great food and service I'll go instead.

Dominic's Trattoria was chosen as the destination for a special family celebration on a Saturday night in November. We had a party of 13 and they have a small semiprivate room which they sat us in. I ordered the Veal Fontina (sautéed in a white wine mushroom sauce) with a side of penne pasta with red sauce. My meal was tasty and well prepared but slightly cold. There were 12 other orders at the table and unfortunately not everyone got to eat at exactly the same time. Obviously this was the kitchen's fault and not the waiter. The waiter kept drinks filled and responded to requests as timely as possible. Our waiter was very good but I think he had a bit too much on his plate that evening. The room was a touch small for 13 people and I felt a little claustrophobic. Definitely an older crowd in here. I'm 41 and I think I was in the running for youngest person in the whole place! I think I'm at a 3.5 for this one but can't in good conscious round up so 3 stars it is.

Great place for lunch during the week.  Very cool little place to stop in in the middle of the day and have some good food and a drink.  Food is phenomenal.  I would definitely recommend the hot roast beef with roast beef gravy and horseradish on the side.  

I've been here a couple of times for lunch but never for dinner or the weekends but they have a very nice menu.  Can't wait till summer time comes so I can hang out on the deck bar.

The hostess, Chris, was a complete ass! I arrived and asked for a table for a party of 2 and was told I would have to wait until the 2nd person showed up. I told Chris I would like to go ahead and order, but nope he would not seat me at a table!
They are good. Maybe it's my preference to another favourite Thai place I have, but their tom yum or kah isn't as tasty as comparison. The pad Thai is great.

I am so sad to see this place is closed. Circa 2009 my wife and I were there three days staying just down the street and ate there for breakfast on the second and third mornings - and wished we'd found it the first morning and we would have made it a triple.

My wife loved whatever she ate enough to want to return and I had the crayfish benedict both mornings. I have ever since called it the best breakfast I've ever had and I have long wanted to return just to eat there again. 

The place was charming and it seemed like a hidden find/treasure (which, if true, might not be the best for keeping busy).

Alas, I guess I'll have to settle for my second best breakfast, eggs bennedict at http://www.yelp.com/biz/sneakers-bistro-and-cafe-winooski?
Delicious food and great service. This was our first time and we will definitely be back!

Great breakfast for a great price. This place is tucked away from the main streets here in Clearwater Beach, but only a short walk away from the Hilton where I'm staying. Definitely worth the extra half-block to walk. Their outdoor seating affords more sun and atmosphere than most places on Mandalay ave.

Their croissant breakfast sandwich was a meal enough by itself, with the perfect amount of egg and cheese plus thick-cut bacon. The homefries reminded me of a very home-cooked feel, but may need salt for some folks.
We are back what more can I say. Friendly good service  the home made (free) are addictive.

Cute place. Huevos Rancheros were prepared well, although it seems a bit overpriced at $12 a plate. I almost feel like I can walk to the 99 cent store down the street and buy a can of beans/bag of tostadas to make it myself. 

I did enjoy the salsas though; they all tasted very bright and fresh.

The Coffee Cake is fine, but a bit dry after I asked them to re-heat it. I probably wouldn't ask them to re-heat it again.

They don't use numbers for your orders; they use emojis. So you'll have waiters come up to your table and ask "Are you unicorn/moustache face/batman?" It's a little absurd; it almost feels like it should be a joke on Parks and Rec that parodies millennial culture.

But it's still a cute place to get brunch.

We always get great service and good food from Pinas.   We have been eating there for years.    They know all their customers by name which makes us feel special.   Love their pizza and steak sandwiches.

I'm slightly conflicted about this because I came here strictly for the chicken Marsala as it's one of my favorite dishes.  My date's dish, the lobster ravioli had delicious scallops, pretty good shrimp, and I really didn't care for the lobster ravioli.  The lobster seemed slightly rubbery and not all that flavorful.

Onto the Marsala, unless there is something I'm not very aware of as far as the potential differences between a Naples Marsala and a northern Marsala, I'm gonna go ahead and come out and say that this isn't Marsala - and this is coming from someone that generally likes a tradish Marsala, then add some heavy whipping cream to the sauce.  This one is just too creamy.  I could barely detect that the chicken itself was cooked in a little bit of Marsala wine, but the creamy mushroomy sauce just completely dominated.  

I still gave it 4 stars, though, because I love places like this, and really, all of the food was cooked very well - nothing burned, dry, etc., but unless they change the Marsala sauce, I won't be back.  Also, the service was very good, and the owner hugged almost every person that walked through the door.  I'm assuming all of the 5 star reviewers really like hugs.
Very good authentic Mexican food. Tamales are excellent and always fresh. I'm a regular at this place. Great prices and good service. Quick service nice atmosphere.

Great burgers at a great price.

I came to Spot for lunch with my coworker earlier, and we were both really impressed with the menu, the burgers, and the service. Spot offers a pretty unique menu (burgers with everything from blue cheese to pickled daikon and gochujung paste) which is definitely enough to bring people in, but it's the juicy burgers, toasted buns, fresh veggies, and great flavors that will keep them coming back. 

We got the cheese-fries (fresh and good but nothing that'll blow your mind), the spot burger, and the umami burger. 

The spot burger was classic with a twist: a beef burger with bacon and chedder, pickles, coleslaw, and spot sauce. The pickles and slaw kept the burger tasting really fresh/not overwhelmingly meaty. 

The umami burger was definitely a bit heavier, but also more flavorful: grilled onions, mushrooms, pickled diakon, cucumber, gochujung, teriyaki, lettuce. I thought it was really great, the flavors were definitely there, but it was a bit too heavy for me so I couldn't finish my half. Definitely not something to get if you're trying to find something light!

Overally I was impressed, and I'd definitely be willing to come back again on a day when I'm really craving a burger! 

*The guys sitting next to me said they come about 2-3 times per week, and they've yet to try something they don't like. I believe it.

I always like the chill ambiance of this pub. It's nestled off on a quieter part of 17th street and you could actually miss the sign if you aren't paying attention. 
I ordered a dirty martini and the seared tuna salad with shaved celery and beets on Bibb lettuce and my friends had the black sheep burger with Gouda and a portabella mushroom... Both were very tasty. In fact my friend said that it was the best burger in the city!

I used to go to elavation. I really liked the grass fed burger, fries, and shakes. But over time, this place has turned into a dirty, greasy, grimy, place. 

You have to wonder, if a place doesn't keep the front of the house clean, what does the back look like. I'm going to stick with shake shack for my burger needs. EB needs to clean house.

Don't work here either. The people are ignorant.
Wonderful, attentive service and amazing food.  I have never been disappointed with any of the appetizers, entrées or desserts that I have ordered here.

Been to a couple Q'Doba locations and this is the best. Friendly and very helpful servers. Yummy food! Queso and guac..what more do you need. Speaking of guac, I LOVE theirs. Creamy and chunky. I'm gonna go get some now.

We were supposed to wait 45 minutes but it was only a 20 min wait. The service was quick, and the rustic environment was mixed with a sporty vibe. The food was very good, and moderately priced. The pickle chips were really good. Will definitely return.

They blend all of the Ingredients together on the bowl items. So essentially you are eating a smoothie with granola and honey.. I have had acai in San Diego and in the Gulf Coast area that was great and in my opinion how acai bowls should be. Acai base and then a multitude of toppings that you can eat, not a smoothie in a bowl. Not impressed. It's not horrible, but I wouldn't go there again. I asked why they blend it all and they said it is because the ingredients are frozen. Assuming they do this to cut down on costs. If you want to have toppings to eat that are not blended then it's a dollar a piece. Granola and honey are good.

The best apple cider donuts I have ever had! These are hands down my favorite and I have been coming here since I was a kid. Now this place has changed radically since then as it used to be an actual orchard with pick your own apples and pumpkins and hayrides, but the donuts at least have not changed. Where other apple cider donuts are heavy and greasy, these are light and airy. When you get them right out of the fryer and the cinnamon and sugar is on yours hands, perfection. 

They also do all you can eat nights and brunch. I have been to the pasta night on Thursdays, and it is a good bargain for your money, but it is not going to be the best pasta you have ever eaten. It is more of a get what you pay for situation. Again the same experience with brunch. It is consistently good food, but it isn't going to blow you away. Except the donut french toast is pretty neat. They cut the donut in half and cook it like it's french toast. That is pretty great. 

This place is also a BYOB which is always great. They have this one room upstairs which is hung with lights and branches and looks like a pinterest-worthy area to have a lady's brunch. Something I may have to convince my friends to try.

I stop in usually 2-3 times a month.  Good bar food...wings, pizza, burgers, mussels, etc...My one complaint is that the pint glasses for all of the great beer on tap are often warm since they come right out of the dishwasher.  I appreciate a clean glass, but you need to find a way to get the glasses chilled.

I have been living in Fountain Square for a couple years and always said there needs to be a deli or butcher. Alas, my prayers were answered with Turchetti's and was so excited to try out the deli when it opened up. My girlfriend got the gem salad and she said it was incredible! The dehydrated then rehydrated tomato based vinaigrette was top notch. I got the Risino sandwich and I only have one word: delectable. The meats were tasty and you could tell they were fresh and had some love out into the process. Definitely will be coming back again and buying as many meats as possible!
Loved the boat and the trip but the supper is trash. I mean come on - this is NOLA where the food is great everywhere... except on this boat. Do yourself a favor and skip the supper.
A great atmospheric place to take out-of-towners for brunch, and it's not a tourist trap.  Our meals were scrumptious.  This place is legit.

Oh yum.  I like the ambiance in here.  I had a couple Abitas and the roast beef, which was amazing- served on fresh bread with a gravy and also oysters.  I scarfed the whole thing down, practically in one bite.  

Aside from kicking myself for forgetting to pick up a matchbook to add to my collection, this was an A+ experience.

The food here is always wonderful. The flavors all seem fresh and detailed. No dish taste like the other and it comes out quickly. Please do not let the illusion of small portion sizes turn you away. In fact, it is properly serve were you wont leave hungry or sluggish. My only suggestion is that if you have a party more than 2, to call ahead. They try to use their space as best as possible but it can feel like you are on top of each other. If you ever get to visit the owners are usually there waiting with a smile and a story.

Came here on a Friday night during pride. It was crowded enough that most of the tables and bar stools were filled but there was ample seating. There are also a few tables outside, which I sadly didn't realize until we left! 

Bartenders are nice, service is quick. The majority, if not all, of the drinks are under $10. I got a mango Long Island. It was very strong and I left very tipsy :D if you're not into mixed drinks and martinis, they also have some beers. I was surprised that they had a stout! I forget which one exactly but it was from Schlafly. 

Good place for a date or a small group of friends. Not a dancing kind of place it seems, purely for drinks and catching up. There are lots of restaurants around, I recommend grabbing dinner then drinks and then maybe heading a few miles downtown or to the grove to hit the clubs!

This is the best place to eat and drink.
The fried chicken is the best ever and brisket hard to beat.

Ordinary sports bar with typical American bar eats. It does have a decent happy hour, which lasts til 7pm (at least add of the date of my visit) so it is reasonably priced. Brick offers one of many very similarly themed pubs in this area of Tampa. There was nothing extraordinary about this place compared to many others in this area.

I was excited to try this place but afraid I can only give 3 stars. 
The food was great.  I had the seitan wings and the seitan Banh Mi and both were wonderful. The spices and sauce used for both were excellent and the seitan was cooked to perfection. My husband got the regular wings and commented they were a little dry. His burger was good BUT he ordered medium well and it came out medium rare. Typically we would have sent it back since he has a sensitive stomach however we waited an hour and 25 minutes for our entrees. I think he would have eaten the plate if they told him his order was out. 
The server kept apologizing and a manager came over to apologize as well. We weren't in a hurry so it wasn't a huge deal but our friends did have their toddler who was (for good reason) getting impatient. Our reservation was at 7:45, we thought we'd be out the door by 9 instead we didn't get our meals until around 9:20. It seemed as though someone lost our ticket or something because the tables on both sides of us, who were seated well after we were both got their food before we did. I am going to assume this isn't the normal occurrence over how apologetic the staff was. They did comp our appetizers and one dessert which was very much appreciated. I would certainly give Bernie's another try because as I said the food was wonderful and the recovery efforts of the employees were great, mistakes happen but they recovered very well. 

One tip-the floors were very slippery and they did not have out any caution signs. It was raining the night we went and I slipped going into the main dining/bar area. I'm 5 months pregnant so thank goodness I caught myself. My friend also slipped on the way out carrying her toddler. So tread carefully, literally.

I used to have lots of friends that were members here and I would visit this venue often.  This can be a fun place with its Asian theme and lots of nooks and crannies to hide away in.  They have some nice wooden carvings of naked ladies in here that are cool.  This place is alright but there are certainly better private clubs in NOLA.   As time passed most of the people I know realized that they really didn't get a lot of value out of their memberships so they dropped out.  Personally I prefer being on the ground floor for shows at House of Blues and I really don't like being stuck up in the balcony area.

Definitely a Nashville institution, and everyone who comes to town wants to go there. Me? I just don't get it. 

There are plenty of pancakes to choose from. I've tried several different varieties and never finished a whole plate...the coffee is pretty poor considering Fido is just down the street. Bacon last time I was there was a little too crisp (i.e., burnt). Oh, and I've always had a pretty inattentive waitress.

The line? Seriously, the food inside is not worth waiting for. Go once (when there's no line!) just to say you've been.
Not the original on the strip in Pittsburgh but I still can not pass up stopping. Bread is different, but slaw is still good. Love Primanti's!
Aside from having a private party room I see little reason to go there.  The food's just okay.  I've had better.
Great portions, affordable prices, and a friendly staff. Highly recommend to anyone dining in Fishers.
Daves is awesome you can't go wrong with anything you get always ask for the secret menu specials when you go!

This place is soooo good. I've been here several times and it doesn't disappoint. Today I tried something new and got the blackened shrimp pasta and added provel cheese. This is the only place in the city I know of where you can try provel cheese. It is a cheese that is local to St. Louis and it is a must try! They put the cheese on just about everything you can imagine, and I had it on the garlic bread, the char grilled oysters, and on the pasta. The service was good, and the happy hour specials made me happy! $4 well drinks made this trip even better. We were here celebrating an in court victory, and the ambiance was perfect! Dont expect a quiet dinner, but expect an amazing experience. I would recommend this place to to anyone wanting to have a casual meal.

Absolutely amazing dinner tonight!  Came here tonight with my son. Came because all the great yelp reviews.  Sashimi was tasty .  The Black widow was a winner.  The press box spicy tuna on crispy rice was really fresh. The service was 5 stars and the fish was fresh and tasty.  The presentation of all the rolls was very artistic.  Easy parking.  I am from LA and consider myself a sushi expert.  I will definitely come back every time I am here in Santa Barbara. I would give 10 stars!

....meh....

 my husband and I are big sushi eaters, so we're always looking for awesome places in town. I saw all the wonderful reviews for this place - so we decided to go. 

Quaint little place- very clean. Got our drink orders and brought us some edamame. It was kinda slimy....

I had read the reviews about the self serve miso station, so I asked if I could get some. She said no, she would get it for me. I also saw her shew another patron away as he was attempting to serve himself.  So I'm not sure if that is still their policy.  

We ordered the 9 piece sashimi plate and a few rolls. Sashimi came out first. Salmon slimy, but tasted good, the tuna tasted a bit like a fish tank smells, and the 3rd fish.... (albacore?) Had no flavor. 

The rolls we got, however, were quite good. Solid flavor, and well put together rolls. We had the Fireball, Happy Roll, spicy tuna roll, and the Eskimo roll. The only complaint I had about them was they were pretty small for the price, and had the smallest amount of fish the could use. Best roll we got was the fireball.

Who knows... maybe we caught them on a bad night, but I don't think we'll be making a point to go again.

The only reasons why this is not a one-star review is because of their prices and the cool JFK artwork in the main dining room. 

Nothing here stood out as even average. Service was extremely slow and short. It seemed like customers were bothersome to the employees. The beans were soggy and water-downed. The food had next-to-nothing flavor. One reviewer here is probably right in that it's probably microwaved. They use a clear and visible part of the restaurant as literally a storage closet. I don't know they do this, but they leave the bathroom doors open and you can have a view of the urinal and people doing their business in the men's bathroom. They don't know how to separate/split a check (see the photo for how they did it). 

You can see in my other reviews of the great options for Mexican food in South Tucson. Do not come to or expect authentic food at El Dorado. Avoid it.

We chose this place based on previous reviews but were disappointed with the food. Would not recommend this place. The cost seems excessive for the items purchased.  We spent about $30 for one pizza steak, french fries, boneless wings and mozzarella sticks.
Not crazy about this place. The staff was VERY friendly, food presentation was gorgeous, but the flavor was lacking!!! The chicken was chewy and the chips were stale. HOWEVER, their CHURROS AMAZING!

Having been to Parlor with my daughter 2 more times since my original review, I have to maintain the 5 star rating!!!  Our latest visit was 5/29/15.  My daughter gets sick immediately with trace gluten and has eaten at Parlor successfully 3 times now.  Only tip is to order the pizza when you sit down because it takes longer than the wood fired oven pizza.

The staff has been incredibly knowledgeable about gluten free needs and confirms when bringing out the food that it is gluten free.
All of the pizzas can be made gluten free as can all of the pastas. He chef's wife has celiac disease so he knows the ins and outs of cross contamination.

My daughter maintains this is the BEST gluten free pizza she has ever had.

Owner Rob Wasserman personally informs the wait staff of the gluten free need and everything has been perfect!  

The gluten containing food is excellent as well, by the way, but to have such yummy GF food in our area is a literal quality of life improvement for our famil you!   We may even go back for a second night in a row!

had breakfast  Sunday morning eggs scrapple coffee toast wife had egg and scrabble sandwich all good will come here again for sure new and clean good fast service going to try dinner soon check it out you will like it

Tried it for lunch on a Monday afternoon. The updates to the restaurant are nice. Service was not great. No direction as to seat yourself or wait for hostess. Finally someone just said "take that booth" service was slow and not at all personable. they were busy but not overly crowded. Menu wasn't what we were expecting, learned later they're more about breakfast. We got an app that was supposed to be hot but was room temp. I got a meatball sub that was pretty forgettable. Didn't seem like there was a person assigned to assist us, just different woman stopping for different tasks and running off. Again, no idea who to pay, at the table or counter. Will try them for breakfast some time just to see if lunch just isn't the right time to visit.

I LOVE this place!  I've only eaten in the restaurant once and the service was friendly and efficient.  I order take-out once a week faithfully.  Everything is fresh and satisfying - and very spicy.  I appreciate having a vegetarian restaurant in the neighborhood, and it even satisfies my carnivorous husband!

What can you say? The food is authentic, delicious, and filling?  All true.   The lamb is some of the best in the city.   The chicken mendi is all that is good about a chicken dish.   Rice is perfect.  

Try it all.  I have and you will enjoy it.

The food was very good and tasted so fresh!!! I ordered vegan spring rolls and cheese wontons! We also ordered Grilled beef with steamed rice and Thai fried rice( we were so hungry that I forgot to take a photo!)I love how they have a lot of options too!  the cleanliness of the place  definitely a big plus!!!

Enjoyed a great dinner with my family this Sunday.  
Husband and I had the Turkey dinner.  Delicious. 
Drinks-- Philly Sour and Thyme were both very good.  
Kids had burgers and toasted cheese with tomato soup.  Everyone enjoyed their choice.  
Would definitely return. 
Great atmosphere as well.

I love this place! The decor is modern and sophisticated in a very cool way. I've dined here twice and was impressed both times. The duck fat olives were just okay but my hubby loved them. The brussel sprouts were  crisp and yummy. The Wagyu filet cuts like butter. The most tasty, tender filet ever! The black spaghetti was phenomenal! It was a little slim on the lobster but had the perfect amount of spice. A friend had the risotto with beef shank that was mouth watering. To top things off, the dessert was crazy good. We had the strawberry rhubarb cobbler topped with buttermilk ice cream. The server was friendly and efficient.

Delicious calzones, friendly service & great atmosphere. New hot spot in The Grove STL next to UCBC. Wife and I went for Valentine's Day (because I was craving pizza which they don't have hence their name) and have no complaints. And like most restaurants in STL, the craft beer floweth...
Saw this place on food channel and decided to try out.  Their Veal and Mussels were SO GOOD!...down side was they didn't take credit card...CASH only...but they do have ATM inside...lol

This place was so good that we made sure to come back a second time during our 4 day trip in Nashville!  The service was VERY slow the first time but it was because they were short on help that night. During our next visit the service was great. Their amazing talent of fusing Indian spices with Chinese dishes left us wanting more!!  And the staff were very friendly and accommodating with adjusting one of the dishes for me. We were surprised to learn that this restaurant is a franchise and that there's one fairly close to where we live in Virginia. We plan to try that one too and I'm hoping that it's as good as this Nashville one. If you love Asian food you won't be disappointed with this Inchins!!

I've been here a lot of times already since i live pretty close by. I've tried most of the tacos. My favorite is the Al Pastor, one of the best I've had. The restaurant is pretty small so sometimes i would get take out if there aren't that many seats available. This place isn't the best but it's definitely in my top ten.

The best 'hole in the wall' places keep it simple and do a few things well - this guy does exactly that.  There's not a lot about bibimbap to screw up, and a lot of it hinges on fresh crisp vegetables and your gochujang/kochujang.  This guy makes a bangin' gochujang and everything is done exactly how it should be.  I had a chicken bibimbap, but the protein you pick really doesn't impact the dish very much, honestly.

It's not particularly traditional, but it does have the basic spirit of bibimbap:  take a bunch of leftover vegetables and turn it into something new.  Mine had fresh broccoli, carrots, cucumbers and sprouts - none of them seemed to be dressed or pickled.  Honestly, no flavor was lost by that - the kochujang seasons it perfectly.

I'll certainly be back.

As average as any subpar bbq place. Nothing worth mention. Honestly. Everything drenched in sauce (which means your covering up something).  Fried chicken was decent-but how do you screw that up. Not a surprise this place always looks empty. Its the equivalent to a Hardees that serves bbq. What a wasted location.

I give it 4 stars, but I think some in my party weren't that impressed by our brunch. I ordered the deconstructed chicken/egg sandwich and really enjoyed this. One in our party really liked the Luke breakfast. 

Where they let us down was the burger, and maybe this is just the usual Jazz Fest season overcapacity issue this city suffers. The menu description sounded unique and appealing as was the actual presentation.  My fiancee ordered it medium, and the kitchen staff just couldn't deliver on this. It came out rare the first time, and slightly less rare after she sent it back.  I like rare, so I thought it was very tasty, albeit too rich for my delicate stomach . Other who ordered the burger thought it was ok, but not fantastic and also a bit rich.  (you may be tempted to judge us unsophisticated for ordering burgers at a Besh restaurant, but most of us have pretty developed palates and just crave a burger sometimes).  

The manager did apologize and offer us a free round and took this off the tab. Everybody who tasted the Bloody Mary's really enjoyed these and the Mary's are now my new favorite.

Well this is certainly one of the better Subways in the area.  Very nice and helpful staff, the dining area was glean and well kept.  I ordered my  usual roasted chicken sandwich topped with nearly everything under the sun.  But like I've written a few times before: Tucson's restaurant scene is just a little bit too great for ANY fast food spot to shine.  From fine dining to sandwich shops, as well as some of the greatest Mexican food in the world, there are just too many wonderful choices to warrant choosing to spend money on another small, bland meal from a billion dollar chain restaurant with nothing special to offer.  
I don't know that I'll ever Visit another Subway if I can help it.  And this was one of my best experiences eating at one.

This was really disappointing, normally diner food is really enjoyable and one of the people in our group had eaten here before. I ordered a breakfast sandwich, which we had to wait for because the kitchen gave away the first one and tried to give the second one away until our waitress caught it. 

My sandwich was okay, but I did notice the bread had mold on it which we quietly brought to our server's attention. She was very apologetic and brought it to the kitchen. She then came back out and explained the chef said it was from cutting spinach for the Eggs Florentine we had ordered. The spot was no where near where the bread had been sliced, and the color was more blue than green. It took a brief discussion with our server to have the sandwich removed from the check. So they're either cross contaminating the knives they're using or they're trying to serve their customers mold. We also never received the grits we ordered which they removed with no issue. 

Jessica the waitress was very apologetic the whole time, and very sweet. The kitchen staff should be ashamed.

The food is good, but the service is terrible. We've gone at least three times and left before ordering because of the lack of attention. The most recent (8/7/14). Went in around 6. One person sitting at bar talking to bartender, who saw us come in. Didn't see others in the dining room. Waited over five mins for someone to greet us or at least be acknowledged by the bartender. Finally decided to leave. Other times we have been seated at a table without a server to take our drink order or never return to take our meal order.

Vincents is consistent in its high quality and large servings at moderate prices. They do not deliver and there is a steady stream of takeout customers. It is basically a well patronized neighborhood spot that earns its special place in the community. It succeeds and has succeeded for years despite being closed on Sundays and not offering delivery. You can pay with a credit card but tips are to be in cash.
Beautiful restaurant with giant aquarium you can sit right next to! Our server was great, so helpful. You should try the papa's dessert, very tasty. Definitely recommend!
My husband keeps taking our kids here. They seem to really like the place, and they're tough customers. Whatever they're doing, they're doing it right!

Honestly, I was a little sketched out the first time I went to Alderto's since the building is an old-ass Taco Time (I feel like anything that starts with Taco Time ends in tears) but I persevered and boy-howdy was it worth it. The cashier was friendly and helpful and once we ordered we went and caught an open booth. We both got shrimp burritos and since they were so cost effective we figured they would be small so we decided to split a super nachos. Mistake. Big mistake. The shrimp burritos were huge and tasty - two of my favorite things. The rice was well flavored and was chock full of shrimp, bell peppers and onions. Honestly, they were good enough to change your religion over. The nachos were really good, too. Thick chips that had just the right crunch. Real cheese too - not that fake, soupy crap. There is a salsa bar your abuela would be proud of and a delicious mix of pickled carrots, onions and jalapeños. This place is the real deal and make no mistake, Alderto's and I will meet again. Soon. Also, as a side note, we finished all of it. I'm a lot of things, a quitter isn't one of them.
Decent Korean barbeque, but subpar cold buckwheat noodles to go with it. Couple notches below what you can get in Atlanta.
Very good food!!! Service a little slow though... but overall, good place for nice Indian food!
I wish I could give it 3.5 stars, it has decent food, though I prefer the sports bar side. They have excellent "boneless wings" and a good drink selection.

Great place for a quick burger.  I like the quick seating, upbeat atmosphere & menu.

My favorite is the turkey burger with sirachi sauce & bottomless sweet potato fries :)

The appetizers are very good & decent prices for the value.

Will return :). RED ROBIN lol....sticks in my head
It took me ages to actually eat here.  It always seemed just a bit pretentious.  Once we got around to trying it we were very happily surprised.  Very good food, good atmosphere, good time.

Day/Time of visit: weekday lunch
Atmosphere: casual

When our group of 4 sat down the waitress immediately plopped down soup (rice and chicken) and a small communal plate with 4 spring rolls and sauce. Someone said 'we didn't order these' and the waitress responded 'you get these with the lunch specials'. Then she walked away and came back a few minutes later to take our drink and food orders. There were no side plates on the table so it was very awkward considering the people in our party didn't really know each other. The soup was not very good and the spring rolls were the typical frozen variety that warehouse clubs sell. 

I ordered Pad Thai with shrimp. I received a huge plate of very greasy noodles with 4 shrimp. The dish seemed to be missing many of the key ingredients in Pad Thai - fresh bean sprouts, chopped peanuts, and a lime wedge. Perhaps there were some sprouts and peanuts, but so few that they seemed nonexistent. The flavor was very bland - couldn't taste any fish sauce - very disappointing. The Thai iced tea was good, a little heavy on the sweet side, but good.

May try again and order something different because several people have recommended.

Group after Work got there last . Great atmosphere on game day I think. Good after work place if you like in tampa area. Servers busy don't see them after initial food delivery. She was ok but could have more personality. Good happy hour I would bring the family to this place

Holy Hot Fudge. Seriously, if there is a heaven...bowls of ice cream topped with The Fountain's hot fudge will be there. 

My dad and his girlfriend came to STL to visit this weekend. After a day of zoo and vising the loop, we all wanted something sweet. Instead of Ted Drews, I decided to take them to The Fountain. So glad i did. 

The Zanzibar chocolate is the most delish chocolate ice cream ever, but the hot fudge. oh god, the hot fudge. please go try it immediately. Even my dad said it was the best he has ever eaten...and he is hard to impress!

 Can't wait to go back, many many times!!!

The fare here is pretty run of the mill grub, and there is nothing wrong with that.  It's more of a place to gather en masse for televised events or to indulge in any number of their fun drink specials.  It tends to be a bit on the loud side and, without extraordinary food or drink to compel me, it's just not a great venue for what I'm usually looking for.  

What I do like about Fox is the hot honey wings.  They're scrumptious!!  Fox has also been above average for me on the carryout front.  The staff is always smiley and pretty efficient when I stop in to grab an order of these wings to go when the crave hits.  So, although this may not be the best dine-in experience, in my humble opinion, they keep me coming back with their friendly attitudes and crave-able hot honey wings!

Bad food in a city full of great food. We were starving and our travel friend forced us in here. By the time I read the yelp reviews it was too late. This food was nasty and over priced.

Avoid if you can!

I've been here twice - once in the early evening when we needed a quick bite to eat before a movie, and the other late at night on a weekend for a relaxing couple of drinks with friends.

For the first meal, I had the crawfish mac and cheese while my boyfriend had a pulled pork slider. The mac and cheese was served in a skillet - definitely a shareable appetizer, or in my case plenty for an entree. It was well seasoned, with the crawfish being flavorful, but not doused in spice, which I appreciated. The pulled pork slider was great - I prefer sauce to a dry rub, and the bbq sauce on this was delicious. He also had a very large portion. We each also had a beer, and the happy hour price was fair. By the time we left, the live music was still setting up, so we didn't get to see anyone perform.

The second time we went there, was for drinks and some snacks late at night. There was a late night menu, with a good number of options to choose from. I don't remember what other people got, but I remember ordering a side of hush puppies. They were so good, they reminded me of the ones I had in North Carolina. Crispy and fried, but not too dry on the inside. The sauces were also very flavorful. 

As a side, a few of my friends ordered the flights of bourbon - each had only great things to say, and it was especially nice that the server explained each one in detail, and the recommended order in which to drink them.

Bummed that I haven't made it back for any live music nights - they happen pretty frequently!

Great little french cafe and breakfast spot.  I have ordered the Brouillade and the eggs provencale.  Both really good dishes.  You won't be disappointed with this choice in breakfast.

The pastries are excellent, and I suggest getting a croissant with your meal, as it is a bread choice instead of toast.

I only give this 4 stars, because the location is not the best.  I would like to see this restaurant move to a nicer location with a better outdoor seating option.  But the food is excellent.

So I was really excited to try this place, and before I start this review let me acknowledge that yes, I do realize that we chose to try this place out for the 1st tim on  Cinco de Mayo, and I probably could expect slower than usual service at a Mexican restaurant, but I also might counter that with it being Cinco de Mayo, that a popular Mexican restaurant should know enough to have proper staffing. And let me also point out, that of all of the many Mexican restaurants in the Fountain Square area, they were by far the least crowded that night. 

Okay so with that out-of-the-way, my wife and I walked in, walked through the front area, through the middle bar, to the back outdoor tiki bar area. And while it was crowded, as I would've expected it would be, there was no standing room only, or people waiting for tables, in fact we found an empty table almost immediately.  We were encouraged, but we probably should have listened to the couple next to us who told us they sure hope we weren't planning on eating there, because they had been there for an hour and were still waiting on their food.  We were approached almost immedietly by a server who took our drink orders.  That had to be a good sign, right!  Well, our drinks took about 20 mins..ok so it's Cinco de Mayo, no big deal.  We figured we had better get our food order in.  Pretty simple order, chips and questo, and two tacos each.  Nothing special.  After about 45 mins and no sign of even our chips, I walked up to bar in front area and ordered chips and queso and 2 more drinks.  He got that all for me in about 5 mins.  I asked him if I could order a couple of tacos and he told me the kitchen was closed.  I told him we placed our order about 45 mins ago and he assured me we would get our food and it was only  closed for new orders.  Took our drinks and chips and queso back outside to tiki bar and relaxed for a while.  

Another 45 mins later and still no food.  We grabbed our waitress and she said she would check.  She came back about 30 mins later and informed us that our order was the last one the kitchen had accepted but they dropped our ticket on the floor and never made our tacos and were now out of everything.  Two hours and no food.  We asked to speak to manager but he/she was not available.  To cap it all off she still charged us for the two drinks we had ordered almost 2 hours ago.  I see that this place is highly reviewed by most for the food, but I doubt we will go back, and if they dont fix their service and management issues, I doubt this place will be around for very long!

This restaurant hit all my marks for 5 stars. The flavor of the food was excellent and you can always tell when the food is fresh. Whatever the seasoning on the breakfast potatoes is I could have ate nine servings.And I don't know how the heck they get their pancakes so fluffy but it was like eating 2 little clouds with chocolate chips in them. One of the friends that I was dining with had glutten-free needs and the server was very helpful with pointing out exactly what items were available and everything was cooked as it should be. Not to mention tasty as all get out. Our server was both friendly and efficient. We went on a Sunday morning and there was a bit of wait but that's just a testament to how good the food is. I'll definitely be going back in the near future.

Worth the cable car ride! Monte Cristo is amazing..only complaint it that we were rushed to order (so busy) that we forgot our drinks and fries..we just got back on line! Cinnamon Sugar donut is light and so tasty!

I really don't like being told that the chef changed how something is made months ago and that I have been eating buttermilk for who knows how long.  That is not cool.  All of the seitan dishes were either removed from the menu or they were changed to include animal junk.  Basically this place has gone from being awesome to just another burrito shop for the vegan community.  Boo!

This is where the cool kids hang and there's reasons for it. The beer and the food! Tons of vegetarian and even vegan options.
I'm not either but I do love that black bean burger and the salads are to die for.
The staff is great and always sweet and accommodating. 
The place is usually filled with great art and an eccentric lot of people. I gave this place five stars because I would be lying if I said I didn't love this place. It's my vibe.
It can be yours also.
Yup! Just referred to myself as a cool kid.:D
The Mama's really good spaghetti and meatballs pasta was not "Really Good." Hardly any sauce, and the sauce was really boring.

I parked right in front of the restaurant and a staff person came out and yelled at me for parking then berated me about how long I was going to be there. My son attends music next door and I had planned on catching a solo bite to eat at Mythos while he had his lesson. Instead the utter rudeness of the Mythos staff completely turned me off of dinning there. The Mythos staff missed turning the increase of visitors to the strip mall into an opportunity and created an unwelcome and angry vibe dissuading people from checking them out.

Good shrimp, quick service (which is a good thing because we order at the window, wait outside and it's cold)...I never get the sides. ..I'm all about the shrimp. .. but they do have Cole slaw/ french fries / macaroni  salad...my only complaint is the paying for cocktail sauce. .. That's just uncalled for...

Been coming here since I was 15. I'm now 27 and this place is hands down my favorite place to grab pizza. Love the slices but only when it's fresh, since they tend to have slices lay out there for a while. (Few hours?) They sell alcohol here too but very expensive compared to the rest of Philly. They are now open 24/7 so enjoy!

I am a big fan of Nico's for late night drunken noms! That being said, I was able to try the breakfast burrito as a sober individual and I gotta say, it was not as good as I remembered. The proportions were off and it just did not impress. I will be sticking to sloppy drunken nicos trips :)

Me and my girlfriend stayed there 12/28/13.  We awoke to find a mystery brown substance on the duvet about the size of a silver dollar .  WTF?!?!  Obviously the maid did not wash it, awesome.   Then we hear loud squawking coming from the hallway.   Mind you its about 8:00am on a Sunday.  Come to find out its the maid yelling about her crappy life to another co worker.  The squawking is perfect because we are both hungover.  This goes on for 20min.   My girl also finds peanuts by the tv stand and hair in the shower.  We complained to the front desk, but got no apology or "will take care of it" attitude.    I dont care about decor or modern furnishings if the room and staff are crap.  I have had cleaner, nicer, and more give a sh*& attitude from staff at a Holiday Inn.  

Take it from someone who travels A LOT,  find another hotel.

The grocery store is great for finding items you can't get at Publix, but the produce is hit or miss so I usually end up at a vegetable stand or a larger grocery store on my way home. The staff is friendly and helpful. 

The cafe is meh. The smoked tofu melt is great, but the vegan breakfast isn't so awesome. The tofu scramble could be much improved with some nutritional yeast, lemon juice, and spices.
I was looking for a delicious and filling Breakfast and this place was amazing the build your own Hash was on point wish we had one of these in LA
Try the southwest grabbagrain box - you'll love it!!! Very convenient parking too! Heading back soon.

Born and raised in Philly. Went to have a sandwich after a few drinks. Listen to the other reviews...yes customer service was whack. Cheesesteak was weak. Very dissapointed. I will give them 3 stars, but this is not a recommendation to say the least.

The staff was incredibly friendly and caring.  Although the menu was difficult to understand, they wanted to teach us so that we could better understand both what we wanted to eat as well as their culture.  On the menu, the pictures appear as if they are very small portions, but when the food arrives on your table, the portions are huge and very filling.

As a Greek-Cypriot I can tell you that the atmosphere and food is authentic.  I brought my grandma here for her birthday and the head chef came out and spoke with her, and gave us a free plate of desserts.  I will definitely be back.  What a gem.

So I usually hate Yelp reviews that rant about the service. Because, I honestly think that if you're a true food lover, you wouldn't give a rats behind about service. Really good food speaks for itself. And it you wanted to be a big baby and spoon feed, you would have went to your mama's place. So with that aside, let's talk about Germantown Pub.

Food isn't good. Everything I've had here has been frozen and reheated/refried. From the fries to the catfish to the chicken tenders. Nothing here is made fresh in-house. So expect things to be overseasoned and oversalted to cover up for lack of freshness. And let's not forget how dry the food usually is. Like your great aunt's cooch, this food hasn't been moist in ages. 

The real insult to injury was the service our group received tonight. Our group of 12 came here for trivia which is actually really fun. And we're not the standard a-holes that move from our original seats, make tons of modifications to the menu and confuse our server. 

So, I was pretty freaking shocked when the server asked me what "number you were" like I was cattle or standing in line at the DMV when I tried to order another beer. When I asked her to clarify, she stated "I gave you a number when you sat down." Um no, you didn't because I would have actually asked you what you mean by number. I've worked in to service industry before so I understand large groups may be difficult but ultimately it's your JOB to remember who orders what. Blaming the customer for your lack of memorization makes the experience uncomfortable for everyone involved. She also claimed my friend's food would "be here in a moment" then 20 minutes later came back and accused him of never ordering it in the first place. Like seriously, we all heard him order it and then heard you confirm his order...twice. She also told me "don't get the Thai sauce on the chicken tenders...it's terrible." so I went with plain chicken tenders and just honey mustard on the side. But guess who ends up with the terrible Thai sauce on her chicken tenders, this girl. But I didn't even bother to send it back and ate my dry Thai sauced chicken tenders anyways because you can tell when things just weren't going ever be rectified. Also, not to the server's fault but due poor planning, ALL BUT ONE of the happy hour draft beers was available going into the 1st hour of trivia. Like, you guys didn't realize that as a bar on an event night you may want to have more beer available?

Short summary is, come here for the trivia and good company. Expect the happy hour beer to run out. Avoid the long red-headed server. And eat dinner elsewhere beforehand.
Some of the best food I have ever eaten. Extremely flavorful. Everything was perfect. Definitely try the fried mac and cheese with bacon and gator gumbo.

Good little mom and pop breakfast place. The food is really good. The price is good and the staff is friendly. Only reason why I'm giving it 4 stars is because it's a small restaurant and gets busy really easily.

I hadn't been there in a few years but nothing has changed much in terms of the quality of the food and service . The food was delicious and the service was fast . I ate the chicken slouvaki pita sandwich and it was really good. A little messy to eat but worth it. The prices are reasonable and there is choice for everyone. They do have daily specials. I will definitely be back .

Well, it has been almost exactly a year since we first tried Johnny G's and after a long day of yardwork today, we decided take-out was on the menu.  We didn't feel like having our normal pizza or cheesesteak delivery, so we settled on Johnny G's because, well, to be perfectly honest, they have ribs!

The online ordering at GrubHub makes it so easy.  We ordered a feast!  Hubs had 1/2 a rack of ribs, potato salad, two meatballs and a house salad with blue cheese dressing.  I had the chicken parm entree which came with linguine and sauce and garlic bread.  

I am going to go out on a limb here and say this was the best chicken parm I have ever had.  The pasta and chicken were cooked perfectly and the tomato sauce tasted homemade, albeit  a tiny bit sweet.  Hubs loved his ribs, they came right off the bone and the sauce was delicious.  The potato salad was excellent and the meatballs were pretty good too.  

Everything was hot and fresh, and even came before the estimated time of delivery.  The driver was very pleasant and efficient. We couldn't have asked for anything more!

We will definitely be ordering from Johnny G's in the future!

Oh, and btw, others have said they are disappointed they don't have cheese fries or onion rings - the delivery guy said they are changing the menu and will be adding more fried items once they get their new, bigger fryer.

This cafe has location going for it, but to the food, I say "meh". Tasted more pre-packaged than fresh. The shrimp po'boy, crawfish pie, gumbo and jambalaya were all disappointing. Very noisy. With all the great places to eat in the city, skip this one.

Randomly stumbled upon this spot while we were visiting SB. When we first walked in...  It looked extremely small and we were so close to leaving.  Walked a little further and there's additional tables in the room next door. So we decided to give it a try. 

We were contemplating to try their Torta Cubana or just stick with our usual carne asada burrito.  So glad we chose to try their torta.  Their bread was crispy and not soggy, their marinated pork was packed with flavors and had a bit of crunch,  it also had beans, cheese, ham and avocado. You must try it with their spicy green  sauce from the salsa bar. Also tried their chicken sope and it was pretty good to our liking.  

At the salsa bar..   We first thought that they mixed up their signs between the medium &  spicy.  Medium was the red sauce &  spicy was the green.  A must try. 

The only con is that they didnt sell chips &  guacamole.

Each course was carefully planned out just as you would expect in a traditional kaiseke Japanese style meal.  The ingredients were all fresh and many of them imported from Japan.  The staff is all top notch, exactly what you would expect from staff in Japan.  Each dish was brought out on a timely basis.  The 7 course meal is large, and I recommend you come in on an empty stomach to be able to get through all of the courses.  This is an excellent date spot or some place to celebrate a special occasion with a food lover who is adventurous enough to try new flavors. Everything was executed 5 stars.  Thanks for a great experience!
Glasses smelled bad. Food was not very appetizing. Seemed like friendly and responsive staff but food standard and hygiene needs to improve.

This place is actually now located on High Street, right in the middle of the historic section of Burlington by the Riverline station.  Because my home and business are directly across the street, their pizza is very much a go-to for my husband and I.  Its only about $10 for a large plain pie, and especially considering the price its a great deal.  This place has a lot of loyal fans, who dine their mostly with their families once a week.  I can't say much for dining in as I haven't ever (living across the street it seems silly), but my watch out for pizza or takeout otherwise is to mind the time.  They close at 9 pm most nights and on some nights, earlier, like a lot of businesses on High Street.  Overall a great value!

This place sucks, everyone that works there does not give a crap about what they were hired to do. I have done nothing but wait for service in this place while the staff are busy chatting away, the lanes malfunction, food is horrible. It's really sad how much this place has declined over the years, i will never go bowling here again.

Their gumbo Ya Ya is excellent. I have been going to this place for years and just love it. At lunch time they have $1.50 bloody marys and they are the BEST bloody Marys I have ever had. The service is great, the gumbo Ya Ya is a glorious rich dark gumbo. I have had the burgers, the BBQ shrimp, the fried catfish fingers, the oysters and the veal meatballs. If I lived in New Orleans I would eat at Mr. B's at least once a week. Every dish I have had there I loved but I am completely in love with the Gumbo Ya Ya! I highly recommend it if you like a dark roux. Mr. B's is awesome!

After hearing so much about the amazing food and "that sandwich" with all the stuff piled high I had to sink my teeth into it!

I went on a Wednesday and the drinks were half off which was GREAT!!! The waiter and the other staff I came in contact with were really nice! I had a bad day so their attentiveness was just what the doctor ordered! 

The place is new so it was clean. I usually check out bathrooms but didn't on this visit because I was alone and had just went shopping so all my bags were with me. 

Now. I had the fish sandwich and i got it in the traditional style with the fries and slaw on top. I was hoping for a creamy slaw since I had fish but it was a vinegar slaw. I wasn't really feeling it. The sandwich was HUGE by the way. I asked for some tartar sauce and at first they couldn't locate any (new business) but they came around. I ended up taking the remainder of the fish off the sandwich. It was just too much to eat! 

I think if I go back I would not order the fish again. When I got back to my hotel I got so sick. I kept (tmi sorry) burping up fish. I dint drink much so I know it wasn't from booze.

As pizza goes it is just your basic run of the mill pizza place. 
It is fine for the basics. 
Fries are always soggy
The Stromboli is surprisingly good. Add ricotta for a nice calzone. 
It is probably the best pizza in the general area.

We went here on out very last day in NOLA it wasn't too crowded when we arrived so that's a good thing. The service was nice and quick and the food was delicious! They had different mimosas. I believe I had the mango mimosa( it was really really good) and the pancakes were super light and fluffy. This hidden little gem is worth it! Make the trip

I have debated posting this review since Mother's Day ( month ago). I want to be fair, but gnawing at my gut is the overall poor food experience I had there. 

Of course I wanted something special for my mother on this day, so I gathered my siblings and their families and selected 3 places to attempt to get reservations. One was at the William Penn Inn, the other Route 6. I scoured the reviews and menus and decided Square 1682 was the best option. 

Square was super accommodating  with my large party of 12 and the customer service was outstanding. I canceled the reservation with the two other places and banked on Square delivering a great day. That was a mistake. 

Positive: The manager, staff, hostess, waitresses were super sweet. 

The mimosas were the best think i consumed that dining experience

Two  items were comped
 
Con's:
Two of our orders were mixed up ( another waitress took the ticket), so 10 of us ate while two of us watched. The late food arrived about 15 mins later. 

The prime rib sandwich was skimpy, grossly over cooked, and barely edible. I have had a LOT of prime rib in my life, this was thin and crunchy. It was served with a tiny bit of sauce on a firm fancy roll. My mother ordered the same and the disappointment on her face was awful. The others at the table had a variety of underwhelming dishes. No one was satisfied, but everyone was polite. I was crushed. 

There were a total of 5 mothers in that bunch and there was absolutely nothing special about it.  It was a nice room, the staff was nice, but it was one of the WORST dining experiences I have had in Philly.

I REALLY regret booking this place. We spent hundreds of dollars and everyone left a little quiet and disappointed. As a matter of fact my mother later confided she was STARVING after we left.
