Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" (roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausage) is my absolute favorite meal in New Orleans. Also their jalapeno cheesy grits is the best in town. No one makes it like them.

The only positive about this franchise location is how new it is. The food, while still pretty good, was not up to the standard we have become accustom to at other Red Robin restaurants. While we were seated relatively quickly that was where the service ended. We were ready for drink refills while waiting for our waitress to return to take our food order... For some strange reason the wait staff at this location does not clear the table as food and drink is finished. Instead they leave everything on the table until after you leave when a busboy clears everything. It was a little challenging to keep young children entertained with a massive pile of dishes and glasses in the middle of the table.

It might be good,  but I'll never know...

I just walked in to this restaurant and almost immediately walked out. As I walked in I was greeted by two people. The first was the bartender who appeared to be very nice. The other was an older gentleman with a bad perm and gold glasses.

I indicated that it was just me. The gentleman looked at the bartender,  paused and let out an audible sigh. He just stood and looked at her as if to say, "what am I supposed to do with this?" She encouraged him to seat me and he shrugged. I just walked out. I certainly don't want or need to be somewhere that it's clear I'm not welcome.

I certainly won't be back.
Well priced, good sushi. Intimate atmosphere with a nice/casual feel.i could see it being loud in there at full capacity. Had a large sake for 2, beer, 4 sushi rolls and a side of rice for $60.
Every time I come here I could just keep eating. All the food is delicious and true to Indian flavors. The staff is very attentive and friendly. My one and only place to eat Indian food!

Visited for restaurant week with my boyfriend... As others have said, the location was strange and kind of unfortunate.  The building is mainly a design complex for home decor.  We followed signs throughout the building leading us up to the 4th floor.  We were greeted by an incredibly friendly waitress who took our coats and introduced us to the French chef and owner.  She then led us through a cozy seating area to the far dining room overlooking the Schuylkill River and 30th St Station.  The chrome wall behind the bar reflected the reds and blues of the neon sign and logo in the window giving off a modern vibe.  

We had chosen it for the restaurant week menu which we'd read online... we ordered some cocktails and double checked our choices from the menu.  An added first course was brought out to us- truffle mushroom soup.  Neither of us actually like mushrooms much, but both enjoyed the light, creamy soup quite a bit.  His appetizer of lobster stuffed calamari was a bit tough, though he easily ate it all anyway. My  eggplant dish was phenomenal.  For the main course, the bf had chicken and I chose striped bass.  We each loved our own dish and liked the other's.  Our desserts were creme brulee (fantastic, I thought, though the boy would've preferred it slightly warmer) and an apple pie tart (quite good I thought, the boy loved).  

Overall, it was a great choice.  We would never have found it if not for restaurant week, and we'd definitely go back in the future.  Service was friendly and prompt, food was fantastic, and view was gorgeous.

Small but very cozy little spot. My co-worker and I stopped by here for lunch on a business trip and were starving. I ordered a cup of seasonal bisque soup with a salad and the lobster tacos. Excellent choice. Lots of flavor and delicious. It helped that we were starving too. I would have tried everything on the menu. It was windy when we went and a bit too cold for people to sit outside, so we sat at one of the exterior tables/counters overlooking the wharf. Great good and great atmosphere...would be happy to come back again if and when I'm back in the area.
This is our favorite restaurant now. Great food and service! The triple vegetable dish was too salty, but so delicious. Will definitely go back. Highly recommended!

A hidden little gem. If you're looking for an authentic NOLA foodie experience come here. Everything we ordered was delicious. Waitstaff were all sweet and accommodating. Just straight up delicious food. Quality is on point.

Once again I have finally stopped into a place in my own neighborhood that I've been passing for years.

An old converted train station, Woodbury Station Cafe's several dining rooms have an odd sort of divided layout.  Still, I'd describe the atmosphere as cozy rather than cramped.  The photos of historical Woodbury that cover the walls are a nice touch, but the plastic tablecloths depicting old 1920s newspaper ads are a little corny.

The menu, though, is anything but corny.  I was surprised to find a place in my own backyard that featured housemade beignets and chicory coffee.  Soon after sitting down, our friendly server brought us a sample plate of homemade biscuits topped with creamy, flavorful cream chipped beef.  My husband went on to order the full cream chipped beef platter for breakfast, which came served over fresh white toast and with crispy, oniony potato cakes.  I went with crepes, which were served paper thin and filled with perfectly tender-crisp asparagus, mushrooms and feta cheese.  My potatoes were more traditional diner hashbrown, but with tiny flecks of crispy bacon throughout and served with my choice of either redeye or sawmill gravy.  I chose both.

Throughout our breakfast, my coffee cup remained full and our server stopped by a number of times to see if there was anything we needed.      I was too full to indulge in the beignets she suggested at the end of our meal, but will definitely be back again to try the doughy fried puffs.  And maybe the brioche French toast.  Or the homemade waffles.  Or the eggs Benedict served on a bialy... Mmmmm... Like I said, I will DEFINITELY be back.

Ate lunch and had the special Red Snapper and we ordered fried Oysters as an appetizier (ordered kids Oysters since they don't have them as appetizer).    The oysters were great and typical of fresh NOLA restaurants.  The special was fried snapper but I got it blackened and the fish was very good although the cream lobster sauce was overpowering.  Good thing I got it on the side cause after one bite I didn't eat anymore.  Overall the place is somewhat a hole in the wall but with good food.  I'm not a fan of fried seafood but would visit again just to try the Oyster Po Boy after having the fried oysters initially.

Definitely one of my favorite Chinese places in the city. I have been going for many years and it's never disappointed. 

Something not to miss are the soups for two - there are multiple interesting and delicious options. The duck soup is great as well as the chicken and vegetables. They are rich and satisfying. 

I usually always get the same entree because it is so tasty - beef with black bean sauce and pan fried noodles. The beef and chinese greens are done perfectly and the egg noodles are buttery and satisfying. One order is enough for at least two and possibly three meals, depending on how hungry you are, so be prepped for leftovers.

It's BYOB and inexpensive. Gets very crowded on weekend eveningsl. So worth it!

Some times things just work. The wildflower is one of those places in time that just works. Leslie one of the two owners met me like an old friend at the door Cathy my waitress made a wonderful suggestion for lunch that was on the regular menu bit not the days special.    I had the roast beef sandwich with tomato jam Lettuce and a special dressing on home made bread.   The roast beef was perfect and tender. I am talking butter tender.  One look at it told the story. Only premium cut cow here.   I had an ice tea and an oatmeal cookie (also home made.   Oh they have a little market if you need things to go.  Clean tastefully decorated with a tree shaded porch.  Parking is good.   Hey I had never been there before today.   I will be back.    Sandwich with chips $11.00. A great deal with the heap of roast beef an attentive service
Normal ice cream - hot fudge was a bit too sweet and not warm on my sundae. Not enough seating space.
Horrible service.  Horribly managed.  Constantly out of something in the mornings.  Drive thru orders are often wrong.  Bad days can be expected anywhere but it's constant here.

This restaurant is absolutely horrendous. I went here with my family after exploring some of the cool historic sites Philly has to offer. This place was suggested after our plans to eat at the City Tavern had changed (they were not open). Upon arriving to the restaraunt, I immediately regretted it. The decor was a mix of gothic, antique and my grandma's house. It smelled so horribly of smoke, I may have contracted asthma. 

    We made our way up to the dining area on the second level. We were seated and waited about 10 minutes for a waitor or waitress to help us. When she finally made her way to our table she took our drink orders and returned shortly with our cokes. She spilt mine, apologized and then continued to clean the table - sticking her armpit in my face. This wouldn't be so bad if she wasn't wearing a skimpy strapless dress and didn't smell as though she had never heard of deodorant (talk about unappetizing).  

     We ordered our food; which included chicken parmesan, a steak burger and a grilled chicken sandwich. We waited AN HOUR or more for our food, during which I suggested plenty of times that we should leave. Also during which, a women who looked like the old witch from Snow White tried to strike up a conversation with my little sister and touched her/was very close to her and made her almost cry in fright (my sister is 9). Creepy. Just creepy. 

     When our food came, we were already having the worst dining experience we have EVER had. Spoiler alert: it didn't get better.
 
      My spaghetti in my chicken parm wasn't even drained and had no sauce!? When I asked for more, we were charged 75¢. My chicken was chewy and disgusting. Same goes for the grilled chicken sandwich. No one enjoyed their meals. Even the pop tasted gross which makes the fact that they charge full price for refills even worse! 
Our waitress was unattentive and made only three trips to our table. 
We paid our bill and RAN out of there. 

DO NOT EAT AT ROTTEN RALPH'S. THE NAME IS NOT CONTRADICTING, IT'S LITERAL. 

-56682838382628393 stars
Prices are too high and if you're not a "somebody" in the New Orleans area, the employees follow and watch your every move.

Food was good but service was poor. Apparently they ask that you order before you sit but when we walked in nobody was even present to greet us. We sat ourselves and it took nearly 15 mins for us to be waited on properly. Other patrons seemed to have this issue as well. My advice to management is to have it more clearly stated on how service is given at your restaurant and also have more attentive staff on hand.
Good Sunday brunch if you don't want the typical jersey diner food. Great atmosphere and service. Special coffees and hot chocolate.

They do have good pancakes and waffles. The prices are a little steep in my opinion, but because they are a chain you know what to expect because they basically are the same everywhere. I have never had problems with service here.

Staff was extremely friendly especially our waiter. I ordered the traditional with potatoes and my friend had ordered the Lucy omelette. Big portions. Everything was delicious. Would recommend this place for breakfast ! Also mimosas were delight too

Drinks, appetizers, dinner and dessert...impeccable. 

Service...impeccable.  Heather was lovely and very knowledgeable. 

Atmosphere...wonderful. 

Prices...very reasonable for all the above. 

Highly recommend!!!!!

I'm super sensitive about restaurant hygiene.  I can't stand sweaty bartenders/servers.  Bit my lady friend and I didn't touch our good and drinks and we had the food packed to go not to look rude.  They should wipe their faces with a towel and bit their hands that's about to handle my food and drinks.  This is like somebody spitting in your food pretty much. Gross!
The food is not making the review since we didn't even get to eat it.  I guess to be fair we're very picky with hygiene to where we'd like to see hair nets on everybody. But sweat dripping from a servers face is unacceptable .

The wait was really long, and it was freezing outside. They only had one heater going, which seemed like a mistake -- and it's entirely possible one of the folks I was waiting with is the one who ultimately turned it on. 

They were out of all but one kind of roll when we did get seated, the ones we had were fairly standard fare. I did love my food, as did my most charming date, but the place is small and cramped and not necessarily in a good way. The prices were kind of high considering serving size and my previous experience with Thai food elsewhere. (I'm used to two meals from one serving in these kinds of restaurants.)

Ultimately I'd come back, because the food really was good, but I'm not sure the value was really 1000% there.

There are a lot of options at Coventry if you've got the urge to feel mega-bloated and uber-satisfied after lunch. During work, I generally avoid mega-bloatation and uber-satisfaction, because they are both feelings that make me want to stop working and enjoy life.

However, I ordered the grilled cheese (provolone) with a tomato slice and rocked some parmesan pepper mashed potatoes on my virgin visit to this calor-ific yuppie feeding frenzy in the heart of Center City and, I must say, the yuppies might just know what's uppie.

The sandwich was not the soggy puddle of buttery cheesiness that I have come to expect from grilled cheese over the years. The bread was crisply toasted, the cheese was melted but not burned or pure liquid.

Somehow, it actually achieved standard grilled cheese satisfaction levels without making me nervous that I'd start feeling pain in my left arm and get light-headed moments after eating it.

The mashed potatoes (which, incidentally, are one of my top three favorite foods in the Milky Way) were awesome and left me sad that it was such a little cup-o-potatoes. 

Bring a few extra bucks for this place (and if you bring a rectangular piece of plastic, be sure to get in the line on the right, so as not to piss off the otherwise friendly Asian women who smilingly stand guard at the registers).

It's a good experience, and I've been told that the one pound baked potato is absolutely to eat for! So I'll probably be heading back for sloppy seconds, right after my next paycheck.

I wanted an above average sammich. What I got was an amazing one. I got the Kalua pork sandwich. The pork was perfectly seasoned and not dry at all. The bread was crispy and soft. Also, the server seems like he used to work at Trader Joe's! Super friendly and welcoming.

This is a cozy place and great for date nights. There is a parking lot across the street, which is convenient. Drinks were good and they have some interesting martini options. We enjoyed the complimentary bruschetta and the arancini. 

The saltimbocca was very good, but the chicken lemoncello was only good. Portions are generous. The service was very good, well above average for Delaware County. We had a nice time and hope to return soon.

The food is worth the wait. Legit charcoal grilled chicken with falafel in a delicious sauce topped with fruit that is the best combination of flavors.  Very fresh.  I will try to go again a bit earlier.
OMG this place defies the standards of fast food. Longer wait in the drive thru than in the lobby. If there was an option for negative stars this location would get it...

I have been here a few times with my family and my mom. We usually don't eat out Thai food because Im half Thai and my mothers cooking is amazing. I was pleasantly surprised that I loved the Chicken Panang. Normally when I have this at other Thai restaurants I don't really like it. At this place it's super flavorful and I can get it spicy like I like. The fried rice is not bad either but not the best. I'm personally not a fan of Pad Thai but my hubby said his was really good. One of my favorite things to drink is Thai Tea which theirs doesn't disappoint. The service is good and the price is reasonable. If you want good Thai food at a decent price then I recommend going here.

After  driving  by Honeygrow  countless  times,  I  finally  went here  for lunch today with a  friend.   I'm  giving   this place  four  stars  because my  salad  was so tasty  and a very nice young woman employee  came  over  to help me and my friend  order  with their  touch  screen system (   much more elaborate  than   WAWA).   AND  because they  offer   healthy food!!!! (  would be  great if there  were   as many Honeygrow  restaurants as  there are McDonalds in this  country) . The   interior  is nice and clean  and bright.  All good.  Here is  the not  so  good:  too chaotic   and VERY VERY NOISY! The  noise  level was  deafening  and  I could not   carry on a  conversation  with   my  friend.  Add to that, the  beat of  some kind of  music  below the  surface (WHY????).   Other patrons in  a  hurry  were pushing  us around (  rude).  I noticed the  assembly line of  workers  behind the  counter were not all pulling their  weight.  This  bothered  me ( some  were   working  so hard).   My last  grievance  was the  price. I bought a  Cesar  type  salad (  forget their name  for it) and added  breaded chicken.  Nothing to  drink and  the total  was $10.02 .   Too expensive.  For  $10, I  should  be eating left over  salad  for the next two meals.   But  this  is a restaurant   that is a giant  step in the  right  direction.  And I   made  sure to thank  the employee  who helped me  and my  friend.  Kindness  never goes out of style!

Extraordinarily average. Food is just "OK" and portions are small and pricey. Service is meh. Restaurant itself is beautiful, and it's not a bad place to grab a happy hour drink, but I wouldn't eat there again. Definitely not one of Jose Garces' better spots.
Worst sushi I've ever had. Worse than all you can eat sushi. The fish is gross, the rolls are terrible. They fall apart. It's not good sushi at all.

I have been platinum player for years there food is great customer service is good but gaming machines are a joke I have noticed in last couple months$200 lasts no less than 45 minutes and I was only playing$0.45 a hand I am seriously considering going to different Casinos I love going there for everything but this place is becoming corporate nightmare and it's far away from being what it used to be

Wanting to change up the Thursday routine, we decided to go bowling after dinner.

Headed here because its close to home, plus they had pay $6 and bowl all you want from 9-close (Mon-Thur, I believe).  So, there was a little bit of a line but it went pretty good. 

Overall, its a bowling alley.  Like most, its dark and a little old, but I don't think I would know what to do if a bowling alley was any other way.

I did have to wait a few times for the bartender to get back to the bar, but overall, it wasn't bad.  And why would I complain when I am paying $1.50 per drink?  

So, for two of us to bowl six games and have 3 beers each, it cost $25, tip included.  And we probably could have bowled more if my arm wasn't getting sore.  (Or if I hadn't been losing, but whatever).

Overall, it was a good deal and I will probably be back.

I love this place, it is definitely a staple in my restaurant reportoire.  My husband and I like to either dine in or get take out, both are great.  Even though you can bring your own beverages, they also carry some Indian beers.  I always get the garlic naan and veggie samosas and pretty much every entree is delicious.  The staff is also very pleasant.
Freaking delicious!!!! Go there! Delicious burgers and chilli fries so good. Kinda pricey but worth it

Before this Saturdays showing of Buddy Holly at the Muny 3 friends and I had reservations at Herbies.  We went there last year and I don't remember anything special except it was a bit pricy.   This time my guest and I ordered a tomato pasta special they had.  I had water to drink and he had a coke.  The pasta was fine, something I'd make at home.  It did give me a bad case of heart burn though.  The description of that special wasn't quite right.  Our bill was $71, tip it was $90.  Two bowls of pasta, 1 coke, $90.  The waiting staff was great.  I won't be back though, that's ridiculous.

This has been my family's go-to Chinese spot since I was a kid. In general I'm not the biggest fan of Asian cuisine in general but the basic stuff I like has always been better here than anywhere else I've been. While not always the quickest of orders (I'm guessing the food in general takes a bit to make), it's always hot and fresh when we do get it.  The chicken here is always flavorful and juicy, the beef is the same and every type of rice here is to die for. Definitely a place for everyone to check out.

Bananas Foster French Toast. Best french toast I've ever had. Not too sweet. I don't normally like ordering sweet dishes, but this was amazing and worth it! 

Shrimp & Grits. Super creamy grits. Delicious.
It's alright...pricey, needs remodeling.  I've had some great things and some mediocre things.  Not my first pick in the area.
Best donuts ever! Light fluffy,always fresh, fast and friendly service,  always!! If you love Apple Fritters like I do go early or they're gone!!!

As a 12 year Customer of the Inn and Restaurant and previous raving Five star supporter....I'm sad to say; the magic seems to be gone. Once upon a time I raved and bragged about the DK and to be sure I have many fond memories. It was my home away from home. I thought they cared for me as much as I did them. Now I see they are a business...I am a revenue source and I understand just how much Sam understood about the difference between pleasing a Customer for the night versus maintaining a loyal Patron for life. Twelve years was a great run though. Thanks for the memories.
Took 20 minutes to get their basic burger. Not worth $12 after tip. Decent atmosphere

All you can eat pizza! Need I say more. The pizza is average but the beer garden is really one of a kind in the area, and quite reasonable. 

We have had large groups here before and they are always very accommodating. It's media so parking can be a pain but the dedicated lot does really help.

My small pepperoni pizza was hot and fresh, right from the oven! Plenty of cheese and there was something quite tasty about the sauce! My only disappointment was that it didn't look like the picture of the pizza on the Yelp review. Mine had sliced pepperoni and it looks like crumbled/diced in the review. The price was right and the service was fast. I love supporting local businesses, so I'll be back!!

Best waitresses (shout outs to Rebecca and Tanya) ever!! I came here practically every week with my husband. I love the environment of being able to bring my laptop and working on whatever I wanted. We even got hugs, when we told them that we would be moving to San Diego. 

I still miss this place and trying to find a replacement for it here in SD. I always got the Kaldis iced tea, which is the best black tea I've ever had and a bagel or an omelet to eat. Sometimes, if I really needed it I'd grab a coffee or orange juice. 

Everything here is phenomenal. If you don't come here for breakfast or brunch when visiting St. Louis, you are missing out!!

My family and I love this place !!  the food is AMAZING!! The pizza is the best I've ever had ..& my favorite part is that they have options for my little guy. My little boy is on the autism spectrum so we have him on a special gluten free dairy free ect diet and they have options for him :-) he loves the pizza here he can eat the whole medium by himself . Definitely recommend this place for family's or for even a guys or girls night out for some pizza and beer !
Can't believe I waited for 1h30min for the dinner! Definitely not a delightful thanksgiving night
Not impressive at all, I ordered turkey hummus wraps, turned out that half of my wraps barely contained any turkey! Only green and hummus. What a surprise!

The service was great and the rolls were fresh and tasty...be sure to try the wasabi fries they are so addicting!....if you like spicy food the volcano roll is the way to go...the special roll the server recommended was also great....will return soon

The General's chicken was really amazing, as was the hot and sour soup. The 5 spice pork and chow mein were both misses, however. Both slightly flavorless and slimey. It also seemed slightly overpriced.
Paula our server was very pleasant and really nice.  All smiles all the time and very polite.  Ordered famous chicken wings and really tasty and delicious to the bone.

We made reservations for Sunday Brunch on October 18, 2015.  The service was impeccable and the food superb!    There were 4 adults in our party and each ordered a different entree.  We had their famous BBQ shrimp, Shrimp & Grits, Brisket and Chicken Pontalba.   We were very pleased with the quality of food and service!

I've been here a couple of times, and would definitely continue to come back.  It's a casual place with great pizza!  But if you're a picky eater, be careful because their pizza is "well done", meaning a crispy crust.  So if that's not your style you may not like it.  However, each time I go I enjoy myself, the service, and of course the fabulous pizza.  Each time I go the manager makes it a point to go to each table and check on everyone, which I love.  One time, he came over to our table and noticed the pizza was a little more well done than usual, and he offered to have our pizza be on the house, and he gave us a free $25 gift card to come back.  We weren't even complaining about the food at all!  Great customer service, definitely how you get customers to come back and share their experience with their friends.
Also, if it's nice out definitely sit outside on the patio!  It's a little more quiet than inside.

This place has the food you need for a Chinese dinner buffet. I am not Chinese food expert, but they seems to do the basics well enough. They had a slightly better than average salad bar selection as well. The rest seemed like like typical Chinese fare to me. The age-based pricing helps when you have a couple kids in tow. Also, these are good folks - I lost my wallet in there and called them the next day and they still had it.

So, my wife and I have been on a 3-week road trip and have traveled to/through FL-TX-OK-NM-AZ-MS-Co-Wy-AL and KS and have had some decent food but when our last stop came we did not expect to hit the jackpot!  Wow!  This place is small but HUGE on Flavor, variety and Customer Service!!!  Our waitress, Sara (with no H) was on point and by far the best waitress or waiter we've had, we never had to ask for refills, she was super fast with any requests we had and I need to tell you that this place was HOPPING so she was moving the whole time but made us feel like we were the only ones here!!  Bottom Line,...Food is fantastic, atmosphere is inviting with a small town warmth!  On a side note, all the staff was super friendly but be warned of Gina, she is LOUD but also super personable!  (And she said I should tell you all that she is "Amazing") Finally, we live in FL, ..... but we WILL be back!

I've had multiple dishes from Roberts, Steak sandwich, grouper pasta, the salad is amazing.. to say the least if you're looking for yummy home cooked meals this is the place to go. Very friendly staff!

My wife and I have visited twice, and another time with friends. While we like the food and beer choices, the service is inexcusably very slow. We visited on a Saturday afternoon around 5:00 and the place was only 1/3 full. Took a while for our server to greet us, arrived just when we were about to get up and leave. Ordered a beer for each of us and waited at least 10 minutes before I finally got up to ask the bartender about our drinks (after watching him not making any drinks for several minutes and serving a few others who just arrived at the bar). I could barely get the words out before he says they'll be right up. I sit back down, and he still doesn't pour them. We were about to leave again when another bartender made eye contact and she poured the drinks and brought them to us. While our waitress was friendly, she should have been checking on our drinks. Same slow experience with the other two visits, this time we are certain we will not be back.

As far as places to eat in Plant City go, having Wayback here definitely adds some variety. That being said, it's not the  greatest burger I've ever had. In addition, adding fries and a drink jacks up the price another 2 or 3 dollars. Not quite the price you're looking to pay for just ok food.

The fries are good. I ordered a milkshake on my most recent visit and it was ok. I'm not sure if it had real banana in it or banana syrup. It tasted rather fake. I thought I was ordering the advertised shake but I couldn't read the menu because I'm red-green colorblind.

So, ate here for breakfast one morning as it was close to the convention. 

I ordered the seafood omelet with croissant and grits. 

The omelet was descent, the croissant dry and bland, but the grits amazing. I recommend you eat the grits, and go for some eggs and bacon. I think i would go back.

Bellagio has proven time and time again to be the hands down best pizza joint in Nashville. Prices, amazing. Food, astounding. Service, extraordinary. Great hours, outdoor seating, speedy delivery, and lovely people. 

I recommend the spinach artichoke pizza, Italian Stromboli, and the fried mushrooms.

Coffee is decent, prices are alright for there coffee the food is way overpriced for the quality that you get. And they have a huge drive thru issue sometimes  you can't even drive down the road because people have blocked it waiting to order.

One of my favorite places to eat in Indy. Food is excellent -- best jambalaya in town, for sure -- and the staff's always friendly and eager to please. I always take friends from out of town when they visit.

My only complaint would be about the Styrofoam plates and plastic ware used in many of their locations. Real plates and silverware would be great, especially for the environment.

If this review were based solely on the waitstaff, and presentation it would get a five.  Our waiter was attentive without being annoying, and when my sister and I said we were going to share everything, they brought the sandwich that we ordered on two plates.  We ordered two appetizers, the chicken tamales and the avocado fries, and the chicken Monsieur sandwich, and just asked the waiter to bring it all at once, which he did.  The avocado fries were pretty delicious and I love the sauce that they serve with it.  The tamales were OK and the chicken sandwich, while it was kind of inventive and the description of it in the menu made it sound delicious, it was just OK also.  The coleslaw served with the sandwich was very oniony.... not to our liking.  Everything was served really beautifully and I really liked the dishware that they use there.  I would go back if I'm ever in the area, and try something different.

Food great!!! .....service is TERRIBLE!!! Business was slow, 5 girls standing around.... I had to flag them down for EVERYTHING. RIDICULOUS!!
2stars for cleanliness and good food

I have been coming here since it opened.  So why the downgrade?   A bad experience last night - me and my regular dining partner here had terrible service while sitting at the bar.  The bartenders were indifferent, we had to practically beg for water, drink orders, dinner order.  While I love the Fish House Punch, the love is tempered when it takes 15 minutes to get it - and no - it was not even that busy.  My pal's burger was delicious according to her, my oysters - which were herb roasted were generally flavorless and the Sly Fox Cheddar Sauce with our duck fat fries was tasteless and runny.  Dear Jose - please come and visit your restaurants and keep them on their toes...

We both agreed that we may cross this off our list after years of it being our go-to spot.

Barone's has all the right ingredients for the possibility of a successful office party.  The restaurant is divided into several separate spaces, so we were able to get crazy with our annual re-gifting game without annoying the rest of the diners.  The pasta dishes were delicious.  They accommodated requests for gift and wine tables to be set up before we arrived.

Unfortunately, there were far more cons than pros.

Barone's seriously lacks organization and professionalism for large group planning.  When I called to ask about pricing packages, I was told that tax would be waived if we paid in cash.  This meant that the total cost per person fell within my budget goal, and so I went ahead and made a reservation.  A couple weeks later, when I stopped in to choose the menu, I was told that the person I spoke with on the phone was misinformed, and that we would be charged 5% tax rather than 7%.  Since this would raise the cost per person by a dollar, and I was not going to go around asking everyone who had already RSVP'd to give me another dollar, I had to go back the next day to speak with a manager.

I explained my concerns to the manager, hoping that he'd lower the cost of the dinner so that the 5% increase in price wouldn't change my total cost per person.  My main concern was that since my total cost included a tip, the restaurant would take what they were owed, but the servers wouldn't receive their 20% cut.  The manager assured me that it would not be an issue because HE would be the server the evening of our event, and since he understood the situation, he just wouldn't take tip.  "Seriously, don't worry about it," I was assured.

So the night of the party came, and there were several red flags from the start.  First, the manager was nowhere to be seen.  It would have been nice to be greeted by someone who was familiar with all of my requests upon arrival, perhaps a review of the menu that had been chosen.  But when I got there, the hostess simply pointed me in the direction of the back room and I was on my own.

Said room happened to be freezing.  I mentioned it to a worker, and was told that the heat was just turned on for that room.  The room never warmed to a comfortable temperature, and I actually had a few diners who ate their entire dinners with their winter coats on.

The bathroom that was at the back of our room was gross.  It looked like someone had given himself a haircut in there before we arrived, little snips of hair all over the sink, and a canister of hair pomade on the counter.  A friend had to wipe up the sink before the rest of the party arrived.  There were also no paper towels and the room was running low on toilet paper.  It took several requests before these changes were made.

The service itself was good.  From what I experienced at my own table, drinks and food arrived in a timely manner, and the servers were friendly.  Aside from the pasta course, no one really seemed impressed by their food.  Portions were huge, but taste was forgettable.  The manager finally showed up about halfway through our dinner to ask how we wanted our dessert served, cut up all the cakes for us, and then disappeared again.

More issues, or maybe the same issue, arrived when it was time to pay.  We were charged for an extra diner; I mistakenly said that we had 31, and that is how many the manager put on our bill, despite the fact that I know he MUST have counted how many plates went out so that he'd be able to tally up our dues later on.  He had to know I had miscounted.

Oh, and hey, remember when I was told that gratuity would NOT be included and that the manager would be our server so we shouldn't worry about an inadequate tip?  Yeah, well gratuity WAS included, and we had not collected enough money to meet the total.  I had to ask the poor server (who was NOT the manager) to remove the gratuity from the check so that we could afford the bill, and then I ended up throwing in some extra cash that I (luckily, and uncharacteristically) had in my wallet to come closer to what the total should have been with a 20% tip.  *MAJOR GUILT*

The manager made an appearance again as we were on our way out, and we pointed to a large bottle of wine that had been opened but not otherwise touched, offering it to him and his servers.  "Ugh, I don't drink wine.  That stuff is like grape juice," he scoffed, as his cell phone rang with some trancey club beats.  Sorry playa.  I'll leave you to your Red Bull and vodka and fist pump my way out the door.  And my coworkers and I will NOT be back for next year's winter soiree.

Let's be honest, anything that isn't a carwash or used car lot is a win as an addition to 12south.  We've got a long way to go but we're getting there.  I must say that we were incredibly excited to have another dinner option within walking distance and the food at Edley's does not disappoint.  It is EXCELLENT.  The nachos with chicken are amazing.  The brisket (only available at lunch) is phenomenal.  The sides are approximately 1000 times better than Jack's (which isn't saying much because Jack's are an atrocity).  We have been several times and love it except their one HUGE detractor:  The Service Model.

It 's easy enough to figure out where and how to order but where to sit, now that is another question entirely.  It is relatively small inside when the weather isn't warm (and the deck an option).  Lately, at dinner time, you have numerous groups of people with one person in line ordering and 3 others hovering, death-staring, and annoying the crap out of those actually eating.  When a table actually opens up, the Black Friday rush to claim it is unbearable.  We've left several times to burger up or mafioza's where they take names...on a list...like adults.  Cafeteria style?  Really?   Come on gang.  We had enough of that in high school.

Don't go with kids, don't go after five with more than four, be prepared for an adventure.

Another of my must haves whenever I come home to see my family. Amazing. I have not eaten anything here that I haven't throughly enjoyed. The crawfish beignets are cheesy and spicy. The stuffed poboy is rich and flavorful with lots of gravy. The redfish and grits is something I still crave. Get there early because they get very busy very quickly, I've even waited in line for them to open. Parking is always a struggle, but it's worth it.

WORSE McDonald EVER. Rude employees except the security, I don't think the cashier knows what she was doing, she couldn't even get my change right. Our hash browns weren't cooked it was still frozen. The chicken nuggets were not cooked through. The inside of the restaurant smells like crap.
I will not recommend this place to anyone, too bad yelp will not allow me to put a ZERO star.

Great experience.  Aly was our server and was so nice and courteous.  We had Ceviche Del Día and the Empanadas de Hongos...DELICIOUS!!  The Ceviche is on the spicy side but lots of shrimp.  Also, the Pollo IRON SKILLET TACOS were awesome as was the Rancheros style ENCHILADAS Costilla(Braised Short Rib).  Will definitely be back.

Yes -- The Mellow Mushroom in Brandon has some of the finest pizza I have ever enjoyed. Even better are some of the appetizers (try the Cheese Bread). The crust is delicious and the beer variety worth the visit. However ... when ordering a pizza be prepared to wait (and wait and wait). While waiting for your main dish it is easy to fill up on apps and beer -- and that can run up the bill significantly. Some people like this and that's fine. My preference is to order ahead and carry-out.

Whats the excitement. This place is not at all special. 
Coffee is awful. pancakes are equal to waffle house (i assume), service is crap,
I fail to understand why there is a line around the block. I fail to understand why people come here at all.

A couple of months ago my coworker and I checked out the menu before arriving so that we could immediately order when we arrived, as we only have a one hour lunch. The place is only about 5 minutes from our job. We were Immediately seated.  I ordered seafood tacos and she ordered a cheeseburger. After waiting for 50 minutes the food still had not arrived at our table we decided to just cancel the order and head back to work and get chips and soda from the vending machine. We were told the food was now finished cooking, so we decided to just take it to go. Well you know fish tacos and fries and not the same when reheated. We were not given an explanation as to why the food took so long nor did they offer any type of future discount or compensation. I'm writing this now because my coworker thinks we should give the place another try which I agreed to. So I shall be back with another review later this week. Wish us luck

Portions are small but it is all you can eat. Only rule I am not a fan of is that everyone at the table has to pick all you eat or all has to pick the regular menu "not all you can eat" so it is all or not.

I agree with the comments in previous reviews.  This is a great place for breakfast anytime (served Tuesday-Sunday 8AM - 3PM), but do be aware: it is popular on weekends.   The breakfast and lunch menus provide many choices, and the sides (many with a Jewish flare) are great, especially the potato latke.  The pancakes and biscuits are exceptional.  Look for the specials, which usually emphasize seasonal fruits or, in the case of omelets, fresh vegetables.  The atmosphere is laid back (maybe a little too much so, service-wise).  A great place to seek out on a nice day.  I note that they will soon open for dinner, too.

I absolutely LOVE this restaurant!  The venue is great, the waitstaff are helpful, knowledgeable about the menu and pleasant and the food is great!!  Also, with it being New Orleans and all there is a definite back story to this establishment and people have attended seances there!  But don't let that stop u--it just makes it all the more interesting!
Amazing food! My husband and I love to eat here. The tatziki is the best I've ever had. Highly recommend to anyone in the mood for great Greek or Italian.
We went here for breakfast. It had a good view of the beach and not very crowded. Service was good. Very expensive though, juice was five dollars and they don't serve waffles.

Not impressed.  All the orders were wrong.   My grilled chicken sandwich was missing the ranch dressing, Barry's buffalo chicken salad was missing the blue cheese crumbles and the blue cheese dressing and MAK was terrible.  The chicken croquet had no chicken and the peas and carrots were seriously over cooked.  The waitress was awful.  ( unless it was her first day.)  Don't think we will be back anytime soon.

I drove to Coffeebar thinking it was the exact location of the prior coffeeshop. However, when I drove by, I noticed that the facade of the building looked unfinished. I had to do two U-turns and look to the west side of the building to find the main entrance - outdoor signage would have been nice.

Regardless, when we walked in, we were welcomed by a very friendly staff. I made sure I didn't make the embarrassing mistake of ordering a "Venti, Grande, or Tall'" beverage.

My girlfriend ordered a coconut chai latte (?) thing and I ordered an Iced Americano. Both were really good. The fluffy cinnamon rolls in the case were calling my name, but due to Paleo restrictions, I chose to ignore their beckoning whisper. 

I really appreciated the fact that the gentleman who took our order remembered my name at the end of our visit and asked how our experience was.

We will be back.

They accept credit card. Definitely not just a juice bar, let alone the first in New Orleans. Given the hype of all these other reviewers with Surrey's shrimp and grits, we had to indulge. You absolutely have to try it. The shrimp is cooked so well, many places tend to overcook, but they are so tender. The grits are so buttery and delicious, and were totally perfect with a few drops of hot sauce. 

Wonderful service, everyone was so friendly and accommodating.

The donuts here are amazing. I have been a few times now. I have not been disappointed with any of the choices. Personally, the hot donuts are my preferred diet destroyer of choice. The flavors are creative, but not overwhelming. The chicken is equally delicious. I liked the zahav spice best, but none of the others were too far behind!

Worst steak I've ever had. Ordered the petite filet. Was mostly gristle. What meat I could find had an odd flavor, color & texture. I ordered it medium well, still no excuse.
The reduction sauce was tasty, and the presentation was really nice. Attentive waiter, but the steak just killed it for me. Hesitant to try this place again.
Great burger! I had the bbq burger which had tons of flavor. Burger comes by itself, so don't forget to add an order of fries. Great location!

Very disappointing experience- we wondered why we were the only people there at lunch on a Saturday, and now I know. We ordered from the lunch menu and were surprised at the size of the portions. When the bill came we found out why- they had stopped doing lunch on the weekends and had let us think we were ordering lunch. They also charged us $3 for a flat Coke we had to send back and never got a replacement for. Don't be surprised when your restaurant stays empty.

We have ordered food to pick up twice and both times it has been great.  It is fresh, well seasoned and plentiful. Additionally, the food is prepared very quickly. Both my husband and I agree that it is the best Chinese we have ever had.  I was pleased to find out that the honey chicken is actually fried and smothered with honey sauce versus being more like sweet and sour chicken where you dip it.  It was so so so yummy. We have also had fried wontons, fried dumplings and cashew chicken.  Definitely a winner!!

I always considered Applebees as an average place. The food is ho-hum nothing special. At times i wonder how long has that food been sitting there. I believe a lot of food is pre-cooked earlier that day, then microwaved and served. I think the Burgers are cooked fresh though. Just fyi, to any of the previous posters or whomever reads this review. This Applebees on Castor is the training/eval center. I havent really had a problem with the actual service here. Its just the food isnt the best. This goes for all Applebees although im sure some are better than others.

4.5 Stars

We came in on a Monday night around 4PM for the oyster happy hour and were surprised that the wait to be seated was a little less than two hours. I guess we should have done a little more research and made reservations, but it was a spontaneous decision, so it was what it was. Once, we were seated, we ordered:

Baked Oysters: A must must get. They were phenomenal. I don't even know how to describe the flavor. It was just really tasty.

Raw Oysters: Fresh and good. And they're really big in size here compared to all the other places I've been to for raw oysters outside of NOLA. And at $0.75 per oyster? Couldn't get any better.

Gumbo: I'm not usually a fan of gumbo and I wouldn't order it ever, but had to try it here after hearing the next table over raving about it with the waitress. I wasn't disappointed. Not too salty and the overall taste is clean and flavorful.

Last night I was pleasantly surprised by my experience at El Camino. The two or three other times I've been have been just ok but last night was better. We decided to go more Tex than Mex and it worked out great. 

In my opinion, they have some of the best margaritas I've had...especially for the price. They're strong and not too sweet, awesome. What really blew my mind this past visit was the pulled pork sammy. We added cole slaw which was the best idea ever. The pork was tasty, moist and juicy and the bun didn't fall apart! I might have to get this sandwich every time I go. 

To wrap up my feelings on this place, 4 stars for the Tex, 3 on the mex so I would give it 3.5 stars.

From the exterior, the restaurant looked cute. I associated it with a diner that you would see off of an old American film. I pictured a sweet old waitress serving me apple pie a la mode. Btw they ran out of ice cream at Dots so... there goes my dream. Oh well. 

I guess I walked into the diner with too high of expectations. The interior looked, without a better way of putting it, dirty and old. The waitress that served us wasn't particularly rude, but she didn't give us a smile either. It seemed as though she was there to do her job, not to enjoy it. 

Now to the food. We ordered meat pies as appetizers. They came out fairly quickly with the wait was less than ten minutes. The meat pies were tiny, fun-sized. But it was an appetizer, so I wasn't expecting a huge portion. There were six of them and they were served on a bed of lettuce with containers of ranch sauce on the side. As far as the lettuce goes, it pathetic attempt as sprucing up the presentation. The filling of the meat pie reminded me of a cheeseburger. Wasn't good, but wasn't bad. 

I ordered the roast beef and gravy on a bun. The bun was grilled and the roast beef was great. It was extremely messy, but hey, I wasn't complaining. After struggling with my sandwich, I finally resorted to using a knife and fork. This just goes to show how packed the sandwich was; again, not complaining one bit. I really actually enjoyed my entree. 

For desert we ordered the strawberries and cream pancakes. The pancakes themselves were good. They had this eggy taste and this fluffiness to them that I found delightful. I do have a few complaints though. They did not let the pancakes cool down enough before putting the whipped cream on it, causing the cream to melt. Also, the strawberries were warm. They probably meant for the strawberries to be heated, but it didn't help with the melting whipped cream situation. 

As far as price goes, it was moderate. For a lunch that consisted of an appetizer, two entrees, and an order of pancakes, the total was around $25. I also gave $5 as a tip so lunch costed just about $30. Not that bad. 

Am I willing to return to this place? Hmm.... I don't think so. I didn't hate my experience there, but I didn't love it either. It was okay and because of that I am not willing to make the trip out to Kenner for an "okay" experience.

Do not eat here.

I ordered online and got three sushi rolls. After an hour of waiting we called to check on the order. They said they were behind and it would be there soon. We waited an additional twenty minutes and when it arrived I was starving and started eating very quickly. Then I found a bone in it. Then another. Then another. On the third bone I stopped eating it and realized it was turning my stomach. We called and complained and in their defence they sent someone out to give us a refund, so at least I got food poisoning for free.

Amazing food!!! Beautiful, exquisitely and carefully thought out courses. Fresh, flavorful and perfectly sized portions.  Even the pork belly did not feel heavy and we left feeling very satisfied but not disgustingly bloated. Attentive but not overbearing service- staff was wonderful.  Cannot wait to come back for more!

I'm not sure what happened in the kitchen the afternoon of December 20th but the chicken cheesteak I just had was not good. I thought it was going to be chunks of chicken breast instead it was dry & looked processed (like steakumm)...I will give them another chance maybe it was an "off" day

This food truck actually comes to my job over in South Jersey and my job goes nuts! 
We get a lot of visits from various food trucks and this one is by far the BEST!
I got the fish, mac and cheese, greens, and rice & beans! Everything was phenomenal! 
I hope they come every Friday!

Last Sunday the 13th the family stopped in for lunch. Friendly staff. TVs if you care to watch a game. My wife and I had the clam chowder for starters. It was good, not as hot as it should have been, We split a grouper sandwich. It was small, the fish was about the size of a Craft Cheese Single. It did taste good, but very small. One of my kids ordered the chicken pasta primavera. She said it was tasteless so we sent it back. My second kid had a chicken nuggets meal. She said is was fair but ate most of it.  We all left hungry and made a stop @ Micky Ds on the way home.

The tour was a little on the long side, but the tasting was absolutely wonderful. The girl who facilitated the tasting seemed more personable. You could really tell both the tour guide and the lady who gave the tasting really loved their jobs.

Amazing food with the best staff! This is always my go to spot!! Prices are great and the quality of service is fantastic. You would be crazy not to make old times your new breakfast destination! Thanks guys always a pleasure to come dine with you!

The Kenner location is just as good as the New Orleans location!! I'm glad that the parking is a bit bigger than the New Orleans location, but it is still a strange parking lot.

We went during the week, and it was surprisingly not that busy, yet my food ticket got lost.

My coworker and I split a salad and two sandwiches (nom nom nom) because that is how we roll at The Big Cheezy. I'm glad that we did split the two sandwiches because I was the second one to order, but my food never came out until I asked about it. They had to reprint my ticket so the kitchen could make my food. Even though everyone was already done with their meal, I gobbled up my food and left.

I really wish they would make Bacon Mac n Cheese fries a thing.

Came here about three weeks ago and was disappointed to say the least. 

To start off the mood is very cool and it's in a great, fun neighborhood. The pretzels soft baked were also great. 

That being said everything else- not so good. We ordered out here and they told us the wait would be about 45-50 minutes. We got there at the 50 minute mark and ended up waiting an additional 45 minutes. The place was not crowded at all which I hear is rare, and the woman who said the food would be right out continued to look at me so she was very aware of my presence. Finally she brought the food out and said "ops sorry for the wait that was totally my fault". Cheesy bread was completely burnt and inedible, and pizza was decent I guess, though the sauce wasn't so good. I"they forgot it in the burner when we were literally the only people waiting on food. I guess people make mistakes but they were not all that apologetic about it especially since I was waiting an extra 45 minutes and my food was burnt to a crisp. It was also expensive. Next time I'll go to "jets".
Terrible service and the food was pretty bad. I couldn't walk around with my family without seeing pants on the ground,  I didn't have an incredible time.

Its okay it one likes overpriced ice cream....'the gotta have' it menu! Nice its 'fixed' in front of you with a few dollops of the stuff and extras.  Without coupons not worth it...cept for those who supposedly have the $ or the credit cards to blow on disposables such as this
Very good food and great service. This is a great place to grab a very unique burger and milkshake in downtown St. Louis. It's a bit overpriced for what you receive but definitely worth trying.

I think the Black Sheep is my favorite in the city. They have yummy food (especially the fries), the first floor is lovely and bright when it's nice weather because of the big windows, and there are 3 floors so usually you can find a spot somewhere to have a drink.

The food was great.  Staff was very friendly. Only feedback I suggest is for the staff to have more of a sense of urgency.  They can easily turn in more tables   Too many trips to and from the kitchen. Ask for more things at once and bring it all together.

Still like the convenience and variety of the flavors on the fly or on the fun. 

I especially like the 
-Tuna tataki w/ sautéed onions on top 
-albacore and truffle ponzu
-tuna tartare

Challenge: I will say it is quite difficult to look at the colorful plays passing by, then look at the menu of pictures to figure out what the item is. By that time, your colorful plate has already passed and someone else my have their hands on it.  

Pros- 
-You can still order through the server
- Child friendly and really cool to the kiddos. They like to grab the plate for you.

Nice! Haven't had E. Coast Italian before and I liked it. The pizza was really good, very addictive. The sausage on it was to die for. The meatballs on it weren't that great but they were edible... The meatballs tasted like only sugar and cumin. 

My friend had the pasta which I posted. We though it was amusing that it looks like maggots. I really liked it though. It was different than any other pasta I've tasted (probably better and more "legit", ha ha... LA has terrible food). The taste of the wheat was more pronounced and the pasta was a bit chewier and bready, though pleasantly so. I wish it had a bit more sauce but I liked it.

Bartender Logan was super helpful. They had a gluten free crust that did not make me sick. (I'm celiac / super sensitive). Only issue was how long it took to get our charcuterie board. We got our pizza and finished it before the board came out. Was hoping to eat the cheese / meat first but everything tasted wonderful.

I've been here two times so far, about a year and  1/2 apart, and both times I've been very satisfied! They're definitely a popular Central West End spot on weekends, so I HIGHLY recommend making a reservation ahead of time via Yelp or Waitlist app.

When we arrived and checked in with the hostess, she said it would still be about a 30 minute wait for our party of 4. A little surprising as we had placed ourselves in line via the Yelp app 30 mins prior on our drive there, but nonetheless we grabbed drinks at the bar after a few minutes of waiting. Our table was ready by the time we received our drinks (didn't take the whole 30 mins).

The overall atmosphere is a very unique one for the STL area. They have a very long bar downstairs with an equally long set of high top tables to eat at and a gigantic wall of antique glass windows. We were seated upstairs which consists mainly of 4-6 person tables that either overlook the main floor or the side streets of the restaurant.

With them being so busy on weekends and usually having a full house, it can get pretty noisy in the restaurant as they have concrete walls with little insulation. Don't expect to have a intimate conversation at your table.

Burgers are excellent quality overall and the fries are always crispy and perfectly cooked. I had the Whiskey BBQ Burger and was very satisfied with my choice. They have a wide selection of sauces to try too, I highly recommend the Roster Sauce. My only pet peeve is that the burgers are pretty pricey ($10+) and a little on the smaller size and they don't come with a side.

Our table split a pitcher of the Peach Ginger Spiked Lemonade and it was delicious! The picture was enough for all 4 of us to have at least 2 servings each. They're famous for their boozy shakes, but we didn't partake in any of those.

Overall great place to enjoy at evening at downtown. Good vibes, friendly staff, delicious food.

Incredibly nice wait staff who serve well very.  They are the only reason for the two stars.  The food was unfortunately NOT properly or well  prepared.  Thin, long haired guy as short-order cook needs serious training.
:-( 
Breakfast time, it wasn't busy and I was in no rush.  Ordered and asked for eggs whites cooked completely and well done hash browns..... What I got was clear, runny egg whites, barely cooked hash browns, and semi-raw bacon.
My mistake was eating most of it.  For a healthy man with no bowel issues, to be forced to run to the bathroom before I even left the restaurant says something!  The rest of my day was spent in or near the latrine.
:-(

Muriel's is by far one of the best dining experiences present in New Orleans today. This is a formal restaurant without putting stuffiness ahead of the comfort and sensibility of their customers. During our dinner there was a group of people who were completely and inappropriately dressed for even the most casual of restaurants. However, the staff is so well polished the group was not turned away but quietly and discreetly covered up with the restaurants T shirts and were seated with out disturbing the other guests. This may seem like an odd event to note, but it finely demonstrates the refined service skills of staff. One is comfortable in a button down shirt or a tie and jacket or even a polo shirt. The food was by far some of the best I've had in the Quarter over the many years I have visited. The duck was expertly seared and served at a perfect temp. The duck fried rice with greens was simply perfect, I could have taken a whole order to go. The service one receives is unmatched and could easily be described as graceful. My birthday dinner was memorable and everything I wanted it to be and I can't wait to return.
One of the best breakfasts I have ever had in my life! The spinach and feta wrap with hash browns and a biscuit is amazing. Friendly staff. If you are in NOLA, this is your breakfast spot!

I'm a fan of the margaritas and the sopas appetizers at Xochitl.  The bartenders are nice, the place has a fun atmosphere, it's clean and well run.  We always have a great time here.  The guacamole is delicious and homemade.

Meh.

My coworkers and I ordered about 10 roast beef sandwiches today.  I have eaten here in the past.  The quality went down considerably.  The cheese on my sandwich wasn't even melted.  They skimped on the meat and overall it wasn't a very good sandwich.  Even the horseradish tasted bland.  It added some moisture but barely any heat.

I got the impression that this place has turned into another American business trying to increase its margins by sacrificing quality.

But then again food in this entire area is pretty terrible.

I'm hitting 4 stars on this out of confidence the next time I go it will be a better experience.  Our server was courteous and friendly, but tended to ignore us during our stay.  Our server came by to greet me before my guest arrived, she poured water for the table and left.  11 minutes after my guest arrived we flagged down another server who offered to fetch ours.  Ordering was fine and the interaction and recommendations were perfectly good.  Food came out eventually, but we had to flag her down to ask for drinks other than water.  

My plate arrived and just wasn't great.  Fish wrap was overloaded with onions and was very salty and very little fish that I could find. I ate much of it so I can't really complain that loudly!  Other than this, the restaurant itself is great.  Location and interior are great, I bet it's a happening place in the evenings.

Oh, the best part was that Serial Killa by RBX and Snoop Dogg off Doggystyle played over the house sound system while we ate and I thought that was badass.

I'll go back, no doubt.

Finally went here in my continued quest of finding decent Mexican located in the greater West Chester area.

Menu is pretty basic fair with limited veterinarian and seafood options.   It was pretty much what you would find on most East Coast Mexican places and that most Americans are familiar with - tacos, burritos, quesadillas, etc.  No tortas or more exotic meats (goat, etc) or sauces.  The most exotic thing on the menu looked to a Mole Poblano.

That's was fine with me and I don't think most of the people who were eating there or taking out (families with kids, retirees, college-aged kids) were looking for anything exotic either. 

Got a carnitas burrito ala carte that comes with a side of chips and some salsa.  Nothing spectacular but solid.  Carnitas was moist, well-shredded, and flavorful with hints of pepper & several other spices.  In fact, I thought the burrito was going to be a bit on the bland side but the carnitas had enough taste to carry it.  'Hot' salsa (spicy pico de gallo) was also very good especially given that tomatoes this time of year tend to be of pretty mixed quality.  Much better than most of the mediocre salsa you usually get at most Mexican places I have been to around the Philly area.   

Only compliant was I wish that the carnitas hadn't been shredded so finely or that the chips would have come with more than a single small container of salsa.  Really minor issue though.   

Service was great and attentive too.  Menus are already on the table and the waitress came right over once I sat down.  Also checked up on me at the appropriate times to refill drinks/check food/give me my check.

All-in-all a pretty solid Mexican place that seems that it would be a good place to take people who are looking for basic Mexican food items.  As for me, I will be back but just grab some takeout instead next time.

The food was very good. Service at the Bar was just unbelievable rude. My boyfriend and I arrived for dinner at 8:30, and service started out great, but then rapidly went downhill. My boyfriend is a bartender and I am a chef, and understand having bad days, not wanting to be there, wanting to have all your side work done and wanting to leave as soon as you can at the end of your shift. One of the bartenders was already breaking things down when we ordered dinner at 8:40, then both of them started completely breaking down the bar by 9,scrubbing, pulling out the grates, etc etc. We both would have had a few more drinks, and we were not the only ones there, so this was not the case of we were the last ones in the bar and didn't realize everyone wanted to go home . There is a way to make your customers happy, and quietly do your side work and not alienating them. We didn't want to make small talk with them, we just wanted service and to not smell cleaning products while we ate. We typically tip over 20%. We did still tip, just not as generously  as we usually do. Though the food was good, we will most likely not return because of how horrible the bar staff lacked in professionalism.

Fresh food and well-prepared, good portion size. Very casual atmosphere, service was fine but not overly friendly. Nice variety on the menu. Coffee is solid and the mimosa was tasty. Location is great with indoor and outdoor seating. Would definitely return when we're in the area.

Four stars for the pizza, which was excellent. The sauce had the right amount of sweetness, and the cheese was fresh and not overcooked as one may see outside of NYC. That's the good news. Now the bad. What's up with their ceaser salad? Skimpy on the chicken and hardly any dressing. Why bother to offer if you can't deliver. A ceaser salad is relatively simple and cheap to make so one would expect more than 8 little pieces of chicken. And I mean little as in smaller than a chicken nugget. But the pizza was the best by far and I can't wait to get another pie.

Best wings in town.

They also have a bunch of other stuff on the menu: burgers, sandwiches, hot dogs, even (huge) salads. And all of that stuff is great. But it's the wings you go for, and they're fantastic. Be sure to check out the lunch special.

great beer selection on tap from many European countries and domestic micro-breweries! The cafe has amazing gourmet plates by Chef Chris Tolan, voted one of Tampa's best up & coming spot for food by Creative Loafing. Try the grilled cheese with pears sandwich, amazing!

I loveeeeeed this place!  I always go to lunch on Friday's with co-workers and we try a new local place each week...preferably a non-chain!  The food was sooooooo good, so fresh and had amazing flavor.  I really forgot I was in Florida when sitting in the room eating...almost made me feel like I was in Georgia or the Carolina's by how they have it staged.

I had the Turkey Cinnamon Tea Sandwich with the homemade and amazing Tomato Basil Bisque....was outstanding and just the right size.  I am a sucker for scones and had to try one to go...was soooo good!

They have a small store/bakery just outside of the restaurant that was perfect.  You can go in and get some items to go and every single item in the case and on the shelves looked amazing.  I highly recommend going here as I will be going back!

So why one star?   Because their ice cream is still good.  But that is where it ends.

I have been to this Twistee Treat at least 40 times since it opened.  I might be the TT Duke on Yelp with more check-ins here than anyone, but that will likely change.  I rated this place a four star a couple weeks after opening, but it has gone down hill, a lot.

With the last ten visits, service and quality has gone down so much, I might never return.

Let's start with product quality.  In the last five visits I have had a stale cone three times...the once perfect cone shape is now nothing but a swirled ice cream mess pressed into the cone and leaning to the side....and several times the sugar cone leaked from the bottom.

Then there is service, or lack thereof.  My only complaint at opening was slow service.  I thought service could not get slower, but it has.  

I fully support giving young adults the opportunity to work, but the culture at this restaurant lacks any customer care.  They seem more interested in socializing with friends at the window or their very exotic fingernails, than they are about customers.  And, the managers lack any empathy or ability to resolve these problems.

So...Back to TCBY for now...

Bar far some of the worst food I've ever had.  I ordered the jambalaya, I've heard that it is a traditional New Orleans dish, and I was clear that it was not fresh and had been sitting out.  The rice was mushy and cold.  For the price it was not worth it at all.  I will go somewhere else for dinner to make up for the experience.

Dam I was so happy with this food last night. Today is a different story.  I'm sicker than a dog. Working my ass off muscling my way through this.  The day is almost over that's what I'm pushing for.  The mana from heaven turned or to be the mana from hell.  Montezuma's reveng, Bubble guts like the volcanoe is active all day.  I would never eat there again.  Whoever runs the joint needs to manage the food better because the only thing you got running was my asshole. Thanks jas. Never again.  Don't recommend this to anybody.

The pics were from my most recent visit with my hubby. I enjoyed the buffalo chicken wrap...it was good but not great. Hubs had the fish Reuben, he said it was ok...the bread was burned and he could taste the char. I ordered an Amberbock beer, it didn't taste good at all, so the kind waitress replaced it with a bud light tasted fine but was not super cold. The fried pickles were greasy and not that good. They have live entertainment on Thursday's so may go back for that and give it another try.

Our extended family brought us here for some hangover therapy. 

ATMOSPHERE:
Its a huge sports bar with big windows, wood everywhere and more TV's than a Vegas kino parlor.  And they have THE coolest restroom decor I've ever seen!

FOOD:
Crab Fries - Apparently their specialty.  The fries were average but the dip is to die for!  Not sure why its named that way as there's no taste of crab. 

Cheesesteak Nachos - Huge portion with a good amount of toppings.  Very good. 

Lobster Cheesesteak - Meat, fresh lobster & cheese sauce.  This isn't the best cheesesteak I've had, but maybe if it came with real cheese it would've complimented the flavors better. 

Mussels Marinara - A family member's dish, so I just tried one.  Tender & lots of flavor but I'm not a big mussel fan. 

Dungeness Crab - Tried a portion from my hubby.  It's good but mainstream.  Nothing unique. 

SERVICE:
We walked in at lunch time and got seated in about 15 mins.  Our female server wasn't the friendliest of people but she did check on us throughout our meal. 

OVERALL:
This is the place to be if you're a sports fan or if you just want some great bar food.

My sister and I decided to have dinner here last Friday. We definitely had high hopes! We left pretty disappointed...

Service is super slow and inattentive. Food is not bad- when they get it right. They completely messed up our whole order.

I expected more...too bad...maybe carry out next time (shrugs)

Stopped by for the world famous Greek salad only in tarpon Springs fla.  We had there fried grouper sandwich.  Taste out of this world. One of the best ever. Service here is always a 10. Top notch. And if you have room. There Greek deserts are to die for.

I like Tavern a lot. The food is very good. I went here for lunch with a friend from work. I loved the vibe, the dim-ish lighting, and the music, and would definitely like to come back at night time. The fish was very good, fresh, and the batter was light and perfect. I loved the sauces that came with my meal. I shouldn't have gotten the sweet potato fries. Didn't care for them. Next time I'll get regular ones. Also loved the fact that they have all of those hot sauces at the table. Any place with an abundance of hot sauces is awesome to me. I would like to go back and try other food. The only negative thing was it took far too long to eat here on our lunch break. The service was very slow, but maybe the server was new. We had an hour break and we are late coming back. However, will go back again, definitely.

Great coffee, atmosphere, and lively service! Visited here while in town and fell in love. 
I was recommended from a local shop near by between this and another and the difference was the warning of sass at this place. Who doesn't love some good sass! 

I was greeted by the owner and she lived up to the warning and was already making me feel welcomed and had me chuckling. 

All I had was as a sugar free caramel latte and sat at the bar and ended up having one of the nicest conversations with a local of St Pete. 

There was so much to enjoy, from the decor and open feel to the out side. 

If you are a coffee lover, you must visit here. It is amongst a strip of non chain shops with so much character! 

Pets are welcome so bring your furry one with you!

My most FAVORITE place in NoLibs.  I'm a vegetarian and this place is my heaven.  They have one of my most favorite veggie wings... they are crispy and spicy and make me sweat (in a good way).  I've pretty much liked everything I've ever gotten here, but I love to go just for wings and a marg... great outdoor seating in summer and just a cool overall vibe.  This is and will continue to be my Philly staple!

I'll just have to agree with all the previous reviews about the Red Pony, this bar and restaurant is very slick and sexy. The mood and decor looks really great and the vibe has a lot of great energy.  I got to spend some time at the bar sharing a drink with friends. 

Everyone on the staff was friendly and the drinks were good.  I got my favorite Manhattan and just absorbed the vibe of the room.

If you are in Franklin, you will enjoy the Red Pony.
The best restaurant I have been to! The sliders are the best sandwiches you will get! The BLT is the best! Great coffee and atmosphere! The staff is also amazing! For sure a must try!

Great location, fun building and delicious burgers!  

We sat at the bar on a Sunday around noon.  They have DirecTV and show the football games - which was a mandatory for my friend.  We shared the Bavarian pretzel appetizer - it was pretty good - served with a mustard and a french onion dip.  I would probably skip these next time and try something else.  My friend ordered the Buy The Farm burger and it was amazing.  The egg on the burger was perfectly cooked and deliciously runny.  I ordered the West Coast - their version of a In and Out Double-Double animal style.  It was the perfect thing for my hangover.  I ordered the truffle tots on the recommendation of other Yelpers... They were tasty but a little too oily for my liking.  Next time I will probably try the regular tots or the salad.
We were also happy with the draft beer selection.  There are many local and hard to find beers on tap and they serve the beer in frosty pint glasses.
The only reason I am giving a 4-star rating instead of 5 is because of the service.  We sat at the bar but unfortunately the bartender wasn't very attentive.   She seemed to still be setting the bar up at noon - filling ketchup, etc.  She was also a little distracted by watching the football game.  We waited for drinks/silverware/etc. several times.   Based on the other reviews I think this was an exception.  We will definitely be back!

Jacksons is not my favorite restaurant but they seem to have managed to pull out that "it's cool to be seen there"  vibe so people keep going back and they have a good drink menu. The outdoor seating is nice as well so I can see the appeal there. However the food is just ho hum as is the service. 

That being said, I have ordered several things on the menu and the only thing I have gotten that I like is the blackened Tuna sandwich. It's seasoned well and cooked rare so if you catch them on a good day, it's quite yummy. Otherwise, it's good. The cookie dough egg roll is disgustingly rich but you know I am surprised more people haven't thought of taking a roll of cooking dough, slathering it in breading, and deep frying it. 

Stick with the drinks and dessert but if you must have lunch, go with the tuna.  If you are there for breafast and can't stomach the pantry line, then hit Fido, their eggs are delisch..

One of the best Indian food spots in town! Don't let the outside appearance fool you, the food is absolutely amazing and the staff is friendly. Get there early, due to the size it fills up quickly. Enjoy and ya welcome!

I've been to this place several times, and everything I've tried has been superb. All the curries are to die for. The service is so friendly, and they go out of their way for the customer. My stepmother wanted water with no ice, so rather than just pour carefully out of the same pitcher, the water server went to the kitchen to get water that was not ice cold. This is just an example of how they go the extra mile.

This place is by my job so I stopped in one evening for lunch
Food was mediocre at best and it's expensive
Could've went to bandanas and had better food
$19 for a chicken dinner

Impossible to get a hot burger here.  They don't have food runners (bad idea) so the food just sits and sits until the waiter has time to get the food and deliver it to the table.  I've consistently been served lukewarm burgers on numerous occasions here.  It's really a shame because their burgers would be fantastic if served hot.  Management, if you're listening, get your act together or I am done with your establishment.
Wish wish wish they would open the balcony on days they don't have upstairs reservations.  The view is wonderful, service impeccable. ..food very good.

My husband and I truly enjoyed our dinner at Rumfish. 
We sat at the bar and had dinner there. The atmosphere is nice and relaxed. We ordered the shrimp cocktail and snapper for dinner. Fresh and Amazing!!! Full of flavor. 
Yummy GF options. Thank you for a wonderful meal.
