The waitress offered was sweet, we got the soup (3/5), arancino (4.5/5 but small portion), huevos rancheros (4/5 but greasy), veggie melt (3/5 bred was greasy and the onions were too sweet it was off putting) and the kettle chips (very nice thin cut but a bit too greasy).
Overall service was slow but friendly. The savory dishes seemed a bit too greasy but the menu is well though of, very creative dishes. The sweet dishes/desserts are a real treat and worth it.
Would I come back? Yes, only to try out the dinner menu or a holiday special brunch but not with kids.

Party of 6 early on a Saturday night, 5pm, or first time in Reno.  Venue looks very promising from the outside, with outdoor seating and an upscale appeal. We were seated immediately, but as soon as we turned the corner from the hostess station, the place was a turnoff. A bit too loudly playing music, but the mostly twenties crowd seemed not to mind it

Our table surface reeked of sour dishrags, very off-putting.  We ordered drinks, took a while, the sangria looked like a blush wine and did not taste like sangria.

Our waitress was pleasant but detached, no interest in boosting our experience or displaying a personality, the smile and pleasantries seemed forced.  We ordered 2 appetizers: onion rings and nachos.  They were served pretty quickly but we were not provided with plates, which made for a messier experience than it should have.  Curiously, the check noted "no plates" for the apps and we were perplexed by this. 

The entrees were just okay. Nobody was thrilled but it was all edible.  The burrito came with chips and salsa, according to the menu, but no salsa was served. When questioned,  the waitress said the salsa was inside the burrito.  Oh, okay a pile of chips but nothing to dip them in.  We asked for boxes for leftovers which were provided, but no bag for carrying them.

All told, we had enough to eat but once we left we had to laugh because we had ALL wanted to leave when we were seated but nobody spoke up. Generally disappointed, in large part because we all liked the outside look of the venue but the experience didn't deliver.

The food/price  is pretty decent. The service on the other hand is ridiculous. I have been in 3 times, and each time I find myself completely annoyed by the immature "playing" that goes on with the entire staff. It's obnoxious, and definitely not someplace to come to enjoy a nice dinner. There are less childish activities at Chuck E. Cheese. Twice now, I have received food before receiving my drink because no one is here to "work." This place will not last.

My favorite dish here is the two way salad with the Curry Chicken and Grape Chicken salads.  I came here today for lunch and noticed the size of the scoops changed from the medium scoop to a MINI scoop.  It was barely a nibble of each of the chicken salads.  I left hungry and had to order more food to go.  Quit being cheap and go back to the medium scoop.  I feel ripped off.

Honestly came here with the folks and was taken away by the Nostalgia.

So glas I got to come in and see all the Forrest Gump references. Also i got a shrimp platter to kind of get a feel for the place.

They were surprisingly really well done. This place is like the swiss chalet of all things shrimp.

We dont have one in Toronto- so it was great to try out!

The gift shop was nice as well.

This restaurant is right off Watson, but offers other entry ways from side roads. There is also a drive through. 

You order at the counter, they call your name to get your food (like a bread co). Seating is limited so be ok with sharing a big table with strangers. There are two double seat tables and a table for parties that are 3 people or more. 

I've been twice and have enjoyed my food every time. The bacon is ultra thick and crispy, and the gravy is so good, and has a lot of flavor but isn't over salted. The iced coffee is great, and has coffee Ice so you don't get watered down coffee. I have asked for one refill at both visits and have gotten them. 

I have a very "spirited" son and he loves this place. There are crayons, as well as an open kitchen to watch. He also loves peeking in the bakery window and seeing what the back of the house is doing.
I loved eating here but they appear to be closed. Tried to eat there today and couldn't.

The food and service is great. A suggestion for improvement: there should be a drink menu, it's uncomfortable to ask bar tenders about the margarita and wine choices and their prices. Help us out, have a menu!

I love sweets and cinnamon rolls but I was very disappointed with this place. The rolls are large but dry and the icing is overly sweet and you can crunch on the sugar granules. I tried a plain and one with various toppings and they were pretty disgusting.

N and I went for dinner with a couple who are from Texas, and they grudgingly admitted that the BBQ was pretty authentic. This pleased me, as it was also tasty. 

Between the four of us we sampled the short rib, the sausage, the brisket, and the enchiladas. Our house vegetarian was thrilled with the cheese enchiladas, and we carnivores enjoyed all the meats, although the short rib was definitely best. Sandwiches were under $10 and came with a side of fries. Good fries, but not outstanding. In Philly your fries have to be something special to stand out.

The night's big winner was the endless chips and salsa. I don't know for sure, but I suspect they make their own chips. In any case, the chips were fried crisp and dusted with cayenne. The green tomatillo salsa was good and the red chipotle salsa was fantastic; both were pleasantly spicy, but not mouth burningly so. As advertised, every time a bowl was empty the waitress offered to refill it. The Texans were miffed that there was a charge for chips and sals at all, but even they had to admit that the $2,50 was well spent.

Although El Camino Real is vegetarian friendly, there are almost no actual vegetables to be had. But the meat is so good it's hard to care.

been a few times.  brisket has improved in s tpa over what I use to get at Carrollwood restaurant much more lean. sides consistently good  although may vary slightly in taste and consistency between visits.  parking can be a bitch like newhere in s tpa. depends on time of visit

Crazy Sushi is by far my new favorite sushi restaurant in the Rittenhouse area! The rave reviews from other members were spot on! I went last night and received a free edamame with my yelp check in. As our main course we ordered the Odessa Roll, The AK 47 (daily special) and the Kk Roll. All of the rolls were delicious and the presentation was excellent! The overall decor the restaurant is very modern and not as dull as it may seem from the outside. The service was just ok but I'm looking past any flaws in that because the sushi was just too good! I will definitely be back!

Very nice lil farm stand. Reasonable prices. They habe some morunusual items like white eggplant and cactus fruit. They also hve a grest variety of honeys. With honeycomb, bee pollen, etc. Some jams, corn relish, hot sauces. But the fruit is the big draw. Avocados (Florida and Haas),  various apples, pluots, etc. Deals for stuff that's going off in the back ($1 a basket). Nice people.

Gosh, I feel like giving Villagio zero stars based on my experience this evening, but that wouldn't be fair as I have been there many times and most weren't as bad as tonight.

Villagio is a very comfortable place to watch a movie because of the reclining chairs. The food is OK. Nothing special. If we get anything, it's a simple pizza and a beer or two. A 17% tip is added to each bill, whether you've received good service or not.

Unfortunately, the last two times I have been the service has been just awful. Tonight, while purchasing my ticket at the front desk I was told to order my food/drink in the theater  ... but I never managed to do that. I tried to get the attention of a waiter. No luck. The only person who came by my seat apparently couldn't help because she told me, "I'm a server. I can't take your order." OK - please help find someone who can! The next time this same person came by my seat trying to give me a pizza that I didn't order, I asked her again if she could help me and I got the same "No, I'm just a server." answer. She said she had asked a waiter to come, but alas... no waiter. When the movie finally started, I just figured she'd probably done me a favor. Saved me $$ and a mandatory 17% tip for nonexistent service. The movie was great and the chair was comfy, so it wasn't all bad.

Now, yes, I could have gone to the bar and placed an order myself when I finally got tired of waiting for that nowhere-to-be-seen waiter, but that brings me to the previous time I was at Villagio. We were a group of four, sitting at the bar and waiting for the movie to start. There were at least 3 employees at the back of the bar, yapping away and pretending to do shots (seriously, they were pretending to do shots!). Oh, and they also completely ignored us as we sat watching them, very amused. Finally, a female bartender (who had been busting her butt helping all of the customers at the bar by herself while these guys messed around) came over and we actually joked about how it was kind of ridiculous to have 4 people behind the bar and yet no one interested in helping the customer. Apparently a lot of people at Villagio have a job. One job. And are completely unable to assist with anything else. Either that, or the majority just aren't that interested in providing customer service. I think it's the latter.

Sigh. I really like Villagio because of the seats, but I am getting frustrated with the poor service.

This is the best rib spot in the city.  It's no surprise, that the people are lining up to get these ribs. Best quality ribs, very tender, a lot of meat, the sauces are delicious. Everything about this place rocks. Drive through is very efficient, with all the traffic they have, it runs very quickly and smoothly.  The service is always top notch. I highly recommend king rib.
I had lunch here last week and it was great! Service was good and I really loved my grilled Chicken and turnip greens! My son had the chili and loved it!

This truck is something to experience. The portions are massive for $10 and the food is cooked with heart. I really enjoyed his chicken. Only downside is the wait. If there are about 8 people in line ahead of you, expect about a 35-45min wait. Something to experience in Philly for sure!

After reading so many positive reviews on Yelp, I just had to check this place out.

Upon walking in, I could tell that Mood Cafe was unique. The man behind the counter just about welcomed us with open arms, asking us if we'd been there before, if we knew what chaat was, etc.

My friends and I looked at each other, then placed our orders of chaat and lassi. What is chaat? To this day, I still have no idea. It's a colorful mixture of spicy meat, vegetables, crispy pieces, yogurt, almonds, chickpeas, potatoes, dried fruit, and about six different sauces. Never in my life have I experienced so many flavors and textures in a single dish. Fortunately, the mixture is both delicious and satisfying. The spices deliver just the right kick to pair perfectly with a sweet, cool lassi. I'll be back to try the other chaats. In the end, what really sets Mood Cafe apart is the exceptional service. The man behind the counter is friendly and loves to share his crazy concoctions with people whether they are first-timers or longtime customers. Heck, some of Starr's restaurant staff could learn a thing or two.

Mood Cafe is a neighborhood gem. So if you're craving something daring, give it a shot!

I have been here a few times but this was the best, I should probably mention that Tuesday is 3 dollar pint night. I had the sidekick supreme and the people next to me recommended the spicy ranch ( house made) for dipping, amazing,try it

My trip to Pub and Kitchen was an unplanned lunch after some hanging in Rittenhouse Square on a perfect fall afternoon.  

Outdoor seating was a must.  

I was looking at a menu and it was rather small and read in an unimpressive way.  

The waiter sold me on a burger which was their special on this day, the meat came blended from a high end butcher in NYC.  Supposedly he had never until now let this blend of meat out of the city.  Pub and Kitchen had exclusivity to this meat which peaked my interest in what can a "high end butcher" from nyc do that I haven't seen before with a burger.  

The burger came with caramelized onions on a bun.  The meat lived up to the height of exclusive beef.  Although I don't plan on spending 18$ for a burger again anytime soon.  My tastebuds were more then satisfied.  I will describe this meal as I would when I describe the eating experience of any of my favorite foods... when the burger was gone, I was a little bit sad.

DISGUSTING!!! I ordered out last night: Sweet/Sour Chicken, Chicken Fried Rice and Egg Rolls. The egg rolls had some weird meat, wasn't pork, I can tell you that. Needless to say, they didn't taste very good, and this was the best part of the order. The chicken fried rice was steamed rice, not fried, still white not even browned. The chicken was rough and not looking too good. The sweet/sour chicken was horrible. The chicken pieces were thin little strips with way too much batter. It was all fried batter and very little chicken. This is the type of chicken I would expect to get at a KFC. This is the first time I ordered food and threw it all out. I can't believe people eat here. I am new to STL and if anyone can let me know where to go for good Chinese food, I would greatly appreciate it.

AMAZING service!!! We wanted to express our gratitude and appreciation especially to Bert. He was great help to us being our first time and then to find out he's the director. He runs this place beyond what you would normally expect from a fast food joint. He made this place a happy environment. All staff was very happy to help and even came around to fill our drinks. We weren't only blown away at the service but the food is amazing!! Definitely our new favorite place! Even has a kid jungle gym for the kids
Thank you again, 
Joshua and Ashlee
This place is so cute! It's insanely busy on weekends, but for good reason. The food is awesome. The servers are really nice. Great breakfast foods.

I held back from giving one star because we didn't get a chance to eat. I'm feeling nicer today than I did last night. Yes. It was a very busy night. Here is how the events went down at the door:

No special greeting like, "Have you ever been here?", just the words "two of you". 

Yes. the two of us. How long is the wait?

"35 minutes"... nothing like, "We're happy you're hear...you see how great the response is...we're doing our best sir to get everyone seated as fast as possible...but it might be 35 minutes or so". Just a flat... "35 minutes" the 7 second answer is way better than the 1 second. 

Ok. How long is it taking to get food out after we've been seated?

"about 45 minutes"..... I wasn't asked what I was thinking of ordering. Just an assumption.

May I see a menu?

Another assumption... "We stop taking preorders at 4 pm...blah, blah". I wanted to see the menue to assess what might take less time to serve. I KNOW deep dish takes more time. I was open to trying something else. 

Ok. I'm not willing to wait an hour & fifteen minutes just to get my meal. 

All I heard was.... "sorrreeee"...

I go out to eat for the experience..... the food is only part of that. Make me feel WELCOMED and not like "oh no. here are more people". After parking blocks away, it was an unsatisfactory walk back to the car. We went somewhere else & it too was on a wait. But we were welcomed nicely, invited to have a drink, sit outside, to review a menu, & once we were sat, the service was divine.  Sooorrreee 312. I'm not eager to head back.

Well i guess its a good thing, there isn't a lot of competition on the mainline for vietnamese food because if there were - they would be in trouble. 

After reading the reviews, we decided to give this place a try. I grew up eating vietnamese food - so I know good, bad, and fair. SO far we ordered the beef and pork vermicelli. What can I say - super bland, barely any veggies - too many noodles. I don't have much incentive to go back. You can always tell if a vietnamese place is good by their vermicelli and their Pho Broth. But after this, I don't think i want to try it - I'll just make the drive to Upper Darby or the city. However it is a cute place.

This is the second time we have eaten here. Both times the food was excellent, from the fresh, warm chips w/ both salsa and bean dip to the delicious chimichanga. They would've gotten 5 stars except for they sat us in the bar. Usually that would be fine, but today we felt like we were in the employees break room. The LOUD bartender (Leo) wouldn't shut up and the waitress was only a little better than okay. At times there were as many as 5 or 6 employees standing around-even climbing up onto one of the booths right next to us putting up Christmas decorations. That didn't change the fact that this is the best Mexican food we have found in NOLA. Just wish they would pay attention to details-$34 for lunch leads me to expect a little more professionalism.

I was in on a Wednesday evening during a pacers playoff game, it was packed, loud and fun. Ate dinner at the bar, beer selection is overwhelming, but I guess that is the purpose!   Food was awesome, hangover burger and fresh cut fries, fries are not something dumped out of a bag into a deep fryer like most joints of this nature. The wings are good but hard to eat, they are literally the entire chicken wing, honey bourbon sauce was great!  I'll be back soon.

Good burgers. We don't have Whataburger in California, so I decided to try one here. Was not disappointed. Good to try a different chain for once. Something different I noticed is that while I'm eating, the employees would regularly come ask for a refill or present to you any napkins or ketchup that you need. Good customer service!

How is this place not packed? All. The. Time. ??? Definitely best burger in The Quarter. I'm assuming best in New Orleans. Maybe the best ever. In the history of always. Go here. Enjoy the food. Keep it open for when I come back.

This is the tastiest ramen in Tucson. The broth is rich and filling. The egg preparation is the only thing lacking in this soup..overcooked, cold, and plopped in as afterthought, not seasoned. Chashu is very yummy. Way better than Oban. Karage-don is also very good. The service is busy but friendly. Go for weekday lunch to avoid the lines at this new and popular spot. I'll be back many times.

Super friendly and helpful staff, and be prepared to get dirty as you're provided a bib, gloves and scissors to tackle the hot delicious bags of seafood that come out. You can choose the type of cooking broth, spice level and order seafood by the pound. We rounded out our seafood boil with corn, sausage (small amount of thinly sliced garlic sausage) and potato, seafood rice (a decent amount of shrimp and scallops in buttery rich rice) and crispy calamari. If you prefer not to have a mountain of seafood carnage on your table, you can ask for a bucket to toss it in.. almost everything is composted, so you can feel good getting messy and filling up on seafood! Only downside is this place is smaaaaaall, so they dont take reservations.. try to pop in during an odd time and you may luck out and get a table without waiting for hours.

A great place for fresh food and a neat little bakery. Breakfast is fantastic, the signature dish "eggs provencale" is great. Very fresh and satisfying. 

The earlier the better, highly recommend you check them out!

Great burgers. I always mean to try the cheesesteak, but can't break away from the Charlie Brown, which I've been ordering since Spot was a cart on Drexel's campus.

It can get crowded in there, but that's what happens when you're serving what is in the running for best burger in the city.

Don't sleep on their specials either - the corn dogs were great!

Came here for my birthday dinner after a local on the beach recommended the place. So glad we did! The coconut shrimp appetizer was delicious. I got the crab cakes and my husband got the steak. We both loved our dishes and left super stuffed. Don't forget the complimentary rolls! Service was nice and quick for a Saturday night.

This place is alright.  They don't have many bakery goods and I did try the ube cake to go.  It looks delicious but taste like a regular cake, I barely tasted the ubeness.  I got the "taho", I guess I'm used to the clear very soft tapioca balls in the Philippines and not the chewy black ones but the main flaw with the taho was the texture of the tofu.  It's like lightly firm tofu when it should be buttery soft, silken tofu.  Where it just breaks apart when you slurp it like soup.  That's how I've always had it when I was in the Philippines of when my mom buys me some in Hawaii Chinatown.  The syrup was on point though.
Best kept secret Italian in the area. Fabulous home-made pastas and excellent service.

My favorite pastry spot in the RTM.  Biscotti is amazing, they serve La Colombe Coffee and they never run out.

Short and sweet.
Could contend for the best thin in STL if they would give you an option to have something other than that awful provel cheese.  Won't come back.

I was recommended to try this place out (particularly the cheese curds!) by my hairdresser. Really happy that my hubby and I gave it a try!

We were fortunately able to enjoy a flight of beer and a couple appetizers outside one beautiful night on their outdoor eating patio. They have a ton of different craft beers on draft and I love the fact that they offer flights- my hubby and I's favorite thing to get when at a restaurant/bar type of place. We like to talk and compare the different ones we order and then we rank our top fave to least fave. It makes for a fun date!

The Cheese Curds were very yummy! Definitely loved the dipping sauce that came with- it is kinda runny, so you may get some drips on your shirt. We also ordered the Blue Cheese Chips which were equally just as good. The service was great- would definitely go back again!

Boy do I love this place! I started going here before it got popular but it is still amazing and worth the wait. Great beer and wine selection, the food is perfect (light fair like sandwiches and salads, cheese, and bruschetta - which you must try!). Great to hang out on Sunday as well - check out Sunday school!!
Great little sushi joint! The sushi is so fresh. I highly recommend the Ocean and Bronze Pebble!
This restaurant failed to proceed my order 2 times at took 15 minutes to make my food.

I had KungPow shrimp for lunch here, it had just right among of hot spice in my meal, and it is very good portion for just $6. Also I got a choice of soul hot soup or egg drop soup as a starter. It's not a fince place but it is worm and clean. Food come out pertty quick. I will come back again to try their dinner sometime in the future.
Oh, they have a pertty good selection of Chinese vegetarian food.

I love this little place. High points: awesome drink specials and awesome food. Decent service, can be hit or miss sometimes. A great place to go with friends to kick off the rest of the night. Their late night menu is great too.
Very good sushi spot, tucked away in a small strip mall. Gyoza and the Spider roll were top notch.  Enjoyed it thoroughly.  Staff was very friendly.  Fyi, this is a byob place.
AWESOMENESS!!!    great  authentic Szechuan food... friendly service certainly one of my favorites. Twice cooked pork, Cumin lamb,  yum......Chengdu classics all good also..

We haven't been by here in some years but the TriCity shopping center is awaiting demolition and renovation. We were instantly greeted and seated.  We ordered the cheese dip(queso blanco).  

For entrées, I ordered the Vegetarian Combo and my partner ordered the Enchiladas Verdes.  I know I don't seem like the type to order a vegetarian dish but I love this one.  It comes with a whole bean layered tostada with cheese and topped with a generous amount of tasty guacamole and a cheese filled chili relleno, I opted for the cheese enchilada and the Mexican rice. It was the lunch portion but it was a whole lot to eat.  The Enchiladas Verdes lunch portion comes with two large chicken enchiladas covered with their verde sauce and then covered with a seasoned sour cream sauce. The dish came with one side dish;  rice was chosen.  The chips and salsa were plentiful throughout the meal.

The service was speedy and pleasant.  If you're on Ulmerton around Belcher and are craving a big plate of Mexican food, come fill your face at Carmelita's.
Good food and seemed authentic to an American whose never been to Greece. Waitress served wrong drink.

Rincon Beach Club is one of the most beautiful places in all of California! Having attended numerous weddings and events at Rincon I can say there is no better place to have your event. With incredible food, great service and an amazing ocean view I would recommend this venue to anyone planning an event in The Santa Barbara Area.

Stayed here for 5 days, 4 nights for Christmas for less than $200/night for a deluxe room. Great value and location. The hotel was gorgeous for the holidays. The service was incredible and the employees are top notch. We got to check in to our rooms early also which was lovely after a red-eye from California. Our room was very nice and quiet (5th level, facing pool). We got a $100 voucher that we were able to use at the jazz club and coffee house which made it even better (the jazz place is one of the best in the city). I would totally recommend it for anyone coming to New Orleans. We were very, very happy with our choice.

You won't find better toasted ravioli than you can find here. I promise. 

The wine is amazing. The atmosphere is amazing. This place is definitely a treat. I would choose this place over every other Italian restaurant in St. Louis, and while that statement is bold, it's definitely true.

We stopped in last night for dinner and really enjoyed this place. The food was great as was the service. We did find their prices were a little high given the quantity of food you get, but we are looking forward to trying their lunch buffet which is a much more attractively priced option.

District is definitely good, but it's more like eating a piece of cake. Personal rule, if the line is past the tap handles, it's not worth the wait. 

The cinnamon roll doesn't get a lot of love but its the best thing on their menu. They torch it right before serving to you. That and coffee is pretty awesome.
Stopped in on a hot day craving some mac. Been planning to come here for awhile. I immediately ordered The Rittenhouse. It was delicious and I would definitely come here again.

Best Sushi I have ever had. I don't know if i would just call it sushi, because it's so much more. I would consider myself a sushi connoisseur, lived in Japan for two years, had sushi in San Fran, San Diego, LA, Florida, and all over. I know a lot of people complain and say this isn't "traditional sushi" like they actually know what they are talking about. So i'll tell you, traditional sushi is plain fish on rice or a roll with one fish in it. There is only so far you can go with flavor when dealing with a piece of fish with no sauce on it. Americanized sushi tastes so much better....period. 
      At Sakana my girlfriend and I got the Pink Bear roll (amazing, made love to my taste buds), the Garlic Albacore (melts in your mouth, delicious), habanero yellowtail belly (still in amazement), Lobster Melt roll (filling but so much flavor its like a flavor bomb went off in your mouth). The last roll wasn't my favorite and my girlfriend didn't really like it, it was the blue fin specialty roll they had.
      This place has really good sauce-sushi combinations, and I love spicy so this was right up my alley. My girlfriend and I are going back again for our second day in a row. As for price, we got all of this for $59 so it was actually cheaper than I expected it to be.

The first time I was here, it was a little crowded and I was the first to arrive for a party of 6. They didn't act like this was a problem at all and moved a few tables around to seat us, then right after we ordered a larger, more comfortable table opened and they moved us over. They acted like they were inconveniencing us and apologized a million times, then sent over an order of rock shrimp tempura on the house. Our waitress mentioned that the tuna was excellent that day so I had some sashimi, and she was right! I also shared the special roll of the day and some tuna and avocado rolls, and everything was really fresh and satisfying. Everyone at the table seemed to enjoy what they ordered and the service was great. I just made a reservation to go back for my birthday!


UPDATE: My birthday was an amazing success. Our server was so sweet and again the fish was so fresh and beautiful. This time the rock shrimp tempura was served in a wasabi aioli and was even better than last time. Also they are participating in foie gras week, and one of my friends did order that dish - I didn't try it but everyone who did seemed to like it. Izumi is now my go-to sushi spot, they make me so happy.

After much deliberation, mostly due to sour reviews here on Yelp, I decided to get my burger on last night. We arrived to find a lot of people hangin' out front waiting. Curses! The Yelpers were right I thought. However, we tempted the gods and continued in. Asked the hostess if there was a wait, and we were promptly seated outside on the patio after zero waiting. The only caveat, we can't order alcohol on the patio: no big deal.

Our server was swamped and he made sure to let us know he would be back around to us. After about five minutes he returned, and we ordered the fried pickle chips, crab cakes, Pimento burger, and the Woodstock. The pickle chips were great, the crab cake was spiced out and delish. Both of our burgers were cooked exactly how we ordered, and we left happy and with our gullets full. 

tl;dr: new restaurant - good food - had no problems - would recommend

I get takeout from here for lunch every so often, and today's curry has motivated me to write a review, finally. I got the mussaman vegetarian curry and it is AMAZING!!  The lunch special is a great deal and this curry is just so delicious.  Just enough spiciness, peanuts come in the sauce.. Just overjoyed with my lunch today!

The gator gumbo is pretty solid - rich with flavor but a little on the salty side. You can definitely tell that it's made from a well-loved recipe. I would highly recommend this dish for anyone who's first coming to Reading Terminal!

The coffee and bentons bacon was good, but I wouldn't order the frittata again, under cooked so runny in the middle, too much caramelized onion and the dressing on the arugula was pouring off the plate. Made for a soggy mess.

What can I say? The donuts are HUGE and DELICIOUS! They served as our breakfast on two different occasions. We ordered takeout so I don't have a good read on the store vibe...but if you're staying near or passing through the 2200 block of Magazine Street, it's worth a stop. Hopefully we'll be able to try the sliders next time!
Deserves zero stars. Tastiest items on the menu are the french fries served with the kids tacos.
I wish there was a time I went here that I didn't have to deal with a hellacious line that doesn't move. I love the salads and the beg cheesesteak is a solid option.

As we have just moved to Conshohoken we wanted to find a nice coffee place that also offered desserts. This is that place. The lattes are delicious. And the place has two rooms inside to chill in, as well as a back  and front yard with tables to enjoy when the weather is nice. I feel this makes it kid and doggie friendly. $4 for a coffee and $3 for a dessert, not to shabby. Take a friend and you will easily hit their $10 credit card min. We will be teg customers from now on.

We had the Onion Rings to start, Excellent!

Next we had the Bone In New York Strips, Lyonnaise Potatoes, Peas. I had the house Cabernet which was really good. 

The service is fantastic. The waitstaff were accommodating and attentive. 

Now, the steaks were not what I expected. They reminded me of something I could have purchased at any mud to low level steakhouse. Definitely not Ruth Chris. My expectation from a classic steakhouse is too notch steaks, all else can be a bit less than stellar, but not the meat. 

I will try the restaurant again to give them the benefit of the doubt.
Been there several times.  Its always delicious!  Calamari & cheeseburger enveloped with pizza dough are out of this world!

Great doughnuts, bagels, & coffee. We enjoy hitting this place for their breakfast bagel sandwiches and the occasional doughnut. Their coffee is great as well. We enjoy the multitude of different flavored cream cheeses they offer. The maple bacon doughnuts are to die for, but usually sell out quick. Best bet is to reserve them the day before if you would like to try them.

Opening day drive thru at 6:30 PM: AMAZING!
They totally ROCKED it! The line and amount of people was super crazy but we were out in about 25 minutes. Well worth it for my chicken nugget meal! I'm so happy to have this in Reno. I hope they keep up the GREAT work!

Wow. Great prices. You walk into and see tasty homemade treats on your right. The music is perfect and fits the nice mood. The place is very fancy and looks very nice. The fried pickles are really great. You must try them. They have homemade lemonades that taste really juicy and sweet. Really good desert. Expensive but it's should be because it is very nice.

This is a tiny little restaurant hidden behind panda express and starbucks. In a way I would like to call it a hidden treasure. It wasn't easy for us to spot this place. Infact, we were looking for Santa Barbara Chicken Ranch went we happened to come across this place. It seems like a family owned restaurant with the entire family working in the kitchen and the kids serving the tables. I totally loved the food here. Especially the pizza dough seemed so fresh and tasty. Must be a secret down their family. ;) we called for chicken parmesan and one of their small sized pizzas and loved both. They also served us some tiramisu - which was on the house. They also had some beer on the tap and wines on their menu. 
A tiny and beautiful restaurant, I would surely like to re-visit.

We went to Nauti Mermaid on a Tuesday evening (no reservation, two people) and were seated immediately. The space is quaint but really cute! The food came out quickly and it was EXCELLENT! The salmon, potatoes and veggies were so tasty. I also tried the fish club - mmmm!! I'll definitely be back.

Took the Sunday brunch cruise and was pretty disappointed. As many people have already stated, the food is terrible, but the service was great. If you're dying to be surrounded by a horde of enormous sweaty people on a vessel, moving down a river, then this is your jam. I feel like they may have over booked it, because once the band came on, there was zero floor space around them. Speaking of the band... holy boring. They looked like they were at their own funeral. I'm pretty sure the horn player fell asleep a time or two. I was looking forward to hearing some loud lively stuff, but these guys couldn't draw a crowd to save their lives. Save your money and head on over to Frenchmen St. It's a better, less-touristy vibe, with much better music and food.

Kind of a hit and miss place depending on what you order. We got the Santa Fe pancakes and the sweet potato pancakes. Santa Fe was absolutely delicious. I loved the Mia of maple syrup and sour cream and salsa toppings. Sweet potato was a bit of a let down because it didn't actually taste anything like sweet potatoes at all haha! We were so surprised we'd thought they'd gotten our order wrong but when we asked them they explained it's because they don't mash sweet potatoes to make them, they use sweet potato flakes.

Alma Llanera is a trip to the heart of Venezuela . We were starving for real Arepas and Empanadas and this place delivered perfectly . Everything was fresh and huge delicious  portions. We have tried other Venezuelan Resturants around florida and   Alma Llanera is the top on our list. Viva Venezuela  !! We will be back !!

I really enjoyed the service and attention from the staff at this hotel. For a weekend getaway, this is a nice option. The views over the water are exceptional. The restaurant was convenient and delicious. Once in the stress melts off. Anything needed was brought to the door for the most part and everyone was pleasant from the moment you step in to the second you drive off. Really happy and will most likely visit again!

Absolutely amazing! Located in a cool area of Nashville by Vanderbilt University. Service is very friendly and the breakfast was awesome. This is a absolute must if you're visiting Nashville for a few days. We had the Southern Benny and it was one of the best breakfast meals I've had, period. They are most known for their East Nasty, which looked really good. You also get a good cup of coffee. Get their early - the line can get long but it's worth the wait.
So many great options here! Everything made fresh when you order. Love the fresh rolls, veggie dumplings, and noodle soup! The owner is very engaged in his business and it shows.
Great fish & shrimp tacos!!! Found this place by asking a local. Really yummy.
Odessa roll was awesome! Fresh fish and I don't normally eat tempura but this has been the best. Presentation gives it that extra star. Coming here for the lunch special would make it 4.6 stars.

Delicious!!!!! Started out with a French 75-light and bubbly but the perfect amount of alcohol followed by the alligator which was very good!   Had the trio: red beans and rice, jumbalya and gumbo. Oh my word was every bite amazing!!!

It seems unfair to write a review after having been here only once, so I'll have to go back for round two sometime soon, but my initial impression is that this place is okay. It certainly wasn't bad, but it didn't blow me away. Perhaps I need to try something other than a plain croissant, but at the time what I really wanted was something lunch-like, and everything they had (as far as I could tell) had meat in it. Something vegetarian along the lines of their turkey sandwich and/or ham and cheese croissant (perhaps a spinach and feta croissant) would've been awesome. Maybe I needed to ask. 

In any event, it's a bustling little place and people obviously love it. But it seemed that you kind of needed to know what to order, since there wasn't a ton on display and there wasn't a list or anything. Next time I'll have to read the Yelp reviews and figure out what to ask for. :)

FOOD: I went in in time to get the $1 pizza slices and was told fresh ones would be coming out shortly so I waited and it took about 6 minuets which was also the quoted time. When I got my pizza (pineapple and ham), I took off one of the pineapples and it just kind of tasted not fresh. My first slice had cheese falling off of it and I was left with just pizza sauce because the cheese just wouldn't stay on the pizza! The ranch made it taste way better though. Granted it wasn't the worst pizza I've had by far, it wasn't the best. If it's supposed to resemble New York pizza, it didn't even come close. However, if you're looking for a quick lunch fix, this is the place. 

SERVICE: The employees were all very nice and even brought my pizza out to me. One thing that stuck out to me though was that even though it was practically dead aside from me, there was still a booth that hadn't even been wiped down. Their store is very modern and has a great atmosphere although the music was kind of slow. As well, the employees were on the phones in plain sight. I don't really care about that, but personally I feel phones should be okay if everything else is done and with a dirty table in plain sight, it clearly wasn't all done. All in all, the place is very nice and is like to see more business here. 
As well, they offered me some free slices since they'd be thrown out anyways. They also offered their maintenance worker which I loved because usually places just throw them out. 

RATING: 4/5 stars because of the dirty table and the pizza quality.

We ate here last week and the cakes were disgusting. My friends and I were staying at the dumpy hotel Ramada in Philly, and decided to eat here for dinner. We decided to have desserts here, and we ordered different cakes. I ordered the red velvet cake which tasted normal, but the chocolate cakes were horrific!  My friend Brett ordered the Chocolate coconut cake, and my friend Frank got the Chocolate Mousse cake. The frosting tasted like nail polish! Yes! Nail polish!  When we told our waitress, she told her manager about it, but he didn't try to fix the problem. We told the waitress to taste the frosting, and she even agreed that both cakes tasted like nail polish. I'm guessing that whoever baked the cake probably just had their nails done, and got some of the nail solution in the frosting. Pretty gross.

The service was solid and friendly. The food was good, but it was a little over-priced. I got the Longhorn burger and ordered it medium rare. It was very yummy. Also, their large fries is enough to feed two people. 

Their milkshake game is a little weak. Oh, and if you want to have a conversation with someone, they play their music a little too loud. Other than those things, it's a solid place for groups, and it has a quirky atmosphere.

Impression: The good thing is that there are like 5-6 of these kinds of Asian Chinese bakeries around Chinatown- Mong Kok is another one that sells the same get up: sesame balls, roll cakes, taro buns, egg tarts, meat buns, ham and cheese breads- your typical Hong Kong South East Asian kinds of bakeries that sell their fares for less than 1$ each. The bad thing is, b/c it is the same as the rest, it may be hard to find something you've never tried before- but their cheese cakes looked to be their stand apart from other bakeries. This is the only "Asian" bakery on this street across from Nine Ting, the new Taiwanese popcorn chicken, right by Red King BBQ, and Wong Wong Restaurant. It's a solid Chinese bakery- neither fancy nor cheap and poor quality, neither special or bland but solid if you're looking for the typical Chinese desserts and pastries 

Because it's cheap, feel free to load up on a large stash of goodies! Egg tarts were 0.80$, sesame balls were also 0.80$ and the green tea roll cake was only 3.50$. I like to take these treats home and eat them slowly over the next few days. The sesame balls and the tarts taste great if you stick them in the microwave and zap it for 30 seconds to 1 min. Pair it with some good tea and you got yourself a nice afternoon tea for your studies/work/friends

Took my husband here on his birthday.  The food, although good, was skimpy on the portions.  My husband had the salmon, which was small and undercooked.  I had the pasta with lobster and again, the portion was small.  The cheese board was overpriced for what we got. I have had much larger cheese boards with more accompaniments and less pricey.  For what I paid, I thought the portions could have been larger.  The dessert menu was very limited.  The service was impeccable and I like that it was a BYOB.  Don't think that I would return.

The service is slow (20+ minutes for a drink? It's not like I ordered a Pousse-Cafe, y'all, it was a basic Old Fashioned; you know? a very quick drink to prepare.). My guest was disappointed that the chicken breast is boneless: a couple of large chicken fingers was his description of the 2 piece meal he ordered. The chairs aren't very comfortable, either. I gave Old Standard Fried Chicken two tries on two consecutive nights, and I will not be back. Overrated, overpriced, and slower than December honey will be my description of the place when asked.

Double check your order because they are new and unorganized.  That said, I like spicy chicken and for fast food, they do it right.  I recommend the spicy fried chicken vs the chicken strips.  I'll be posting review updates over time because like I said, this place is new.  Glad they moved to the area.

Not closed. They have temporary hours right now because the owner who usually is the one who seats you and cooks the food is travelling, so she has friends and family helping.  So, with that said, last night we came to eat and I have to admit, was the best dinner I've had here from the handful of times I've dined at this restaurant.  My family and I always order the same thing here: kitfo (cooked medium) although they say rare is the way it should be eaten, and zilzil tibs which is a sautéed beef dish with caramelized onions and spices.  However, last night, the serving size was bigger, and it was much more flavorful.  
The server was on point. He kept our water glasses full, and was so very polite. The lady who cooked the food came out and asked if we enjoyed the food.  
I think when the owner comes back, she should consider hiring a server to help her because it seems as though when she works alone, the food and service is affected. 
I hope this place doesn't close since my family really loves Ethiopian cuisine, and our favorite place is actually in Sacramento.

Great deal for happy hour -- fifty cent raw oysters, one dollar fried oysters, 50% off drinks.

Unfortunately, other than the oysters and drinks we were a little disappointed. The Etoufee was moderately tasty but very small for the prince, the complementary bread was frankly inexcusably stale and un-appetizing and the foie gras terrine was on the edge of frozen when it came out.

Come for the happy hour drinks and oysters but skip the rest.

Stopped in today.  Pleasantly surprised.  People behind the counter are SUPER nice.  Ordered two Chicago hot dogs.  They were better than Portillo's in Chicago. Service was very quick.  They have several different types of dogs on the menu including chili, slaw, etc.  
I will return.  Definitely.

I love Hot Diggity! I think their dogs are the best vegan dogs I have had. The bread is great, too. My favorite dog is the fiesta dog (minus the sour cream), as I love guacamole. I also like the one with the chili. The fries are good. Staff is very friendly.

I would give the restaurant five stars because I really love the hot dogs, but $6.99 is quite steep for a delivery fee. I wouldn't mind $2 or so. I won't be ordering the food to be delivered again.
Havent had this place since Chicago and was better than I remembered... Had the Chicago special and it came out hot and delicious... Order the garlic fries - they're fantastic

Yelpers have seriously dropped the ball on this one, I just wasted an hour and a half going to this place only to be served a shit ton of dissatisfaction. First, they flat out lied to me that they could not validate my restaurant.com certificate. My bad, I guess I should've listened to the one yelper that shared the same experience. Don't bother ordering $10 shrimp tacos, the shrimp are flavorless and the "soft corn tacos" were an abomination that I really don't know how to describe properly. I had heard such great things about their ceviche, so i decided to order the campechana. It is now sitting in my refrigerator until I figure out a way to salvage the shrimp from that disaster. The octopus is a total loss though. If you don't know how to prepare octopus without turning it into shoe leather,  do not serve it at your establishment. I honestly feel embarrassed for these people. I'm pretty certain it's generally a bad idea to throw some seafood in a cup with a bunch of ketchup and sugar, and have the balls to think that it's ok. If I could give negative stars, I would. I hope this place shuts down. The only positive is that my senior citizen relative enjoyed the asada burrito. If she had been disappointed I probably would have written a much longer review of this nightmare. It is a disgrace to food trucks across this great nation. Save your money and ffs don't support this madness.
Delicious food! Their hot sauce is one of the best I've ever had so flavorful and actually spicy which is nice!

A group of us visited La Casona for a friend's birthday.  The mofongo is amazing, great red sangria and wonderful little empanadillas for an appetizer.  The portion size is huge at a very low price.  I got the shrimpt mofongo.  Others at the table got chicken and steak mofongo.  No complaints except for the fried plantains which were dry and had zero flavor.  We had to soak them in the garlic dipping sauce to make them worth eating.  

Service leaves something to be desired but I don't think the intention is to be rude, just not top notch.  You can tell this is a family run business as the chef came from the kitchen to chat with the diners and the older gentleman behind the bar.  It seemed like a mother, father and son dynamic.  The female was extremely nice and came to the table to make sure the food was ok and to tell our friend happy birthday.  One odd note, they seem to close whenever they want.  We arrive at 7pm and the place was full with exception of three tables.  As soon as we came in, they turned the "open" sign to "closed" and would not accept any more diners.  

All in all, great experience and would definitely go back and recommend to others.

Latte was decent but the place has all the charm of a fast food restaurant. It's not very conducive to lingering, which is exactly what I want when I visit a cafe. 

Also tried their biscuits and gravy. Odd offering for a cafe, but whatever. Two sliced and slightly toasted biscuits with a dollop of fairly bland gravy on each slice. I guess someone in the kitchen didn't want to have a messy plate to clean afterwards. Disappointing. 

If someone could combine the coffee of 6 North with the charm and atmo of Picasso's Coffee House (horrible capos by the way), they would have a winner. Second visit, but drive-thru or drive on by in future.

Was here for about 12 days for a convention and came here almost every single day, and it was my favorite part of the day. The servers are incredibly friendly and the food was amazing. The first day I had the Papa's French toast, and that's when I fell in love with the place. Never had French toast rolled in corn flakes and that really made it special. Will recommend this place to all that want a nice friendly atmosphere and delicious food.

This place IS NEVER EVER open past 9pm or 9:30pm. They refuse service on a constant basis. The falsely advertise being open until 10pm. Their food is meh, but they are the only place in for sushi in the area. Do not believe their hours. If you are lucky to get past 9pm, you will be rushed at, and judged. Why are they even in business if they don't want customers? Tonight was my LAST attempt to eat here.

Was in Tucson on business and the Trident Grill was recommended by the customer I was visiting.  Great food (apps and entrees), excellent selection of beers at the bar, and a very lively, fun, and comfortable atmosphere.  I don't envision in being in Tucson very often but if I ever am I will definitely eat at the Trident again!!

I've heard SO many great things about this place and I was finally able to try it today. We arrived around 3:30pm and the place was empty... like no customers, no staff members. We walked further inside, past the hostess stand back towards the bar before someone randomly passed by and noticed us. The female who noticed us was very kind, welcoming and apologized for the wait. She sat us immediately and explained the "all you can eat special" and went to find our server. Well, about 10ish mins later she comes back and apologizes again saying she cannot locate our server but would get us drinks. Finally, our server was located and came back with the girl to deliver our drinks and took our order. We ordered General Tsos chicken, tuna avocado roll, California roll, Philly roll, yummy yummy roll and the Philly roll. Everything was good, except the sushi has a fishy after taste. Tuna shouldn't be fishy. I expect salmon to have a slight fishy taste, but not tuna. So, the all you can eat is cool but there's a catch- YOU HAVE TO EAT IT ALL, or else you'll be charged a surcharge and you cannot take anything to go. Luckily, since it was our first time eating here we were cut some slack and were able to take some food to go and not charged the surcharge. I still can't get over the fishy taste of the sushi so I dont know if I'll be back.. I'll have to think about it.

Just ok. Our group had salads and Impossible Burgers. The meatless burger. Yeah, it was edible, but not something worth more than actual meat unless you're veggie. Salads were also just OK.  Good draft beer prices though.

The food is Szechuan at its best. The food is HOT!  I highly recommend the Dan-Dan noodles at the spice level they give. 

The decor provides are a modern industrial ambiences that is more suited for a Modern American restaurant instead of an authentic Szechuan restaurant.  

My only negative about this place is that its really pricy eating alone.
Food was not fresh. The Jalapeños on my Cliff Drive roll looked like it had been out since last night. I did not trust eating the food.
Came here a second time. Unless you want food poisoning like I'm going through as of right now, don't come here.

RAIDER NATION FOR LIFE ~~ RN4L

This location of Famous Sam's is the Die Hard Raiders Booster Club Tucson Chapter's home base and because of that simple fact, I get a tug in my heart, a tear in my eye...awww hell, I get all verklempt. Raider Nation, baby!!!

So yeah, I'm going with 4 stars because the owners basically hand this place over to Raiders fans on game day and their staff works EXTRA hard trying to keep the sea of silver and black happy and for the most part they truly do keep all the patrons happy. 

As for the food - it's fair, probably above fair. The wings are average - the "hot" isn't really hot at all. Chicken strips are fantastic - meaty, moist and BIG!! Steak fingers are just okay. The Jalapeno Bottle Caps are pretty good if you like spicy. Most places seem to use very mild jalapenos for a lot of their dishes like nachos so I was expecting to be bored with the bottle caps. WRONG. They're spicy little battered and fried sliced jalapenos. Delicious! And I've always been a fan of Famous Sam's pastrami sandwiches. It's been years since I had one and they're still as tasty as I remember them. Mmm, mmm, good. 

I must say that Famous Sam's fails in the French fry department. Despite numerous attempts, every time we order fries or they are included as part of our meal, they come to the table limp and undercooked. Recently we ordered fries with nacho cheese sauce and the fries were literally uncooked in the middle. Had to send them back after explaining the raw potato product and our server brought us a new plate. Excited to finally get the fries and dip them, L & I each took a bite and the look of disappointment appeared on our faces. They were just as bad as the first helping. We explained to our server that the fries were inedible but we did not wish to send them back again. She checked on us a few more times throughout the game for beer and water and even mentioned the uneaten fries and how she knew they were unacceptable. But when our bill came, guess what was still on there? That's right - the fries. A quick talk with the manager fixed remedied the situation and all was right with the world again. 

How could it not be? After all, the RAIDERS WON!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

3.5 STARS for this Embassy Suites despite it being in one of the worst tourist cities that I have ever traveled to.  The freeway and airport proximity is nice but the neighborhood in itself is not very well lit.  In other words, I didn't feel safe walking outside on the streets.  

Other good things about this hotel is the lobby which was outfitted with lots of places to sit and mingle.  The check-in area was composed of individual stands and not a traditional big front desk thing.  For signing up for their Hilton Honors program, Embassy gave my whole party WiFi coupon codes for each of us to use for our devices for the entire stay.  Make sure if you stay there, join their program.  It's free wifi, you won't have wifi unless you enroll in their program.

As usual, Embassy has their free morning breakfast as well as their evening cocktail happy hour usually composed of beer, wine, and well spirit cocktails.  Free booze is free booze so that was cool.

The parking wasn't free but it was $9 per night to self park and the garage is a bit challenging to navigate.  None of the hotels that I visited on this recent trip had free hotel parking.  Seems like that perk has long gone now.

The beds were OK, the TV was tremendously smaller than what I expected.  Is a 40 inch TV not the expectation nowadays?  Housekeeping was very attentive to my request for more towels.  So why the low-ish rating?  Well it's Tampa and most likely, a place I won't come back to.  However,if you were to stay somewhere in the area, this place is a decent option.

Our family loves Uncle Maddios! We love that we can each order our OWN personal pizza just the way we like it! They "build" your pizza right in front of you with your choice  of toppings (just like Moe's or Chipolte) and then finish it off in the oven. Fresh, hot pizza is at your table in about 5 minutes. You can make a custom pizza or chose some of their unique speciality pizzas- I love the Steak & Blue pizza and my husband loves the Mushroom Truffle. They also have gluten free crust and Vegan Daiya cheese which my 2 Vegan daughters appreciate.

I will never (never say never) eat here again. Our table of four was expecting a fabulous experience in a classic Italian setting. What happened was quite the contrary. The service was untrained and uneven. The main course came before the appetizers (the amount of mussels for cost was pathetic). All of the orders had food delivered incorrectly and had to be taken back for adjustments. The "steamed" vegetables were raw, the Mahi Mahi was so dry it couldn't be swallowed. I sent my dinner back refusing any more indignation and was still charged. With much discussion with management and server to adjust an inflated, incorrect bill, and very little apologies, we left shaken and unhappy.

This place has grown on me over the years. I find myself going here more and more, despite the (fantastic) proliferation of coffee places in the northern Camden County area. It's just a solid place to come back to again and again, and hopefully this'll give you some insight into why.

Let's start with the seating. It's got a lot of different areas to hang out; aside from two large seating areas on either side of the counter, there's an awesome courtyard right on the corner of Haddon and Redman Avenues and plenty of sidewalk seating out front for the warmer months. Not enough places in the suburbs have outside areas for hanging out, so these spots for people - and puppy - watching is much appreciated.

Their coffee's always been pretty good, and I think they keep switching up what beans they get. From what I can remember, I've seen Rival Brothers, Square One. They do pour overs, which I love, and they've got some more exotic things sometimes, like the Gibraltar (a variation on a cortado) and the "Americola", a fascinating mix of Mexican coke and a shot of espresso. To eat, there've got a variety of pastries like muffins and homemade pop tarts and quiches.

Also, it's worth noting that this is one of the only coffee places open on a late Sunday afternoon/early evening worth going. There're a lot of coffee places around here, but they all seem to close between 1 and 3PM. For years now, Jersey Java's open open til 6PM on Sundays, which I really appreciate. I don't know if the other places think people just hide out at home on Sunday afternoons or what, but it's great this place stays open.
The food, drinks and ambiance were great! We ordered three different types of empanadas and two main courses. Great Friday night dinner spot.

Man oh man was this some delicious, fresh amazing seafood. The service was prompt and all the food was everything we thought it would be. We tried the BBQ Shrimp, Boiled Shrimp and Hubby had the Seafood Quesadilla. Boiled Shrimp was my favorite but everything was so good. Definitely a must try.

I wish this place was better being in my neighborhood and in walking distance. But it's pretty mediocre. I wish they'd address the gummy flour tacos. The fillings - when they're hot - are pretty good but honestly the tacos ruin it.

My favorite -- the chicken pot pie on Sundays and their herbal iced tea!  Much of the rest of their food is good -- I try to avoid the fried foods as my heart isn't appreciating those these days, but the sweet potatoes, cauliflower (OMG -- yum), and banana pudding are pretty darned good.
Definitely give this place a stop if you enjoy good old comfort food.

I literally just came home for the burgerking marlton location. I wanted to try the "new chicken sandwich". I opened up the sandwich and it looked disgusting. It was small, burnt (some of it was black) and dry! I decided to pull it apart and try it. It tasted even worse than it looked. This is bad! I had a horrible feeling driving up to this location as the road conditions were horrible and it looked as if they were closed. I Should have went with my instincts. I will never go back to this location!
Love This Place! Great Good and Great Fast Service.  Kevin, The Bartender Is Excellent!
If you are looking for a healthy, light and refreshing meal this is the place to go. The staff is very friendly and the food is pretty good too.
Awesome Indian cakes. Had to try them. Staff was chill & fun. Waiter explained the items we asked about very well. My dish was tasty even with the anchovies :)

What a joke of a place. Placed an online order around 2:30pm on a Saturday afternoon. After an hour or so with no food, I call, no answer (to a cell phone mind you). I decide to take a trip there to see what's going on (since my credit card was charged). They said they just opened, even though the website said they've been open since noon. Ok, looks like a glitch in the system that left me hungry. No problem, you would think they would try and resolve the issue by offering to make the food, or giving me some sort of discount/credit/whatever to make me happy. Instead the guy grabs the order off the printer and says I need to call their online ordering vender to get my money back. Talk about terrible customer service. They are destined for failure.

Solid homey Italian food in a byob setting. The waitstaff and manager were very accomodating. The food was solid homestyle Italian, not much flair and small portions, but very delicious. Some of the best tomato based sauces in Philly can be found here. The restaurant is very loud and there can be a long line, even at an early hour, but all in all I would recommend the place. Only three desserts to choose from and I thought the apple one was by far the best.

Busy place.  I was disappointed since the reviews were so high I thought it under delivered.  

We came in on a Friday morning around 10am.  I had the French toast and it came out cold. The syrup was cold also, but I ate everything.   The fruit was yummy but I was surprised they would cut up and serve unripe cantaloupe. I ordered a cup of drip coffee and the coffee was excellent.  Serve your self water, it was unfiltered and tasted nasty.

After we place our order and paid and tipped....we were told food will take 25 to 30 minutes to receive.  This would have been nice to know prior to ordering.

My son had the build your own potato with gravy and my husband had same with salsa.  They  both seem to enjoy it but both mentioned they didn't have enough potato?

One star for coffee and one star for the good location. Bathroom was dirty.

OMG. I finally gave it a try and what a waste of my time! Me and my significant other decided to give ourselves a break from looking at houses for hours. We came here found a table and nothing else was accomplished except I did get my sweet tea. It was downhill from there. We got there at 3 and we left at 3:52. We never got our drinks we ordered with my sweet tea. All the manager could say was the bar is backed up I'm sorry. We never got our apps or any other food. Only the sweet tea in 45 mins. No drinks we ordered or anything else. Our server walked around like she wasn't bothered and didn't have a care in the world. Just taking a stroll around the area and had such a calm passive attitude about how long it was taking. Horrible first experience. Won't be going back even with the kids.

Always delicious. Fresh, beautifully prepared food. This is a must-visit locale anytime I'm in STL. Wait staff is always very nice and friendly. Sometimes you have to wait for your food but it's a tapas restaurant; things come out as they're prepared. In nice weather I always enjoy the outdoors seating and summer drinks. In winter it's cozier seating inside this old gas-station turned restaurant. Fun & funky decor. But come for the food! Best hummus (King of Kings) but just know it's heavy on the tahini (it's in the middle so you can swirl in as much as you'd like). Zucchini carpaccio (it's actually grilled think ribbons) is sublime. Charred tomato bruschetta... these are my go-to three choices and it makes for an amazing and delicious vegetarian lunch. My friends always get the egg salad (w/anchovy) and rave about it.  Home made breads. The larger dishes all look beautiful and scrumptious. They also do an honest and generous wine pour-/ which I always appreciate!

Food was fairly good. ( Chefs obviously know what they are doing, & use care. ) The big salad I had was good, except it was mostly iceberg lettuce. In 2016, other options like redhead, or spinach would be great. Our waitress wasn't friendly. Her name was Tracy.

Phenomenal food. The stuffed dates app was amazing, a symphony of flavors. The dueling bread app was great too. The midsize plate of grilled octopus was incredible, so perfectly cooked and seasoned just enough to flavor while still letting the subtle flavors of the meat come through. A true gastro pub.

The atmosphere of this restaurant is very appealing, however if you'd like to drink hot water disguise this coffee this is the place you belong! I ordered the avocado toast which was very good my son ordered pancakes and bacon and the bacon was practically raw and had to be sent back to be cooked. I told the waiter to not give my husband his English muffin because he can't have gluten and there it was on the dish and then he took it off when I reminded him, the waiter that is but his hands.I also asked for egg whites with cheese on the side but was charged for nasty home fries and a horrible English muffin as well. I do not recommend this place as after the hot water disguise as coffee was replaced with the French press that too is hot water disguised as coffee. We are avid coffee drinker's so after our meal we went to Starbucks to get real coffee.  Save your money and go somewhere else.

Amazing sushi! It tasted fresh and yummy! We brought our own wine and ordered a few appetizers to share but when it came to sushi we did not want to share! That's because it was delicious! Will definitely be back!

Ordered a 1/2 chicken combo in drive through.  Get to window and they wanted confirm a 14 piece chicken combo which they said they did not have.  Clarified that the order was a 4 piece half chicken combo.  Ran my card for $14 when the order board said $8.70 price.  I questioned and they said our prices went up
 yesterday.  She did not care what the price said.  Asked for the store manager, assistant came to window, also stated price went up and didn't care and even argued.  She agreed to call the manager for the stores in Carson.  Came back and said we can refund the money or you have to pay the higher price.  HORRIBLE the training and operations management.  AVOID THIS LOCATION AT ALL COSTS.

I stop by here every morning for coffee, so good! There breakfast is really great too, Brie stuffed French toast and chocolate croissants are to die for. Wait staff is always very friendly. Can't say enough good things about this place.

I was in town for a wedding this past weekend and my husband and I needed a place to grab breakfast. We loved Henry's so much we came here twice! I had a breakfast bagel sandwich and the breakfast burrito. Both sandwiches were delicious and fresh! The coffee is hot and strong. The staff at Henry's are friendly. We will definitely return when we are in the area.

Place is super cool they have tons of different Burbon to try. Wait was very short to get in and sit down. Everyone treats you like a friend when you walk in especally from giving me shit about my Chicago blackhawks credit card. Lol. We sat down for breakfast and by far they have the best biscuits and gravy I have had to day. The pineapple mimosas were stellar as well. Give this little hole in the wall a shot. Well worth it!

I seriously wake up at 7 AM thinking about these cheesesteaks-- Best cheesesteak I've ever had. Period. 
Choice of American, Wiz, or Provolone.

Great cheesefries, too. They are the crinkle fries with a side of wiz.

Steve's Prince of Steaks is second.

I almost hate to write too glowing of a review for this place because I worry people will discover it and the lines will become ridiculous! But it's really too good not to share. A friend and I stumbled across this place one day and it's now become our go-to. Whatever you do, GET THE TILAPIA BURRTO. Don't let the captain crunch scare you because somehow it works. The short rib tacos sell out if you arrive too late in the day, but I actually prefer the chicken anyway. And the curry is sweet, savory, and piping hot. The katsu is probably my least favorite thing on the menu, and I even love that. Everything from the tortilla to the rice, and even the garnishes and sauces at this place are perfectly made and balanced. DEFINITELY worth a visit!

Their bathroom was clean, and service was good, but the food was not. Santa Barbara has some of the best Thai food I've had, and this place definitely does not live up to the standards. The food was so incredibly bland, and that's one weird you really should not use to describe Thai food. The presentation was so bizarre, it made the food unappetizing. We ordered drunken noodles, curries and fried rice, and everything just tasted so average. There are better options in the area, so I won't be back.

I tried this place for the first time recently for my fiancées birthday .. We both liked it very much .. The place was very nice .. The food was fantastic .. We started with the duck salad and rolls, the duck was cooked perfectly, the butter that came with the rolls was tasty ..  For the main courses I tried the short rib stroganoff which is really a must try, and my fiancée had the veal lasagna .. Both were amazing and the meat was cooked very well .. For the dessert we had the salted chocolate slice and the pucker up citrus .. Both very good .. I highly recommend the place, especially for dates and would definitely go back there again ..

This was hands down one of the worst dining experiences that I've ever had in Philadelphia.  Ultimately, Xochitl gets one star because I do not have a "no star" option.  My friend and I dined here last night for restaurant week and had really been looking forward to it.  Neither of us had been before, so we thought Philadelphia's Restaurant Week would be a great place to give it a shot.  WRONG.

We arrived on time for our 7 pm reservation and were asked to wait in the bar area until our table was ready.  Not a problem.  And understandable on a Friday evening. Although the restaurant was not at capacity we didn't think twice about being asked to wait. About five minutes later, we were seated and our very nice server came to explain the menu and the customizable guacamole.  

We made our guacamole selection and placed the order for the remainder of our 3 courses.  As far as the food goes, the guacamole was the best thing we had.  I ordered sangria that was supposed to have peaches, but instead had grapes and apples.  I'm not saying that's impermissible, but it's totally different.  Lol.  Just saying.
Anyway, from there, the courses went down hill.  The four cheese empanadas were a bit undercooked.  My main course, which the waitress described as their signature dish, was ok but did not make a real impression.  And the dessert....the churros.  I thought that was a safe choice.  WRONG.  They're probably normally excellent, but when I bit into it instead of the lovely, sugary sweetness that I was expecting, I tasted onion and garlic and lots of other savory spices.  Perhaps they had a shortage of oil in the kitchen.  Who knows?  

BUT HERE'S THE REAL PROBLEM: Our waitress brought us the bill and we were winding down when the manager, Adam, came over to our table and said, "ladies, I hope you've enjoyed yourselves and that you will come again.  If you'd like to continue enjoying yourself, I suggest you go to the bar, but we need the table."  Now is probably when I should point out that there were other vacant tables in the dining room and that the couple next to us was in the process of leaving, But I digress.  Apparently there was some special reason why he needed our table.  So we proceed to stare at him like he was crazy.  He took that as his cue to continue talking.  He said, "we've been TRYING TO WORK AROUND YOU, but you've been here for THREE HOURS and we need the table."  We had not been there for three hours, it was slightly over two, and it was a four course meal. Moreover, we had to wait for our table.  Ultimately, however, if their primary concern is just turning tables and not providing a nice dining experience, then they shouldn't be in the restaurant business, nor should they participate in Restaurant Week.  

When we started gathering our belongings, my friend asked the manager to move because he was blocking her chair.  After which he said, "I don't allow people to talk to me like that."  This was unbelievable.   I have never been treated so poorly by a staff member at a restaurant...EVER.  I would not be able to recommend this establishment to my worst frenemy.

The place has a cute atmosphere. Our waitress was really nice. I was not impressed with the food. There were only a handful of people there. Everything we orderd was barely warm, except the grits. My pancake was not fully cooked in the middle. The hollandaise sauce is served room temperature, which we thought was strange.

My favorite hang out on University.  It's a combination of delicious food and great drinks.  It is so laid back and servers so friendly, you don't feel out of place just coming for the pizza (why not, it's good!) but it's equally respectable to be downing shots in the middle of the afternoon.  :)
Good mix, love this place

Attended a 70th birthday party in the Jamison Room.  The buffet food was hot,  plentiful and tasty.  The wait staff were attentive and cheerful throughout the evening.  I'd recommend Dooney's to friends planning an event.

Santana's is the only bakery I know that has the taste and flavor of Puerto Rico, Spain, Argentina, Costa Rica, and all of the South America bakeries! I drive over 30 miles one way to taste this amazing delicious, hot to the touch bread! Also they have lots of pastries, cakes, candies, & exotic dishes, like passion fruit, and Guayaba Mmmmm!
Go there and check it out its amazing

Solid place.  Prices aren't bad.  There are better sushi places in the city for sure, but  definitely a welcome dining option to the area.  Got a tuna roll, some salmon sashimi, and a spider roll.  Cash only operation, and not a heck of a lot of seating inside (well, with '2 go' in their name, that's to be expected).  Would definitely stop by again when I'm in the area and craving sushi.
Really, really good stuff. Creole hot sausage po boy w/ mac and cheese for me, vegetarian nachos for her. Would recommend all of it.

Haven't posted in a long time. This is a great Asian fusion place we found in Nashville near Vanderbilt university. Actually craft cocktails, good wine list and awesome Asian fusion food with Thai themes

I fell in love with Wang Gang while living in Edwardsville a year ago.. Now I try to visit every couple of months. I just went to the new location a couple weeks ago.. no surprises, still very amazing!! actually, they do have a $2 mystery beer special which is pretty cool.. my beer wasn't the greatest, but that's the trade-off of not knowing what you'll get. It was exciting! and my date's beer was pretty tasty. 

I've actually recently transitioned to a plant-based diet, and I love that I can still enjoy Wang Gang while on this diet.. I had the Thai Spiced Peanut with brown rice & Tofu.. sooo tasty. My date had the pineapple fried rice w/ chicken. She loved her dish as well. We also had some lettuce wraps for an appetizer.. I'd definitely recommend these-- the portion size is very generous! 

The staff was also amazing. The host was very courteous and the waitress was very kind and attentive! I've only had ONE problem with Wang Gang and that was about 6 months ago. Our waiter (lead waiter) forgot to put our order in and our wait was a little long.. but they made up for it and comped our appetizer, so all was well! I LOVE restaurants that take pride is customer service. Some do, but sadly, many don't. It shouldn't be so difficult!

I love Wang Gang!!

The only reason I'm giving them a 1 rating is because they don't have a 0 rating. This is the second time I've ordered from here, and the last time. Both times were disasters. Today, I ordered a Turkey & cheese hoagie with banana peppers and yellow mustard. The counter lady was very rude and acted like each customer was an annoyance. After waiting 15 minutes (for a cold cut hoagie, may I add), I finally got it. But it wasn't what I ordered. It had sweet peppers and honey mustard. I then proceeded to say that I ordered banana peppers, in which the rude lady quickly said that they didn't have. SO WHY DIDN'T YOU SAY THAT WHEN I ORDERED?!!?!?! I would have ordered something else. Rudest lady I've ever met. If this place didn't have such a great location, it would become bankrupt. Don't go here if you want an accurate order.

2015- below is an old review of Pinas, however my last few experiences with Pinas have been less than satisfactory. I use to think that they made the best strombolis, but at some point they made changes to how they make their strombolis and they are now mediocre at best. I ordered an Italian stromboli and what I got was a stromboli with a ton of red and green peppers and a bit of sausage chunks. The last time that I checked an Italian anything constitutes of multiple types of meat. I will not be ordering strombolis from them in the future. 

2013- Best pizza in the area. Have never been disappointed by anything my roommate and I have ordered from here.

I give up.

The last three times I've eaten here, something involving shitty customer service, or shitty food has happened.
